## P18-55 - How fighting games show move lists and combos (researched 2026-11-10)

Read: the publishers' own pages first (official sites, patch notes, store pages, the Street Fighter 6 web manual and its character command list pages), then press and community pages, each marked below. Summaries are paraphrased; no name, icon, art or text is taken into Breakpoint, and what is listed are genre conventions. Limits of the reading: the Street Fighter 6 character pages answered the page-fetch tool with HTTP 403, so their text was read with a plain HTTP request (page text only, nothing run); the Street Fighter 6 web manual is a script page, so its text was read from the public data file it loads (`game.capcom.com/manual/SF6/locale/data/en.json`); I did not play the games, so what the in-game screens look like beyond these pages is not verified (the `Not verified` lines).

**Tekken 8 (and 7)**
- Official. Patch notes v1.08.01 describe the in-game Command List, found under PRACTICE and also reached from Sample Combos: it has section headings that the shoulder triggers jump between, an All Techniques list that a button press narrows to the moves that have icons, and (new) a list of the techniques used in Special Styles. So: one list per fighter, split into headings, with a filter and a second list of sample combos.
- Official. The closed-beta guide page of the publisher offers a command list for each new fighter (its layout was not read); press coverage of the official site says every launch fighter has a move list page that is not complete (some fighters have over 100 moves), names the fighter's country and style, lists the Heat (power-up state) moves and gives one example combo per fighter.
- Official. Tekken 7 sold a Frame Data Display add-on with a Simple and a Detailed view, usable in Practice, in the warm-up while waiting online, in online player matches and while spectating (the page does not say what each view shows). Frame data is therefore a layer that is switched on, not part of the plain list.
- Community / press. Main Techniques and All Techniques are two sorts of the Training command list (about 20 main techniques per fighter and about 10 example combos, per Automaton). Notation: directions as letters, buttons as numbers 1 to 4, `+` for together, `,` between the steps of a string, `~` for "immediately", capital letters for a held direction; hit levels as `h m l` plus `sm`, `sl` (special mid, special low), `!` for unblockable; frame columns for active frames, recovery, total and advantage (wavu.wiki). Training display options include a command history and attack and frame readouts (Fresherslive, low quality, only for the existence of the options). Not verified: how the screen draws icons per controller.

**Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. (Ultimate Showdown before it)**
- Official (series site). The command list page of each fighter is a table with the columns Command, Dmg, Lvl, Exe (frames to hit), Act, Tot, Grd / NH / CH (advantage on guard, normal hit, counter hit), Evd (which way a side step beats it) and Notes. Inputs are written for a fighter facing right, so the same list serves both sides. Three views: Tabs (one category per tab), Flat list (for printing) and Icons (thumbnails by category); a click on a column heading sorts; a click on a move opens a detail dialog. Level symbols: H, M, L; a star marks a special variant (for example a high that beats lows when timed); throws have their own codes (high throw, low throw, catch throw, attacking throw, throw combo); other tags for down attacks, reversals and movement.
- Official. The beginner guide on the official site writes commands from the first player's side, left to right; letters side by side are pressed one after the other and `P+K` together; arrows show the stick (a white arrow is a tap, a red arrow a hold). Move lists also have a Down Attacks section for hitting a fallen foe, plus the basic attacks and the guard options. Hit levels are explained as high, mid, low and throw, with what each guard beats.
- Official. The update notes show that the game has a Command Training mode of numbered lessons (for example "14. Throw Escapes - 1": the opponent performs the move, you answer), a command display window while practising, and a replay view with input history, damage, frame advantage, a command display, a High / Middle / Low hit indicator and the evade direction. Battle Tips and Character-Specific Details show an "OK" mark when a listed combo is performed (fixes in v1.07 say it appeared wrongly when the combo failed). Control mapping allows two buttons or keys per function.
- Press. Command Training (original Virtua Fighter 5): perform every move of the list in order and skip the ones that are hard (Giant Bomb). A beginner's guide says the move list opens from the pause menu in Training (Final Weapon). Not verified: the in-game layout of Command Training.

**Street Fighter 6**
- Official (web manual). PRACTICE has four parts: Tutorials (the rules and the battle system), Character Guides (what is special about each fighter and how to use its special moves), Combo Trials (learn the combos that deal big damage when there is a chance in a real fight) and Training (customise the practice routine; a "Simple Training Settings" menu is there for those who do not want detail). Training can record up to 8 action sequences of the dummy and replay them. The battle screen shows a Control Type Icon, so the game always says which of its three control types (Classic six buttons, Modern with one button plus a direction for a special move, Dynamic auto-attack) is in use.
- Official (character command list page). Per fighter: an Icon Legend button, then groups in a fixed order (Special Moves, Super Arts, Unique Attacks, Throws, Common Moves). A row is the move name, a strip of input icons (directions and buttons, with a small H, M or L mark on the buttons of an attack that has a level), a condition in brackets where needed (for example "after ..." or "hold the button to change the effect") and, for the highlighted move, a one-line description. Tabs next to it: COMMAND LIST, FRAME DATA, COSTUME. So the plain list shows no numbers; the numbers live on their own tab.
- Official (character frame data page). Columns: move name, start-up, active, recovery, hit and block advantage, cancel code, damage, combo scaling, resource gain and loss, and a properties code (H, M, L for levels; T throw; P projectile; MP mid-air projectile). Rows are grouped (Normal Moves, ...). A note under a row says when the recovery is longer after a miss. There is also a Battle Change List (what the last patch changed).
- Official. Combo Trials are per fighter and are re-issued when a patch changes the balance (the May 2024 notice for the balance patch; the October 2025 notice added a new fighter's guide and trials); Training gained a Reset Combo Damage option.
- Press. Combo Trials come in three tiers per fighter (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced), the later tiers add a technique at a time, and each trial shows when it was last updated (The Sixth Axis; EventHubs). Character Guides split a move into short segments, each practised in a small scenario (The Sixth Axis). Not verified: the exact trial screen (an on-screen input list with each step ticked as it is done is the common pattern in the genre, but I did not find an official description).

**Soulcalibur VI**
- Official. Patch notes (v2.30): in Training the move list of the opponent's fighter can be viewed and the move list menu got an icon; the command input history stays on screen when the pause menu opens. v1.30: a random option for the command input replay display and a mode switch for it on the touchpad plus Square; Training remembers some settings for the session. The platform blog's starter tips describe a full Training mode and three core attacks (horizontal, vertical, kick) plus guard impact, with no move list screen description.
- Community. A guide says Command List is an item of the pause menu and that Training has a Display Settings page with hit confirm, damage display and frame data options (ludo.guide, may differ by version). Frame data and properties of every move are published on community wikis (the SRK wiki says its data come from FrameCalibur). A Steam thread of 2018 says the game had no manual, only the in-game help. No official move list page was found. Not verified: the in-game layout.

**Patterns every game shares (what Breakpoint takes, as conventions)**

| Pattern | Seen in | Use in Breakpoint |
|---|---|---|
| One list per fighter, in headed groups in a fixed order (basic and special moves first, throws, common moves last); a way to jump between headings | Tekken 8 (shoulder triggers), Street Fighter 6, Virtua Fighter (tabs) | headed groups, a Show filter, heading jump on L1 / R1 and PageUp / PageDown |
| The plain list is names, inputs, a level mark and a short note; the numbers (frames, advantage, scaling) are a separate layer: a tab, an add-on view, a display option | Street Fighter 6 (tab), Tekken 7 (add-on), Tekken 8 (display options), Soulcalibur VI (display settings) | owner's rule: frame data only in Training; the plain list stays short |
| Inputs are icons for the controller in use, with a legend; a text form exists for wikis only | Street Fighter 6 (control type icon, legend), Virtua Fighter (arrows, white tap and red hold), Tekken (numbers) | device chips for the device in use; a legend of the five buttons; text names for screen readers |
| Hit level is a small mark next to the button (H, M, L), and the colour is never the only sign | Street Fighter 6 (mark on the button icon), Virtua Fighter (Lvl column and H, M, L symbols), Tekken (h, m, l) | a glyph (shape plus letter plus colour) |
| Inputs are written one way for every fighter (facing right), conditions go in brackets or tags | Virtua Fighter (faces right), Street Fighter 6 (brackets) | the chips never depend on which side a fighter stands on; conditions are small tags (AIR, RUN, CLINCH, COUNTER) |
| A string is one input line with its steps named; a prefix of a longer string is not listed again | Tekken (commas), Virtua Fighter (letters in order) | leaf strings only, with each step named and marked |
| Sample combos and combo trials are a second list per fighter, in tiers, ticked when done, re-issued when a patch changes the numbers | Tekken 8 (Sample Combos), Street Fighter 6 (Combo Trials), Virtua Fighter (Battle Tips OK mark) | trials generated from the tables, so they cannot go stale |
| A show-me: Command Training performs the move and the player copies it; Character Guides practise one move in a short scenario | Virtua Fighter (Command Training), Street Fighter 6 (Character Guides) | "Show me" in Training: the dummy-side scenario plays the move, then the player tries |
| The list reflects the control scheme in use and the opponent's list can be viewed | Street Fighter 6 (control types), Soulcalibur VI (opponent's list in Training) | device switches the chips; the Training dummy's list is one Show choice away (optional) |

### P18-57 - Real techniques of the 16 fighting styles: sources and technique notes (2026-11-10)

Task: BP-P18-57 (research only; the owner asked on 2026-11-10 for animations that look like the real techniques, for example Capoeira without negativa or spinning kicks). The per-move briefs, the ranking and the work order for P18-58 and P18-59 are in Appendix C, "P18-57 per-move animation briefs". Original work: techniques are public knowledge, every sentence below is written for this game, and nothing is copied from a game, a video or a book.

**How the sources were used.** Read 2026-11-10 (`official` = a governing body, federation, founding school, public institution or the publisher's own page; `reference` = a well-known instructional page, magazine or encyclopedia; `search only` = seen in search results, not opened; `unreachable` = the fetch failed, reason given). A rule book says what is legal and how a blow scores, not how the body moves, so the body mechanics below come from the instructional pages marked `reference` and from the standard public description of each technique; what a cited page does not state is the standard public description in the author's own wording (the pages named under each style are what was checked; where a page was thin, the facts it did give are listed and the rest is standard). Names are the style's own (Japanese, Korean, Thai, Portuguese, Tagalog). Plain ASCII is used, so the Portuguese role (a low roll on the hands and feet) and bencao carry no accents.

**Sources by style (every URL was opened unless marked).**
- Boxing: official https://worldboxing.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/World-Boxing-Competition-Rules-March-2026-v5.0.pdf (Article 7.2: a scoring blow lands cleanly with the knuckle surface of the glove and has the weight of the body or shoulder behind it; used for "weight behind the punch"); reference, search only: https://www.britannica.com/sports/hook-boxing , https://www.britannica.com/sports/uppercut , https://www.britannica.com/sports/jab , https://www.britannica.com/sports/straight-right (orthodox stance: lead foot slightly ahead, left arm partly extended, right arm close to guard stomach and jaw; hook: short lateral arc, elbow bent, force from the hips; uppercut: twist of hips and lead foot raised on the toes; slipping, ducking, rolling with a blow; the pages answered HTTP 403 to the fetch tool, the facts are from the search summaries).
- Kickboxing: official https://www.wako.sport/post/wako-k1-rules (WAKO: K-1 rules score clean punches, kicks and knees that are not blocked or redirected; no leg catching or throwing; two-handed clinch of at most 5 seconds; a 2009 note, current rule books are on https://www.wako.sport/rules-overview and https://www.wako.sport/rules-forms-docs which loaded without their document lists); official, search only: https://www.wako.sport/kickboxing-today (three ring disciplines: Full Contact, Low Kick, K-1).
- Karate: official https://www.wkf.net/files/pdf/documents/WKF_2026_Kumite_Competition_Rules_MASTER_COPY_V13FINAL.pdf (Article 8: scoring areas jodan and chudan; yuko for tsuki or uchi, waza-ari for a chudan kick, ippon for a jodan kick; a score needs good form, sporting attitude, vigorous application, awareness (zanshin), good timing and correct distance); official, search only: https://www.jka.or.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/MANUAL-TECNICO-DE-INSTRUCTOR.pdf (JKA instructor manual, Spanish: gyaku-zuki from zenkutsu-dachi with a full hip turn, hikite, the feet about twice hip width apart, kekomi thrust against keage snap, yoko-geri kekomi on the foot's edge; HTTP 503 with Retry-After 3600 to the fetch tool, facts from the search summary); official: https://www.wkf.net/news-center/article/!/1334/douglas-brose-shows-secrets-in-new-episode-of-learnkaratewith (search only: keep the body upright in a mawashi-geri chudan).
- Wrestling: official https://cdn.uww.org/2023-01/wrestling_rules.pdf (United World Wrestling: Article 35 danger position, Article 37 grand amplitude throw: the foe loses all contact with the ground, is controlled, describes a broadly sweeping curve and lands in direct danger; Article 38 values 1, 2, 4, 5; the opening rules text: Greco-Roman forbids grasping below the belt line, tripping and using the legs actively, Freestyle and Women's wrestling allow leg grasps, trips and active leg use); reference, search only: http://content.themat.com/CoachesCorner/7-Basic-Skills-Guide.pdf (USA Wrestling: the five key positions head up, back straight, hips in, knees off the mat, toe pressure; level change with the penetration step; the certificate failed for the fetch tool).
- Judo: official, search only: http://kodokanjudoinstitute.org/en/docs/nage_no_kata.pdf (Kodokan Nage-no-kata textbook: Ura-nage is a ma-sutemi-waza; kuzushi, tsukuri, kake) and https://kodokanjudoinstitute.org/en/waza/list/ (the Kodokan list; both unreachable: SSL protocol error WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER, and https://www.kodokan.org/e_waza/list.html answered with a certificate for another host); official: https://www.ijf.org/news/show/nage-no-kata-more-than-a-sequence-of-throws (IJF: kuzushi creates imbalance, tsukuri builds the entry, kake executes; the 15 throws of Nage-no-kata in five groups: te-waza uki-otoshi, seoi-nage, kata-guruma; koshi-waza uki-goshi, harai-goshi, tsurikomi-goshi; ashi-waza okuri-ashi-harai, sasae-tsurikomi-ashi, uchi-mata; ma-sutemi-waza tomoe-nage, ura-nage, sumi-gaeshi; yoko-sutemi-waza yoko-otoshi, tani-otoshi, uki-waza); official: https://www--gcp.ijf.org/news/show/the-big-bold-beautiful-ura-nage (IJF: Ura-nage engages the whole chain from ankles to hips and shoulders, a firm hold round the waist, best as a reaction to an attack, demands power and speed).
- Street Brawler: no federation exists. Boxing sources above for the swung hand and the guard; the self-defence pages of Krav Maga Worldwide below for the head and the stomp; the rest is the standard description of untrained fighting (wide loops, planted feet, slow recovery).
- Capoeira: no single federation. Founding-school and federation pages (Fundacao Mestre Bimba, the International Capoeira Angola Foundation) did not appear in the search and were not found. reference: https://papoeira.com/en/the-8-training-sequences-of-mestre-bimba/ (Mestre Bimba's eight training sequences: ginga, meia-lua de frente, armada, au, role; cocorinha and negativa; queixada, martelo, bencao; galopante, godemi; giro and joelhada; meia-lua de compasso; bencao pulado); reference (ABADA-Capoeira): https://akban.org/wiki/Ginga , https://akban.org/wiki/Armada , https://akban.org/wiki/Negativa , https://akban.org/wiki/Bananeira , https://akban.org/wiki/Martelo , https://akban.org/wiki/Meia_Lua_de_compasso (ginga: a dancelike movement that hides the intent and is the platform for kicks, "very free" in Angola and "much more structured" in Regional; armada: from ginga shift the weight, turn about 270 degrees, the rear leg swings out in a spinning arc and comes back to ginga; negativa: crouched, weight on the bent rear leg, front leg extended on its heel, one hand on the floor beside it, the other forearm raised in front of the face; bananeira: turn away, both hands down, kick up into a handstand facing the foe, legs straight or bent; martelo: rotate the standing leg inward, lean the pelvis at the target, knee up then the lower leg out, instep strikes, one hand guards the body and one the face, torso slightly back; meia-lua de compasso: hands on the floor between the legs, chest bent down, eyes on the foe, the free leg sweeps a circle on the pivoting foot); reference, search only: https://periodicos.univasf.edu.br/index.php/revasf/article/download/27/35 (a Brazilian university paper on 23 basic capoeira movements; certificate error for the fetch tool), https://repositorio-aberto.up.pt/bitstream/10216/22047/2/38491.pdf and https://seer.ufu.br/index.php/rascunhos/article/download/35690/20861/165335 (academic texts on Regional and Angola: negativa "denies the body to the attack", role gets up from or escapes low attacks, Pastinha's core list ginga, negativa, cabecada, rabo de arraia, rasteira).

- Krav Maga: official (Krav Maga Worldwide, trained under the founder): https://www.kravmaga.com/kmw-blog/learn-the-most-powerful-groin-kick-for-self-defense (groin kick: fighting stance, curl the heel to the glute so the leg is a triangle with the knee at its tip, drive the knee forward and out so the belly button leads and the shoulders go back, the leg unfolds up and through the target, foot flat with the toes at the opponent, laces or shin strike, recoil the leg to the start); https://www.kravmaga.com/kmw-blog/three-krav-maga-techniques-that-everyone-should-know (long-range groin kick; lower the weight for a base; RCAT: redirect, control, attack, take away); search only: https://kravmaga.com/krav-maga-striking-hands/ (straight punch, palm heel, hammer fist, elbow; the striking surface of the hammer fist is the part of the hand under the little finger; power from hips and shoulders; the page itself answered 404); official, search only: https://www.krav-maga.net/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2024/09/Yellow_belt_2024.pdf and the Blue, Green and Brown belt files of the same folder (a European federation's grading syllabi: 360 degree defences with counter-attack, groin kick, palm strike to the groin in a hug; the files answered 404 to the fetch tool).
- MMA: official https://www.ufc.com/unified-rules-mixed-martial-arts (Unified Rules, adopted by the Association of Boxing Commissions on 30 July 2009: fouls include strikes to the spine or back of the head, downward elbows, groin attacks, kicks or knees to a grounded foe's head, stomping a grounded foe; judging criteria sit in a linked pdf that was not opened).

**Sources that were unreachable or thin (nothing in this appendix depends on them).** Kodokan Judo Institute (SSL error) and kodokan.org (certificate for another host); JKA manual (HTTP 503); Britannica (HTTP 403); the Hong Kong Ving Tsun Athletic Association Origin page (not found); krav-maga.net syllabi and kravmaga.com striking page (404); the Sambo 2023 rules (404); WAKO rule documents (the page loaded without its list); Fundacao Mestre Bimba, the International Capoeira Angola Foundation, the Korea Hapkido Federation, Doce Pares and Arnis Philippines (not found by search); USA Wrestling guide and the Brazilian capoeira paper (certificate errors); the Kukkiwon terminology dictionary (not found as a pdf). The IFMA, WT, UWW, FIAS, IBJJF and WKF pdfs were saved by the fetch tool and read with pdftotext.

**Notation used below.** Phases are: stance, chamber (load), pivot and hip, path of the limb, guard hand, shoulder and hip line, contact, recovery. "Fault" is what makes a drawing of the technique look wrong. J keys are the pose joints of the game: `torsoLean`, `torsoTwist`, `torsoRoll`, `headX`, `shL/Rx z`, `elL/R`, `hipL/Rx z`, `knL/R`, `rootFwd`, `rootDrop`, `bodyPitch`, `bodyRoll`, `bodyYaw` (arms: x = swing forward, z = out to the side; hips: x = swing forward, z = out to the side).

**Shared technique notes (the other styles refer to these).**
- Orthodox punching base (Boxing, Kickboxing, MMA, Krav Maga, Muay Thai): feet a shoulder width apart and a long step staggered, rear heel up, knees soft, chin down behind the lead shoulder, hands up. Jab: the lead shoulder rises to cover the chin as the arm goes out on a straight line, the fist turns palm down at the end, the rear hand never leaves the chin, a small slide step, the arm returns on the same line. Fault: the rear hand drops, the head leans past the lead knee, the elbow flares, the arm swings back before it goes out. Cross: the rear heel turns out and the hip and shoulder drive round together, the chin stays tucked, the lead hand returns to the chin, the weight moves onto the lead leg. Fault: arm only, no hip, flat rear foot, lead hand dropped. Lead hook: the lead foot pivots, hips and torso turn as one block, the elbow is bent about 90 degrees and level with the fist, the arc is flat and short, the rear hand guards the chin. Fault: a long swing from the shoulder, a dropped elbow, no weight shift. Uppercut: knees dip, the shoulder drops to the punching side, the legs drive up and the hip turns, the fist travels up palm to the face on a short vertical line. Fault: the hand winds down by the hip first. Slip: the head moves off the centre line by turning the shoulders and bending the knees a little, the hands stay up. Bob and weave: bend the knees and move under the hook in a U, rise on the far side. Roll: lean into the punch's direction to take the force off.
- Round kick (Karate mawashi-geri, Taekwondo dollyeo chagi, Muay Thai te, Kickboxing round kick, Hapkido and MMA versions): chamber the knee at the front and to the side, turn the support heel toward the target (a half turn or more), the hip opens so the knee points across, the lower leg whips out in a flat arc, contact with the instep (karate, taekwondo) or the shin (Thai, kickboxing), the support leg is nearly straight, the hands keep the guard (karate and taekwondo: the opposite hand pulls in to cover the chin, Kukkiwon), the leg folds back through the chamber and the foot lands in front again. Fault: no support-foot turn, the foot is lifted from the side with no chamber, the body folds forward at the waist, the arms fly out, the kick is a straight leg swing, the recovery goes straight down. Thai style: the whole body swings through, the arm on the kicking side swings down and back, the torso leans back; the leg stays long and the shin lands.
- Front kick (karate mae-geri, taekwondo apchagi, Muay Thai teep, Kickboxing teep): chamber the knee high in front, then the lower leg extends and the hip drives forward; karate keage is a snap (the foot returns before the hip commits), kekomi is a thrust (the hip follows), the Thai teep pushes with the ball of the foot or the sole at the hip or chest, the body leans back and the hips go forward; taekwondo apchagi hits with the ball of the foot. Fault: no chamber, a straight leg lifted from the floor, the support foot flat and the torso leaning forward, the foot pointing up instead of the toes pulled back, the leg dropping instead of snapping back.
- Side kick (yoko-geri kekomi, yeopchagi, sokuto): chamber the knee to the chest, turn the body side-on with the support heel pointing away, the head turns to look over the shoulder, the hip thrusts, the blade of the foot (or the heel) strikes, the leg goes straight out in a line with the shoulders and the torso leans away. Fault: a front kick turned sideways with the body square, a bent support knee collapsing, the head looking at the floor.
- Back kick and spinning kicks (dwit chagi, ushiro-geri, spinning heel hook, armada): look over the shoulder first (head, then shoulders, then hips), the back turns to the target, the kick goes straight back (back kick) or sweeps round (hook) at the end of the turn. WT: the head and shoulders must turn for it to count (Article 11 interpretation). Fault: the kick starts before the head has turned, the body stays square, the foot lands where the hip points rather than where the eyes look.
- Axe kick (naeryeo chagi): the leg goes up straight in front (or from the side) at least to head height, then the heel drops down on the target; the support leg is straight, the body leans back a little to let it go up. Fault: a bent knee swung like a front kick.
- Elbow (Muay Thai sok): the horizontal slash: the arm is folded tight, the elbow is level with the shoulder, the hip and shoulder turn the elbow across, the rear hand covers the chin; the vertical (up and down) elbow uses a rise or a drop. Fault: the arm extends like a punch, the forearm does not stay folded.
- Knee (kao, hiza-geri): clasp or pull the foe, push the hips forward and drive the knee up, the toes point down, the support leg rises on the toes. Fault: the knee goes up with the hips behind, the torso stays upright and far away.
- Takedowns: level change (the hips and chest drop, the back stays straight, the head stays up), penetration step (the lead foot drives between the foe's feet), then lift or drive. Double leg: head beside the foe's hip, both arms round the legs, the lifted foe goes over or back. Single leg: one leg is lifted to the hip, the head is on the inside, the foe's knee is trapped. Sprawl: the hips shoot back and down, the legs go back wide, the chest lands on the shoulders. Faults: dropping the head first, bending at the waist with the legs straight, a step that does not reach.
- Judo structure: grip (sleeve and lapel), kuzushi (the foe's balance is pulled forward or to the corner), tsukuri (the body turns and fits in), kake (the throw is executed), then the follow-up (osaekomi). Faults: kake without kuzushi (the foe is lifted with arms), the throwing hip too far from the foe, the thrower's head dropping.

**Boxing (Boxing: yuki, deacon).**
- Stance and guard: orthodox, lead foot ahead of the rear, weight even, knees soft, chin tucked behind the lead shoulder, the lead glove at cheek or eye height and slightly forward, the rear glove at the chin, elbows in on the ribs, shoulders rolled up (Britannica: lead arm partly extended, rear arm close to guard the stomach and jaw).
- Idle: a constant light bounce on the balls of the feet, small head moves, feints with the lead hand and shoulder, never standing flat; the hands never drop.
- Steps and evasions: step and drag (lead foot first, rear foot follows, feet never cross), pivot round the lead foot; slip, bob and weave, roll and cover (Britannica names slip, duck, roll).
- Jab (jab, body_jab): shared; the body jab bends the knees and dips the shoulder so the fist lands at the belt. Cross (cross, power_jab): shared. Hook (hook): shared; the body hook (body_hook) bends the knees and rotates the same way to the ribs. Bob and Weave Hook (bob_hook): duck under, then rise through the hook from the legs; the head moves from the centre line. Uppercut (uppercut, heavy_uppercut): shared. Liver shot (heavy_body_kick skin): the lead hook to the right ribs, the boxer leans away a little and bends the knees. Clinch shove-off (throw front.fwd): in the clinch both hands push the foe's chest or shoulders as the boxer steps back out. Clinch body shot: short hooks to the ribs.
- Faults that look wrong: kicks (there are none), a stiff upright pose, hands dropped when punching, a wide round arm hook.

**Kickboxing (Kickboxing: kai, femke).**
- Stance: a boxing stance, more upright, narrower and a little more sideways than Boxing, the lead foot light and ready to teep or check, hands high, a rhythmic lead-leg bounce and a quick step in and out of range; the rear heel is up.
- Steps and evasions: step and slide, a switch of stance, slip and counter, leg check (lifting the lead knee to take a low kick on the shin).
- Round kick (roundhouse, heavy_roundhouse): shared; the support foot turns, the hip over, the arm swings; the hands stay up. Switch kick (switch_kick): a small hop that swaps the feet, then the new rear leg kicks as a round kick; the Breakpoint row has the left leg kicking. Heavy Push Kick (heavy_front): teep, the knee up first, the foot pushes at the belt, the body leans back. Spinning Backfist (backfist): a full turn on the lead foot with the head first, the whole arm whips round at shoulder height, the back of the fist lands, the eyes look over the shoulder; fault: the arm swings without the turn. Low Kick (low_kick): a round kick to the thigh, the support foot turns, the shin lands, the body leans away. Counter Low Kick: the same on the foe's step in. Flying Knee (jump_kick skin): a step and jump, one knee drives up, the arms hold the guard. Clinch Sweep (throw): a short push with the front hand and a leg sweep; WAKO K-1 limits the clinch to a two-handed 5 seconds and bans throws.

**Karate (Karate: zero, amara).**
- Stance and guard: zenkutsu-dachi (front stance), the front knee over the ankle and bent, the rear leg straight, the feet about twice the hip width apart (JKA manual summary), the hips turn from half-facing to square (hanmi to shomen) quickly, smoothly and parallel to the floor; the guard: hikite, the non-punching fist pulled to the hip; in free fighting the stance is higher and the hands are up. WKF scoring wants zanshin: the fighter stays facing the foe after a technique.
- Idle: still and low, a few small steps, then a burst; no bounce.
- Steps and evasions: step in and out in a line (yori-ashi), tai-sabaki (a body turn off the line), block then counter; the game's Sway pose shows a lean back.
- Reverse punch (cross, gyaku-zuki): the rear fist goes out as the rear hip turns forward, the rear leg pushes, the opposite hand is pulled to the hip with the same timing, the fist turns palm down at the end, the shoulders stay level, the head stays still, then the muscles tense at contact and relax. Fault: the fist turns early, the hikite is late, the body leans in. Lunge Punch (power_jab, lunge_punch, oi-zuki): a step forward into a deep front stance with the punch landing as the step lands, the punching arm on the side of the front foot, the hips square. Gedan Punch: a punch to the belly with the stance low. Front kick (front_kick, mae-geri; heavy_front, kekomi): shared; the toes are pulled back and the ball of the foot strikes. Side Thrust Kick (side_kick, yoko-geri kekomi): shared; the edge of the foot strikes. Round kick (roundhouse, heavy_roundhouse, mawashi-geri): shared; the body stays upright (WKF note). Foot sweep (sweep, ashi-barai): the sole sweeps the foe's lead ankle from the side. Foot-Sweep Throw (throw front.fwd): a sweep while pulling the foe's sleeve and pushing his chest. Kyokushin Round Kick: the shin lands on a leg or the ribs.

**Wrestling (Wrestling: kelsey, dmitri).**
- Stance: staggered, hips low, knees bent, chest over the knees, head up, back straight, weight on the balls of the feet, the hands forward at chest height reaching for ties (USA Wrestling's key positions: head up, back straight, hips in, knees off the mat, toe pressure).
- Idle: low and heavy, small shifts, the hands moving in constant hand-fighting (collar tie, wrist control), never still.
- Steps and evasions: shuffle steps (no crossed feet), circle, the sprawl against a shot, the hips shooting back.
- Snap Down (snap_down): both hands on the back of the foe's head and neck, pull it down hard, the hips back, then circle to the side or go behind. Ankle Trip (foot_sweep, trip) and Single-Leg Trip: a level change, one hand behind the heel, the other pushes the knee, the head to the inside. Shoulder Charge (heavy_front): a shot with the shoulder into the thigh or belly, the head up, the legs drive. Underhook Smash (hook) and Underhook Lift (heavy_uppercut): the arm goes under the foe's arm, the hand reaches the back, the hips close in, the chest on the chest; the lift is a body-lock or a hip-through. Sprawl and Drive (counter_kick): the hips drop and shoot back, the legs go wide, the chest lands on the foe's shoulders, then he is driven forward. Fireman's Carry (throw low.back): the thrower drops to one knee, an arm goes round the neck and the other under the near leg, the foe is lifted over the shoulders. Pin (hold): kneeling across the foe, the arms clamping a limb; UWW: a fall needs the shoulders held to the mat for a moment.
- Faults: standing tall with straight legs, rounded back, head down, hands low, kicks and punches that wrestling never uses.

**Judo (Judo: elise, naran).**
- Stance and guard: shizen-hontai, upright and relaxed, the feet a shoulder width apart, the knees soft; the hands in front of the chest reaching for the sleeve and the lapel (kumikata); jigotai (a lower crouch) for defence.
- Idle: calm weight shifts side to side, a slow pull and push with the grips (kuzushi attempts), no bounce.
- Steps and evasions: tsugi-ashi and ayumi-ashi (never crossed feet), turning (tai-sabaki), the pull-and-resist of the grips.
- Collar Pull (collar_snap) and Low Sleeve Pull (body_jab): a quick pull of the lapel or sleeve to take the foe's balance forward (kuzushi), the other hand holds the sleeve. Push-Out (heavy_front): a push of the shoulders or chest that moves the foe back to prepare a throw. Lift-Up (heavy_uppercut): the foe is pulled up on his toes (tsurikomi), the knees bend and the hip goes under. Reaping Foot Sweep (sweep) and Counter Sweep (counter_kick): de-ashi-barai or okuri-ashi-harai: the foe's foot is swept as it is about to take the weight, the pull turns him over the swept foot (ashi-waza of Nage-no-kata, IJF). Ura-nage (throw front.back): arms round the foe's waist from the front, the thrower steps in close and bends back, lifts the foe over his own body while falling back; ma-sutemi-waza (Kodokan); the whole kinetic chain from the ankles to the hips and shoulders (IJF). Hold-Down (hold, kesa-gatame): the scarf hold, from the side, one arm round the neck and the other holding the foe's arm, the chest on his chest, the legs apart; the arm lock (ude-hishigi) and the choke (shime-waza) follow.
- Faults: kicks and punches, a stiff straight-arm shove, the thrower's head far from the foe.

**Street Brawler (Street Brawler: brutus).** No governing body; the notes follow the boxing sources and the standard picture of untrained fighting.
- Stance: square and wide, the hands loose at chest height, the chin dropped, rolling shoulders, heavy steps, the weight on the heels.
- Idle: slow sway from foot to foot, the shoulders rolling, the head moving a little.
- Steps and evasions: crude (a step back, a lean, a flinch), covering the head with the forearms.
- Haymaker (hook): the whole body swings: a wide loop from far back, the hips and shoulders turn first, the weight goes onto the front leg, the head follows the fist, the guard hand drops, the recovery is slow. Wild Jab and Big Right (jab, cross): the same loop with a lunge. Head Butt (headbutt): the hands grab the foe's head or shoulders, the neck is braced, the forehead goes into the face. Swing Kick: a wide round kick from the hip with no chamber and the body leaning away. Stomp (stomp): the knee lifts, the heel drives down on the foot or shin. Bear-Hug Slam (throw front.back): both arms round the foe's body, a lift, a drop of the weight, the foe slammed.
- Faults: crisp boxing technique (the brawler should look slow and big).

**Capoeira (Capoeira: mara, tiago).**
- Stance: ginga. The feet are apart and the knees bent, one leg steps back in a triangle path and the other follows, so the body rocks side to side; one arm guards the face and the other is at the chest or low, the arms alternate with the legs; the eyes stay on the foe (the step, arm and eye details are the standard description; AKBAN says only that the ginga is a dancelike movement that hides the intent and is the platform for every kick, Regional's more structured and Angola's freer).
- Idle: the ginga never stops (about one step a second); the weight drops lower on the back step, the arms alternate.
- Steps and evasions (Capoeira has no blocks): esquiva (a side step with a lean that takes the head off the line, one hand up); negativa (low, the weight on the bent rear leg, the front leg extended on its heel, one hand on the floor and the other forearm over the face, AKBAN; Bimba: "denies the body to the attack"); cocorinha (a squat with the hands covering the face); role (a low roll on the hands and feet to the side to escape a low attack or to get up from a negativa); au (cartwheel); queda de rins and bananeira (handstand, AKBAN).
- Tapa (jab skin): an open-hand slap to the face during the ginga with the free arm. Bencao (front_kick, heavy_front): the bencao: the sole of the foot pushes the chest or belly, the body leans back, the hand covers the face. Meia-lua de frente (not in the game): a leg arc from outside to inside. Queixada and Martelo (roundhouse, heavy_roundhouse): queixada: a wide arc kick that hits the jaw from the outside; martelo: the hammer (AKBAN): the standing leg turns inward, the pelvis leans at the target, the knee rises and the lower leg extends, the instep strikes, one hand guards the body and the other the face, the torso leans back a little. Armada (armada): from the ginga the body turns about 270 degrees, the rear leg is swung round in a spinning arc and returns to the ginga (AKBAN); the head looking back first, the leg at head height and the heel or outer edge striking at the end of the turn are the standard description; the hands stay up (or one on the floor). Meia-lua de compasso (the compass half-moon, not a game row): hands on the floor, the leg sweeps a circle. Au Batido (cartwheel): a cartwheel, the legs strike in the air. Bananeira kick (handstand_kick): from the handstand, a kick with the legs bent, the body inverted. Rasteira (low_kick, sweep): the body drops to a crouch (an esquiva or a negativa), one leg sweeps the foe's supporting foot low and wide, one hand down for support. Cabecada (headbutt): from a negativa or a low crouch the head goes into the chest or belly, the hands cover. Flip Kick (jump_kick): a flip (au sem mao or a back flip) with a kick.
- Faults: spinning with no ginga entry, kicks from a standing guard, no hand on the floor in low moves, straight upright posture, the kick far above the head height needed.

**Wing Chun (Wing Chun: rosa, hao).**
- Stance and guard: yi ji kim yeung ma, the two-character goat-gripping stance: the feet about shoulder width and turned slightly in, the knees bent and turned in, the weight even, the back straight; the elbows are low and near the body, the hands on the centre line: one hand forward (the lead hand in front of the chin), one at the elbow (WCI: the elbow is kept behind the fist in a straight line, the power comes from turning the body in time with the hip and elbow).
- Idle: quiet, high and compact, a small sinking in the knees, no bounce; the hands feel for contact.
- Steps and evasions: the centre line principle (guard your own, attack the foe's), the turning stance (pivot on the heels to face a corner), shifting steps; deflection with pak sau (a slap to the side), the wing arm (bong sau) and the palm (tan sau); sticking hands (chi sao, "the nucleus of Ving Tsun", WVTAA).
- Chain Punch (chain_punch): a vertical fist (thumb up) straight from the centre of the chest, alternating hands without a pause, each fist returning to the centre; the elbows stay low and the shoulders relaxed; little body turn. Centre Thrust (power_jab): one heavier chain punch with a step. Trap Strike (trap_strike, pak sau + strike): the lead hand slaps the foe's guard across and down (or grabs it: lap sau), then the rear hand punches over it on the centre line. Thrust Kick (front_kick, jing geuk): a low front kick with the heel or the sole to the shin, the knee or the belly, the lead hand stays up, the torso upright. Pak Da (counter_strike): pak sau and a punch with the other hand at the same time. Trap Trip (throw front.fwd): the foe's arm is trapped and the leg hooks his lead leg.
- Faults: a wide boxing stance, a bouncing idle, hooking arcs, a torso turned wide, a punch with a horizontal fist, the trailing hand dropped.

**Muay Thai (Muay Thai: pranee, lars).**
- Stance and guard: more upright and square than boxing, the weight a little back on the rear leg so the lead leg is free to teep or check, the hands high and wide at the temples with the elbows in, the chin tucked, a long guard.
- Idle: a heavy rocking bounce on the lead leg and a steady rhythm of small steps; the lead leg lifts and settles. The ring entry, Wai Kru and Ram Muay (IFMA: Mai Muay) are the formal ritual.
- Steps and evasions: step and angle off, the leg check (lift the knee and meet a kick with the shin), the shoulder shrug against a punch, the push with the lead foot.
- Teep (heavy_front, teep): shared. Round kick (roundhouse, heavy_roundhouse): shared (the Thai version): the whole body turns through, the arm swings, the shin hits. Body Kick (heavy_body_kick): the Thai round kick to the ribs: the same hip turn at the lower line. Elbow (elbow_strike): the horizontal sok. Counter Elbow: the elbow thrown as the foe steps in. Knee (clinch knee): the plum clinch (both hands behind the foe's head, elbows tight on his collarbones), the head pulled down, the hips forward, alternating knees. Knee-Lift Dump (throw front.back): a knee under the foe's thigh while pulling him down and back. Clinch Sweep: a push and a leg sweep. Flying Knee: a step and jump with a knee, the hands up.
- Faults: a bouncing boxer's stance, kicks with no hip turn, the arm extended in an elbow, the guard down.

**Taekwondo (Taekwondo: sora, diego).**
- Stance: the fighting stance (gyeorugi): the body sideways (about 45 degrees), the feet a shoulder width or more apart front to back, the lead hand at the chin and the rear hand at the chest, the weight light on the balls of the feet, a constant bounce or hop.
- Idle: a light bounce with a switch of the feet, the lead foot up and ready.
- Steps and evasions: step in and out with a hop, back-step then counter-kick, the turning side-step, fast retreat.
- Ap Chagi (front_kick, heavy_front, low_kick): the front kick: the knee up, the ball of the foot snaps out, the hips forward, snapped back. Dollyeo Chagi (roundhouse, heavy_roundhouse): the turning kick (shared): chamber, the support heel turns, the instep whips round, the opposite hand pulled in (Kukkiwon). Spinning Back Kick (spin_back_kick): the dwit chagi, the head turns first and the shoulders follow, then the leg shoots back with the heel; WT counts it as a turning kick only if the head and shoulders turn. Jump Round Kick (jump_round): twieo dollyeo chagi: a jump off the rear foot and a turning kick in the air. Axe Kick (axe_kick): naeryeo chagi: shared. Tornado Kick (jump_kick skin): dolgae chagi: a jump with a 360 degree turn and a kick at the end (nbtkda: a double pivot). Hook Trip (throw): a foot hooks the foe's lead ankle. Reverse Punch (cross skin): the rear straight punch with the knuckles, only on the trunk (WT).
- Faults: a hand-first fighter with a flat stance, a kick with no chamber, a back kick without the head turn, a kick that lands high with a bent support leg.

**Sambo (Sambo: giorgi, armine).**
- Stance: a wrestler's stance upright to low, the hands forward on the jacket (sleeve and lapel), the lead leg ready to hook; Sambo shoes (boots) on the feet.
- Idle: low and slow, the hands in constant grip fighting, the weight shifting side to side.
- Steps and evasions: shuffle steps, pull and turn out of a grip, the sprawl.
- Sambo Hip Throw (throw front.fwd): a hip throw (the FIAS book values a throw by the foe's landing and the lift): the arm round the neck or the belt, the hips under the foe's hips, a bend of the knees, the foe turns over the hip; the Breakpoint pose drops to one knee at the lift (a kneeling hip throw). Leg Hook Throw (throw low.back): a hooking leg trips the foe's lead leg while the arms pull. Boot Kick (front_kick): a front kick with the shoe to the shin or knee, a combat-sambo idea; the sport rules have no strikes. Leg Pick (leg_pick): a level change and a grab of one leg. Leg Lock (hold): the foe's leg is trapped under the arms, the thrower sits back and pulls the heel (FIAS: a painful hold on the leg, 60 seconds, ends when the defender stands); Heel Hook is not allowed in the FIAS sport book read (the book only says arm locks and leg locks; check before showing it). Hold-down: the chest across the foe.
- Faults: a boxer's stance, kicks higher than the knee, throws with straight arms.

**Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu (BJJ: reid, camila).**
- Stance: standing: a crouch with the hands forward gripping the collar and sleeve, the head low; the fighter pulls guard (sits and brings the feet up) rather than throwing; on the ground: guard, the legs round the foe's waist or the feet on his hips, the forearms as frames, the hips mobile.
- Idle: low and still, the weight shifting, the hands feeling for grips; on the floor, the hips move side to side (the shrimp).
- Steps and evasions: hip escape (shrimp), the technical stand-up, retreat to guard, the grip fight.
- Guard Pull (throw low.back): sit to the floor while holding a grip, the feet go to the foe's hips and pull him in (IBJJF: a takedown that starts after the pull does not score). Guard Kick (guard_kick): from seated guard the foot pushes the foe's hip or knee. Frame Jab and Guard Push (jab, heavy_front): the forearm and the palm frame the foe's neck or chest to hold the distance. Scissor Sweep (sweep): from the closed guard, one shin across the belt, the other leg on the floor, a sleeve and collar grip, the legs scissor, the foe rolls over and the sweeper ends on top (IBJJF: a sweep scores 2). Butterfly Sweep (foot_sweep): hooks inside the thighs, the body falls to the side and the hooks lift. Single-Leg Takedown (throw low.fwd): a level change, one leg held to the hip, the head on the inside, the foe driven down. Armbar (hold): the foe's arm between the legs, the thumbs up, the hips lifting; on the back, the legs across the foe's body and chest.
- Faults: standing striking, kicks, upright posture on the floor, the body lying flat.

**Hapkido (Hapkido: vikram, lucia).**
- Stance and guard: half-facing (the body turned about 45 degrees), the feet staggered and a little wide, the knees soft, the hands open and forward at the belly or chest height ready to catch a wrist; a relaxed, calm guard.
- Idle: small circular weight shifts, no bounce; the hands move like water.
- Steps and evasions: circling away from the force (a side step and a turn so the attack passes by), then joining its line to lock or throw; principles of harmony (hwa), the circle (won) and water (yu).
- Palm Strike (palm_strike, cross skin): a palm heel to the chin or the chest, the fingers back, from a relaxed arm, the other hand open. Heel Push Kick (heavy_front): a front kick with the heel to the belly or the knee. Low Front Kick (front_kick skin): a short kick to the shin or the knee. Spinning Heel Kick (spin_heel): a spinning heel (hook) kick; in the game it is a Low row: a low spin that sweeps. Wrist-Lock Throw (throw front.back): the foe's wrist is caught, the hand twists outward over his centre line, the hapkido fighter steps and turns in a circle, the foe's arm drives down and he falls. Wrist Lock (hold): kneeling low, one hand twisting the wrist, the other on the elbow. Reaping Foot Sweep (sweep): a sweep of the lead foot.
- Faults: a hard linear stance, a boxer's bounce, locks with no circle.

**Kali / Eskrima (Kali: marlon, nia).**
- Stance: bladed, staggered, the knees bent, the weight 50-50 and ready to move on triangle paths (the ascending and descending triangle, diamond, pendulum shuffle, step and slide, from the Oxnard outline); the weapon hand (here the striking hand) is up and the live hand is up near the chin or shoulder to check, trap and defang the snake.
- Idle: continuous movement, small steps along the triangle, the hands flowing (the live hand moves in small circles), the head moving.
- Steps and evasions: angling off the line (zoning), weaving, "breaking the vertical plane" and "controlling the center line", checking with the live hand.
- Angle 1 (angle_one): a diagonal strike from the shoulder down to the foe's right neck (the forehand), the body turns with it, the live hand checks; Angle 2 (angle_two): the diagonal backhand to the foe's left neck; Angle 3 and 4: horizontal strikes across the midsection; Angle 5, Thrust (jab, power_jab, body_jab): a straight thrust to the abdomen (the Oxnard list). Redonda (hook): the round strike, a flowing circular strike with the body turning behind it. Live-Hand Trap (grab): the live hand pins or hooks the foe's arm while the other strikes. Arm-Drag Takedown (throw): the foe's arm is dragged across and pulled while the leg trips. Shin Kick and Knee Kick (front_kick, low_kick): low kicks to the shin or knee.
- Faults: straight line boxing strikes without angles, a static stance, the live hand dropped, strikes that do not flow into each other.

**Krav Maga (Krav Maga: yoav, kasia).**
- Stance and guard: the fighting stance (a modified boxer's stance): the feet staggered, knees bent, the hands up and open or loosely closed in front of the face, the chin tucked, the weight balanced to move in every direction (KMW: a reset point that allows stable movement and primes the body for explosive strikes).
- Idle: ready and mobile, a small bounce, the eyes on the threat's hands; a scanning head.
- Steps and evasions: defend and attack at once (the hands deflect as the counter lands), the 360 degree defences (the forearm sweeps the line of the attack), the step back into the safe angle.
- Parry Strike (parry_strike, counter_strike): an inside parry with one hand while the other punches; Hammer Fist (hook): a closed fist striking with the heel of the fist, the arc short from above or the side (KMW: the striking surface is the part of the hand under the little finger), the power from the hips and shoulders; Groin Kick (groin_kick): shared by KMW: the heel to the glute, the knee drives forward and out, the belly button leads, the leg unfolds up and through, the foot flat with the toes forward, the laces or shin strike, recoil; Stomp Kick (heavy_front): a heel stomp at the knee or shin; Defend-and-Strike (counter_strike): the same counter. Wrist Takedown and Collar Takedown (throws).
- Faults: a long, low stance with no hands up, stylish spinning kicks, kicks above the waist, blocks with no counter.

**MMA (MMA: cruz, tessa).**
- Stance and guard: a boxing stance with the hips a little more square and the feet a little wider than a boxer's (the takedown defence), the hands high, the chin down, the lead leg ready to check.
- Idle: a mobile bounce with a level change threat, the hands feeling; the feet shift in and out.
- Steps and evasions: pivot off the fence, circle away, the sprawl, the head off the line.
- Overhand (overhand): the rear hand goes up and over in an arc, the torso rotates and drops its weight, the head leaves the centre line, the guard hand covers; Superman Punch (superman): a rear-leg kick feint swings back and up, then the body leaps forward behind the rear hand; Oblique Kick (heavy_front): a straight push of the lead foot into the foe's lead knee from the side, the hips turned; Round Kick (roundhouse): a Thai-style round kick; Cage Takedown (throw low.back): the foe against the fence, a double leg with a drive and a trip; Mount (hold): sitting astride the chest with the knees at the foe's ribs, one hand pinning and the other ready to hit (the Unified Rules ban strikes to the back of the head or spine and downward elbows).
- Faults: one pure style (a karate stance or a wrestler's low stance with no striking guard), a flat flying move, a mount that floats over the foe.

### P0-01 - Baseline commit (2026-10-28)

- Baseline = commit `c760489` (main), annotated tag `breakpoint-1.0.0-baseline`. `breakpoint.html` there is VERSION '1.0.0', 585241 bytes in the repository (LF), 594996 bytes in the Windows working copy (CRLF).
- Reason: every later change can be compared with, or rolled back to, this tag.

### P0-04 - Low-spec performance method and baseline (2026-10-28)

- Target device class: low-spec Android phone (about 4x slower CPU than a desktop i5-9600K, weak GPU), landscape 640x360 CSS px, browser Chrome.
- Target frame rate: 60 fps. Pass rule: frame interval p95 <= 18 ms and main-thread work p95 <= 8 ms (half the 16.7 ms frame, leaves room for the GPU and the browser).
- Test scene: `BREAKPOINT.benchmark(seconds)` from the main menu (default 10 s plus 1 s warm-up). It picks the arena with the most destructible objects (now `warehouse`), runs two Expert AI fighters (current maximum: 2) and smashes every object again every 2 s so debris stays at the quality cap. Real rendering, real HUD.
- Metrics returned: frame interval p50 / p95 / max, main-thread work per frame p50 / p95 / max (simulation start to render submit; not capped by vsync), draw calls, instances, debris, particles (peaks), JS heap (Chrome only), startup time, quality level, render scale, resolution. File size: bytes of `breakpoint.html` on disk.
- Low-spec emulation (repeatable on a desktop): Playwright Chrome, viewport 640x360, CDP `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` 4, setting `quality: 'low'`. A real-device row is added in P16-03.
- Baseline (Chrome 156, i5-9600K, after the P0-05 / P0-06 additions, which do not run during play):

| Run | Frame p50 / p95 / max (ms) | Work p50 / p95 / max (ms) | Draws | Instances | Debris | Particles | Heap (MB) | Startup (ms) | Quality / scale / resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop 1280x720, auto quality | 16.7 / 16.8 / 17.0 | 1.1 / 1.7 / 3.7 | 12 | 476 | 79 | 233 | 10.4 | 87 | high / 1.0 / 1280x720 |
| Low-spec emulation | 16.7 / 16.8 / 16.9 | 3.2 / 4.5 / 13.0 | 10 | 262 | 60 | 140 | 9.9 | 162 | low / 0.6 / 384x216 |

- File size baseline: 585241 bytes (LF, repository). Headless AI vs AI simulation speed: one 38 s match in 35 ms.

### P0-05 - Performance overlay (2026-10-28)

- The existing overlay (setting "Performance overlay", `showStats`) now also shows frame time p50 / p95 over the last 240 frames. The URL flag `?perf` or `#perf` shows it without changing the saved setting. Off by default.

### P0-06 - Headless AI vs AI runner (2026-10-28)

- `BREAKPOINT.simulate(opts)` from the main menu (code: `SimRunner.run`). Options: `playerId`, `opponentId`, `arenaId`, `difficulty` (both sides) or `difficulty1` / `difficulty2`, `seed`, `winsNeeded`, `timer`. Both sides deal unscaled damage (`evenDamage`), so the result shows the fighters, not the CPU difficulty bonus.
- Returns winner (0 / 1, -1 if the 15-minute cap is reached), seconds, ticks, rounds, wins, health left and damage dealt per move type per side (`punch`, `kick`, `heavy`, clinch categories, `ground`, `throw`, `other` = walls, objects, chip).
- Runs with no rendering, sound, effects or HUD (event listeners are swapped out for the run). Self-test case "Headless AI vs AI runner" checks a seeded match ends with a winner and the same seed gives the same result.

### P1-03 - Best ideas not already implemented (2026-10-28)

- Rule (owner): accept only mechanics with Modern Urban fit = yes and mobile complexity low or medium, or that replace an existing mechanic without adding inputs. Mechanics already fully in BREAKPOINT are not listed again.
- Notes: grab knee / elbow strikes already exist (CLINCH_MOVES, 2 strikes per clinch), so P3-03 only adds per-style animations. Two rejections are judgment calls (bound / wall-bound duplicates the juggle limit and wall slam; aging on death duplicates the Age slider P6-04). The three new tasks add systems: the owner may drop them.

Rule applied: accept = fit yes AND mobile low or medium, OR replaces an existing mechanic without adding inputs. "Already in" = In BREAKPOINT is yes. Overlaps resolved: accept one, reject the other.

Already in (not accepted again): small attack set, knockdown flow (juggles, launchers, quick rise), sidestep, block with perfect-block window, strike / throw / guard triangle with escape, grip throws and throws into scenery, grab strikes (knee / elbow, 2 per clinch), destructible walls and objects, survival and practice modes.

### P1-04 - Martial arts styles (2026-10-28)

- The 7 existing style ids stay (old saves and share codes keep working); 9 styles are added. Block / Sway defaults are design choices, balanced later in P3-02 and P14-04. Savate and Silat are the first candidates if more styles are wanted.

#### P1-04 style list (decision)

Decision: 16 styles in 7 families. The 7 existing move styles are all kept (same ids, so old saves keep working) and 9 are new. Defense type below is only the DEFAULT for a new character of that style; the creator may change it (P3-01), a character still has exactly one.

| Style | Family | Signature traits (own words) | Default defense + reason | Replaces / extends existing | Shared animations with |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boxing (boxer) | Hand striking | Hands-only; tight high guard and tucked chin; jab-cross-hook-uppercut strings; bounce on the balls of the feet; head movement (slip, bob, weave) instead of kicks | Sway - real boxers defend mostly by slipping and bobbing | Extends `boxer` (keep id) | Western punch set shared with Kickboxing, Muay Thai, MMA, Street Brawler, Krav Maga |
| Wing Chun | Hand striking | Narrow, high stance with elbows in; guards the centre line; fast chain punches; traps and pins the opponent's arms at very short range; low, quick kicks only | Block - parry-and-strike deflection is its core defense | NEW | Chain punch is its own; shares straight-punch base with Boxing; traps shared with Kali (live hand) and Hapkido |
| Kickboxing (kickboxer) | Clinch kickboxing | Upright long guard; boxing punches blended with karate-style and Thai-style kicks; rhythmic lead-leg bounce; body knees and short clinches | Block - raised guard and shin cover both punches and kicks | Extends `kickboxer` (keep id, stays the default style) | Punches from Boxing; round kick from Karate/Muay Thai; knee strike from Muay Thai |
| Muay Thai | Clinch kickboxing | "Eight limbs": fists, elbows, knees, shins; neck clinch with knee strikes; push-kick (teep) to hold distance; round kick with the shin; blocks round kicks by lifting the shin | Block - shin check and forearm cover are its signature defense | NEW | Punches from Boxing; clinch/knee/elbow set shared with Kickboxing, MMA, Krav Maga; grab knee/elbow (P3-03) is its showcase |
| Karate (karateka) | Kicking arts | Long, low, still stances; sharp straight punches (reverse punch); crisp front, round and side kicks; hard blocks (uke) then counter; full-contact Kyokushin flavour | Block - hard blocking is the defining karate defense | Extends `karateka` (keep id) | Linear kick set shared with Taekwondo; blocks shared with Kickboxing |
| Taekwondo | Kicking arts | Kicks are the main weapon, hands support; head-height kicks; fast jumping and spinning kicks; light bouncing footwork and distance control | Sway - it avoids by distance and angle rather than blocking | NEW | Linear kicks shared with Karate; spinning/jump kicks shared with Capoeira (variant pivot) |
| Capoeira | Kicking arts | Constant rocking step (ginga); dodges low and to the side (esquiva); low spinning kicks; handstands, cartwheels and inverted moves; almost no hand strikes | Sway - evasion is the whole art | Extends `capoeira` (keep id) | Round kick base shared with Taekwondo; low sweep with Judo/Wrestling takedown family only as a trip |
| Wrestling (wrestler) | Throws and takedowns | Low level, wide base, hands up hunting for ties; single/double-leg takedowns and body-lift throws; pins and top control; no strikes in the sport | Block - hand fighting and sprawling absorb and stop attacks | Extends `wrestler` (keep id) | Takedown and lift set shared with Judo, Sambo, MMA; ground control shared with BJJ |
| Judo (judoka) | Throws and takedowns | Upright relaxed stance; grip fighting on collar and sleeve; off-balance then throw (hip, shoulder, foot sweep, sacrifice); hold-downs, chokes and arm locks on the ground | Sway - judo uses body shifting to dodge and set up counter throws | Extends `judoka` (keep id) | Throw set shared with Wrestling, Sambo, Hapkido (judo-derived); newaza shared with BJJ |
| Sambo | Throws and takedowns | Soviet military/police origin; wrestling-judo mix in a jacket; throws then ground control; leg locks and heel hooks; combat version adds strikes | Block - tough, forward, stand-your-ground military style | NEW | Throws from Judo/Wrestling; leg locks shared with BJJ; combat strikes from Boxing/Kickboxing |
| Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu | Locks and submissions | Fights well from the back (guard); sweeps to reverse position; pins (side control, mount, back); chokes and joint locks to make the opponent tap; pulls guard instead of throwing | Sway - guard retention and hip movement slip pressure rather than blocking | NEW | Submission set shared with Hapkido (arm/wrist locks) and Sambo (leg locks); ground states shared with Wrestling, Judo, MMA |
| Hapkido | Locks and submissions | Korean self-defense mix; wrist and elbow locks; judo-style throws; low sweeping and spinning heel kicks; circular movement redirects force; cane as a training weapon | Sway - circular evasion and redirection | NEW | Wrist/elbow locks with BJJ and Krav Maga; throws with Judo; kicks with Taekwondo |
| Kali / Eskrima | Weapon styles | Philippine art built on the rattan stick (baston); numbered angles of attack; fast double-stick weaving (sinawali) and flow drills; the empty "live hand" traps, locks and disarms; same movement with empty hands and improvised tools | Sway - uses footwork and body angle to take the body off the line of the strike | NEW | Stick moves = weapon move set (P7); live-hand traps shared with Wing Chun; disarms shared with Krav Maga |
| Krav Maga | Hybrid and street | Israeli military self-defense; blocks and counter-strikes in one motion; very aggressive finish once a fight starts; hits vulnerable targets (eyes, throat, groin, knees); defends against weapons; uses nearby objects as weapons | Block - "defend and strike at once" is its core idea | NEW | Punch set (Boxing), knee/elbow (Muay Thai), disarms (Kali), wrist locks (Hapkido), object use (P7) |
| MMA | Hybrid and street | Cage sport mixing striking and grappling; uses takedowns, clinch work, submissions; ground-and-pound (strikes on a downed foe); fighter switches between ranges | Block - a high guard plus sprawl suits the all-range mixed game | NEW | Punch set (Boxing), kicks (Kickboxing), takedowns (Wrestling), submissions (BJJ); mostly reuses, few unique moves |
| Street Brawler (brawler) | Hybrid and street | Unsanctioned, unschooled fighting: loose square stance, heavy looping swings, shoves, headbutt-style closing, wild and slow to recover; no formal technique | Block - instinctive covering up and taking hits | Extends `brawler` (keep id) | Looser version of the Boxing punch set; shove/grapple from Wrestling |

Old-save mapping (P5-03): boxer -> Boxing, kickboxer -> Kickboxing, karateka -> Karate, wrestler -> Wrestling, judoka -> Judo, brawler -> Street Brawler, capoeira -> Capoeira. Creator archetypes keep their current default style (balanced=kickboxer, striker=boxer, kicker=karateka, brawler=brawler, grappler=wrestler, counter=judoka, speedster=capoeira).

Default defense counts: Sway 7 (Boxing, Taekwondo, Capoeira, Judo, BJJ, Hapkido, Kali), Block 9 (the rest). Both types are well represented for the P3-02 balance test.

#### Families

| Family | Styles | Shared animation set |
|---|---|---|
| Hand striking | Boxing, Wing Chun | Punch set: jab, cross, hook, uppercut (Boxing); Wing Chun adds chain punch, trap, pin. This punch set is also reused by Kickboxing, Muay Thai, MMA, Krav Maga, Street Brawler (Street Brawler uses a looser, slower variant) |
| Clinch kickboxing | Kickboxing, Muay Thai | Boxing punches + round kick + knee + elbow + neck clinch; Muay Thai adds shin check and teep (push kick) |
| Kicking arts | Karate, Taekwondo, Capoeira | Kick set: front, round, side, hook, spinning; per-style variants of chamber, pivot and height (Karate crisp and linear, Taekwondo high/jumping, Capoeira low/inverted) |
| Throws and takedowns | Wrestling, Judo, Sambo | Grip/tie-up entry, off-balance, hip throw, shoulder throw, leg takedown, sweep, pin; Wrestling = leg shots and lifts, Judo = collar-sleeve throws and sacrifice throws, Sambo = both plus a leg lock finish |
| Locks and submissions | Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Hapkido | Submission set (P3-04): arm lock, wrist lock, choke, leg lock; ground states (guard, mount, side control, back); BJJ = ground-first, Hapkido = standing wrist/elbow locks and throw-lock combinations |
| Weapon styles | Kali / Eskrima | Stick set: numbered angle strikes (forehand/backhand diagonals, thrusts), block-and-strike, double-stick weave if two sticks are held, disarm; same footwork empty-handed |
| Hybrid and street | Krav Maga, MMA, Street Brawler | Mostly reuses other families: punch set, knee/elbow, takedown, ground strike (ground-and-pound), improvised-object strike; few unique animations (Krav Maga defend-and-strike, MMA sprawl) |

Family count: 7. Each style belongs to exactly one family (its primary one); the "Shared animations with" column in the style table lists the cross-family reuse.

#### Notes
- Savate (French boot kicking + boxing): rejected, overlaps Kickboxing (boxing punches plus kicks); could become a Kickboxing variant later.
- Pencak Silat (Indonesian strikes, sweeps, locks, weapons): rejected for count; its sweeps/locks are covered by Hapkido and Capoeira, its blades fail the "urban, non-lethal" weapon limit.
- Jeet Kune Do: rejected as a separate style; it is a concept (Wing Chun + boxing + fencing), covered by MMA/Wing Chun/Boxing.
- Aikido: rejected, overlaps Hapkido (joint locks and redirection) and has no sport or competitive use.
- Sumo: rejected, heavy-push tackle belongs to P3-06 and the Wrestling family, not a street style.
- Greco-Roman / catch / folk wrestling, Kyokushin / Shotokan / Kenpo, Taekkyon, Lethwei, Dutch kickboxing: merged into Wrestling, Karate, Taekwondo, Muay Thai, Kickboxing respectively (same technique family).
- Kendo, swords, nunchaku, knives, firearms: rejected, not Modern Urban fit or lethal weapon training (consistent with P1-03 rejection of carried-item management). [Knives and firearms overridden by the owner on 2026-11-10: see P18-66; swords and nunchaku stay rejected.]
- Bartitsu (cane/umbrella), police baton systems: rejected as separate styles; Kali already teaches stick, Krav Maga improvised objects (bottle, chair) and defense against weapons, so they cover the P7 improvised-weapon moves.
- Bokator, Pankration, Systema, Tai Chi, Baguazhang, Kyudo: rejected; low recognition or low fit for fast mobile fights.
- Weapons rule: only Kali carries a stick as its own style item; Krav Maga and Street Brawler use improvised objects through the shared `use` pickup (P7), not their own weapon animations.
- Budget note: the 9 new styles are mostly data rows reusing shared set animations (about 4 genuinely new animation groups: Wing Chun traps, Taekwondo/Capoeira jump-spin variants, BJJ ground set, Kali stick set); this keeps file size low per the global rule.

### P1-07 - Theme audit of existing content (2026-10-28)

- Budget: final `breakpoint.html` <= 1,200,000 bytes (LF, as stored in the repository; the Windows CRLF copy is about 1.6 percent larger), target about 1,050,000, hard stop 1,300,000 unless a later decision accepts it. Reason: parse cost is small (V8 compile of the current 579,419-character script measured 13 ms on the desktop, so about 27 ms at 1.2 MB, about 110 ms under the 4x CPU throttle of P0-04, on top of the 162 ms baseline startup); the gzip ratio measured 3.5 to 1 (602,057 -> 173,357 bytes; brotli 141,383), so 1.2 MB is about 345 KB over the wire, once, then cached. The real limits on low-spec phones are per frame (instances, draw calls, AI cost), not file size, so the budget is about twice today's file instead of a tighter number that would cut variety. If over budget, cut in this order: QR encoder, 2 of the 5 new levels, 8 of the 28 emotes, 8 of the 24 faces, countries 64 -> 40 (together about 45 KB).
  - Counts `breakpoint.html` only (owner decision 2026-10-29): the self-tests moved to `breakpoint-tests.js`, which is not part of the game file and is not counted. The stored (LF) game file went from 1,194,076 to 765,075 bytes (see Appendix C, "Self-tests in their own file"). The projection below still includes the self-test bytes, so it now overstates the game file.
- Total projected file size: 602,057 (current HEAD, LF) + 186,152 (content above) + 224,000 (system code) = 1,012,209 bytes (about 1.01 MB); with a 15 percent estimation reserve 1,164,209 bytes (about 1.16 MB), inside the 1.2 MB budget. P15-03 (dead code, shared generators) should win back 5 to 10 percent, so the expected final size is about 0.95 to 1.1 MB. System code estimate (not content; scaled from measured module sizes INPUT 25,229; WORLD 39,633; FIGHTER 46,699; AI 23,937; MATCH 40,924; CREATOR 24,259; CREATOR UI 33,836; UI 76,624; SELF-TEST + BOOT 126,120): Controls overhaul (P2) 3,000; Block / Sway, submissions, grab strikes, falling, boost (P3) 16,000; Multi-opponent, group AI, lock-on, camera, co-op (P4) 22,000; Style engine hooks (P5) 6,000; Creator UI expansion + fitness / age / gender / story pickers (P6) 14,000; Photo face + face texture in the renderer (P6-06 / P6-07) 9,000; Weapon, pickup, hazard systems (P7) 14,000; Level systems: verticality, breakable floors, 1v1 variants (P8) 10,000; Interactivity matrix (P9) 9,000; Story, progression, unlock screen, cutscenes, grade (P10) 20,000; Tournament (P11) 9,000; Online: WebRTC, code compression, lobby, lockstep, checksum (P12) 30,000; Audiovisual feedback (P13) 10,000; Balance tables (P14) 4,000; Self-test additions: about 40 new checks at 1,200 B (existing 126,120 B for about 100 checks) 48,000; system code total 224,000.
- Method: a Node script read `breakpoint.html` (HEAD working copy, CRLF converted to LF, 602,057 bytes) and summed UTF-8 bytes (Buffer.byteLength) of line ranges: ROSTER 3,553 for 6 entries, ARENAS 4,907 for 3 (objects 883-974 for 8-9 each), buildProps 3,428 for 3 branches, MATERIALS 854, defAttack lines 5,755 for 22, THROW_SETS 2,341 for 12, CARRY_PATHS 1,111 for 7, THROW_POSES 3,443 for 8, STRIKE_BUILDERS 1,893 for 11, MOVE_STYLE 4,090 for 7, VICTORY_POSES 3,762 for 5, ARCHETYPES 2,225 for 7, LOOK_CHOICES 1,744, drawHead + drawHair 2,846, section sizes from the "====" headers. New rows (fighter, face, weapon, hazard, country, origin, goal, tattoo, style row) were drafted in the same format and measured the same way; they are drafts, so expect +-25 percent. Gzip, brotli and V8 compile times were measured with Node zlib and vm.Script. Note: HEAD is 602,057 bytes now (the 585,241 baseline plus the P0 work).

### P2-01 - Final action list (2026-10-28)

- Owner decisions: no hold-to-strengthen on any device (attacks fire on press); strong attacks are kept only as steps of fixed attack strings, with a combo balance audit (P3-10). Overrides the P1-03 "tap / hold strength" row.
- Still a hold: USE tap = drop, hold = throw comes from the owner's ideas file and is kept until the owner says otherwise.

Basis (fact, read from breakpoint.html 1.0.0): ACTIONS has 15 entries (breakpoint.html:574). Touch has a stick plus 8 buttons (PUNCH, KICK, BLOCK, GRAB, JUMP, DUCK, DASH, II; buildTouch, :7332). Touch already uses tap / hold for strength (TOUCH_CHARGE_MS = 220, :770) and picks height automatically (touchAttackChoice, :784). `dash` is also the back double-tap (:1082) and quick recovery (Fighter.updateDown :3504). Crouch is already the "low" modifier for Grapple (low grab, :3281).

Strong moves are reached only as steps of fixed attack strings (see "Attack strings" below). The intent no longer carries `strong`; `height` is derived from crouch held at the press.

Strong throws are removed (every throw uses the normal values). | Owner decision 2026-10-28: no hold anywhere; strong attacks live in combos. Overrides the P1-03 "tap / hold strength" row. |

Touch keeps its existing automatic height choice when DUCK is not held. | P1-03 "button-set height": the button plus the crouch state set the height. Uses an existing action, no new input. |
