- What a new player must learn today before a first win (counted from the code; the first four are what a win needs, the rest can wait):

  | # | Thing | Needed for a first win? | How it is taught today |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | Move, and the camera-relative stick (Movement directions) | yes | controls card (once) |
  | 2 | Punch and Kick, and chaining: press again as a hit lands, within the string window (`ATTACK_STRING_TICKS`); some strings need Duck held | yes (a jab alone wins Easy) | one line on the card; Move list |
  | 3 | Defend: **Block** (hold) or **Sway** (tap just before the hit, 0 to 6 ticks is perfect) depends on the fighter's style; Duck + Defend for low | yes (Easy still lands hits; blocking halves the loss) | card names the fighter's own defence; Move list |
  | 4 | Stamina: every move costs, an empty tank hits at x0.6 and starts slowly, a run or a sway needs some | yes | LOW STAMINA banner when it is already low |
  | 5 | Stun: you cannot act while hit, a chain cannot be stopped, a guard held through it starts the moment you are free (combo break) | no (it is why you lose, not how you win) | `COMBO_HELP` in the Move list only |
  | 6 | Grab, throw, escape, clinch, hold, tackle | no | grab hint when alone with a foe; clinch and hold tips once |
  | 7 | High / mid / low and which move hits what | no on Easy, yes from Normal | frame-data lines in Move list and Training |
  | 8 | Jump, sidestep, run, items (USE / LOCK), walls and ring-out | no | card (jump), item hints |
  | 9 | 32 fighters with 16 different styles: which to pick | no | Move list per fighter, the creator |

  A new Tekken player faces about 100 moves per fighter and frame data for all of them; here the same entry costs 4 ideas and then 5 optional layers, so the gap is already smaller. What is missing is that the game does not say which ideas matter first, and does not explain 4 and 5 until the player has lost to them.
- Comparison (sources, URLs, dates read and verified marks: Appendix B entry "P18-27 - How fighters ease new players in (researched 2026-11-07)", file `P18-27B.md`; own words; claims no source confirmed were dropped, the list is at the end of that entry):
  - Street Fighter 6 has a second control scheme (Modern, a four-button layout where a special move is one button plus a direction), is the default on first launch and can be switched to Classic in the settings; press reports a price, about 20% less damage on specials done with Modern's one-button shortcut (Capcom's wording not found; verified partly). Lesson taken: the on-ramp is a choice the player can leave later, with the same fight rules underneath, and it carries a price so skill still pays.
  - Tekken 8 has Special Style (one button per recommended move or combo, switched on or off at any point of a match with one button; the auto-combos are not optimal, so strong players still do it by hand; verified partly) and Arcade Quest (avatar, a mentor, demos then practice, then fights against the computer; reviews are mixed: some praise the teaching, others call it a slog or too heavy on tutorial; verified partly). Lessons taken: teach inside play, keep the lines short and shown once, keep the assist a switch and its ceiling low on purpose (it must never be better than skill), and do not make it a mode.
  - Super Smash Bros. (one normal and one special button, a held direction picks the move) and Fantasy Strike (stick plus three buttons, no motion inputs, made easy for everyone, not as a mode; reviews praise it and some say it is thin) show that a small button set can carry a big move list. Lesson taken: our four buttons are enough, and the learning cost is in the layers, which the tips and "Start here" order. Too little depth reads as shallow, so the depth layers stay.
  - Tekken 2 onward guards high and mid for you while you stand and retreat (Appendix B, P1-01, Tekken, neutral guard, REFERENCE line 301), and crouching guards low: the high/low rule is learned by being hit. Lesson taken: our Duck + Defend is the same two-button chore, which is worse on a phone.
  - Our own reading, not a source: Arcade on Easy is already the first-fight guide; it only lacks narration.
- Decided: **"Easy to enter, deep to master" in four parts, none of which is a new mode, a new screen or a new on-screen button.** The first fight is taught by short coaching lines at the moment the player meets each thing (shown once, saved), a second assist makes guarding one gesture, the Move list opens with a "Start here" block, and the game offers help after repeated losses. Defaults for a new save stay as they are (Easy everywhere, Auto-assist Off). Nothing in the simulation changes for anyone who leaves the new switch Off, so every recorded fingerprint and the P14-01 balance are untouched.

  | # | Part | Decided | Because |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | **Coaching lines** (the "first-fight guide") | A table `COACH_TIPS` of 10 one-line tips, each tied to an event the game already emits; a tip shows once, ever (`Progress.d.tips`, a small object of booleans read through the cleaner like `seenClinch`), on the existing hint strip (the one the grapple hint uses, `showHint` defined at 14783, called at 14687, not a modal and not a new element), for 4 s, never during the countdown, a replay, a Versus seat 2, the benchmark or when the controls card is open; at most one per round; none at all after the player's 20th fight (the fight count is `wins + losses`). The list is in "The tips" below | Teaches at the moment of need, as Arcade Quest does, without a tutorial mode; the show-once rule is kept; one table holds text, trigger and key, so a tip cannot exist in the code and not in the tests |
  | 2 | **Guard assist** (new setting, default Off) | `SETTING_DEFS.guardAssist` bool, label "Guard assist", hint "Defend alone guards high and low for you (no Duck needed). The CPU does not get it. Perfect blocks still need good timing, and a guard that has to switch height is never perfect." Human input only, exactly like Auto-assist (`it.assist` 1338 gets a sibling `it.guardAssist`). Rule: while Defend is held and the player is standing or ducking, a strike that would be blocked only at the other height is blocked anyway, as a plain block (no perfect, no counter, no combo break from that block); everything else about the guard (stamina cost, the front half-plane, the 30-tick perfect cooldown) is unchanged. Sway fighters: a tap sways away from either height (already true) so the setting changes nothing for them. Auto-assist keeps its row and its meaning. | Duck + Defend is two inputs held together; on a phone it is the stick-down hold (18 ticks, P17-19) plus a thumb on DEFEND, which new players do not manage. A one-gesture guard is Tekken's neutral guard with our button; it removes the high/low guess without removing timing or stamina, so skill still beats it (perfect block, sway, grabs and throws ignore it) |
  | 3 | **Start here** in the Move list | A block above the signature moves: "Start here: 1 Punch, Punch, Punch = your first string; 2 hold Defend when the foe starts a move; 3 Grab when the foe is guarding; 4 stop hitting when the stamina bar is low." The first string and the best-known three moves of the fighter are marked with a star in the list (a `first` flag on three entries of each style's `signature`, or the first row of the style's string table: no new data if the first row is used). Plain words, touch labels and key names by input type (the Move list already does this) | The Move list is where a stuck player goes; today it opens with data, the thing a beginner does not need |
  | 4 | **Help after losses** | One tip (a coach tip, once): after the second loss in a row in the first 10 fights, a toast "Hard fight? Settings has Auto-assist and Guard assist, and Training shows every move." with no button (tap anywhere closes it). No dynamic difficulty: the CPU level never changes by itself (it would hide Easy from the player and break replay and the P14-01 ladders) | Offers the lever at the moment it matters, without deciding for the player |

- The tips (text is plain, ASCII, uses the key names of the player's device through `keyName`; trigger = an existing event; key = field in `Progress.d.tips`; all once only):

  | Key | Trigger | Line (max 70 characters) |
  |---|---|---|
  | `punch` | the first fight ends round 1 without the player having thrown a second Punch within a string window, after 15 s of fight | "Press PUNCH again as a hit lands to chain a string." |
  | `stam` | the first time stamina drops under 30% | "Strikes cost stamina. Stop attacking for a moment and it fills again." (the existing LOW STAMINA banner still shows) |
  | `block` | the first block (any) | "Blocked. Strong moves break a block unless it is perfect." |
  | `perfect` | the first perfect block or sway | "PERFECT! That breaks a combo." |
  | `low` | the first time the player is hit by a low move while not ducking, in the first 5 fights | "That was low. Hold DUCK with DEFEND to guard low." (Guard assist On: not shown) |
  | `stun` | the third consecutive hit on the player (combo) | "While you are hit you cannot act. Hold DEFEND to guard the moment you are free." |
  | `down` | the first knockdown of the player | "Press DEFEND on the ground to get up quickly." |
  | `grab` | the first time the player is grabbed (a grab or throw) while holding Defend | "Guards do not stop a grab. Move away, or tap GRAB to escape." |
  | `item` | the first time the player stands within reach of a lying item | "USE picks it up. Hit with it, or throw it." |
  | `lose` | part 4 above | see part 4 |

  The existing controls card, clinch tip and hold tip stay as they are. The ten keys add up to under 700 characters of text. Tips are plain text on a strip and never flash, so Reduced motion does not hide them (it only turns off the strip's fade). Tips are never shown for the P2 of Versus or co-op seats 2 to 4 (the first seat of a human gets them), and `Progress.d.tips` is saved once per tip, not per input type (a player who learns on a phone does not see the same line on a keyboard).
- Rejected: **a separate tutorial mode or forced first fight** (an extra mode, extra save state, and the show-once rule says teaching lives in play; a forced screen is what makes people quit before a first fight). **Dynamic difficulty** (the sim stays the same for all; see part 4). **A third control scheme** (Modern-style one-button specials: the game has 4 buttons and 16 styles, a scheme would need its own move table per style, about 3 to 5 KB per style and a new balance pass; Auto-assist plus Guard assist already cover the same ground). **A fixed "easy mode" with damage reduction** (the Difficulty row is it). **A new on-screen button** (nothing needs one: Guard assist removes the need for the DUCK + DEFEND chord, and the tips use the existing strip). **Turning Auto-assist on by default** (it changes how strings feel for everyone who just wants to play; the first-loss offer is better, and a veteran does not have to find an off switch). **Showing frame data to beginners** (stays in Training and the Move list).
- Touch, gamepad, keyboard: nothing new to press; Guard assist is a setting (works on all three, since it is read from the same Defend intent); tips name the control of the device used last (`keyName`, 13362). On the 390x844 and 844x390 phones the strip is the one the grapple hint already uses, so no layout work; the longest line is 70 characters at the small hint size, which fits two lines at 390 px.
- Determinism, replay, online and balance (P14-01): the simulation reads `Settings.v.autoAssist` once per human intent (1338) and does not read it anywhere else; Guard assist follows the same path (a field of the intent), so with it Off nothing changes in any run. With it On the input stream is the same; the only change is which strikes a held Defend blocks. For replay and online it must be a per-seat `cfg` field (`cfg.assist` bit mask for strings and guard per seat), not a viewer setting read inside the sim; today Auto-assist is read from `Settings` at the human intent, so P18-19's single `cfg` builder or the online task must copy both into `cfg`. The build task below adds the `cfg` fields, reads them in the intent step for human seats and keeps the Settings as the source for local play. Balance: P14-01 ladders and the Block-vs-Sway 45 to 55 % split are measured with the AI as the player and neither assist on, so they do not move; one extra measurement (below) checks the assist does not beat Hard.
- Performance: coach tips run on events and once per round, so no per-tick cost; `Progress.d.tips` is one small object; Guard assist adds one comparison in the block test of a player with the flag.
- Edge cases:

  | Case | Result |
  |---|---|
  | Guard assist On, a Block fighter, a mid strike while ducked | blocked as a plain block (the height is ignored) |
  | Guard assist On and a perfect-timed press against a low move while standing | perfect rules unchanged: a stand guard against a low move is a plain block, never perfect, so the timing skill is still the way to a break |
  | Guard assist On, Sway fighter | no change (a sway already dodges both) |
  | Guard assist On in Versus | per seat; P2 has its own switch via the seat's own setting; both shown on the Versus card line |
  | A throw, grab, tackle or thrown body at a guard | not blocked at all, as today |
  | Tips and Reduced motion / High-contrast | the strip uses the HUD text colour; no flash, no animation beyond the existing fade (off under Reduced motion) |
  | A tip fires in the same tick as a story scene or the controls card | the card wins; the tip waits for the next round (the key is not set until it is shown) |
  | A new save reaches a fight on a different device | the tips are per player, not per device; the controls card stays per input type |
  | The player turns Auto-assist or Guard assist off after the loss offer | nothing nags: the `lose` key is set |
  | Old save without `tips` | all false; players with many fights (`wins + losses` over 20) get none |
- Bytes (LF, estimated; the file is 1,178,607 bytes (LF) at 8aa8c39 and the budget is 4,000,000, so all of this fits twice over; the estimates are for the task's own cap):

  | Part | Bytes |
  |---|---|
  | `COACH_TIPS` table (10 lines, keys, triggers) | 1,500 |
  | `Coach` helper (show once, suppress rules, event hooks into `Events.on`), save field and cleaner | 1,100 |
  | Guard assist: setting + hint, intent flag, block-height rule, `cfg` field for replay | 900 |
  | Move list "Start here" block and the star marks | 700 |
  | Loss offer | 350 |
  | **Total** | **about 4,550**; cap for the task 5,500 |

  Fallbacks if the measured size is over the cap, in this order: shorter tip lines (about 300 bytes); drop the `item` and `grab` tips (about 350, they are the least needed for a first win); drop the stars in the Move list (about 150). None of the four parts is dropped without asking the owner.
- Self-tests the build must add (names start `Accessibility (P18-27):`; none may skip, weaken or delete an older test):
  1. the tip table: each key fires once on its trigger with a human in seat 1, never twice in the same session or after a reload (read back through a fresh `Store`), never for a CPU, seat 2, the benchmark, a replay or a countdown, at most one per round, none after 20 fights;
  2. text: every line is at most 70 characters, plain ASCII, passes the P17-05 design-note scan, and names the control of the device used last (touch names DUCK / DEFEND, gamepad names R1, keyboard the bound key);
  3. Guard assist: standing with Defend held blocks a low move as plain, ducked blocks a mid move as plain, never perfect on a height switch, a CPU never gets it, Off changes nothing (a seeded 1v1 hash with the flag Off equals the recorded one), a Sway fighter unchanged, grabs and tackles still not blocked;
  4. replay: the same input log with the `cfg` flags Off, On and On through JSON round-trip gives the Off, On and On hashes; `Settings` changed mid-fight changes nothing;
  5. save: `Progress.d.tips` cleaned (missing, wrong type, extra key), an old save loads with all false;
  6. Move list "Start here" shows the device's key names and the star marks the same three moves as the Training panel's signature list;
  7. the loss offer shows after the second loss in a row inside 10 fights, once;
  8. layout at 390x844 and 844x390 (strip does not cover the stamina bar or the buttons; two lines fit), in the browser run;
  9. balance run (below), recorded in the log.
- Balance check the build runs and records (method of P0-06 / `BREAKPOINT.simulate`, 12 seeds per cell): the P18-33 Press script in a variant that never ducks (so it only has the standing guard), with Guard assist On against Off, and the normal Press script (which picks the right guard height, `it.crouch = tr.kind === 'block' && tr.h === 'L'`, 8993 and 9277) as the ceiling; each against Easy, Normal, Hard and Expert. The AI picks the right height when it reacts, so a plain AI-as-human run would hardly show the assist. The aim: Guard assist On moves the never-ducks variant's win rate by at most 15 points at Easy and Normal and by at most 8 at Hard and Expert, and never takes it above the normal Press script (the ceiling), so the assist makes up for a missing duck and adds nothing beyond right-height play. If it moves more, narrow the rule (for example, plain blocks only from the second hit of a string), not the CPU numbers.
- Open (for the owner; each is decided above and can be changed): (1) Guard assist is a second switch, not a value of Auto-assist (a saved bool keeps its meaning). The alternative is one "Assist" row with Off / Strings / Strings + Guard, which saves one row (about 120 bytes) and one tap but needs a migration of the saved bool. (2) Assist is not marked in grades (there is no ranking to protect; the owner can add a small "ASSIST" tag in the result card). (3) Tips stop after 20 fights; the limit is a constant. (4) No tutorial mode; if the owner wants a guided first fight in Arcade, the cheapest version is a "stage 0" Training scenario using the six existing scenarios with the coach lines on (about 1,500 bytes), not a new mode.
- Inputs for P18-14 (X-factor):
  - Accessibility is the first half of the game's identity; the X-factor should be a feature that gives depth to players who stay: something that a new player can use at once (one gesture) and an expert can play with. Candidates from this entry: (a) **the perfect-timing layer** (0 to 6 ticks, Block and Sway, combo break) is already unlike other 3D fighters, because it is the same window for both defences and it is one button; it can be the signature if the cues are good (P18-04) and the tips teach it (`perfect` tip); (b) **the environment** (breakables, hazards, ring-out, raised ground, items) is a thing Tekken only has in a small amount, and it is easy to understand on a phone (a tip per hazard family could follow the `item` tip); (c) **a comeback mechanic** in the spirit of Tekken 8's Heat or Tekken 6's Rage would suit this audience (a trailing player gets a short buff), but any such mechanic must be explained by one coach line and be inactive for a new player's first two fights, and it needs a balance run like the Guard assist one.
  - Constraints the X-factor must keep: no new on-screen button; every new idea gets one coach line and a Training line; nothing that makes a first fight harder to read; anything numeric goes through `cfg`, not Settings, so replay and online hold.
  - A design rule to carry: "a new idea costs one line the player sees once, or it does not ship".
- Build notes for the implementing task (task **BP-P18-48 "Implement P18-27 accessibility"**, created by the coordinator in the tasklist with depends_on BP-P18-27; run it after P18-19 (the `cfg` builder) and P18-43; one batch, Sonnet implementer then Opus reviewer):
  - Order of work: (a) `COACH_TIPS` table and `Coach` (one source for text, trigger, key); the `tips` field in `Progress.fresh` (946) and its cleaner (962), reusing the `seenClinch` pattern; (b) hooks: use `Events.on` where the game already listens (13289, 13292); add the few events not emitted yet (first block, first knockdown of seat 1, stamina under 30%) as read-only events; (c) the strip: reuse `showHint` (defined 14783); (d) Guard assist: `SETTING_DEFS.guardAssist`, the intent flag next to `it.assist` (1338), the block-height test in `Combat.evaluate` (6966 to 6969: `S.BLOCK_H` blocks H and M, `S.BLOCK_L` blocks L; the search words `blockHigh` / `blockLow` only find key bindings), the `cfg.assist` field filled by the single `cfg` builder and read by `Fighter` for the human seats; (e) Move list block (14231); (f) the loss offer on the `matchEnd` event (11331 emits it for every mode; `onMatchEnd` 12546 is only the Tournament's handler, so do not put the offer there); (g) tests; (h) the balance run.
  - Traps: the assist must be read from `cfg` inside the sim, not from `Settings` (online and replay); with the flag Off every recorded hash must match; a tip trigger must never call anything that touches the sim state (read-only events only); do not set a tip key until the tip is actually shown (a suppressed tip comes back); `Progress.save` writes once per tip (the same as `seenClinch`); the Move list star must read the data (first string row), not a second list.
  - Docs: update the Settings hint list, the Move list help text and Appendix C in the same change; the P16-03 owner device list gets: on a phone, play the first fight at Easy with the tips On and read each line once; turn Guard assist On and block a low move without Duck; turn it Off again.
  - Checks: the node one-liner for size (cap 5,500 bytes over the base), the full browser self-test (the count must grow by the new tests), P0-06 reduced rows unchanged with the assist Off.
- Checks done for this entry: reading only (`breakpoint.html` at 8aa8c39, the tasklist, SPEC, Appendix B and the P18-42 entry); web research on 2026-11-07 for how Street Fighter 6 Modern controls, Tekken 8's Special Style and Arcade Quest, Smash and Fantasy Strike lower the entry barrier (written up with URLs, dates and verified marks in `P18-27B.md`, Appendix B; unsourced claims were dropped). Line numbers and the file size re-checked against 8aa8c39. No game file, test file or fingerprint was touched, and no test was run.

### P18-48 built: accessibility as identity (the P18-27 decision)

- Built as decided, none of it a mode, screen or on-screen button. (1) **Coaching lines**: `COACH_TIPS` (10 keys, one table of key and text) and `Coach` next to `Progress`; `Progress.d.tips` is an object of booleans, cleaned like `seenClinch` (missing, wrong type or extra key reads as not shown). The events that ask for a line are read-only listeners (`Coach.hook`); a line waits as `pending` and its key is saved only when `Coach.line` puts it on the grapple hint strip (`hudUpdate`, after the clinch and hold hints), for 240 ticks, at most one per round, only for a person on seat 1 in the fight phase, never in Training, a benchmark or replay (`cfg.benchmark` / `cfg.replay`), a crowd of several people, with the controls card open, or after 20 fights. (2) **Guard assist** (`SETTING_DEFS.guardAssist`, Off by default, after Auto-assist): `Combat.evaluate` blocks the other height as a plain block while a guard is up (`switched`: never perfect); grabs, throws, a Sway fighter and the CPU are untouched. (3) **Start here** block (the first string is read from the fighter's own table: three presses, twice or once, Kick when a crate is carried; a review fix) and `*` marks (signature moves of the style, from `style.signature`, in the Data cell because the name cell is parsed by the Move list test) in the Move list; one sentence about Guard assist in About and Help. (4) **Loss offer**: `Coach.matchEnd` (a listener on `matchEnd`), second loss in a row, first 10 fights, once, not when both assists are already on, as a toast of 6 s.
- `cfg.assist` (bit 1 = Auto-assist strings, bit 2 = Guard assist) is copied from Settings by `Game.beginMatch` (a rematch re-reads it) and read by `MatchSim.readAssist` for human seats only, so a replay or an online seat does not read the viewer's Settings. A match with no `cfg.assist` (a test, the simulator) has no assist at all: the sim never reads Settings (review fix). One mask covers every human seat; a future online or replay task must turn it into a per-seat mask. `'assist'` joins the keys the Free Fight merge test ignores when it compares `Game.config`, as `items` and `hazards` already were.
- Differences from the decision, all small: the `stam` line comes from the existing low-stamina event (under 25 %, the LOW STAMINA banner) instead of a new 30 % event; the `stun`, `grab`, `block`, `stam` and loss lines are shorter than the decision's text (the stun line was 79 characters, the limit is 70); the loss toast closes by itself (no tap handler); only the signature moves are starred (the first string is named in Start here); Guard assist is one setting for every human seat, so the Versus card line is unchanged; the layout check at 390x844 and 844x390 is a browser check (not run here).
- Size (LF bytes): breakpoint.html 1,178,914 to 1,186,047 (+7,133). The decision's cap was 5,500 (estimate 4,550): over by 1,633; the total budget is 4,000,000. Fallbacks left, in the decision's order: drop the `item` and `grab` lines (about 450 bytes), drop the stars (about 150); the rest of the overage is the Coach code (about 3,300, the decision estimated 1,100 for the helper) and comments.
- Tests (11, names start `Accessibility (P18-27):`): the tip table (each key fires once on its event, shows 4 s, one per round, saved when shown, kept after a reload); suppression (CPU, seat 2, benchmark, replay, countdown, Training, open card, 20 fights; a held-back line is not used up); text (ASCII, 70 characters, no design notes, the device's names); Progress cleaning; Guard assist rules (both heights, perfect, grab, Sway, CPU); the three recorded 1v1 fingerprints with the bits 0 and 3; replay (same log, JSON round trip, Settings changed mid-fight; On differs from Off; strings from the config); `beginMatch` and rematch copy; Move list (Start here in the three devices' names, stars equal the signature list of all 16 styles); the loss offer. Checked with mutants (perfect allowed on a height switch, Settings read in the sim, no phase gate, the CPU seat reading the flag, a key saved before it is shown): each fails a test. The self-test count went from 607 to 618 in the headless run. Review fixes: the tip strip is `width:max-content` with `max-width:min(92%,26em)` and sits at 34 % from the top in portrait (away from the stick and buttons); the layout test for it is a browser check, left to P16-03 (it needs the touch controls and a real layout, and no browser was run); both assist hints end with "From the next match."
- Balance (headless harness, a scratch script not kept in the repo): the P18-33 player-like script as KAI against MARA (CPU damage levels, no items or hazards), 12 seeds on both start sides (24 matches per cell; Hard and Expert also seeds 13 to 48, 72 more), wins of the script. The variant that never ducks with Guard assist Off / On, and the normal script (ducks to the height it sees) as the ceiling:

  | Level | Never ducks, Off | Never ducks, On | Ducks (ceiling) | On minus Off |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Easy | 24 / 24 | 24 / 24 | 24 / 24 | 0 points |
  | Normal | 24 / 24 | 24 / 24 | 24 / 24 | 0 points |
  | Hard | 77 / 96 (80.2 %) | 70 / 96 (72.9 %) | 69 / 96 (71.9 %) | -7.3 points |
  | Expert | 32 / 96 (33.3 %) | 28 / 96 (29.2 %) | 30 / 96 (31.3 %) | -4.2 points |

Easy and Normal are full (the script wins every match), so the assist cannot show there; at Hard and Expert the assist does not raise the win rate (it lowers it a little, since the guard spends stamina), and it sits within one match of the ceiling. The first 24-match Hard cell read 19 / 20 / 19 and Expert 11 / 12 / 14: single cells of 24 move by a few matches, the 96-match cells are the ones to read. The Press-script rows of P0-06 and the three 1v1 fingerprints are unchanged with the assists Off.

### P18-14 X-factor recommended (2026-11-07)

- Owner (2026-11-01, Appendix A, REFERENCE line 186): "The main thing I feel is currently missing is an X-factor: one genuinely unique feature that gives the game its own identity. Something memorable that makes it stand out from other games in the genre." The same writer (line 180 to 182) likes the new levels and "the interaction with objects in the environment" and wants it "developed further". Task rule: the owner picks from the options; the coordinator gives a recommended one. So this entry is a **recommendation, not the pick**: BP-P18-49 below is written for the recommendation and starts only after the owner's OK (human_intervention of BP-P18-14). If the owner picks another option, the row is swapped, not stacked. BP-P18-14 is not ticked until the owner picks; the coordinator sets `tracking.human_intervention.required` to true with this entry as the resume point. Written by the coordinator's delegate under the standing "select the correct option" go, which does not cover this pick (TASKLIST line 3071 put it back to the owner). Nothing here changes the game code, a test or a fingerprint. Base: `main` at 2041038, `breakpoint.html` 1,178,914 bytes (LF, BOM counted) of 4,000,000; line numbers below are of that commit and move when P18-13, P18-48 and P18-45 land.
- Research: Appendix B, "P18-14 - What the closest games do for identity (researched 2026-11-07)" (file `P18-14B.md`; URLs, dates read and verified marks there; claims no page confirmed were dropped, the list is at its end). Read there: Dead or Alive (Danger Zones), Def Jam: Fight for NY (environment, crowd, momentum), Injustice and Mortal Kombat X (interactive objects), Smash (18 stage-hazard kinds), Tekken 8 (Heat, stage destruction, Super Ghost Battle), Smash Figure Players, Virtua Fighter 4 Evolution, Street Fighter III parry, Garou Just Defend, Sifu (structure, aging), Grand Theft Auto (wanted level), Shadow Fight 2. P18-27's entry (Appendix B, "P18-27 - How fighters ease new players in") is option A.
- What the sources say about the genre, in short (own words; marks as in Appendix B):
  - Scenery that hurts is the genre's normal form of "environment": Dead or Alive's Danger Zones (extra damage; falls, explosive and breakable walls, moving obstacles), Def Jam's walls, gates and crowd, Injustice's per-character objects, Mortal Kombat's weapons from the scenery, Tekken 8's break-through walls and floors. Smash lists 18 hazard kinds and has a few one-step triggers (a switch, a trapdoor, a vehicle that explodes an item), and no general chain system. None of the six environment pages describes one scenery effect lighting, breaking or crushing another by a rule (not found in the part read; absence is not proof).
  - A comeback state is the other standard identity move (Tekken 8 Heat and Rage, Mortal Kombat's meter, Def Jam's Blazin' Moves, Garou's T.O.P.); here that is the Momentum gauge and the ultimate (P18-08), already planned.
  - A defence-timing reward is established in 2D (Street Fighter III parry, Garou Just Defend) and in the 3D brawler Sifu (parry, structure gauge). An AI that copies a player exists in Tekken 8 (Super Ghost Battle), Smash (Figure Players) and, as top-player styles, Virtua Fighter 4 Evolution. A police or heat clock is known from Grand Theft Auto; no fighting game with one was found. The nearest mobile fighter, Shadow Fight 2, is 2D, silhouette art, fantasy and energy-limited, so it does not compete on identity.
  - Sifu shows that one systemic hook that touches every fight (aging) is what reviewers remember a small brawler by.
- What the game already has that an X-factor can stand on (`breakpoint.html` at 2041038):
  - A rules matrix of nine scenery rules (P9, "System rules matrix", R1 to R9) that already chain by material: an arc runs through metal conductors (`Arena.linkConductors` 3508, `CHAIN_MAX` 6 at 2858, `hazardStart` 10538 damages them), a spark-sensitive material lights in an arc or fire zone (`MATERIALS.paper` and `.plastic` carry `spark: 1`, 2844 to 2853; `stepFire` 10648 to 10683 with `FIRE_MAX` 4 at 2859 and `FIRE_SPREAD_R` 1.0), fire spreads to near objects every `FIRE_SPREAD_TICKS` 60 (10678 to 10682), a burnt object breaks (`burnObject` 10695), a broken support drops what rests on it (`Arena.dropSupported` 3500), a collapsed deck crushes neighbours and the fighters under it (`stepCollapse` 10629, `CRUSH_OBJECTS` 4 "so a collapse can chain, deterministically", comment at 10638), a thrown or tipped barrel pools fire (`hazardArm` 10527, `HAZARDS.fire` 5600), an extinguisher puts fire out (`douse` 10705). Credit follows the cause: `h.by` on every hazard, `blazeFor(o).by` for a fire (10686), `hazardHit` 10759 names `by` only when `canHurt` allows (9946, which also excludes the fighter itself).
  - The CPU already lures into, waits at and walks out of those zones (`considerHazard`, `hazardLure`, `hazardBait`, `holdAtHazard`, `leaveHazard`, P18-12 text), so a chain started by anyone is lived with by everyone.
  - Events for every step (`hazardTrigger` 10534, `hazardStart` 10541, `objIgnite` 10687, `objBreak` 3464, `deckCreak` 10625, `hazardHit` 10774) with popup text (`popAt` 14615 and the listeners at 13294 to 13298), sound (13068 to 13077) and effects (12777 to 12784) already attached. No event says which effect caused which, and no counter says how long a chain ran.
  - Environment damage gives no momentum today (`hazardHit` 10759 to 10775 has no call to `Combat.momentum` 6927; every strike, throw, clinch strike and tackle has).
  - P18-12 (decided) adds 16 interactions, six of them chains (W1 warehouse stock, S2 subway bundle and scaffold, G2 garage tyres, C1 live fence, R1 rooftop air-conditioning units, P2 live cage) and a hydrant that cuts fire; BP-P18-13 builds them. P18-27 (decided) adds the Coach (once-only lines) and the saved `tips` field; BP-P18-48 builds it.
- The options (3 to 5 asked; five written; cost = bytes added to `breakpoint.html` plus the batch size; all fit the 4,000,000 budget many times over, so the size is a budgeting figure, not a gate):

A shared window for two defence types is not described by any page read; whether a 3D fighter does it is unknown | about 1,400 bytes, 1 batch (the cues are P18-04, done) | Not unclaimed; hard for a first-time player to read a 7-tick window; it rewards the already skilled |

- **Recommended: C, Street Chain, on top of A.** Reasons, in order: (1) the owner named the environment the part to develop (2026-11-01: "the interaction with objects in the environment ... another layer to the gameplay"), so it answers both of his points at once; (2) it is the one option whose core already exists and is invisible: nine rules chain scenery by material, and nobody can tell, because no effect says what caused it and nothing counts it; making it legible costs about 2.9 KB, against 4 KB for D and a new save format; (3) the pages read describe single-step scenery in other games and no rule-driven chain, so "the street fights back, one thing sets off the next" is a claim the game can make without copying anyone's names, characters or look; (4) a newcomer uses it with the controls they already have (strike or throw a metal item at a panel, knock a foe into a jet) and sees a result within seconds, and an expert plans routes, lures a foe into a zone and cuts a chain with the hydrant or the extinguisher; (5) it asks for nothing new from the simulation's random numbers, buttons or Settings. A stays as the front door (it is already BP-P18-48); C is the room behind it. D is the runner-up and stays a later extension (see Rejected); B stays what it is (P18-04 cues, the `perfect` coach tip) without being promoted.
- Honest limits of the claim: "unique" here means "not described by any of the six scenery pages read"; it is never to be written as "no game has it" in the game's text, store page or release notes (Appendix B, claims dropped). The identity line to use is the player-facing one: "Light the street. Watch it spread."

#### Street Chain, as decided for build

- Name in text and on screen: **CHAIN**. A link is a scenery effect whose cause is another scenery effect or a fighter's trigger, not the fighter's own hit. The chain's number N is the depth of its deepest link (the spark is 1); links of the same depth are siblings. One popup is shown per new depth per chain id, so a chain shows at most `CHAIN_SHOW_MAX` popups.
- The links (this table is the list of what counts; nothing else does). A cause is carried by one field `link` on the hazard or object (`{ id, by, depth }`, `id` from a per-match counter like `hazardSeq` 10464, never a random number) and by one variable `cause` that `MatchSim` sets around the four step functions that fire effects and clears afterwards:

  | # | Link | Where it happens (2041038) | Cause passed on by | Depth |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 0 | **Spark**: a fighter sets a hazard off (strike, thrown item, knock) or breaks a glass wall | `hazardStrike` 10549, `hazardItem` 10559, `hazardKnocked` 10566, `hazardBreak` 10570: the first three via `hazardArm` 10527, and `hazardBreak` 10574 directly | `h.link = new link(by)` (by = the credited fighter, or null for a timer hazard) | 1 (never shown alone) |
  | 1 | **Arc**: the panel energises its conductors | `hazardStart` 10540 (loop over `h.chain`) | conductors get `o.link` = next(`h.link`). In `hazardEffects` (10718) a fighter of an arc hazard that is reached only through a conductor (10511, not inside `def.r`) is hit with that conductor's `o.link` (depth 2), passed to `hazardHit` as an argument | 2 |
  | 2 | **Ignite**: a fire or arc zone lights an object | `stepFire` 10664 to 10672 (the `hot` hazard), `ignite` 10684 | `o.link` = next(`hot.link`) | +1 |
  | 3 | **Spread**: a burning object lights a neighbour | `stepFire` 10678 to 10682 | `next.link` = next(`o.link`) | +1 |
  | 4 | **Fall**: a broken object drops what rests on it (supports, scaffold tiers, speakers) | `Arena.dropSupported` 3500, `breakDeck` 3470, the queue push at 3482 | the dropped piece and the collapse record carry `Arena.cause` | +1 |
  | 5 | **Crush**: a landed collapse breaks a neighbour or hurts a fighter | `stepCollapse` 10629 (neighbour loop 10639 to 10643, fighter loop 10634 to 10637) | `cause` = the record's link while the loop runs | +1 for each neighbour that breaks |
  | 6 | **Burn**: a fighter set alight in a linked zone | `hazardEffects` 10725 (`f.burnBy`), `stepFire` 10653 (`BURN_SRC.by`) | `f.burnLink = h.link` next to `f.burnBy`; `BURN_SRC.link = f.burnLink` at 10653, cleared after the call | same depth as the zone |
  | 7 | **Payoff**: a linked zone, a burn or a crush hurts a foe | `hazardHit` 10759 | reads `h.link` (and the crush source's) | not a link; a stat and momentum |

  A burnt object that simply burns out (`burnObject` 10695 then `Arena.breakObject` 3407) is not a link of its own: only what it drops or crushes is. A weak deck that gives way (`stepLoad` 10610), or any break whose cause is a fighter's own hit, starts no chain: its fall and crush carry `link: null`. The chain ends by itself; depth is capped at `CHAIN_SHOW_MAX` 9 for display only. A burning object keeps its link across rounds (10492 keeps its fire and credit), and `Arena.reset` (3354) rebuilds objects with `link: null`, so a new level state starts clean.
- What the player sees and hears (all existing channels, no new element): at depth 2 and above, each new depth of a chain shows one popup "CHAIN x2", "x3" ... at the place of the link that reached it (`popAt` 14615, the colour of the hazard warning '#ffb000' used at 13298), once per depth per chain id; a rising two-note motif (a `chain` entry next to `CUE_NOTES` 12731, volume as the existing hazard sounds, through `allow`); at depth 3 and above a small camera nudge through `Camera.impact` (2574, which Reduced motion already switches off). The popup is plain text and does not flash, so Flashes and Reduced motion need no new rule. A chain with `by` null (a timer hazard) is shown in the neutral '#d0d8e8' (the stage-name colour at 13295), counts for nobody.
- What it pays (one rule, no new number): damage a **linked** zone, conductor shock, burn or crush does to a foe counts for the fighter who lit the chain at the strike rate. In `hazardHit` (10759), when the hazard's link has a `by`, depth is 2 or more, `canHurt(by, f)` holds (so never the fighter itself, never a teammate with Friendly fire off) and the hit did damage, call `Combat.momentum(by, f, amount)` (6927), the same function and the same `MOMENTUM_PER_DAMAGE` 1.6 and 0.5 share as a strike. The street therefore pays like a punch, but only for a chain, not for a plain barrel or a plain panel (depth 1). A panel's 14 shock through a conductor (depth 2) is about 22 gauge points, and a linked fire zone's 4 about 6. For a crush hit the call also sets `f.lastFoe` to the lighter (6928), which moves later scenery credit; self-test 4 checks it. Both sides can earn it, and the CPU that stands in a zone it did not light pays the player, not itself.
- Counted and shown afterwards: per fighter `chains` (chains of depth 2 or more that fighter started), `chainMax` (the deepest) and `chainDmg` (damage from linked zones to foes), in `newStats` 9857; one line on the results card ("Chain: best 4, 31 damage", only when `chainMax >= 2`; the card code is at 14429 to 14490); `Progress.d.chainBest` (a number, cleaned like `arcadeBest`, `Progress.fresh` 946). **No change to `fightGrade` 924** (P14-01 targets stay as measured).
- Teaching: one Coach line (P18-27's table, saved in `Progress.d.tips`, shown once on the first time a player's own spark gets a second link): `chain` "Sparks and fire spread. Each link in a chain is counted." (55 characters, ASCII, device-neutral). One Training scenario (a 7th entry in `SCENARIOS` 13240, "7: A chain", loader `scenario(n)` 11257, key 7: the key regex `/^Digit[1-6]$/` at 13597, the "also keys 1-6" text at 14417 and `tscenGo` at 13715): the player stands within a strike of the level's first chain post and the dummy in its zone; it is offered only on a level whose rows have an arc or fire post with something flammable or conducting beside it, and is not listed elsewhere. One help line in the Help text (P16-04): "Chain: scenery that sets off scenery. Look for panels, barrels and cardboard."
- Not changed: Settings (no new row; Hazards, Breakables and Items rules of Free Fight, P18-43, switch it off by removing its parts: no hazards, no chain; no breakables, no burn, no collapse), `fightGrade`, the CPU, the AI, the controls, any cost, any damage number, the ring, the camera, the levels (BP-P18-13 owns the rows).
- Rejected inside C: a chain bonus in the grade (changes P14-01; the results line is enough); a chain multiplier on damage (the zone's damage is the level designer's number and both sides take it); a chain meter or a new bar (a gauge exists: Momentum); a lights-out or alarm chain (P18-12 rejected them); chain-specific CPU play (the CPU already lures to posts and leaves zones; measured first, see the balance check); a separate "chain" mode (not a mode).

- Touch, gamepad, keyboard: nothing new to press; the spark is the strike, the throw or the knock the game already has. The popup is the one used for "WALL SLAM" and "CRASH"; at 390x844 and 844x390 it sits at world height 1.0 to 2.0 above the link, never on the HUD. The Training scenario is picked in the same menu on all three inputs (key 7 on a keyboard, the row on touch and gamepad).
- Determinism, replay, online: the link fields and the `cause` variable are write-only bookkeeping; the only effect on the simulation is the momentum call, a pure function of the sim's own damage, ids from a counter and no clock, no random number, no Settings value. So the same seed and inputs give the same chains on every peer. The momentum call changes outcomes of fights that contain a chain, so the recorded hazards-on fingerprints that contain a linked hit must be re-recorded once, with the list and the reason (as P18-12 does); every fingerprint without a chain, and every 1v1 recorded without hazards, must stay equal. The online task (P12-05 determinism audit) only has to carry `link` in its checksum list if it checksums object fields; nothing else.
- Performance: no per-tick cost (links are set at the step functions that run every 10 or 60 ticks, or on a trigger), no new draw call, no new particle type; the existing caps hold (`FIRE_MAX` 4, `CHAIN_MAX` 6, `CRUSH_OBJECTS` 4, `MARK_MAX` 32), and at most `CHAIN_SHOW_MAX` popups per chain (one per depth). The BREAKPOINT.benchmark (P0-04 method) must not move.
- Edge cases:

  | Case | Result |
  |---|---|
  | Hazards off (Free Fight rule, a Settings value), or the ring drops the posts | no spark, no link, no popup, no momentum |
  | Breakables off (`Arena.solid`) | no object burns or collapses; only the arc and its conductor shock exist (depth 2): a chain never passes x2, and only a conductor shock pays |
  | Items off | a panel can still be struck by a fighter's hit if the row allows it; a metal-only panel needs a metal item or an item thrown, so it cannot start; barrels and jets still can |
  | Two fighters strike the same post in one tick | the first `hazardArm` wins (it needs state `idle`); one chain, one credit |
  | A chain lit by a timer hazard | popups in the neutral colour, stats and momentum for nobody |
  | A weak deck gives way, or a break caused by a fighter's own hit | no chain starts (`link: null`) |
  | The lighter walks into their own zone | `canHurt` excludes self: the damage counts, the momentum does not |
  | A teammate is hurt by a linked zone with Friendly fire off | `by` is null for that hit (as today); no momentum |
  | The foe is already down or KO'd | `hazardHit` returns early for a terminal state (10760); no payoff |
  | Fire put out by the hydrant or extinguisher (`douse` 10705) | the object's fire and `blaze` end; the chain simply stops; no extra text |
  | Round reset in a best-of | burning objects keep `link` and credit (10492); new objects start with `link: null` |
  | Replay, Training with infinite health, CPU vs CPU (`SimRunner`) | the stats listeners run in a headless run (they are in `MatchSim.subscribe`), the popup and sound listeners do not; the numbers are available to the balance run |
  | Versus seat 2, co-op seats | same rules; each fighter earns its own momentum and stats |
  | Reduced motion on | no camera nudge (`Camera.impact` returns early); popups stay |

- Bytes (LF, estimated; file 1,178,914 at 2041038; budget 4,000,000):

  | Part | Bytes |
  |---|---|
  | Link bookkeeping: `link`, `cause`, `nextLink` helper, 7 call sites (`hazardArm`, `hazardStart`, `stepFire` twice, `dropSupported`/`breakDeck`/collapse queue, `stepCollapse`), `link: null` in `makeObject` (3256) | 650 |
  | Conductor link (the shock reached through a conductor passed to `hazardHit`) and the burn link (`f.burnLink`, `BURN_SRC.link`) | 250 |
  | Stats (3 fields in `newStats`) and the momentum call in `hazardHit` | 260 |
  | Display: `chainLink` event, popup with the per-depth gate, sound motif, camera nudge | 510 |
  | Results line, `Progress.d.chainBest` and its cleaner | 380 |
  | Coach line | 140 |
  | Training scenario 7 (text, loader, key regex, list) and the scenario-list test site | 510 |
  | Help line | 150 |
  | **Total** | **about 2,850**; cap for the task 3,200 holds |

  Fallbacks if over the cap, in this order: drop the camera nudge (about 90); drop the Training scenario and keep the Coach line (about 450); shorten the results line (about 100). The links and the momentum rule are not dropped without asking the owner.
- Self-tests the build must add (names start `Street Chain (P18-14):`; none may skip, weaken or delete an older test):
  1. Links in order: on a level with P18-12's W1 rows, a scripted spark at the W1 panel gives ignite `cardboardC` at depth 2 and spread to `crateD` at depth 3 (plus depth 2 on each conductor the arc energises), each with the lighter's index; the same seed twice gives the same ids and depths;
  2. One case per link kind (arc, conductor shock, ignite, spread, fall, crush, burn), table driven; a fighter's plain strike on a breakable is not a link; a burnt-out object with nothing on it adds no depth;
  3. Off switches: Hazards off, ring drops the posts, Breakables off (no link beyond the arc), an idle fight with no spark (no event, no stat);
  4. Credit and pay: a linked zone hurting a foe gives the lighter `Combat.momentum` exactly as a strike of the same damage would (compare to the gauge change of a strike); depth 1 pays nothing; self, a teammate (Friendly fire off), a null `by` pay nothing; Friendly fire on pays a teammate-hit as `canHurt` says; for a crush hit `f.lastFoe` becomes the lighter (6928);
  5. Stats and save: `chains`, `chainMax`, `chainDmg` per fighter; results line only when `chainMax >= 2`; `Progress.d.chainBest` cleaned (missing, wrong type, negative, huge); an old save loads with 0;
  6. Text: popup strings, the Coach line (at most 70 characters, plain ASCII, the P17-05 design-note scan) and the help line; the Coach line shows once and not for the CPU, seat 2 or a replay (P18-48's rules);
  7. Training scenario 7: loads on a level with a chain post, places the fighters, is not listed on a level without one;
  8. Fingerprints: every recorded fingerprint without a linked hit equals the old value; the ones that change are listed in the test with the reason;
  9. CPU: across 20 seeds of KAI against KAI at Hard on each chain level, no fighter stays inside a linked zone after its warning (the P18-12 `leaveHazard` test, extended), and at least one chain of depth 2 or more starts somewhere in the 20 (report how many; the CPU does not have to start any);
  10. Layout at 390x844 and 844x390 in the browser run: the popup does not cover the stamina bar, the buttons or the hint strip; a chain of 4 links in a row stays readable;
  11. Balance run (below), recorded in the log.
- Balance check the build runs and records (method of P0-06, `BREAKPOINT.simulate`, KAI against KAI, 600 seeds per chain level, Easy, Normal, Hard, Expert): the seat band stays inside the recorded one (40 to 60 percent at Hard and Expert, 35 to 65 percent at Easy and Normal, REFERENCE line 1774); the share of all damage that came from linked zones is at most 10 percent; match length changes by at most 5 percent against the same seeds before the momentum call (switch the call off with a test hook, not a Setting); the boost (Momentum) starts per fight no more than 1 more time on average than before. If any cell fails, move the rule (for example, pay only from depth 3, or half the strike rate), not the CPU or the level rows.
- What the owner can change (each is one line or one row): the pick (A on its own is already tasked; B, D or E replace C); whether the chain pays Momentum at all (remove the call, 120 bytes less); the pay rate (the strike rate now) and the minimum depth (2 now); whether a chain counts in the grade (no now); the name CHAIN; the camera nudge; whether the Training scenario ships; whether neutral (null-credit) chains show; whether the results line shows for 1-link sparks (no now).
- Rejected as the X-factor (and why):
  - **Challenge codes with verifiable replays** ("every fight is a code": the input log of a fight packed as text, a friend plays the same setup and the game re-runs the log to check the result): needs the determinism audit (P12-05) and the lockstep work first, and 1 to 3 KB of text per fight is long for a message; it is the right extension of option D after online play exists, not before.
  - **A comeback state** (Tekken 8 Heat and Rage, a Blazin' Move): the Momentum boost and the ultimate (P18-07 to P18-09) are that; a second one would compete with them. Tell P18-08 that chain damage now pays Momentum.
  - **Style clash** (a type chart between the 16 styles): a fixed advantage table breaks the Block-versus-Sway 45 to 55 percent split and the owner's "balanced" rule, and P17-09 already makes the styles distinct.
  - **Rewind or retry from here** (the simulation is deterministic, so it could rewind): fits Training and an easy Arcade, but it is offline-only and a free retry already exists (Continue Arcade); not an identity.
  - **Injuries that carry across the Arcade run**: a balance burden on every stage and on the story rewrite (P18-35).
  - **Aging on death** (Sifu's hook): copying another game's hook is against the rule for this task, and P1-03 already rejected it as a duplicate of the Age slider.
  - **The crowd as a living ring** (Def Jam's crowd shoves, holds and arms fighters): the crowd is drawing only by decision R8 and making it a body changes the camera and the nav map.
  - **A new on-screen button for anything**: none of the above needs one.

#### 1. The one defence rule (Block and Sway)

- Words (P18-02's, in ticks, 60 a second): contact C = the tick a strike goes active on the defender; free tick F = the first tick the defender can act again (the end of a hit stun, a block stun, an attack, a recovery, a get-up); the defence starts on D = the tick the guard state begins (Block), the tick of a fresh Defend press (Sway), or F when Defend was already held (either). Age = C - D.
- Decided:
  1. **Perfect = the defence starts at most 6 ticks before contact** (age 0 to 6, seven ticks counting the contact tick, 0.117 s), by a press or by Defend held into the free tick. `PERFECT_BLOCK_TICKS` 6 stays the one window of Block and Sway, which is what the code has had since P18-02 (Block) and P18-03 (Sway). The "7 ticks" of the row B sketch counted the same seven positions; the rule is written as ticks before contact, so the number is 6. Why not wider: a window of 12 ticks or more lets a plain reaction press (a human reacts 12 to 15 ticks after a wind-up starts, P18-02's estimate) be perfect against any slow strike, and the window stops being skill. Why not narrower: 0.1 s is already tighter than a reaction press can hit against any move with a startup under 11 ticks (P18-02), so a perfect is a read of the rhythm, not luck; narrower makes it a guess. Free choice 1.
  2. **Cooldown 30 ticks, shared.** A defence (Block or Sway) that starts less than 30 ticks after the start of the previous defence of either kind is never perfect; it still guards or slips as usual and reads TOO SOON. Today only Block against Block has this (`PERFECT_BLOCK_COOLDOWN`, `lastBlockAt`); the build sets the same `lastBlockAt` (the name stays: two self-tests write it) when any Sway defence starts, so a Sway after a Block, a Block after a Sway and two Sways all count. A hold counts once, at its start: only a Block entry, a press that starts a sway and the free tick with Defend already down (after a stun, a recovery, an attack, a get-up or a round start) stamp `lastBlockAt`; a dodge made by the prepared hold never stamps it and never sets `readyFresh`, and a sway that ends with Defend still down is the same hold continuing, so it stamps nothing (a re-stamp there would make the next perfect wait 57 ticks).
  3. **Block** keeps today's rule (hold Defend; Crouch + Defend for the low guard; a perfect block pays no stamina, refunds `R`, staggers the attacker 26 ticks, opens the 50-tick counter window and pays Momentum) and keeps its block cost (section 4: unchanged). `R`, the refund of a perfect Block or Sway, is the one number of the edge table: Easy 8, Normal 7, Hard 6, Expert 6 (was perfectBlock 8 / 7 / 6 / 6 and perfectSway 5 / 3 / 0 / 0: a perfect Sway now pays what a perfect Block does).
  4. **Sway, held to prepare.** A Sway fighter (`guardMode === 'sway'`) who keeps Defend down while free (IDLE, WALK, CROUCH) without having just pressed it is **prepared**: a flag `swayReady`, not a state. It happens when a sway ends with Defend still down, when Defend is down on the free tick (held through a stun, a recovery or a get-up), and when a round starts with Defend down. A prepared fighter walks at `BLOCK_FACTOR` 0.6, refills at 0.3 of the rate (a guard has 0.4: holding the button must not be a safer rest than a guard) and shows the ready pose (section 1.1). When a strike (not a grab) would land on a prepared fighter, the sway starts on the contact tick itself (lead 0; the strike goes to `swayHit` as a miss), leaning the way the stick points at that tick (left or right when its side value is at least the dead zone and at least its forward value, else back: `startSway`'s rule), and **each strike so dodged costs stamina**: by the strike's tier, 5 (tier 1), 6 (tier 2), 8 (tier 3, the strong moves) (section 1.2 explains why 0.7 times the first guess of 7 / 9 / 11). A dodge that finds the tank unable to pay fails (item 6). The sway is the sway of P17-03 and P17-11 unchanged: 12 i-frame ticks, 15 recovery ticks in which the fighter can be hit, the same pose, the same room checks; strikes that meet the i-frames of a sway already running are dodged the same way, each at its own cost. Grabs are not dodged (as today). A strike that comes while the fighter is in the recovery hits.
  5. **A fresh press still sways at once: the tap is unchanged** (a press kept 6 ticks while the fighter is busy, `SWAY_BUFFER_TICKS`, as today). This is a decision forced by the code and the tests, not a preference: the sway of P17-03 and P17-11 starts on the press tick, the perfect window counts from it, and nine pose and timing self-tests press Defend with the foe idle 4 m away and read the sway they get (three prototypes on scratch copies of the tree, run with `tools/run-tests.js --only "Sway pose"`, logs kept in the probe folder under `logs/log-proto-*.txt`: today's tap 11 of 11 pass; a press that sways only when a foe's strike is within 11 ticks of going active 2 of 11, with or without the late-lead edit of the clearance test; a press that sways only when a foe is within 2.7 m 4 of 11). So the tap stays and the hold is added after it: a sway that starts on a press and meets a strike within its first 12 ticks dodges it; age 0 to 6 (the strike goes active at most 6 ticks after the press) is a perfect (counter window 50, `swayEnd` 21, Momentum, refund `R`, no cost), age 7 to 11 a plain dodge (cost as above). **Tap late = perfect, hold = plain.** The honest price: the press that starts a hold is itself a tap, so it leans out at once whether or not a strike is coming and leaves the swayer in its 15 recovery ticks, which a strike 13 to 26 ticks later finds (today's trap, not new). The way round is the hold itself: press Defend before the foe is close (the lean is a harmless backstep), keep it down, and every strike after that is slipped at its cost; the Coach and help text say so. A fighter who holds Defend into the free tick is prepared at once, with no sway wasted. A CPU never holds (section 1, CPU).
  6. **An empty tank fails like a broken guard.** When a dodge's cost is more than the tank holds (`stam - cost <= 0`, the test `blockHit` uses), the dodge fails: the strike lands as on a broken guard (`reactDur` 80, state STUN, 30 % of its damage as chip, knocked 2 m/s along the strike, hit-stop 12) and the next hit lands at x 1.2 and replaces the stun, exactly `blockHit`'s `broke` branch (factor it into `Combat.guardBreak(att, def, mv, match)` and call it from both). A Sway press with 0 stamina still starts the sway (it is the strike that finds it empty); a perfect needs no stamina, so a perfect with an empty tank is still a perfect.
- Inputs, existing buttons only (no new button, no Settings row; a Block fighter's controls do not change): touch, the Defend button (hold it; a quick tap is the late tap); gamepad, the Defend button (hold / tap); keyboard, the Defend key (hold / tap). The stick at the moment of the sway picks the lean on all three (left or right slips to that side, otherwise back). Guard assist (P18-27) is a Block aid and does nothing for a Sway fighter.
- 1.1 The ready pose (visual only): `SWAY_POSE.back` x 0.25 (lean, tuck, knees) held while `swayReady`, blended with `SWAY_POSE_BLEND`; no new pose data, about 120 bytes. Reduced motion needs nothing (the pose is a hold, not a motion).
- The CPU (`swayAim`, `swayRead`): both fields and every value stay (Expert `swayAim` 0.7 as set in P18-03/04; `swayRead` 0.4 / 1.3 / 0.2 / 0.1). The CPU's one Defend press at the planned tick is the tap of item 5 (contact falls `AI_SWAY_AIM` 9 or `AI_SWAY_AIM_PERFECT` 3 ticks into the dodge), so it starts the sway on the press as today and the perfect, plain and missed cases are unchanged. What changes for the CPU (BP-P18-62): (a) it knows its cooldown: inside 30 ticks of its own last defence start `swayResponse` plans the plain aim, never the perfect one (a human reads TOO SOON; the CPU reads its own timer); (b) `f.stam < SWAY_COST` becomes "the planned strike's dodge cost fits the tank with 1 to spare" (a CPU that cannot pay the dodge does not plan it, as it does not plan an attack it cannot pay: `cost * 2 + 10` rule of `pickMove`); (c) it never relies on the prepared sway (no `swayHold` field is added: it stays a tapper at every difficulty; free choice 2). `blockSkill`, `parry` and the Block CPU are unchanged. The Block CPU's perfect rate (`parry`) and the Sway CPU's (`swayAim`) are what the balance runs of P18-02 and P18-03 fitted; they are not touched here.
- Training readouts (the panel's `defRead` line, `defenceReading(e)`, and one new line): the reading keeps its four forms and gains the stamina and the Beat: `PERFECT SWAY, 3 ticks before the hit, +6 stamina, BEAT x3`; `SWAY (held), -6 stamina`; `BLOCK, -6 stamina`; `TOO SOON (14 ticks since the last defence)`; `EARLY 4 ticks` (the tap was 4 ticks too early: age - 6); `SWAY FAILED - out of stamina`; the new line under it reads `Defence: ready` or `Defence: cooldown 14` (ticks left of the 30) and `Beat x3`. Scenarios 1 to 6 are unchanged. The panel texts are English plain text; no Settings value is read by the sim (the readouts are view code).
- Help text (`DEFENSE_HELP.sway` and `COMBO_HELP`, P16-04): sway: "Press Defend before the fight reaches you and keep it down: the press leans out at once, and then each strike that would hit you slips by (Stick left / right leans sideways, otherwise back) at a cost of 5 to 8 stamina; grabs still land, and you can be hit for 0.25 s while you recover. Tap Defend just before a hit lands (up to a tenth of a second) for a perfect sway and a counter." The move-list text (`DEFENSE_HELP` is the one place; the move list shows it) follows. `COMBO_HELP` loses "(Sway: tap just before)": a held Defend now works for the Sway too ("keep it held and you are ready the moment you are free").

- **1.2 The held Sway, probed** (added after the gate review: the first version of this entry decided the hold without running it). Patched into a scratch copy of the stamina candidate by `mkhold.js` (the probe folder is named at the end): the tap stays with no cost at the press; 5 + 2 x tier (7 / 9 / 11, the first guess) per strike dodged, nothing for a perfect, the refund `R` (the decided 5 / 6 / 8 is 0.7 times the guess and was probed through `COSTMUL`); an empty tank fails like a broken guard (STUN 80, chip 30 %); the prepared hold dodges on the contact tick, leaning where the stick points; the shared cooldown is stamped by a press and by the free tick only (a dodge made by the hold stamps nothing); prepared walk x 0.6 and refill 0.3; the CPU plans the plain aim inside its cooldown. Variant **re-arm**: a strike that lands on the 15 recovery ticks of a sway while Defend is down is dodged again (plain cost, i-frames restart). Scripts (all KAI's body with the Sway; `pl.js`): **HoldOnly** stands 1.6 m from the foe, never attacks, and keeps Defend down on every tick, through the sway, a stun and a get-up; **Sway-Press** is the Press script on that body, keeping Defend down through its own sway while the guard window it opened is running (the plain Press script lets go on every helpless tick, which made its next guard tick a fresh press, a tap, again; fixed after the second review). Its windows are about 15 to 20 ticks, shorter than a sway, so it never reaches the prepared hold: in 12 fights at Hard it made 1 hold dodge and 217 taps, at Expert 0 and 165, which is why its numbers measure the tap, not the hold. **Sway-Hold** keeps Defend down through every guard window it opens and for 60 ticks after the last guarded tick (the 60 restart on each guarded tick, `pl.js` line 34; not while an attack of its own runs): 108 hold dodges against 102 taps at Hard, 162 against 131 at Expert. **Hold** (Press attacks, Defend never released) makes only hold dodges (302 and 571). **Block-Press** is the Press script as it is. 1v1 at Health Normal, 24 seeds (48 where marked), evenDamage off.

  HoldOnly, strikes slipped / strikes that hit / share slipped / % of the fight under 25 % / dodges that failed (tank empty):

  | Foe | Easy | Normal | Hard | Expert |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | CPU, no re-arm | 2816 / 10 / 99.6 % / 0 / 0 | 2383 / 88 / 96 % / 6 / 24 | 2341 / 705 / 77 % / 77 / 610 | 2101 / 748 / 74 % / 70 / 507 |
  | CPU, re-arm | 2813 / 9 / 99.7 % / 0 / 0 | 2384 / 86 / 97 % / 6 / 24 | 2242 / 685 / 77 % / 80 / 684 | 2121 / 748 / 74 % / 73 / 543 |
  | the Mash script, no re-arm | 2544 / 1512 / 63 % / 50 / 576 | 2088 / 1404 / 60 % / 45 / 408 | 1788 / 1128 / 61 % / 35 / 300 | (the scripted foe ignores the level) |
  | the Mash script, re-arm | 3168 / 1560 / 67 % / 90 / 1368 | 3024 / 1500 / 67 % / 89 / 1272 | 2712 / 1368 / 66 % / 88 / 1152 | |

  (The Mash foe is a fixed pattern, so its clock starts on tick `seed mod 12`, which makes the 24 seeds 12 different fights, two of each; the HoldOnly script is a fixed pattern too, so against the Mash script the rows are the spread of those 12 starts, not 24 independent fights. Against the CPU the 24 fights differ by the CPU's seeded choices.)

  Read: against the CPU a hold slips 96 to 99.6 % of what comes on Easy and Normal, and on Hard and Expert the limit is the tank (under 25 % for 70 to 77 % of the fight), not the 15 recovery ticks. Against a string every 12 to 25 ticks (the Mash script) the recovery ticks do cost: about 4 strikes in 10 hit. The re-arm variant slips 4 to 7 points more of those and halves the damage taken (0.8 / 1.0 / 1.2 a second against 1.8 / 2.4 / 3.0) but spends the tank doing it (88 to 90 % of the fight under 25 %, 1150 to 1370 failed dodges, every failure an 80-tick stun): so **decided: no re-arm**. The 15 recovery ticks stay the Sway's price against strings (Block's strength) and the per-strike cost already limits a hold; the re-arm is one `evaluate` line and a flag if the owner prefers the literal "every strike slips while the button is down" (free choice 2).

  What the table says, in the order the first two rounds got wrong:
  1. **The gain of the Sway script comes from repricing the tap, not from the hold.** On the new stamina the old Sway (10 at every press) leaves Sway-Press at 27 / 27 % at Hard / Expert (today 48 / 48); pricing the dodge per strike instead (nothing at the press) puts it at 73 / 67, and the prepared hold changes it by nothing (73 / 63: it makes 0 or 1 hold dodges). So the "33 and 11 points over today" and "23 over Block at Expert" of the previous round were the repricing (and the new stamina taxing the Block script: 83 / 71 to 73 / 48), and the claim that the AI-against-AI check cannot see the shift was wrong: the CPU taps at the new prices, and that run moves.
  2. **For a player who really holds, the hold is a cost.** Sway-Hold on the tap-only game wins 71 / 60 at Hard / Expert; with the prepared hold at 7 / 9 / 11 it wins 35 / 19: 1156 and 1307 dodges, 16 and 10 % of the fight under 25 %, and 27 ticks of lost action for every strike slipped. #### 2. The Beat (option B, as decided for build)

- Name on screen and in text: **BEAT**. A Beat is a run of perfect defences.
- Window: the one window of section 1 (6 ticks before contact). Cooldown: the shared 30 ticks (a perfect needs a fresh defence, so the fastest Beat is one perfect every 31 ticks).
- Counting (field `beat` on the fighter, `beatAt` the age of the last perfect): every perfect Block, perfect Sway and perfect thrown-item block counts 1, all alike. A plain block or plain sway neither adds nor breaks (the defence worked, the beat was missed, no more). **A hit taken resets it to 0**: the one `Combat.momentum(att, def, dmg)` call that every damaging hit already passes (strike, ground hit, clinch strike, throw, tackle, thrown item, thrown body) sets `def.beat = 0`, and so does a guard break (the chip path has no momentum call) and `Fighter.reset` (a new round starts clean). It also resets after `BEAT_GAP_TICKS` 180 (3 s) without a perfect (the foe's strings come every 0.3 to 0.8 s; a perfect every 3 s is a rhythm, one every 20 s is luck). Scenery damage (hazards, objects) is not a hit taken (it has no momentum call; BP-P18-49 may add one).
- Momentum paid per step: section 5 (one budget for all sources).
- Cues (all existing channels, nothing new on the HUD): **sight**: the PERFECT ring (P18-02 / P18-04, `FX.ring`, ice-blue `CUE_COLOR.perfect` '#bfeaff') grows with the step: step 1 as today (speed 5), step 2 speed 5.8, step 3 speed 6.6 with a second ring at speed 4, step 4 and above speed 7.4 with the second ring; the popup text of `onBlock` gets ` x2`, ` x3` ... from step 2 ("PERFECT SWAY! x3", "PERFECT BLOCK! x2"; the popup colour stays '#9cf4ff'; the combo-break popup keeps its gold and gets the same suffix). **Sound**: the existing `CUE_NOTES.perfect` [1320, 1980] at step 1 and a rising chime after it: `BEAT_NOTES` = [[1320, 1980], [1480, 2217], [1661, 2489, 3322], [1865, 2794, 3729], [2093, 3136, 4186]] (a whole tone up each step, a third note from step 3, the same sine voice, gains and `allow('block', ...)` gate as the perfect cue in `Sound.block`, and the same x1.35 for a sway); steps above 5 play step 5; a perfect that breaks a combo keeps the `brk` chord. The Beat is readable by sight alone (ring size and doubled ring, the "x3" text, the results line) and by sound alone (the pitch climbs a whole tone per step, three notes from step 3; no cue depends on colour or on a flash). **Flashes and Reduced motion**: the ring is drawn particles, not a flash; the build adds no `FX.flash` and no camera nudge, so Flashes (Full, Reduced, Off) and Reduced motion need no new rule; the existing white sway flash stays under the Flashes setting as P18-04 has it.
- Teaching and record: one Coach line `beat` in P18-27's table, once, saved in `Progress.d.tips`, shown the first time the player's own streak reaches 2, never for the CPU, seat 2 or a replay: "Perfect defence in a row builds your Beat and Momentum." (55 characters, ASCII, device-neutral). One help line (P16-04): "Beat: perfect blocks and sways in a row (x2, x3 ...) pay more Momentum. A hit ends it." Results: per-fighter stat `beatBest` (next to `perfect` in `newStats`), the results card shows "Best Beat" (a row of the stat grid next to "Best combo", only when some fighter's `beatBest` is 2 or more) and "Beat: best 4" on the one-person card; `Progress.d.beatBest` (a number, cleaned like `arcadeBest`, `Progress.fresh`: missing, wrong type, negative or huge become 0; an old save loads with 0) keeps the best of all fights of the people's side. No change to `fightGrade` (P14-01's targets stay as measured).
- Not changed: Settings (no new row), the buttons, the CPU's tap, `fightGrade`, the sway geometry, every move table.

#### 3. The two scripts, the fights and what stamina does today

- Words: **under 25 %** = `Fighter.lowStamina` (stamina under `LOW_STAMINA` 0.25 of the tank, the LOW STAMINA warning); **exhausted** = under 25 % as well (one threshold for both targets); **empty** = 0; **damage per second (dps)** = damage the script's fighter deals divided by the seconds it is up with a foe alive; **a fight** = the ticks the script's fighter is up with a foe alive in the fight phase (waiting and round-end ticks do not count).
- **Press** (the P18-33 player-like script, copied exactly into the P0-06 runner as test support in BP-P18-52; it is `staminaPlayer` of `breakpoint-tests.js`): a scripted controller on fighter 0 (not flagged human), per tick, nothing while helpless (HIT, STAGGER, STUN, CLINCH, THROWN, FALL, DOWN, KO, VICTORY, DEFEAT, SWAY, GRAPPLE, SUBMIT). It looks at every living foe of another team: `nearest` = the smallest distance; a foe whose strike has started (state ATTACK, a `strike` move, `moveTick` at most its startup, a different `moveId` than the last one seen) and who is within `reach x its reach stat + 0.9` m is "seen": with probability 0.65 (an LCG: `state = seed * 7 + 1`, `state = imul(state, 1664525) + 1013904223`) the script holds Defend (Crouch + Defend when the move is Low) until `startup + active + 3` ticks after the move began, and does nothing else while it does. Otherwise: LOW STAMINA starts a rest, which lasts until the tank is at 55 %; resting, it walks backwards (`fwd` -0.7) while a foe is within 2.6 m and presses nothing; not resting, it walks forward (`fwd` 1; Run too when `nearest` is over 4.5 m and stamina over 20) while `nearest` is over 1.6 m, and within 1.6 m, when `lock` is 0 and 20 ticks have passed since its last press, presses Punch, Punch, Kick, Kick, Punch, Punch ... (one tick each, alternating pairs). It never jumps, sidesteps, grabs or uses items.
- **Mash** (new; added to the runner next to Press by BP-P18-52): a scripted controller on fighter 0 with an own clock `c` starting at 0; per tick, nothing while helpless (same list). `nearest` as above. If `nearest` is over 1.6 m: `fwd` 1, and Run when `nearest` is over 4.5 m and stamina over 20; the clock does not advance. Within 1.6 m: on the tick where `c` is a multiple of 12 it presses Punch (one tick), on the tick where `c` mod 12 is 6 it presses Kick (one tick), no input on the other ticks, then `c` goes up by 1: **Punch, Kick, Punch, Kick, one press every 6 ticks, 10 presses a second, alternating, whatever the fighter is doing** (the buffer keeps the latest press for 12 ticks and chains it as soon as the string rules allow, so the attacks come as fast as the moves recover). It never holds Defend, never crouches, jumps, sidesteps, grabs or uses items, and never rests: "no pauses".
- **The fights** the targets are measured on (all KAI on the Warehouse, the CPU damage levels on, seeds 1 to 24, `evenDamage: false`): **F1 long duel** = KAI against MARA, best of 3, 60 s rounds, `hpScale` 2 (the Free Fight Health rule set to Double: both fighters have twice the health; MARA is a Sway fighter, so the duels also run the Sway CPU); **F2 brawl** = KAI against 3 CPU enemies (`enemies: 3`, no clock). Not a target, reported for information: **F0 short duel** = F1 with `hpScale` 1. Why F1 has twice the health: a tank only matters in a fight that lasts, and today's Easy and Normal duels end in 9 to 13 s a round (the Mash script wins them 100 %; the CPU does not answer mashing, which BP-P18-73 changes), shorter than any stamina rule that does not starve the Press script can make a masher feel; the Health rule is a game option, so F1 is a fight a player can actually set up, and Hard and Expert duels last this long today. F0 is information only: no task re-runs it.
- Today (b74821b, 24 seeds, % of the fight under 25 % of the tank / dps; Press | Mash; "empty" = Mash at 0 stamina):

Refill from empty, standing still, without being hit: to 25 / 50 / 100 % in **Easy 1.1 / 1.9 / 3.7 s, Normal 1.4 / 2.6 / 4.9 s, Hard and Expert 1.7 / 3.1 / 5.9 s**; walking 1.8 / 3.3 / 6.2 s (Easy) to 2.9 / 5.2 / 9.8 s (Hard); guarding 2.7 / 4.9 / 9.2 s (Easy) to 4.3 / 7.8 / 14.8 s (Hard).

#### 4. Stamina, decided (replaces P18-33's per-difficulty shares)

- The idea in four lines: **a strike costs 15 % more, an attack started by cancelling the last one costs 60 % more than that (for people, not for the CPU), a pause of 24 ticks (was 36) starts a refill that is 30 % quicker, and a tank that is low makes the fighter weaker in steps** (damage, speed and walk, not only under 25 %). Why this and not dearer prices: P18-33 measured and the probes above confirm that Press and Mash pay alike per press and press about as often as the moves recover; what separates a player who paces from one who mashes is whether the next attack starts before the last one is over (a string step, the cancel) and whether there is ever a pause. So the price of a cancel and the length of the wait are what bite a masher, and the pause is what pays a player. The tank (60 + 10 x Stamina attribute, 70 to 160) and the attribute slopes are not touched (the balance work of P14-01 and P17-10 stands on them).
- **Prices** (KAI's numbers; `x` = times; the table rows keep their P18-33 values and a constant scales them once, so the AI, the HUD and the tests all read the real price):

  | Action | Today | Decided | Reason |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Tier 1 punches and kicks (jab 3, chain punch 2, front kick 5) | 2 to 5 | 2.3 to 5.8 (jab 3.5) | `STAMINA_PRICE_K` 1.15, rounded to 0.1 |
  | Tier 2 punches and kicks (cross 5, roundhouse 7) | 4 to 8 | 4.6 to 9.2 | same |
  | Strong moves (tier 3: power jab, hook, heavy kicks) | 9 to 13 | 10.4 to 15 | same |
  | The running lunge, air strikes, counters | 8 / 4 and 6 / 4 and 6 | 9.2 / 4.6 and 6.9 / 4.6 and 6.9 | same |
  | A strike started from the ATTACK state (a cancel into the next string step: `chained` in `startAttack`), by a person or a script | the same price | **x 1.6** (`CHAIN_PRICE_K`); a CPU fighter (`Fighter.cpu`) pays the plain price | the stamina sink of a masher; Press never cancels (its 20-tick spacing is past the cancel window), Mash cancels on nearly every press; the CPU does not mash, and charging it left a Hard or Expert CPU under 25 % for 22 to 23 % of a duel (below), which would soften those levels before the balance pass |
  | Grab (the tier 2 row) | 10 | 11.5 | same as strikes |
  | Clinch knee 4 and elbow 6; the 12 throws 6 to 13 | as listed | x 1.15 at use, rounded to 0.1 where shown (4.6, 6.9; 6.9 to 15.0) | same |
  | Weapon steps, tier 1 / 2 / 3 (light, medium, strong) | 3 / 6 / 9 | 3.5 / 6.9 / 10.4 | same (`WEAPON_MOVES` scaled after it is built) |
  | A blocked hit | `damage x guard factor x 0.9 x (1 + 0.15 x hits blocked lately) x taken x guard` (jab 4.5, cross 6.3, heavy body kick 14.4) | unchanged | measured 0.1 to 2.4 a second against 5 to 11 for attacks: not what drains a fight; the guard keeps its wait of 40 ticks and its refill share of 0.4 (a quicker refill while guarding was tried and moved nothing that mattered) |
  | A thrown item blocked | 1.5 x a weapon block; a perfect one costs nothing | unchanged | rare |

  | A Sway | 10 when the press starts it, whether or not a strike comes | **per strike dodged: 5 / 6 / 8 for a tier 1 / 2 / 3 strike** (section 1); a perfect pays nothing | the hold must cost per strike; a tap that dodges nothing is free |
  | Sidestep, jump, run | 6, 4, 7 a second | unchanged | measured 0.01 to 0.08 a second in a fight: not a drain; the wait after running (20 ticks) and the 3-stamina floor to start running stay |
