- **Refill** (KAI's rate 21.5 a second before the edge; `STAMINA_REGEN_K` 1.3 multiplies the fighter's `12.5 + 1.5 x Recovery`, so 18.2 to 35.8 a second, KAI 28): the wait before it starts after an attack is **24 ticks** from the start of the attack (`ATTACK_NO_REGEN`, was 36), after a blocked hit and a weapon block `GUARD_NO_REGEN` 40 (was 50), after a Sway 24, a run 20, a throw 40 and a clinch strike 30 (unchanged). Shares of the rate by state: standing or crouching 1, walking 0.6, guarding 0.4 (0.1 in block stun), prepared Sway 0.3 (section 1), knocked down and getting up **0.4 (was 0.6)**, jumping and sidestepping 0.2, being hit 0.15, attacking `edge.attackShare` (0 on Hard and Expert), running, swaying, pinned or in a hold 0. Multiplied by the band's refill factor below (was x 0.8 under 25 %). Why a wait of 24: a chained or mashed attack comes every 12 to 25 ticks, the Press script's presses 33 to 60 ticks apart (1.0 to 1.8 a second); 24 ticks sits between them, so a pause longer than a string's own beat refills and a string does not.

#### 5. One Momentum budget

- **Decided: one gauge, five sources, one number to keep inside**: with every source on, the boost starts **0.5 to 2 times per fighter per round** at every difficulty (the boost: gauge `MOMENTUM_MAX` 100, 300 ticks, x 1.15 damage; unchanged, and it still cannot fill while it runs).

  | Source | Gauge paid | Status |
  |---|---|---|
  | Damage dealt | 1.6 per hp (`MOMENTUM_PER_DAMAGE`) | unchanged |
  | Damage taken | x 0.5 of that (`MOMENTUM_TAKEN_RATIO`) | unchanged |
  | Every perfect: Block, Sway and (new) thrown-item block | `MOMENTUM_PERFECT` **20** (one fifth of a boost; today's value) | the thrown-item perfect paid nothing before |
  | Beat step 2 / 3 / 4 and above, on top of the 20 | `BEAT_STEP_PAY` **+6 / +10 / +14** (so the perfects of a Beat pay 20, 26, 30, 34, 34 ...: a Beat of 2 is 46, of 3 is 76, the boost starts on the 4th perfect) | new |
  | Street Chain (BP-P18-49: damage a linked zone, shock, burn or crush does to a foe, depth 2 or more) | the strike rate (1.6 per hp, the receiver's share as above), **at most `CHAIN_MOMENTUM_ROUND_MAX` 40 gauge a fighter a round** (a counter in the fighter, cleared with `reset`) | the cap is new: it bounds the source at 0.4 of a boost a round on any level; BP-P18-49's Momentum call adds it |
  | A hit taken | resets the Beat (no gauge) | new |

  Why these numbers: damage alone gives about 1.0 boost per fighter per round today at all four levels (below), so there is room for about as much again and no more than that before a round is decided by the boost; a perfect keeps its 20 (it is the skill the game pays for; lowering it would make the Beat cost the player), the steps are paid only for a run of perfects (the cooldown makes the fastest run one perfect every 31 ticks, so a Beat of 4 needs four defences read in a row without a hit), and the chain is paid at the strike rate with a cap so a level full of chain posts cannot decide the round.

##### BP-P18-62: hold-to-prepare Sway (about 2,100 bytes in `breakpoint.html`)

- Constants (replace `SWAY_COST`, 4933, 8 uses): `SWAY_COST_BY_TIER` `[5, 6, 8]` and `swayCost(mv) = SWAY_COST_BY_TIER[mv.tier - 1]`; `SWAY_READY_REGEN` 0.3. `SWAY_IFRAME_TICKS`, `SWAY_RECOVERY_TICKS`, `SWAY_POSE`, `SWAY_BUFFER_TICKS`, `SWAY_NO_REGEN` and every sway pose number stay.
- `Fighter` fields (reset, 6180 to 6211): `swayReady` (bool), `readyAt` (the age of the tick the current defence started: the press that started the sway, or the free tick when Defend was already down), `readyFresh` (that start was at least `PERFECT_BLOCK_COOLDOWN` after `lastBlockAt`), `stickSide`, `stickFwd` (the intent's stick of the last update, for the sway that starts in `Combat.apply`). Set in `update` (6496) after the `defendPressed` / `swayBuffer` lines (6514 to 6521): `swayReady` = Sway guard mode, `it.defend`, state IDLE, WALK or CROUCH, not airborne, and no sway started by a press this tick; a **defence start** is (a) a press that starts a sway (set in `updateFree` where the tap is, not in `startSway`: `readyAt = age`, `readyFresh = age - lastBlockAt >= PERFECT_BLOCK_COOLDOWN`, `lastBlockAt = age`, `swayAuto = false`) and (b) the first tick `swayReady` is true after a tick it was false: the same three assignments. `readyPrev` stays true through a sway of the fighter's own while Defend is down, so a sway that ends with Defend still down is not a new start. The dodge made by the hold (`Combat.apply` calling `startSway` with `swayAuto = true`) stamps nothing and never touches `readyFresh`. `lastBlockAt` is the one shared cooldown stamp; `setState` keeps setting it for a Block entry (6276). A tap's perfect is `stateTicks <= 6 && !swayAuto && readyFresh`.
- The tap stays (6587 to 6588): `updateFree` keeps "a fresh press (kept `SWAY_BUFFER_TICKS` while busy) starts the sway on the tick the fighter is free" but drops the `stam >= SWAY_COST` condition and the `lowStamina` refused event (6588); `startSway` (6629) no longer subtracts stamina (the dodge pays, see below); the defence-start fields are set where the tap is, as the fields bullet says. Verified on a scratch copy of the tree (a prototype of exactly these three lines plus the per-strike cost): **33 of the 37 tests with "Sway" in their name pass without an edit** (every P3-11, P17-03, P17-11 clearance, pose, room and hold test, "Timing (P18-03): the Sway window is the Block window", the momentum and cue tests); the four that fail are the four that state the old cost rule, listed in the self-tests below.
- The hold (`Combat.evaluate`, 7591): before the Sway i-frame line, a strike on a fighter with `swayReady` in IDLE, WALK or CROUCH returns `{ type: 'sway', att, def, mv, auto: true, perfect: def.age - def.readyAt <= PERFECT_BLOCK_TICKS && def.readyFresh }`; the existing i-frame line (the tap) keeps `def.stateTicks <= PERFECT_BLOCK_TICKS` and adds `&& !def.swayAuto && def.readyFresh` (a tap, not a hold's dodge, and the shared cooldown), so a tap's perfect is exactly today's. `evaluate` stays pure: `apply` (7603) calls `def.startSway(stand-in intent { side: def.stickSide, fwd: def.stickFwd }, att)` before `swayHit` when `d.auto`.
- The pay (`swayHit`, 7843): `cost = perfect ? 0 : swayCost(mv)`; not perfect and `def.stam - cost <= 0`: `def.stam = 0` and the dodge fails through `Combat.guardBreak(att, def, mv, match)` (new: the `broke` branch of `blockHit`, 7821 to 7827, moved out and called from both; the event `block` carries `broke: true`); otherwise `def.stam -= cost`, and a perfect refunds `def.stats.edge.perfect` as the perfect Block does (7807); counter window, `swayEnd`, Momentum and hit-stop as today. The `block` event gains `cost`, `auto` and `age = def.age - def.readyAt` for the readouts.
- `regenerate` (6564): a `swayReady` fighter in IDLE, WALK or CROUCH uses `SWAY_READY_REGEN` instead of 1 or 0.6; `updateFree` (6604): `mul *= BLOCK_FACTOR` also when `swayReady`; the ready pose: `if (this.swayReady) this.readyPose(p)` next to the `tiredPose` line (7051), `readyPose` = `SWAY_POSE.back` x 0.25 (about 120 bytes, no new data).
- Readouts and text: `defenceReading(e)` (10038) as in section 1 (the six forms), the Training panel `defRead` line and the new `Defence: ready | cooldown n` line (the panel code at 10821 and its HUD row), `DEFENSE_HELP.sway` and `COMBO_HELP` (5427 to 5431) as written above (the numbers in the text come from the constants), the move-list help screen (it reads `DEFENSE_HELP`).
- CPU (`swayResponse`, 9729): `const cool = f.age - f.lastBlockAt < PERFECT_BLOCK_COOLDOWN;` and `const aim = (simRng() < this.d.swayAim && !cool) ? AI_SWAY_AIM_PERFECT : AI_SWAY_AIM` (the `simRng()` call stays first so the random sequence does not shift, and a CPU that cannot aim perfect plays the plain aim); `f.stam < SWAY_COST` becomes `f.stam < swayCost({ tier: snap.mvTier }) + 1` with `mvTier` added to the AI snapshot (9155 and 9476). - Constants (next to `MOMENTUM_PERFECT`, 5007): `BEAT_GAP_TICKS` 180, `BEAT_STEP_PAY` (section 5), `BEAT_NOTES` and `BEAT_RING_SPEED` = [5, 5.8, 6.6, 7.4] (section 2). `MOMENTUM_PERFECT` takes its section 5 value.

The reset: `Combat.momentum` (7553) sets `def.beat = 0`, `Combat.guardBreak` too, and `Fighter.reset`; the 180-tick gap needs no tick code (`beat` compares ages).

### P18-45 built: Tournament Ring-out row

- The Tournament join screen has a Ring-out row (Off, On) after Entrants and Difficulty; it is hidden when a saved bracket is continued, like the other two. A tap, the arrow keys and a gamepad change it through `changeLocal('tring')`; `Game.saveLevel` stores it with the Difficulty as `setups.tournament.ringOut` (a boolean), `Game.loadLevels` reads it into `selection.tournamentRing`.
- The bracket carries it: `Tournament.draw` (`options.ringOut`, only `true` counts), `blank`, `pack` and `clean` (`t.ringOut`). A saved bracket without a boolean `ringOut` takes the saved Tournament row when it is cleaned (so an old bracket gets the old Settings value, seeded below), and the next save pins it. `Tournament.simulate` and `beginTournamentMatch` read `t.ringOut` (`ring` and `ringOut` the same), so a continued bracket, the CPU fights and the live bouts agree.
- Settings: `SETTING_DEFS.ringOut` and its row are gone. `Setups.init` seeds `setups.tournament.ringOut` once, when it is not a boolean, from the old `ringOut` switch in `breakpoint.v1.settings` (read raw before any `Settings.save` can drop it), next to the Free Fight rules seed, and changes nothing else; an entry with an unknown `v` is left alone. `Game.beginMatch` no longer reads a setting: a start without `ringOut` is the whole room (Free Fight and the Tournament pass their own).
- Text: the mode description and the join screen hint name the row, not the Settings.
- Tests: three named `Tournament ring-out (P18-45):` (the bracket stores, saves and cleans it and an old or damaged one takes the saved row, Settings has no row; the join screen row on a gamepad, arrow keys and taps, saved with the Difficulty, hidden with a saved bracket, carried by the draw and its save; the start-up seed). Updated, not weakened: "Arena bounds (P17-08)" plain 1v1 (now whole room whatever an old value holds) and Tournament bout (the bracket decides, an opposite old value is ignored), the ring test that checked `SETTING_DEFS.ringOut` (now checks it is gone), the P11-02 title, the seeded walk and the hash test no longer set the removed key.

### P18-21 built: Arcade goons, allies and Survival brawls (P18-20 + P18-37)

- Goons (`goonRecord`, `goonProfile`, `GOON_VARIANTS`, `GOON_SCALE`, `breakpoint.html` before `const Story`): a crew is built in code in the creator's record format from any `ROSTER` id (colours, move style and defense of the theme; a missing or bare-top colour is the neutral grey `#808894`); 3 variants (BRUISER, SCRAPPER, RUNNER) and a leader, ids `g:0`, `g:1`, `g:2`, `g:L`, no custom slot, no `ROSTER` entry, no `rank`. Every record passes `validateCustom` (tested for all 32 themes). Points 35 / 34 / 35 / 38 (budget 36, leader 38), every attribute 3 to 7, speed at least 4.
- Sim: `cfg.goons` (theme id) and `cfg.goonLeader` (name). `waveProfiles` deals the variants by the running `waveCursor % 3` (no random number, same crew every try) and puts the leader goon in slot 0 of the leader row (`cfg.rival` still wins when set). `MatchSim.crewScale` applies the table at the CPU level (health x0.30 / 0.32 / 0.275 / 0.16 for Easy / Normal / Hard / Expert, damage x0.50 / 0.48 / 0.455 / 0.32 before the level's `dmg`, stamina x0.8; re-fitted in the review, see "Review fit" below; the leader 2x health and 1.3x damage) in the constructor and in `enterEnemy`. Non-Arcade brawls keep the roster cycle.
- Story: stage 1 rival A's crew (leader row cut as before), stage 3 the boss's crew with its leader goon (`waveBeat` still fires on it), stage 5 the champion's, stage 6 the champion's after "Offer a hand" (also with no choice) with rival A as an ally, rival A's own crew led by rival A himself (an unscaled roster profile) after "Walk away". `waveCut` is no longer set by the story (the engine keeps it). Rival B is gone from `Story.start`, `pack` and `restore`; an old save's `rivalB` is ignored. The leader's name is `Story.leaderName(run, crew)` (`NAME_IDEAS` without GRANITE, index `(seed + 5 x crew) % 28`); B7's `R2` is the leader goon (`Story.profileOf`, `idOf('R2')` is `g:L`, token `{rival2}` kept). Stage info reads "led by <leader>" for stages 3, 5 and 6 and "with <rival A>" on stage 6 after the hand.
- Allies (`cfg.allies`, up to 2 roster ids, never the player): `MatchSim.allies`, `peopleCount` (people first, then allies; `partySize` counts both, one more enemy per ally in every wave, as decided), an `AIController` at the run's level, the level's `dmg` factor, no stamina edge (`giveStaminaEdge` loop over people only), full health at every start (`placeFighters`), `playersAlive()` for the loss rule (only a person counts when there are allies; the clock still beats the people). Brawls (`nextSurvivalBrawl`): enemies by CPU level and allies exactly as the decided table (min of 6), drawn in turn from the lap with no fighter twice in a fight even across a lap end, allies after the enemies; `cfg.mode: 'brawl'` with `cfg.survival`; group health `SURVIVAL_GROUP` (x0.50, 0.40, 0.33, 0.28, 0.24 for 2 to 6 enemies, 1 for 1), damage x0.7 (`crewScale`); clock `max(30, 50 - 2 x extra) + 8 x (enemies - 1)`; heal `0.25 + 0.04 x (enemies - 1) - 0.02 x extra`. An ally lowers the clear rate of the AI person at Hard and Expert; Normal is in step. The likely cause is the AI person and the AI ally competing for the same attack tokens (`CrowdDirector`), which a human does not do, but this was not tried out. ### P18-53 built: hit freeze with more than two fighters

- Owner 2026-11-07: in a Free Fight free-for-all of 4 CPUs and the owner, a CPU's strong hit froze the whole fight ("this abrupt timestop ... disoriented me"); the owner asked for the best rule for modes with more people and delegated the pick ("go with the best choice").
- Decision: a 1v1 keeps every freeze as before. With more than two fighters a freeze stops everyone, so only a hit the one person lands or takes freezes, at most `CROWD_HITSTOP_MAX` (4) ticks; with two or more people, and on every CPU against CPU hit, nothing freezes (flash, shake, sound and rumble still mark the hit). It depends only on the seats, so replays stay the same.
- Code: `MatchSim.addHitStop(ticks, att, def)` replaces the 15 direct `match.hitStop` writes; test `Hit freeze (P18-53)`. Chrome self-test 625 of 625 with no fingerprint change (the fingerprint fights are 1v1s).

### P18-16 start side (decided and built 2026-11-09)

- Decision (the recommended one of BR-001, nothing changed): the start side is offered in Free Fight, Arcade duels and Training. "Automatic" stays the default, so the P9 seat balance and every recorded fingerprint hold when nobody picks a side.
  - Free Fight has had the row since P18-43 ("Player 1 starts", the last row of More options). This task adds the same row, with the same name and labels, to Arcade (the fighter screen, under Difficulty) and to Training (the setup screen, above the sparring partners). It is an ordinary spinbutton row, so a tap, the arrow keys and a gamepad all step it; no new button.
  - Automatic: today's rule exactly (a 1v1 draws the first fighter's side from the match seed in round 1 and swaps it every round; `cfg.sides`, `MatchSim.sideFor`; no random number). Training never drew a side (it always started left), so its Automatic is Left and its row offers Left and Right only, default Left.
  - Left or Right: the first fighter (player 1) starts there in round 1 and the sides swap every round after, as now. Training has no rounds, so its choice holds.
  - Two people: the row is player 1's side, so two people can never pick the same one; player 2 takes the other side. The CPU takes the other side. Arcade has one person.
  - Arcade: the choice is part of the story run (`Story.start` takes it, `Story.pack` and `Story.clean` keep it, so Continue Arcade plays on with it). It sets round 1 of the duel stages 2, 4 and 7 (`Story.cfg` gives them `startSide`; `Story.cast` stands the scene's cast there); the brawl stages still start on the left. A save from before the row reads as Automatic.
  - Not offered: Versus, Survival and Tournament (every bout keeps the drawn side, which is what keeps their seats fair), and lineups of three or more teams and the crowd (Free Fight dims the row, P18-43).
- Config and saving: `cfg.startSide` (0 drawn, 1 left, -1 right) is the field Free Fight already used; `MatchSim.startSide()` now also reads it in Training. The Arcade and Training choices are saved as `setups.arcade.side` and `setups.training.side` (0 Automatic, 1 Left, 2 Right) beside Difficulty, only when they are not the default, and read back by `Game.loadLevels`; a missing or damaged value reads as the default.
- Balance: nothing moves when nobody picks a side (Automatic runs the code it ran before; the pinned fingerprints and the seat-balance tests pass unchanged). A chosen side is a choice of the level's lopsidedness for round 1 only, so it carries the seat effect of that level for one round of a best-of-3 (the swap gives the other side in round 2). Measured with the headless runner (`SimRunner.run`, KAI against KAI, Hard, items and hazards on, no ring, seeds 1 to 60 per cell, default rounds, so the side holds in round 1 only; the heavy slots were busy, so the sample is 60 and one standard error is about 6 points; first fighter wins, left / right / Automatic): Warehouse 33 / 55 / 43 %, Dojo 38 / 58 / 40, Pit 48 / 58 / 55, Rooftop 57 / 35 / 43, Subway 42 / 67 / 57, Garage 70 / 38 / 55, Construction 40 / 45 / 38, Club 55 / 50 / 55; pooled over the eight levels (480 matches per column) 47.9 / 50.8 / 48.3 %. So a chosen side tilts single levels by up to about 20 points from even (Garage 70 % on the left, Subway 67 % on the right), the two sides cancel over the levels, and Automatic stays inside the same band; no level or number was changed, because the choice is the player's and one round of a best-of-3.
- Tests (3, 'Start side (P18-16)'): the sim (Free Fight, Arcade and Training, two levels, four seeds: Left, Right, drawn and unset in rounds 1 to 3; Training holds); the story run (duel stages have the side and the cast stands on it, brawl stages and an Automatic run have none, pack and restore keep it, damaged values read as Automatic, the stage fight opens and swaps); the rows (a tap, the arrow keys and a gamepad on Arcade and on Training, the labels, the saved value read back, damaged values, the Arcade run and the Training fight take the side).
- File size: stored LF `breakpoint.html` 1,209,623 -> 1,211,803 bytes (+2,180); the budget is 4,000,000.
- Owner device check for P16-03: on a phone, step the Start side row on the Arcade fighter screen and the Training setup screen by tap; start a duel and a Training fight on each side.

### P18-54 (with P18-51 and P18-35) Arcade story rebuilt from fighting-game tropes (2026-11-09)

- Owner (verbatim): 2026-11-09 "source the narrative,story from games that provide influence (tekken,urban reign etc) / We will rework the story using tropes from scratch. Currently its 100% ai sounding"; 2026-11-07 "Rewrite the story/Arcade to be human sounding. It still sounds ai made"; 2026-11-03 "The dialog in story beats is cheesy and definitely reads as AI made it and without cohesion". Research: Appendix B, "P18-54 - Story tropes of the reference games". Nothing supernatural is used.
- Tropes picked, and why they fit the data the game already has:

  | Trope (Appendix B) | Where it sits in a run | Why |
  |---|---|---|
  | A belt whose owner has his own reasons; family money behind it | ZERO's city belt; ZERO's family owns the club building and its roof (stages 5 to 7) | the run already ends with ZERO on the rooftop after a club night; ZERO's origin is Wealthy family, his goal Stay undefeated |
  | Underground fight clubs owned by bosses, climbed place by place | gym (stage 2), the Pit (stage 4), the club (stage 6), the roof (stage 7) | the four fixed levels of the run are already that ladder |
  | One crew per boss, the crew goes first | rival A's crew at home (1), the Pit boss's crew (3), ZERO's crew (5, 6) | P18-20 + P18-37: every boss brings their own goons |
  | The rival who becomes an ally or turns on you | B5 choice, B12 and stage 6 | "Offer a hand" puts rival A beside you, "Walk away" brings rival A's crew against you (P18-21) |
  | The final fight at the top of the boss's building | stage 7 on ZERO's roof | the rooftop level |
  | The boss who taught the champion | HAO taught ZERO (and every belt holder) to fall at the Pit | HAO is 57, Wing Chun, Martial arts family |
  | Debt, missing sibling, revenge with names, police family, the old champion's last run | the 24 goals and origins | the goal and origin lists already hold these; the lines make them concrete |
  | Fighters from many countries, each with a private reason | Country, Origin and Goal | the three choices of the creator |

- Story bible:
  - The city is the player's own ({city}: the country's city). Fight money there runs through one belt. ZERO (33, karate, masked, Wealthy family, never lost) holds it; his family owns the building with the Night Club and the roof. ZERO only fights people the Pit sends up, and only on his roof.
  - Below the club is the Pit, a boiler-room cage. Three old hands each run one night of it and take the door money: HAO has Thursdays, MARLON Fridays, YOAV Saturdays. Whose night you get is the run's boss (the region and the clears pick it, as before). Above the Pit is legal sport: the City Fight Gym, where rival A trains and where the belt queue starts.
  - Why the fights happen: the belt pays, and the only road to it is gym, then Pit, then club, then roof. Every name on that road has a crew that fights for them in the street, so a new name meets a crew before each door.
  - The three bosses and what each wants: HAO (57, Wing Chun) taught ZERO to fall on the Pit floor before the family bought better coaches; he wants to see someone take ZERO apart, but only someone who can get past him. His B9 line says everyone who has worn the belt learned to fall on his floor, so it also holds in ZERO's own run. MARLON (49, Kali, dockhand) runs Fridays like a dock shift and hands half his door to the club every week; he wants someone worth sending up who will cost the club. YOAV (34, Krav Maga, reservist) works security for ZERO's family; the Pit is a paid shift and stopping people going up is his job; he wants to do it well and go home.
  - The champion: ZERO in every run except ZERO's own, where MARA holds the belt (P10-02). Lines that name the champion use the new `{champ}` token, so they stay true for MARA; only goals no ZERO run can have (Win the title, Beat the champion, Earn respect) name ZERO. One character is the same in every run: DEACON works nights in his own run too, DIEGO has four hundred followers as a player and four hundred watching as a rival.
  - Rival A (by the goal's motive) mirrors the player's reason: DEACON (title: twenty years of bakery night shifts for one more go at the belt), FEMKE (body: counts every wasted step), DIEGO (fame: streams everything, even from his sock), KELSEY (past: did three years in the Pit, worked the club door, got out), GIORGI (family: eleven cousins, takes a walk-off as an insult), ROXY (bond: came because she was bored and loves the bit where it goes wrong). Rival A now always says their own lines, also when they stand in for a player whose motive names that player (DEACON, DIEGO and KELSEY's own runs).
  - The leader goon (B7, `{rival2}`) is the Pit boss's man and talks about his boss; crews never speak.
  - Origin sets the tone (rough, ordinary, strict) and with it who is around the fighter: rough has no safety net (sofas, changed locks, clips filmed by strangers), ordinary has family (an aunt who rings, frozen peas, a mum who asks), strict has rules (letters, an old coach's texts, drills). The B1 line says where the fighter comes from in one fact.
  - Goal sets the reason and the through-line: B2 states it with one concrete thing (a cleared space on a wall, a date in pen on a hand, three emails), B10 (after the Pit) moves it on with the same thing, B14 (on the roof) answers it with the same thing again.
  - One line per preset: KAI mops the gym he trains in and takes everything literally. MARA keeps her kid's drawings in her kit bag and says out loud it's for the rent. BRUTUS is big and quiet, owes a loan shark and says sorry after he hits you. YUKI is small and fast and keeps a list of everyone who said no. DMITRI works at a steel plant and rings his mother after every fight. ZERO has never lost, partly because his family never let him meet anyone who could beat him. DEACON bakes on nights and lost a belt final long ago. ROSA runs the family grill and someone is leaning on it. HAO keeps the Thursday Pit and once taught ZERO. FEMKE counts reps, steps and seconds and has no small talk. PRANEE was turned away by every gym and doesn't smile in photos. LARS does payroll, joined on doctor's orders and is surprised he's good. AMARA grew up in a police house and knows the crews' names from the files. SORA talks too much and wants people at her birthday. DIEGO delivers food and streams every fight from his handlebars. TIAGO runs a free kids' class and counts the coins in the jar. KELSEY got out of the Pit and came back to set something right. ELISE has a new name and always sits facing the door. NARAN came from the steppe with one bag and says very little. GIORGI wears the ushanka, has eleven cousins and wants the man who hurt his brother. ARMINE shows her brother's photo to everyone at the Pit. REID's coach died owing the belt a rematch. CAMILA has TV parents and came to get fit, then stayed for the chokes. VIKRAM works a wedding-hall door and knows when not to fight. LUCIA makes pastry and her nonna thinks she does yoga. MARLON keeps the Friday Pit and wants his half back. NIA is nineteen and looking for her sister. YOAV works the Saturday shift for ZERO's family. KASIA does two jobs at a bottling plant and fights on her day off. CRUZ has ZERO's poster in his locker with the eyes scratched out. TESSA drove twelve hours from the farm for the belt. ROXY laughs when she gets hit.
- Method (P18-35: one voice, one through-line): every beat follows from the one before it. Stage 1 is rival A's crew at home, so B3 names rival A and the City Fight Gym; B4 and B5 are rival A; B6 is rival A pointing at the Pit and the boss's crew; B7 is that crew's leader talking about the boss; B8 is the cost of stage 3 the night before the Pit; B9 is the boss's night at the Pit; B10 is the goal after the Pit; B11 is the champion's crew at your door; B12 is rival A again (beside you or against you); B13 is the champion on the roof; B14 answers B2 with the same object; B16 answers B1: each region now has an epilogue line set in the same place as its opening (the car park, the underpass tape, the cafe). The setbacks return: B8 before the Pit, B15 after any lost stage, B16's continues line.
- Voice rules used on every line (P18-51): plain British English as the game already used, short sentences, contractions, one concrete thing a line (a bakery, a sock, a bedsheet, a receipt), people answer their own worry instead of the question (KELSEY, GIORGI, DIEGO), threats said as jobs or bets (YOAV, the leader goon), no speech about what fighting means, no tidy moral, no rule-of-three lists, none of journey, destiny, legacy, rise, forge, embrace, unleash, testament, no em-dash rhythm, not every line a joke (B1, B8 and most B14 lines are plain, and boxes do not all end on a short punchline). Each line was checked for a detail only Breakpoint has (its levels, its fighters, the Pit nights). A script checked every line at its limit with the longest tokens (90 characters, origins 64, creator hints 60) and for non-ASCII characters before the game file was written.

### P12-04 CSP under WebRTC (2026-11-09)

- Result: the policy needs no change. The meta tag in `breakpoint.html` stays exactly as it was; WebRTC works under it in every engine that has WebRTC on this PC.
- Final policy (unchanged): `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; media-src data:; connect-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`.
- Method: a Node Playwright script (Playwright 1.64.1, headless, TEMP in the scratch profile folder, every browser closed in `finally`, a throw-away http server on 127.0.0.1 stopped at the end) loads the real `breakpoint.html` from the worktree over http and over `file://` (players may open the file directly), plus a control run over http with the meta tag removed by `page.route`. In the page, under the policy: two `RTCPeerConnection`s, one `RTCDataChannel` (`ordered: false, maxRetransmits: 0`, the P12-02 input channel), the offer and answer exchanged as copied strings (`JSON.stringify` of `localDescription`, `setRemoteDescription(JSON.parse(text))`, ICE gathering finished before the copy, as in P12-01), the channel opens, `ping` goes one way and `pong:ping` comes back. Run twice per page: with no ICE server, and with `stun:stun.l.google.com:19302` (a public STUN server). A `securitypolicyviolation` listener (added before the page's scripts) and the console record every violation.
- Media: `breakpoint.html` has no `srcObject`, `getUserMedia`, `captureStream` or `RTCPeerConnection` use today (`rg`), so no violation can come from the game itself; the planned QR scan (P12-01) was checked as a stand-in: a `<video>` fed from `canvas.captureStream()` and from `getUserMedia({ video: true })` (fake camera device) through `srcObject`, then `play()`.

| Firefox 157.0 | file:// | yes | pass, 0.12 s | pass, 0.14 s | host / host + srflx | pass / pass | 0 |
| WebKit (Playwright build, Safari 27.2) | http and file:// | no: `RTCPeerConnection`, `getUserMedia` and `captureStream` do not exist in this Windows build | not testable | not testable | - | not testable | 0 (nothing ran) |

- The control runs (meta tag removed) gave the same results in Chromium and Firefox, so the policy changes nothing for WebRTC. WebKit has no WebRTC in that build with or without the policy.
- Why no change is needed (measured, not assumed): `connect-src 'none'` did not stop the data channel, the ICE traffic, or a `stun:` URL in `iceServers` (srflx candidates were gathered, no violation event, no console message) in Chromium 156 and Firefox 157. `media-src data:` does not apply to a `MediaStream` on `srcObject` (no URL is fetched). So nothing was added; adding `connect-src` or `media-src` entries would only widen the policy.
- Not covered: Safari and Safari on iPhone (this PC's WebKit has no WebRTC), Chrome on Android, and a `stun:` or `turn:` server that is blocked by the network (the CSP is not what blocks it). For the P16-03 device list (BP-P16-03): open the game on an iPhone and in desktop Safari, run the self-test and read the `CSP under WebRTC` line (it must read pass, not skipped). If a future engine starts to apply `connect-src` to `stun:` or `turn:` URLs, the test fails with the violation named, and only then `connect-src` gets the single scheme it needs.
- Self-test: `CSP under WebRTC (P12-04)` in `breakpoint-tests.js`: skipped where `RTCPeerConnection` does not exist (the headless stub, an engine without WebRTC); otherwise it checks the page policy still holds `default-src 'none'` and `connect-src 'none'`, opens two loopback connections with no ICE server (candidates cross in-page by trickle, which is quick), opens the channel, sends `ping`, receives `pong`, over a reliable channel, and fails on any `securitypolicyviolation` event or after 5 s (the message says "no ICE candidates gathered" when the device offered none, e.g. airplane mode). `test()` also fails any async test that has not settled after 10 s. It closes both connections and removes its listener in all cases. WebRTC needs the event loop, so `test()` in `run_all` now accepts a test that returns a promise: the result is filled in when it settles, `results.settled` resolves when all have, and `UI.runSelfTestWith` awaits it before it counts. The skip check P17-15 lets this one test skip only when `RTCPeerConnection` is missing. Measured: Chromium 1.3 to 1.4 s, Firefox 0.13 s, in the browser self-test over http and `file://`; WebKit skips cleanly.
- Runs: headless `node tools/run-tests.js --affected --also "CSP|Online|WebRTC"` picked all 649 tests (the harness change touches every test): 632 passed, 17 known headless limits (16 "needs the main menu", 1 "blank faces"), 0 other failures, 733 s; the WebRTC test skips cleanly there. Browser run of the two tests (this one and P17-15) over http and file://: Chromium pass, Firefox pass, WebKit skipped (no WebRTC) with P17-15 passing. The full Chrome self-test (the merge gate) was not run for this task.
- Note for P12-01 and P12-02: Chromium needs about 1.5 s to finish ICE gathering for the copy-paste offer (all host interfaces), Firefox 0.1 s; the "Copy code" step should wait for `iceGatheringState === 'complete'` and show a progress hint. No `frame-ancestors` is possible in a meta tag (Appendix D row D29).

### P12-01 Signaling by copy-paste, no server (2026-11-09)

- Result: built as decided in "Online signaling (P12-01)" above (packed `BPO-` / `BPA-` codes, `iceServers: []`, gathering ends when complete or after 3 s, whole-SDP fallback, inline QR display, scan only where `BarcodeDetector` reads `qr_code`). The packed form connects Chromium 156 and Firefox 157 in every combination over http and `file://` (table below). Not proven here: Safari, iPhone, Android (owner checks below), and the QR scan itself (no browser on this PC has a QR reader).
- Where it lives in `breakpoint.html`: `OnlineCode` (format), `Qr` (encoder), `createOnlineLink` and `Online` (peer link and the small API), `OnlineUI` (the screens; section 09d). About 50 KB (1,217,859 to 1,267,739 bytes LF, budget 4,000,000); the QR encoder is about 10 KB with its comments, more than the 4.5 KB estimated.
- Code format, version 1 (what the decision left open is fixed here):
  - Text: `BPO-` (offer) or `BPA-` (answer) + base64url of the bytes below. Whitespace and line breaks anywhere in a paste are removed; the prefix is case sensitive.
  - Byte 0: format version (high nibble, 1), kind (bit 3: 0 offer, 1 answer), form (low 3 bits): 0 packed, 1 whole SDP deflated (`CompressionStream('deflate-raw')`), 2 whole SDP as it is. The decision's "mode" is this form. Byte 1: seat (high nibble, 2 to 4; the answer repeats the offer's seat) and net protocol version (low nibble, 1; P12-02 raises it when its messages change). Last two bytes: CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over everything before.
  - Packed body: ufrag length + characters (4 to 32), pwd length + characters (22 to 32), DTLS fingerprint 32 bytes (sha-256 only), candidate count (1 to 6), per candidate a type (0 mDNS name, 1 IPv4, 2 IPv6) + address (16, 4, 16 bytes) + port 2. UDP host candidates only; TCP candidates (Firefox lists two) are dropped.
  - Rebuilt SDP (what `setRemoteDescription` gets): `v=0`, `o=- 1 2 IN IP4 127.0.0.1`, `s=-`, `t=0 0`, `a=group:BUNDLE 0`, `m=application 9 UDP/DTLS/SCTP webrtc-datachannel`, `c=IN IP4 0.0.0.0`, ice-ufrag, ice-pwd, fingerprint, `a=setup:actpass` (offer) or `active` (answer), `a=mid:0`, `a=sctp-port:5000`, `a=max-message-size:262144`, the candidate lines (foundation 1 to n, priority `(126 << 24) + ((65535 - index) << 8) + 255`, `typ host`), `a=end-of-candidates`.
  - The whole SDP is sent instead (form 1, or 2 where `CompressionStream` is missing) when the packer cannot say something: another media line shape, another SCTP port or mid, another or a second fingerprint, a server-reflexive or relay candidate, a host name that is not an mDNS UUID, over 6 candidates, no candidate, an offer that is not `actpass`, an answer that is not `active`. The reader limits the inflated size to 16 KB (a deflate bomb is refused) and the paste to 4,000 characters.
  - Reading order, so each mistake gets its own plain message: prefix, expected kind, alphabet and length, CRC (a changed character is "Code damaged or incomplete. Copy it again, all of it."), then format and net version ("This code is from another version of the game."), kind bit and seat range, then the body with every length checked. A paste of the wrong kind says which code goes where; a wrong seat says so.
  - Real address case (found by a run with mDNS off): a browser then puts its first candidate's port and address on the `m=` and `c=` lines; the packer accepts any port there (the template always writes 9).
- Sizes measured on this PC (characters of the whole code, 2 candidates each): Chromium offer 144 (105 bytes), Chromium answer 144, or 119 when only one candidate was ready within the 3 s window; Firefox offer and answer 160 (117 bytes). The same SDPs are 715 (Chromium) and 907 (Firefox) characters, so the packed code is about a fifth of the SDP. QR versions: 119 characters version 6, 144 version 7, 160 version 8 (capacities 134, 154, 192); the largest code that fits is 425 characters (version 13), longer shows "Too long for a QR: use Copy." Phone: 318 px square at 390x844 (6 px modules), 265 px at 844x390 (5 px modules).
- Flow (the smallest one that tests the link; the lobby of P12-06 replaces it): main menu > Online > Host a game or Join a game. Host: the screen makes the code for seat 2 (about 1 s), shows it with Copy and Show QR, a box for the answer, Connect (and Scan where the browser can read QR). Guest: a box for the host's code, Make answer code, then the answer with Copy and Show QR. Both screens show one status line (aria-live): making the code, waiting, connecting, "Connected (round trip N ms)." (the host pings once when the link opens) or the plain error. Show QR is a screen with the canvas and Back (portrait: canvas above, landscape: canvas left), the largest module size that fits. Back ends the link and the camera (every way off the screen does: `UI.go` and `UI.hideScreen` call `OnlineUI.leave`, and a closed link's late answer is ignored). Keyboard and gamepad: the focus starts on Copy (host), Make answer code (guest) or Back, never in a code box; Esc and Backspace go back from a read-only code box, in the box the player writes in Backspace types and Esc leaves the box first. No new on-screen buttons on the fight screens; the one new menu item is Online on the main menu. The test list of the seeded random walk (`Mode flows (P18-40)`, `FLOW_SCREENS`) now knows the four Online screens.
- Errors the player can read (all in `ONLINE_MESSAGES`): empty paste, not a code, wrong kind, damaged or cut off, another version, another seat, no network address found (after the 3 s gathering), the browser refuses the code, ICE failure ("could not reach each other ... same Wi-Fi or network ... VPN, firewall, guest-network isolation"), no connection within 20 s of the answer reaching the host, a host that never answers (guest waits 180 s), connection lost. A bad paste never ends the link: the player pastes again.
- Transport API (for P12-02 and P12-03), `Online.createLink('host' | 'guest')` returns one link per peer (the host makes one per seat):
  - `makeOffer(seat)` (host, seat 2 to 4) resolves to the `BPO-` text; `acceptOffer(text)` (guest) resolves to the `BPA-` text; `acceptAnswer(text)` (host) starts the connection. A bad code rejects with `error.code` and `error.message` and leaves the link usable; a failure of the connection itself ends it.
  - `state`: `idle`, `gathering`, `waiting`, `connecting`, `open`, `failed`, `closed` (only forward, except to the last two); `error` (`{ code, message }` after failed or a lost connection); `seat`; `form` (0, 1, 2 of the code made here).
  - `send(data, quick)`: strings or ArrayBuffers; `false` when the link is not open (nothing is queued). `quick` = the unordered channel without resend (`ordered: false, maxRetransmits: 0`, for the P12-02 inputs); the default is the reliable ordered channel (lobby, config, pings, checksums). Both channels are negotiated (ids 0 and 1), so neither side waits for `ondatachannel`; a link is open when both are open.
  - Hand-off point: `OnlineUI.release()` (call it when the link is `open` and a match or the lobby takes over, BEFORE `UI.hideScreen()` or `UI.go()`, which leave the Online screens and close the screen's link). It returns the open link, which the caller owns from then on: the screen sets its own reference to null, removes its own listeners (state and the `bp-ping:` / `bp-pong:` test flow) and neither `leave()` nor `reset()` closes it. It returns `null` and changes nothing when the link is not open. The caller adds its own `onMessage` and `onState` listeners; P12-02 and P12-06 start from here.
  - `onMessage(fn(data, quick))`, `onState(fn(state, error))`: several listeners, each returns a function that removes it. `close()` ends it and drops the listeners. A refused description (the browser throws a `DOMException` with a numeric code) becomes error code `sdp` with the plain message, never the browser's text. `createOnlineLink(role, options)` takes `gatherMs`, `connectMs`, `guestWaitMs` and `connection` (a stand-in for `RTCPeerConnection`) for the self-tests.
- QR: `Qr.encode(text)` returns `{ version, size, mask, dark }` (byte mode, level L, versions 1 to 13, 8 masks with the standard penalty score, Reed-Solomon over GF(256)) or `null` over 425 characters; `Qr.draw` paints it with a 4-module quiet zone. Scan: `Online.canScan()` needs `isSecureContext`, `getUserMedia` and `BarcodeDetector` listing `qr_code`; the Scan button opens the back camera in a `<video>` through `srcObject` (no CSP change, P12-04), reads every 200 ms, takes the first value with the expected prefix and starts the next step by itself (host: Connect, guest: Make answer code); the camera stops on a scan, Stop, Back, Show QR and a failure. Checked here: `BarcodeDetector` does not exist in the Playwright Chromium 156, Chrome 157 and Edge 157 on Windows (also with experimental features on), Firefox or WebKit, so the scan path and a camera read of the drawn QR are owner checks. The drawn QR is checked by an independent reader in the self-test instead (format bits against the standard's table, mask, data modules, Reed-Solomon syndromes, text), for every capacity edge of versions 1 to 13.
- Cross-browser proof (Node Playwright 1.64.1, headless, TEMP in the scratch profile folder, browsers closed in `finally`, a throw-away http server on 127.0.0.1 for the http rows): two browser contexts drive the game's own Online screens; the script reads the host's code from its box, pastes it (broken over two lines with spaces) into the other page's box, reads the answer, pastes it back, presses Connect, and waits for "Connected". Both pages are on this PC, so the codes carry this PC's mDNS names and the browsers resolve each other's.

Before the media-line fix the same run fell back to the deflated SDP (608 characters), which also connected..
- Found and fixed on the way: (1) a race in the link. On a fast network the channels open before `setRemoteDescription` of the answer reports back, so the host went `open` and then back to `connecting` and timed out 20 s later: one run in three between two Chromium windows. Now the host is `connecting` before the call and the states only move forward; a test opens the channels first (`openFirst`). (2) The packer refused real-address SDPs (media line with the first candidate's port); fixed and tested. Ask the host for a new code, then send your answer faster."); the guest screen then lets the player paste again (the failed link is replaced by a fresh one).
