### P12-02 built (2026-11-09)

- What was built (all in `breakpoint.html`, one section before `Game`, "Online lockstep (P12-02)"): delay-based lockstep on the fixed 60 Hz sim, star topology, the host relays. `LockstepSession` runs one match on one peer; `NetSeatController` plays a seat's input through the same path as a local human (`controllers[i].think` fills the intent, then `updateLock` and `readAssist`); the CPU fighters run on every peer. Only the intent crosses the network: `encodeInput` packs it into 32 bits (fwd and side as signed bytes in steps of 1/127, 12 button flags, sidestep, grapple direction); the sender plays the decoded value too, so a peer never plays an input the others did not get. `assist` and `guardAssist` stay the match's `cfg.assist`.
- Hand-off point for P12-01 (connection), P12-03 (4 peers) and P12-06 (lobby): production uses `LockstepTransport.fromLink(link)` on the link of P12-01 (`Online.createLink`: `send(data, quick)`, `onMessage(fn(data, quick))`, `onState(fn)`, `close()`): input rides its quick channel (unordered, no resend; ArrayBuffer in, Uint8Array to the session), control its reliable one (strings). `close()` of that transport only detaches its listeners: the link and its `RTCPeerConnection` belong to whoever made them. There is no adapter for a bare `RTCPeerConnection` any more (the first one created its own channels, which would have collided with the link's ids 0 and 1): `fromLink` is the one production path. Then `new LockstepSession({ match, seat, seatCount, host, links: { seat: transport } (host) | hostLink: transport (guest), delay, fighterOf, localController (default P1's controller on every peer), onWaiting, onDesync, onDrop })` and `Game.attachNet(session, { onRematch, onLeave, onDesync, onDrop })`. `Game.endMatch` (called by a rematch, a restart and the next tournament fight) only calls `session.detach()`: the transports stay open, make a new session on them for the next match. The connection owner closes the connection: `session.close()` only detaches a link transport, and the link and its `RTCPeerConnection` are closed by their owner; `Game.leaveOnline()` (the Leave and Menu buttons) does `quitToMenu`, `session.close()` and `hooks.onLeave()`, where the owner closes the link so the others see it at once. A transport is any object with `send(channel, data)`, `close()`, `onmessage(channel, data)`, `onclose()`; the tests use an in-memory one and a stand-in with the link's shape. No `RTCPeerConnection`, code, QR or Online screen was built here (P12-01 has them). The lobby still has to: build the `MatchSim` from one config on every peer (same seed, same `cfg`, `cfg.assist` fixed by the host), pick `fighterOf`, call `session.retune()` (host; sets the delay from the pings and tells the guests) in the lobby and between rounds, leave `Game.onNextRound` as it is (it starts the next round on every peer on the same tick), and decide what "Rematch" does (the "Out of sync" button calls `hooks.onRematch`; no state transfer).
- Rules as built: each seat sends its input for frame n + delay when frame n starts (the first `delay` frames are empty); a peer steps frame n only with every seat's input of frame n. Every packet carries the last 8 frames of one seat (`NET_REDUNDANCY`), the host forwards each guest packet verbatim to the other guests. The delay is chosen by each sender (the tag on the frame), so the host can change it at any time with no agreement: a longer delay fills the gap with empty frames, a shorter one takes effect after the old frames are used up. `retune()` = clamp(ceil(RTT / 2 / 16.7 ms) + 1, 2, 6) from the median of the last 20 pings per guest link; with several guests the slowest path is guest to host to guest, so the two largest round trips are halved and added. A stalled peer repeats its newest packet every 16 ms and, after 100 ms, asks on the reliable channel for the missing frames (answered with up to 120 frames): this covers a gap longer than the 8 frames, which a delay above 4 can produce. "Waiting for P3..." (the seat's number) is shown after 0.5 s through `onWaiting`; after 10 s the host drops the seat (a guest waits 10 s for the host, 15 s for another seat so the host decides first) and tells everyone the first frame the seat has no input for; every peer plays the drop on that frame: `MatchSim.forfeit(index)`: a 1v1 or a bracket fight is lost by that fighter (the match ends, `matchWinner` is the other; the tournament code sees an ordinary `roundEnd` / `matchEnd`), a brawl, co-op or lineup seats it out (a knock-out, and `reviveTeam` skips it). A closed link is dropped at once, without the 10 s. Nothing a dropped seat sends counts any more. Every 60 frames each peer sends `matchChecksum` (FNV-1a 32 over every fighter's position, velocity, health, stamina, state, timers, the items, hazards, breakables and the `simRng` state, which `makeRng` now exposes as `next.state()`); any difference stops all peers with "Out of sync" (`onDesync`; the match does not step again) and offers the rematch.
- Presses during a hit freeze: the sim does not read intents while `hitStop` runs, but the device is read once per sampled frame, so a press made then would be lost; the one-tick presses (jump, punch, kick, grapple, use, set down, lock, sidestep) of a frame the sim did not read are merged into the next sampled frame (only the sender decides this, so peers need no agreement). Test: a press during a 10-tick freeze is read exactly once, on the first tick after it.
- Viewer settings never change the sim (the P13-03 note): the sim code reads `Settings.v` only for drawing (poses, trails, flashes: `Fighter.animate` and `draw`) and `reducedMotion` no longer touches hitstop (P12-05); the existing "Determinism: viewer settings, clocks and Math.random" test passes in Chrome and in the headless run. The lockstep tests run the guests with every viewer setting flipped (Reduced motion, shake, flashes, rumble, trails, high contrast, effects low, movement mode, both assists): all checksums stay equal. Tick pacing (coordinator note for BP-P13-02): an online match is paced by the lockstep schedule only and has no slow motion, so no viewer setting can make one peer tick slower than the others. Hook: `Game.clockScale` (P13-02's render-clock scale, read by `Game.update`) returns 1 whenever `Game.net` is set (`attachNet`), whatever the Slow-motion finisher setting. The sim's own `slowTicks` still counts down, it just no longer changes the pace. An online match cannot pause (the other seats would wait): `Game.pause` online does not stop the sim, it asks "Leave the match?" on the status line (the pause key and the pause button).
- UI hook: `UI.netStatus(text, ...[label, action])` shows one line over the fight (`#netwait`), driven by `Game.netShow`: the waiting text with a Menu button, "Leave the match?" (Leave, Stay; opened by the pause key or button while the sim goes on), "Connection lost" (the host left, or this peer was dropped: Menu) and "Out of sync" (Menu, and Rematch only where `hooks.onRematch` exists). The lobby (P12-06) is not built.
- Review of P12-02 (Opus, 13 findings, all fixed): (1) the round-end skip ran on one peer only: online it is an input of the frame, `LockstepSession.skipPressed` (any seat's jump, punch, kick or grapple bit) calls `skipRoundEnd` on every peer on the same tick, and `Game.pollMatchInput` leaves the presses to the session online; the training reset is refused online too, nothing else in `pollMatchInput` / `Game` changes the match from local input (the pause menu's training rows are not reachable online); (2) a way out of an online fight (above); (3) `endMatch` detaches, it does not close; (4) the host calls `retune()` when the phase leaves `roundEnd` (only once it has ping samples); no agreement on a tick is needed because each sender tags its own frames, proved by a test that changes the delay (5, 2, 6, 3) while the peers keep stepping over a lossy link; (5) presses are carried only when `hitStop > 0` before the step (not while knocked out or locked); (6) the default device is P1's controller on every seat; (7) `sum` and `desync` messages are checked (integer frame near the tick, a multiple of 60, a 32-bit sum, a valid seat) and `theirSums` is pruned; any other message on the reliable channel (such as P12-01's `bp-ping:` and `bp-pong:` strings) is ignored, with no error and no desync, which a test covers; (8) dropped seats are skipped in pings, input broadcasts, relays and `recommendedDelay`, and the host ignores what they send; (9) a dropped peer's own `onDrop` names its own seat; (10) the connection owner closes the link and its `RTCPeerConnection` (code comment and the hand-off above); (11) the checksum also holds `phaseTicks`, `matchTicks`, `slowTicks`, `endTimer`, `locked`, `blockStun`, `boostTicks`, `chainCount`, `comboHits`, `juggleCount`, `counterWindow`, `reactDur`, `lockCool`, the indexes of `lockOn`, `partner`, `pinnedBy` and `target`, and each CPU's `tickNo`; (13) the `#netwait` CSS sits after `#banner small`.
- Second review of P12-02 (4 findings): (1) `skipPressed` now counts a dropped seat up to its drop frame like every other check (`from === undefined || frame < from`), so peers that learn of a drop at different ticks agree whether its last press skips the round end; a 3-peer test drops a seat that is holding Punch during the round end and checks the checksums, and a unit check covers the frame rule; (2) `Game.pause(by, automatic)`: online the pause key and button toggle the "Leave the match?" question, but window blur, a hidden tab, leaving fullscreen and a lost graphics context (the automatic callers, `Game.pause(null, true)`) only open it; (3) `match.endTimer` stays in the checksum: it does exist, it is `MatchSim.endTimer`, the knock-out delay counter of `checkRoundEnd` (set in the constructor and `startRound`), so it is sim state; (4) a match number: `LockstepSession` takes `matchId` (the same on every peer, new for each match; default the match seed, which the lobby shares, so a rematch gets a new one; pass your own counter to be sure), a 2-byte field in the input packet header and `mid` in every control message; a packet or message of another match is dropped on receipt (a late sum, desync, fill or input after an "Out of sync" rematch). Test: wrong and missing numbers are ignored, the right one is taken, and a second session on the same link ignores the first one's late packet and control message. (12) Tests: a Game.frame plus `attachNet` test (two peers, a round ends by the clock after 2 s, the guest's device presses Punch in the round end: both sims start round 2 on the same tick, well before the full 110 ticks, checksums equal, the host retuned the delay from 2 to 4 at 80 ms round trip), the delay change test, the hit-freeze press now read on exactly tick 13, a resend test (the host's inputs to the guest stop for 400 ms at delay 6: the guest asked for and got the frames: `stats.needs`, `stats.fills` above 0), the way-out test, a stand-in link test for `fromLink`, and, after merging P12-01, the real-link test below.
- Tests (in `breakpoint-tests.js`, the in-memory link has configurable latency, jitter and loss on the input channel and a virtual clock; each peer owns a context swapped around its sim because the sim keeps `simRng`, the arena, the move and flight counters and `Match.current` in globals): two peers with 30 ms plus up to 20 ms jitter and 10 % input loss, 3,600 frames, 60 checksums equal; three peers (a brawl, three people and three CPU fighters), 1,200 frames; 30 % loss against a lossless run, 1,500 frames, all checksums identical; stall: the text after 0.5 s, the drop after 10 s, the sim standing still meanwhile, a 1v1 lost by the dropped fighter; brawl: seated out, the other two play on equal; desync: a corrupted hit-point caught at the next checksum (frame 240) and both stop; delay formula (table 0 to 400 ms, two guests, one ping spike, 20 samples, pinged through the link: 80 ms round trip gives 4, the guest follows); codec, packet, spoofed seat, a late guest drop and the hit-freeze press; two real `Online.createLink` links of P12-01 (the copy-paste handshake in this page, no server) wrapped by `LockstepTransport.fromLink` carry 120 frames of a 1v1 with equal checksums, while `bp-ping:` / `bp-pong:` strings of P12-01's own flow arrive on the reliable channel mid-match and are ignored (skipped where the browser has no WebRTC, which the "Skipped tests" check allows; delay 6: the headless Chrome page renders slowly, so each round trip moves the peers on by up to 6 frames). Results: the Lockstep, Determinism, CSP, Online and Pause tests plus the Skipped-tests check in headless Chromium (Playwright 1.64.1, file://), after merging P12-01: 45 of 45; the headless Node runner, affected set with the Lockstep, Netcode, Online, WebRTC and Determinism parts, after the merge: 668 of 685 pass, the 17 known headless limits, 0 other failures (its `listeners before/after: 40 / 83` is the P13-02 tests alone: `--only P13-02` gives the same, the Lockstep tests leave 40 / 40; after the second review the 16 Lockstep tests alone pass 16 of 16 headless); the full Chromium run before the review was 660 of 660. The real-link test waits with events and `MessageChannel`, not `setTimeout`: in a full run of over 5 minutes Chromium throttles the timers of a page it counts as hidden to one a minute, and a timer-based wait took 70 s
- Measured. Packet: 40 bytes (8 header with the 2-byte match number + 8 x 4) per seat per frame (38 before the match number was added; the numbers below were taken at 38 and scale by 40 / 38); 2 seats = 2 packets a frame = 80 bytes, 4,800 bytes/s over the link (2,400 each way). Packets a frame in total = seats x (seats - 1): 2 seats 2 (measured 2.002 over 36,000 frames, stall repeats included), 3 seats 6 (measured 6.84 over 1,200 frames under 10 % loss and jitter, the repeats of stalls included), 4 seats 12 (not run; P12-03 tests it): 480 bytes a frame, 28,800 bytes/s in all; the host sends 21,600 bytes/s (3 guests x 3 packets), each guest receives 7,200 and sends 2,400. Payload only: UDP, DTLS and SCTP add about 50 bytes a packet. The control channel adds one 60-byte checksum message per peer per second and one ping per second per link.
- 36,000-frame run (the 10-minute acceptance at 60 Hz, run headless once in scratch with `BP_LOCKSTEP_FRAMES=36000` on the first test): two peers, 30 ms plus up to 20 ms jitter, 10 % input loss (7,213 of 72,080 packets lost), delay 4, the guest with every viewer setting flipped: 600 checksums equal, neither session ended, 8.5 s for the whole test on this PC (headless Node, the two sims together); the 3,600-frame form is the test that stays.
- Size: +25,926 LF bytes in `breakpoint.html` when first built (1,217,859 to 1,243,785), +7,395 with the review fixes (1,262,603 to 1,269,998 on top of P13-02): +33,321 in all, inside the 4,000,000 budget.
- Owner device check for the P12 gate (BP-P12-07 / P16-03): a 10-minute 1v1 between two real devices on the same LAN (for example a phone and a laptop, once P12-01 and P12-06 can connect them): no "Waiting" text under normal play, no "Out of sync", the same score on both screens at the end; then switch one device's Wi-Fi off for 12 seconds and see "Waiting for P2..." after half a second and the other side win after 10 seconds.

### P12-03 built: up to 4 peers (2026-11-10)

- Result: the host and up to three guests play one 1v1, one brawl level or one tournament fight together over the P12-01 links and the P12-02 lockstep; star topology, one `RTCPeerConnection` per guest, the host relays. Everything is in `breakpoint.html`: the host screen (one block per guest), `OnlinePlay` (section 09e, the start path), a few lines in `LockstepSession` and `Game`. About +23 KB (1,320,821 to 1,344,042 bytes LF, BOM counted; budget 4,000,000). The net protocol number in the codes is now 2 (the start message and the watching seats are new): a code from before says "another version".
- Host screen (Online > Host a game): the first guest's block is made when the screen opens, "Add another player" makes seats 3 and 4 (a block per guest, each with its own code, Copy, Show QR, Scan where the browser can, answer box, Connect and status line; a failed or closed guest gets a "New code" button for its own seat). Below them: Mode (1 vs 1 for exactly 2 players, Brawl for 2 to 4, Tournament for 2 to 4; until it is pressed it follows the number of connected players; the decision row "Online signaling" had the mode first and then the offers: here the mode is on the same screen after the guests' blocks, because the number of connected players decides what is allowed), Level (not for a tournament) and Start. Start is disabled with the reason ("Connect at least one friend first ...", "A 1 vs 1 needs exactly 2 players ..."). Start hands every open link to `OnlinePlay` (`OnlineUI.releaseGuests()`, the hand-off of P12-01 for many links: the open ones are returned as `{ seat, link, roundTrip }`, the ones that are not open are closed) and starts the match; unconnected seats are simply absent. The guest screen is as before; once its link is open it says "Connected. You are player N. Wait here: the host starts the game." and hands its link over (`OnlineUI.release()`) when the host's start message arrives. The ids are now per seat (`onCode2`, `onAnswer3`, `oncopy:4`, `onconnect:2`, `onStatus2`); the guest keeps `onCode`, `onOffer`, `oncopy:answer`.
- Seats: a seat is the seat of the link's code minus 1 (code seat 2 = session seat 1; the host is seat 0), so a guest that never connected leaves a gap. `LockstepSession` now lets a seat watch: `fighterOf[seat] = -1` (nothing steers a fighter, the seat sends no input, nobody waits for it, its checksums still count); the same for a seat with no link at all. That is what a tournament fight needs (two people fight, the host and the others watch) and a brawl with a gap.
- The start: the host builds one config (`Game.beginMatch` fills `items`, `hazards` and `assist` from the host's own settings, so they go to the guests as the host holds them; `seed`, `keepSeed`, `online: true`), sends `{ t: 'bpstart', id, mode, seat, seatCount, fighterOf, delay, cfg }` as JSON on each link's reliable channel (the lockstep ignores it: it has no match number), builds its `LockstepSession` over `LockstepTransport.fromLink` of each link and attaches it. A guest checks the message (`OnlinePlay.problemWith`: mode, level, fighter, seed, seat equal to its own, seat count, `fighterOf`; anything else gives "The host started a game this version cannot play ...") and builds the same match: equal config and equal checksum at tick 0 (a test). `matchId` is the host's counter, so a rematch has a new number. The first match's input delay comes from the round trips measured when the links opened (the host screen pings once), then the lockstep retunes it at every round end as before. Fighters are fixed here: seat n plays `DEFAULT_UNLOCKED[n]` (Kai, Mara, Brutus, Yuki). Modes: 1 vs 1 = `versus` (first to 2 rounds, 60 s), run mode `versus` with a session score; Brawl = the co-op crowd config (`coop` = the people, `enemies` = `coopEnemyCount`, `waves` where the level has them, `goons` = a fighter that is not in the party) as run mode `coop`; Tournament = `Tournament.draw` of 8 with the people on their seats, shown on the host's own bracket screen; the host's Continue plays the CPU fights on the host and starts every fight with a person in it on all peers (`Game.beginTournamentMatch` calls `OnlinePlay.startBracketFight`; the people in the fight steer the fighters, everyone else watches the same fight). The online bracket is never saved (it would replace the owner's saved bracket). A person whose link is gone is a CPU entrant from the next fight on (`OnlinePlay.demoteGone`, called by `Game.tournamentContinue`).
- Input and screens online: everyone plays with their own device as P1 (`Game.inputPlan` returns 'solo' for `cfg.online`, and the Versus keys card is not shown); the fight is graded nowhere (`gradeResults` skips it when `Game.net` is set); the results screen online has "Rematch" (host) / "Continue" (host, bracket fight) and "Main menu" (everyone; it leaves the online game and closes the links). A guest has only "Main menu" and waits for the host's next start message. The match end: from the match end on the session needs no input (`stepIdle` reads none), so a peer that leaves after the end, or the host going to the bracket, stalls nobody and reports no lost connection (a change to P12-02: before, the results kept waiting for every seat; its round-end test now drops the seat inside the round end).
- Drop behaviour for 3 and 4 seats, as decided: a seat that stops answering for 10 s (the host decides; a guest waits 5 s more) or whose link closes is dropped on the same frame on every peer: in a brawl it is seated out like a knocked-out co-op player (`seatedOut`, the others play on equal, the host keeps relaying the remaining guests), in a 1v1 or a bracket fight its fighter loses (`forfeit`), a watcher that drops changes nothing. The host closes the dropped link and the seat is gone for the rest of the game (no rematch of a fight that needs it: "A player left, so this fight cannot start again.").
- Review fixes (the Opus review of this task found ten things; all are fixed, each with a test in `Online play (P12-03 review)` or the changed P12-02 test):
  1. `Game.inputPlan` follows the live online state (`Game.net` or `OnlinePlay.starting`), not the sticky `config.online`: after an online match an offline Tournament gets its co-op seating again.
  2. The results of an online duel come from the local seat's own fighter (its stats, names, round wins and Victory or Defeat; the second fighter that wins sees Victory); a seat that only watches gets a neutral "X wins"; an online fight writes no records or grades.
  3. The limits note says only the same Wi-Fi or router, or one phone's hotspot (see P12-07).
  4. A peer that leaves while the results are up is reported ("Player N left." / "The host left the game."), and Rematch then says the `someoneLeft` text instead of "Connect at least one friend first".
  5. `Game.quitToMenu` calls `OnlinePlay.leave()` (the way out of the fatal-error screen too), so no link outlives the game; an offline bracket saved afterwards is untouched.
  6. A start message from the host is checked with `Object.hasOwn` on every table (level, fighter ids, difficulty) and for the party (`coop` entries, seats, `fighterOf` against the party, the enemy count); anything wrong, or a build that throws, gives the "cannot play" text, closes the online game and never lets an exception out of `guestBegin`, and the same for the fighter ids a wave reads mid-match: `cfg.goons` and `cfg.rival` must be a fighter of the roster (or empty), `cfg.slots` must be a list of at most 8 entries of roster fighters (re-review).
  7. The `guestWait` text (see P12-07) no longer says Firefox is the only browser that waits only a few seconds.
  8. The round-end drop test of P12-02 now keeps a played press of the dropped seat before its drop frame (asserted on every peer: same presses, same drop frame, the round end ran its full length). `NET_SKIP_BITS` joined the test export list for it.
  9. Start is refused while a connected guest uses another kind of browser (Chrome or Edge, Firefox, Safari), with the `sameBrowser` text on the host screen and in the toast, until P12-08 (the J01 sim math). A guest that is connected but has not said its kind yet counts as still joining (re-review): Start stays off with the `joining` text ("A player is still joining. Start is on in a moment.") until the hello arrives or `ONLINE_HELLO_WAIT_MS` (2 s) have passed, and the screen redraws when the 2 s are up; a guest whose link is not open does not count; the same kind starts. This replaces the warning the first build only showed on the guest's line. **Lifted by P12-08 (2026-11-10): the refusal, the `sameBrowser` and `joining` texts and the 2 s wait are gone; the kind is only shown.**
  10. Rematch and the next bracket fight start from the session's retuned delay, not from the delay measured when the links opened. The first build read `Game.net.delay`, which is gone by the next bracket fight (the bracket screen's Continue, the CPU matches and `Game.showBracket` all call `Game.endMatch` first), and the next fix read a leftover `Game.net` of an older, closed session (found while running the tests: a new session started at the old session's delay). Now `OnlinePlay.lastNet` is the lockstep session of this session's last match; `Game.endMatch` saves that session's retuned delay into `OnlinePlay.delay` before it detaches it (only when it is `lastNet`), a Rematch reads the live `Game.net` while it is `lastNet`, and `leave()` clears `lastNet`, so a new session starts from the round trips measured when its links opened. Test: an online bracket retuned to 6, the match ended as Continue does, fight 2 starts at 6; a new session starts at its own 2.
- Headless Node runner, `--affected --also "Online|Lockstep|CSP|Mode flows"` on the first build: 697 tests picked, 680 passed, 17 known headless limits (16 "needs the main menu", 1 "blank faces"), 0 other failures, 572 s. After the ten review fixes and the re-review fixes (the retuned delay kept across bracket fights, the roster check of `goons`, `rival` and `slots`, Start held while a guest is still joining, a waiting-guest check that tests a waiting guest) the whole suite ran once (`node tools/run-tests.js`): 686 / 703 passed, the same 17 known headless limits, 0 other failures, 596 s; the scoped run of the Online, Lockstep (P12-02), P12-03, P12-07 and review tests: 33 / 33; `listeners before/after: 40 / 40` in both. No fingerprint or hash constant was touched (offline play is unchanged: the tests of it pass unchanged). Ten tests were new in the build and six more came with the review fixes (the `Online play (P12-03 review)` tests; the bracket delay test is the newest), and two old ones changed: the host-screen test of P12-01 (one block per guest now, with the new Start rows) and the round-end drop test of P12-02 (the drop comes inside the round end, see the match-end rule above); the other P12-01 and P12-02 tests pass as they were.
- Tests (`breakpoint-tests.js`; all run headless except the four-link test, which is skipped without WebRTC): four peers, a brawl of four people, 1,800 frames over a lossy jittery star (25 ms + up to 15 ms, 10 % loss), all 30 checksums equal; the stall rate at delay 4 and 6 under jitter, with the retuned delay; one guest drops in a four-person brawl (the three others equal, the same drop frame everywhere); a 1v1 of two guests with the host and a fourth seat watching (900 frames, 10 % loss, equal) and a drop in it (lost by that fighter on every peer, a seat that leaves after the match end is not a drop); OnlinePlay with stand-in links (the config and each seat's message for 4 people, a guest rebuilds the match with equal config and start checksum, a game another version sends is refused, a 1 vs 1 with 3 players says why not, a gap in the seats, Rematch, the host's and the guest's buttons); a bracket fight between two guests (`fighterOf` -1,1,-1,0 with the host and seat 2 watching, nobody reads this PC's keyboard, a fight with a gone person is refused, `demoteGone`, the saved bracket untouched, `leave()` closes every link); the host screen (blocks per guest, Start and its reasons, the Mode and Level buttons) and the hand-off of every open link; four real `Online.createLink` links (host and three guests, three copy-paste handshakes in the page) carry 180 frames of a brawl with equal checksums (skipped without WebRTC, like the two-link test).
- Measured on this PC (in-memory star with the 4-seat brawl, virtual clock; `BP_LOCKSTEP_REPORT` in a scratch copy of the runner): the nominal load is 12 input packets a frame in all (seats x (seats - 1)), 480 bytes a frame, 28,800 bytes/s, as computed in P12-02. In the 1,800-frame run with 25 ms + up to 15 ms jitter and 10 % loss: 26,302 packets were sent (14.6 a frame: a stalled peer repeats its newest window every 16 ms and the host relays those repeats too), 2,669 lost (10.1 %), no resend request needed; the host sent 19,400 packets = 10.8 a frame = 775,388 bytes in 30 s = 25,850 bytes/s (nominal 9 a frame = 21,600 bytes/s: its own packet to 3 guests and the relays, 3 + 6); a guest sends 1 packet a frame (2,400 bytes/s) and receives 3 (7,200 bytes/s nominal). Payload only: add about 50 bytes a packet for UDP, DTLS and SCTP, so the host's upload is about 50 KB/s on the wire at 4 seats, 540 kbit/s of the Wi-Fi uplink.
- Stall rate (the share of virtual 60 Hz frames in which a peer could not step at all; after a stall the loop catches up by up to 4 ticks, so it is the hitching, not a loss of time): 20 ms latency + up to 10 ms jitter, 5 % loss, delay 4: 8.8 %; with up to 40 ms jitter: 43.9 % at delay 4 and 20.5 % at delay 6 (a guest-to-guest input goes over two hops, so the worst path is twice the link: 2 x (20 + 40) = 120 ms against a 6-frame (100 ms) delay). With the formula: a match that starts at delay 2 on 25 ms + up to 15 ms links (guest round trip about 64 ms) stalled 53.8 % of the frames; 5 s in the host's `retune()` chose delay 6 (the median of 5 early pings, the first of which waited for the guests' first packets) and the stalls dropped to 2.7 %. So the formula's two-largest-round-trips rule (guest to host to guest) holds, but the delay should follow the jitter and not only the median round trip: P12-06 should pick the first delay from several pings before the first countdown (and may add a frame when the spread of the samples is large).
- Real browsers (Node Playwright 1.64.1, Chromium 156, Firefox 157, WebKit 27.2, one run per browser over http and over `file://`): the Online, Lockstep, CSP, P12-03, P12-07 and Mode flows tests gave 56 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped in Chromium 156 and in Firefox 157 over http and over `file://`, and 52 passed, 4 skipped (no WebRTC in this Windows build), 0 failed in WebKit 27.2. The four-link test connects three guests through three copy-paste handshakes in one page in Chromium and Firefox (4.4 to 4.9 s in Chromium, 0.7 to 0.8 s in Firefox on this loaded PC) and is skipped in WebKit (no WebRTC in this Windows build). A first run had failed the P12-04 CSP test in both engines: the new heavy synchronous tests had been registered after it and starved its 5 s event loop; they now sit before it (the comment above the CSP test says so).
- End to end, on the game's own screens (a Node Playwright script drives one host page and up to three guest pages: the guest pastes the host's code, the host pastes the answer, Start; scratch script `e2e4.js`, headless): four Chromium pages, a brawl: all three guests connect (seats 2 to 4), Start, countdown, all four pages reach FIGHT and stay there for 20 s with no "Waiting" and no "Out of sync" text and no page error; four Chromium pages, Tournament: the host's Continue plays the CPU fights and the first fight with a person in it starts on all four pages (FIGHT, 20 s, no text); four Firefox pages, a brawl: the same; a Chromium host with a Firefox guest, a 1 vs 1: the same (20 s). A Chromium / Firefox mix of four pages in a brawl with waves stops with "Out of sync" at the first checkpoint (frame 60): see the next point.
- Found: different engines do not stay equal (the J01 risk of Appendix D, now measured). The cause is one last bit: in the brawl with waves, the z of a wave enemy placed at the level's door is -0.3361215932167726 in Chromium and -0.3361215932167727 in Firefox 157 and in WebKit 27.2 on the very first tick (fighter index 8, placed by `MatchSim.putWaveFighter`: `waveSpot` for the position and `Math.atan2` for the yaw), and the yaw of fighter index 9 differs by one bit too (-1.7231840654744992 against -1.7231840654744994); the scripted 1v1-like brawl without waves was equal in all three engines for 150 ticks, and a 20 s Chromium + Firefox 1 vs 1 stayed equal. Measured with a scratch test that steps one scripted match and prints the checksum of every tick (the same cfg in the three engines: Chromium against Firefox and WebKit differs from tick 1; Firefox against WebKit is equal). The fix is the sim-math task of Appendix D row J01 (deterministic `hypot`, `sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, `exp` in the sim; it changes every fingerprint, which are recorded in Chrome only): not done here, offline play is unchanged. Until then the Online screens say "use the same kind of browser on every device" (`ONLINE_LIMITS`), each guest tells the host its kind when its link opens (`bp-hello:` on the reliable channel, `onlineEngine()`: Chrome or Edge = blink, Firefox = gecko, Safari and every browser on an iPhone or iPad = webkit), the host screen shows it on the guest's line ("Browser: Firefox.") and refuses Start while a connected guest's kind differs from the host's own (`OnlineUI.mixedKinds`, the `sameBrowser` text below; a guest that has not said its kind yet does not block; this stays until the J01 sim-math task and P12-08 lift it), and the match stops with "Out of sync" if they drift anyway. The four-device owner check below must be done with one browser family first, then with a phone against a PC.
- Owner device check (4 real devices; the owner list for P16-03): one host and three guests on one Wi-Fi, first all with the same browser family (for example a Windows laptop with Chrome and three Android phones with Chrome, or an iPhone host with three iPhones; do not mix families before the J01 fix: Start is refused with the `sameBrowser` text while a guest uses another kind of browser, so a mixed run can only be tried by temporarily lifting that rule in a scratch copy; expect "Out of sync" in the first seconds of a brawl with waves, and write down which pairs of devices do and do not stay in step). Steps: Online > Host a game, Add another player twice, send each code to a device, paste the answers back, wait until all three say "Connected" (the round trip shows), Mode Brawl, Start. Check: all four devices show the same fight after the countdown and the same K.O.s, no "Waiting for P2..." text under normal play and no "Out of sync" in 5 minutes; then switch one device's Wi-Fi off for 12 seconds: the others see "Waiting for P3..." after half a second, and P3 is seated out after 10 seconds while the other three play on; then a 1 vs 1 (Add only one player) and a tournament fight (Mode Tournament: the host presses Continue on the bracket, the guests see the fight start; leave the Wi-Fi off in the middle of a fight of two guests and check the bracket records a loss for that fighter). Note the host's phone or laptop temperature and the frame rate of the weakest device.
- What P12-06 (the lobby) must add: a fighter pick per seat (seats play the first four starters now), the level and rules rows of Free Fight, names, a "ready" step and a visible list of who is connected (the host screen shows only the links), the first input delay from several pings before the first countdown, a guest's view of the bracket and of who is fighting (a guest only sees the fight when it starts, and the plain results screen after it; a watching seat has no "you are watching" banner), what Rematch does for a bracket fight, someone joining after the first match, a Firefox guest (see the P12-01 handover limit: either side may offer, or a third message), the touch buttons and the rumble of the seat's own fighter (rumble and touch use the P1 device and `Inputs.forFighter` still maps a fighter to input seat = its seat), and P11-02 the bracket for several people on every device.

### P12-07 built: the limits of the connection and the reason for every failure (2026-11-10)

- Result: every way the link can fail ends on a short plain reason with what to try (the same Wi-Fi, a phone hotspot, Firefox as the host); the limits are in the game (the first Online screen, the host and join screens, Menu > About) and here. Everything is text: `ONLINE_MESSAGES` (the failure texts of P12-01 were reworded), `ONLINE_LIMITS` (one sentence shown on the Online screens and in About) and a Firefox line in About. No new code path.
- The texts (all at most 200 characters, ASCII; a failed link carries `error = { code, message }` and the host's guest block, the guest's screen and the status line show `message`; a browser's own error text never reaches the player): `nonetwork` "No network address was found. Connect to Wi-Fi or a router first (mobile data and some VPNs hide the address), then try again." (after the 3 s gathering, no candidate); `ice` "The devices could not connect. Some networks block direct connections: guest Wi-Fi, office or school networks, VPNs, some mobile data. Use the same home Wi-Fi, or a phone hotspot." (ICE state failed, on either side); `timeout` "The connection did not open in time. Make new codes and try again on the same Wi-Fi or a phone hotspot (some networks block direct connections)." (20 s after the answer reached the host); `guestWait` "The host did not answer in time (some browsers, like Firefox, wait only a few seconds). Ask for a new code and answer faster, or try Firefox as the host." (the guest's ICE gave up, or its 180 s wait ended: the Firefox-guest limit of P12-01); `lost` "The connection was lost. Check the Wi-Fi, then join again."; `sdp` "This browser could not use the code. Ask the host for a new one."; `unsupported` "... (no WebRTC). Try the latest Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari."; the paste errors (empty, not a code, wrong kind, damaged, another version, another seat) as before; and for the start: "Connect at least one friend first ...", "A 1 vs 1 needs exactly 2 players ...", "A player left, so this fight cannot start again." (`someoneLeft`, also what Rematch says when a person left since the match), "Start is off: the devices use different kinds of browser (Chrome or Edge, Firefox, Safari), which can fall out of step. Use the same browser on every device." (`sameBrowser`, a Start refused), "The host started a game this version cannot play ..." (also for any start message that fails the guest's checks). A match that loses a peer says "Waiting for P3..." (0.5 s), then "Connection lost" or the seat is dropped (P12-02).
- The limits note (`ONLINE_LIMITS`, shown on the Online screens and in About; reworded by the review, which found that the first wording promised "most home networks" and "a phone hotspot" as a cure for any block): "Works only when the devices are on the same Wi-Fi or router, or on one phone's hotspot. Networks that block direct connections (guest Wi-Fi, office or school networks, VPNs, mobile data) do not work. No server is used: the devices talk to each other. Use the same kind of browser on every device (Chrome or Edge with Chrome or Edge, Firefox with Firefox, Safari with Safari): different kinds can fall out of step."
- Limits list (what cannot be fixed without a server; nothing here is a defect of the game):
  1. No STUN and no TURN server (`iceServers: []`, the decision of P12-01): the browsers offer only the addresses of their own network. Two devices connect when they can reach each other's local address (the same Wi-Fi or router, a hotspot, a VPN that makes one network). Devices on different networks never connect (no way across a NAT: this includes two phones on mobile data and a home network against a friend's).
  2. Networks that block it: guest Wi-Fi and hotels, cafes, schools and offices with client isolation or a firewall that drops UDP between devices; a VPN that routes everything away; separate VLANs or an Ethernet segment against a Wi-Fi segment on some routers; a network that blocks multicast DNS (the codes carry `.local` names that browsers resolve through it; a browser with mDNS off sends real addresses and does not need it). The result is `ice` or `timeout`.
  3. Mobile data: carrier networks use symmetric or carrier-grade NAT; a phone hotspot is the way (the host phone makes the hotspot and the others join it), no mobile data is used for the game itself.
  4. Firefox as the guest: its ICE agent gives up 5 s after it has the offer, so a person cannot carry the answer back by hand in time (P12-01 measured: 5 s to 90 s all failed); Firefox as the host waits for any time, and a scan of the QR is quick enough. Use `guestWait`'s advice: Firefox hosts, or answers at once.
  5. Safari: not measured here (no WebRTC in the Playwright WebKit on Windows). A tab that goes to the background or a phone whose screen locks pauses the page and stops the sim; the lockstep drops that seat after 10 s (P12-02). Keep the screen on.
  6. A device on each side must run the same version of the game (the code's net protocol number), and at most 4 devices play (host + 3); one match at a time; the host's device carries the relay (about 50 KB/s of upload at 4 players, measured above).
  7. Different browser engines do not stay equal yet: the simulation uses `Math.hypot`, `sin`, `cos`, `atan2` and `exp`, which engines round differently in the last bit (Appendix D row J01). Measured: Chromium against Firefox 157 and WebKit 27.2 differ on the first tick of a brawl with waves (see P12-03), and a mixed match stops with "Out of sync" within a second; the same browser on every device (Chromium x4, Firefox x4) ran 20 s with no drift. The Online screens say so and the host screen refuses Start while the kinds differ (`sameBrowser`); the fix is the J01 sim-math task, after which P12-08 lifts the rule. Owner check: the same fight on an iPhone and a PC to see which pairs drift. **Done in P12-08 (2026-11-10): the simulation is exact in every engine and the rule is lifted; the owner check stays (P16-03): any mix of devices, 5 minutes, no "Out of sync".**
  8. No encryption beyond what WebRTC does (DTLS) and no sign-in: whoever has a code can answer it; give a code only to the person you mean.
- Tests: `Online failures (P12-07)` (the advice words each text must hold, the limits note, every failure through a link with a stand-in connection: no network, a refused code, ICE failure, timeout, a guest the host never answers, a lost connection; the host's guest block and the guest's screen show each text; no WebRTC disables Host and Join; the limits note is on the first Online screen, the join screen and About, with the Firefox line); the old link, code and screen tests (P12-01) still run unchanged except for the host screen, which is per guest now.
- Owner device checks for P12-07 (also on the P16-03 list): turn Wi-Fi off and press Host a game (the `nonetwork` text after 3 s); connect two phones on mobile data (the `ice` or `timeout` text); the same two phones on one phone's hotspot (connects); a guest Wi-Fi with client isolation if one is at hand; Firefox as the guest with a slow paste (the `guestWait` text).

### P12-06 built: the online lobby (2026-11-10)

- Result: Online > Host a game and Join a game are now the lobby. Everyone sees the same list of players with the fighter each one picked, Ready or Not ready, and the round trip in ms (good under 60, fair under 120, poor above). The host picks the mode and the level and presses Start. A guest picks a fighter and presses Ready. Start stays off until every guest is Ready. It works with touch, gamepad and keyboard. The net protocol number in the codes is now 3 (the lobby messages and the Free Fight start are new): a code from before says "another version". Everything is in `breakpoint.html` (`OnlineUI`, `OnlinePlay`, `createOnlineLink`, `MatchLineup`, `Game`, a few lines in `UI`).
- The list: one row per player (`OnlineUI.playerRow`): seat (P1 to P4), name (Host or Player N, "(you)" on the own row), the browser kind on the host's screen, the fighter, Ready, the latency, and Remove for the host. On the own row the fighter is an arrow row (`data-local="olb:fighter"`): left and right on the keyboard, the d-pad on a gamepad, a tap on touch. Only the 32 presets can be offered (a custom fighter exists on one device only), and only the ones this device has unlocked. A row that is not yours shows "Choosing..." until the pick arrives. On a narrow phone the row wraps into three lines.
- The host's screen (`renderHost`): the list, then the blocks of the seats nobody has joined yet (code, Copy, Show QR, Scan, answer box, Connect, New code as before), "Add another player", the Game rows (Mode, Level, and the Lineup button for Free Fight) and Start. A connected player is a row of the list, no longer a block with codes. Remove closes that player's link and the seat offers a new code.
- The guest's screen (`renderGuestLobby`, after the link opens): the list, the host's mode, level and one line of the lineup, the Ready button (a toggle; a new pick withdraws Ready) and the status line. The guest takes the host's word for its own Ready.
- Messages (JSON on the reliable channel, both read through a strict reader and anything else is refused): `bpme` from a guest to the host (`fighter`, `ready`; at most 400 characters), `bplobby` from the host to each guest (`you`, `mode`, `arena`, `text`, `seats[{ seat, fighter, ready, rt }]`; at most 2,000 characters, the text is cut to 120). A peer of another version may send anything: ids are looked up as own keys, numbers and lists are checked. The old `bp-hello:`, `bp-ping:` and `bp-pong:` strings stay. Both JSON messages also carry `rev` (the settings revision, review fix 4) and the host sends the string `bp-removed:` to a guest it removes (review fix 7).
- Latency and the first delay: the host pings every connected guest every second while the lobby shows (`ONLINE_PING_MS`), keeps the last 8 round trips per guest and shows the median of the last 5. Start waits until each guest has 3 round trips ("Measuring the connection to player N"). The first input delay is the delay of the two slowest medians (`netDelayFor`) and one frame more when one guest's samples spread over more than 30 ms (`onlineDelayFor`, never above `NET_DELAY_MAX`). The lockstep still retunes it during the match.
- Ready and the settings: a changed mode, level or lineup (the lineup is compared once a second and on every redraw, `lineupSignature`) withdraws every guest's Ready and tells the guests. The mode row cycles 1 vs 1, Brawl, Tournament, Free Fight. A mode that does not fit the number of players says why and Start stays off.
- Fighter picks: every seat plays the fighter it picked (1 vs 1, Brawl, the Tournament bracket and Free Fight). Before this the seats played the first four starters.
- Free Fight online: Players and teams has an "Online friends" row (off by default). Where it is on, the control cell of every slot after the first has a third value, Online (a friend on another device). Where it is off the cell has its two values as before, and the saved setup never keeps an Online slot (it saves it as a CPU). Start fight with an Online slot opens the lobby on the Free Fight mode. In the lobby, slot 1 is the host, each Online slot takes the next connected friend by seat, a friend plays the fighter it picked, the CPU slots stay. The lobby refuses a crowd lineup, a lineup with a local Player slot after the first, and a lineup whose number of Online slots is not the number of connected friends. A plain 1v1 between two people starts as the same duel as the 1 vs 1 mode. Other lineups start as `mode: 'free'` (a start message the guests check: slot count, humans, teams, seats that steer a person's fighter and never a CPU's).
- Local fighter: online, each device plays its own seat's fighter as P1 (`Inputs.forFighter`, `Game.localFighter`), so the rumble, the cues and the touch buttons (USE, LOCK) follow the fighter of this device. A seat that only watches has none.
- After a match: the results screen has an "Online lobby" button next to Rematch and Main menu (the host: Rematch or Continue, Online lobby, Main menu; a guest: Online lobby, Main menu). `OnlinePlay.toLobby` hands the open links back to the lobby (`OnlineUI.resume`): nobody is Ready, the picks and the settings are kept, a friend that left is a free seat and a new friend can join. The guests follow the host when its list arrives and their own match is over; a list that comes while a match is live is ignored. A guest whose link is gone gets "The host left the game." Each match from the lobby gets a new match number.
- Firefox as the guest: either side may make the first code. A guest presses "I send the first code (Firefox)", sends its code, the host pastes it in a block set to "My friend sends the first code" and sends the answer back, the guest pastes the answer and presses Connect. The link takes `offerer` as an option (`createOnlineLink(role, { offerer })`): the side that makes the first code waits for ever, the side that answers waits only a few seconds in Firefox. The host's `acceptOffer(text, seat)` gives the guest its seat in the answer, and the guest learns it from the answer. Scan works in both directions. A new text `answerWait` says the friend did not answer in time and names the way round. The `guestWait` text now also says "send the first code yourself".
- Review fixes (the Opus review of this task found 8 things; all are fixed, each with a test named `(P12-06 review)` or a new check in a P12-06 test):
  1. A Free Fight start message must carry `teamNames` as a list of at most 8 strings of at most 40 characters (`problemWith`); before, `[null]` passed and the guest threw in `roundSub`.
  2. A guest's Ready and the host's last list belong to one connection (`OnlineUI.forgetLobby`): they are cleared when its link closes or fails, in `makeLink` and in `stopFirst`.
  3. The lobby screens have a layout test at 390 x 844 and 844 x 390 (host with three guests, Remove, the browser text and a guest with no reply; Free Fight; a waiting and a failed seat; the guest lobby; the guest after Remove; Players and teams and the first Free Fight screen with Online friends): no sideways scroll, every control and every part of a row inside the screen, nothing clipped, no two controls on top of each other. It runs only where there is a layout engine (the headless stub skips it); it was not run in a browser by the builder.
  4. The host numbers its settings (`OnlineUI.rev`, raised whenever the mode, the level or the lineup changes). `bplobby` carries `rev`, a guest's `bpme` carries the `rev` of the list it saw (0 before any list, -1 on the wire when absent), and the host takes `ready: true` only for the current `rev`; the list then tells the guest.
  5. A pong that is not a finite time (`bp-pong:abc`, empty, Infinity) is dropped, so `samples` never holds a non-number and the list stays readable.
  6. A guest that misses `ONLINE_MISSED_PINGS` (3) pings in a row shows "no reply" (round trip -2 in the list), Start says that player does not answer, and the next answer clears it.
  7. Remove sends `bp-removed:` first, takes the guest off the list and the seat free at once and closes the link `ONLINE_REMOVE_CLOSE_MS` (250 ms) later so the message can arrive; the guest's screen says the host removed it (`ONLINE_MESSAGES.removed`), not "check the Wi-Fi".
  8. The Firefox-flow test and the new Remove test are deferred tests (`test(name, fn, 10000)`): they run after every other test, and their time limit starts then.
- Re-review fixes (three Low findings, each with a test named `(P12-06 re-review)`): `releaseGuests` takes the guests that `isOpen` (a guest removed a moment before Start is closed with the rest, not handed to the match); the "Player N left." toast is not shown for a guest the host removed; a mode that follows the number of players is part of `lineupSignature`, so a friend who joins or leaves raises the revision and withdraws Ready like a press on the Mode row (a lobby with nobody counts as two players, so the first friend changes nothing).
- The random-walk failure in Chrome ("MENU with the lineup screen", walk 2 step 94; Mode flows P18-40): the walks reach the online lobby only where the browser has WebRTC (the headless runner has none, so they never met it there). The lobby's Lineup button (`onlineup`) opens Players and teams in the menu state, and a walk that pressed it met a state/screen pair the checker did not know. It is a legal pair and not a game fault: the lobby is a menu screen, and moving the game to the fighter-select state would send the screens to Free Fight (`UI.onGameState` resets the screen stack and shows the Free Fight first screen) and drop the lobby; Back from the lineup and from the fighter cards returns to the lobby with its guests. The checker now allows exactly this pair (`lobbyLineupLegal`: the menu state, the `lineup` or `char` screen, an Online screen under it on the screen stack) and nothing else. The walk also showed one real fault: Back from the fighter cards reads `Game.selection.mode`, and with a Tournament left in it went to the Tournament join screen and out of the lobby; `onlineup` now sets the selection to Free Fight, as the Free Fight screens expect. A debug run of 40 walks with a stand-in WebRTC (the lobby reachable) passes; the new test `Mode flows (P12-06 re-review)` replays the path with a Tournament left in the selection.
- Tests: 11 new tests named `(P12-06)`, 5 named `(P12-06 review)` and 4 named `(P12-06 re-review)`: the first code from either side, the message readers and the delay, the host's list, the guest's lobby, Start from the lobby, the lineup row and its saving, the Free Fight start, keyboard / gamepad / touch reach every control, the local fighter, the Firefox guest flow, the lobby after a match; and, from the review, Ready and the list per connection, the settings revision, pongs that are not numbers and the "no reply" guest, Remove with its message, and the phone layout.
- Tests that were edited, each because the behaviour changed on purpose (none weakened, the old checks stay where the old behaviour stays): `Online UI (P12-01, P12-03)` (a connected guest is now a row of the list: its test checks the latency words, Ready and the row, and the code blocks only for the seats that are not connected; the mode and level are rows, `olb:mode` and `olb:arena`, not buttons; the Mode row now passes through Free Fight, so a cycle of three presses comes back to Brawl), `Online UI (P12-03)` Start hands the links over (a guest now says its pick after its browser: two messages, not one), `Online play (P12-03)` the host's buttons (the online lobby is one of them, for a guest too). The stand-in links of the first test got a `send` and the guest blocks a `ready`, `samples` and `fighter`. In the new tests: a lobby message longer than 120 characters is cut, not refused; the tests of the Firefox flow type into the page's boxes through the stub's `getElementById` because `saveFields` reads them there; an async lobby test waits for the earlier async tests (`pendingTests`) because they and the sync tests after them share `OnlineUI` and `Online.createLink` (a sync test runs in the middle of an earlier async one).
- Out of scope, with the reason: custom player names (the task asks for create / join, player list, ready check, mode select and latency; a name needs a field on touch, a message and a place in every screen, and the list says Host and Player N for now) and a guest's view of the bracket and of who is fighting (a bracket for several people on every device is P11-02; a guest sees the fight when it starts and the results after it as before). Both stay on the list of what a later task may add.
- Runs (2026-11-10): after the review fixes the headless Node runner (`node tools/run-tests.js --affected --also "net|online|lobby|menu|P12|Layout"`, which picked 739 tests) gave 722 passed, 17 known headless limits (16 "needs the main menu", 1 "blank faces"), 0 other failures (the layout test is skipped there). The old temp harness (`harness.js`) does not wait for the async tests, so it shows them as "still running"; use the runner. The Chrome run of the whole suite is the coordinator's gate before the merge.
- Size: `breakpoint.html` is 1,448,805 bytes (LF, BOM counted) of 4,000,000; this task adds 40,039 (main 1,408,766 with P18-29).
- Owner device checks for P12-06 (also on the P16-03 list): two phones and a PC on one Wi-Fi: join, pick a fighter, Ready, Start, play a match, Online lobby on the results and go again; a Firefox phone or PC as the guest with the first code from the guest; a pad as the host (arrows on the rows, A on Ready); Remove and a new friend; Free Fight with one Online slot and CPU slots.

- Rejected (cost): real shadow maps (a second render pass and a depth texture, too much for low GPUs); bloom or a post pass or FXAA (one more full-screen pass and render target, plus fill); texture or normal maps (size, and a texture fetch per pixel); per-pixel point lights on low (kept per vertex).

Against the measured baseline (above) that is +3 to 6 percent of the instances on low (183 to 338), +2 to 5 percent on medium (361 to 700), +4 to 7 percent on high (335 to 653); draws stay inside the 6 to 13 of P18-46 (14 to 17 on high only with the soft shadow). A rectangle is the text's width (`POP_CHAR_EM` 0.6 em a letter) by `POP_BOX_EM` (0.9 em) at the pop's own scale: a new pop starts at 1 + `POP_GROW` (1.25) and shrinks to 1 over its 0.95 s, so two new pops (1.25 x 0.9 = 1.125 em) clear each other at one step and an older, smaller one clears a new one too (the first version ignored the start scale and pops touched 1 to 3 px). The live pops are taken where they are now: projected at their height after the rise they have made (`POP_RISE` 0.6 m) minus their lift, so a word that has climbed leaves room below it and two words close on screen, though 0.9 m apart in the world, stack. The text size is `popPx()`, measured once (`getComputedStyle`) and kept with the HUD edge until `popReset()` (a resize, a match start): no style read per hit. The pile may not climb into the HUD: `popHudBottom()` measures the lower edge of `.hud-top`, `#party` and `#modeinfo` once, and an upward step is allowed only while the pop, at the top of its rise, keeps its whole rectangle under that edge; past that the pile continues below the hit (up to `POP_STEPS_DOWN` 3 steps, a negative lift); with no room at all `popAt` ends the oldest pop that is IN THE WAY (one of its column: rectangles overlapping sideways; a world-near one where there is no projection), not the oldest anywhere, and asks again. Every frame `popLayout()` puts the live pops on screen (`sx`, `sy`): a pop whose top has been carried into the HUD by a camera move after it was placed (a hit punches the camera in) gets a drop, and pops of one column are one pile and all take the largest drop (`popSpread`, repeated until no pair differs), so the gaps between them stay and no two meet; the first version gave every pop its own clamp, which put a pile on one line. Placing against natural positions is enough because a pile moves as a whole. With no pop in the HUD a frame costs one projection per live pop (at most 16). Without a projection (behind the camera, headless) the world distance of 0.5 m and the steps taken decide, with no HUD limit. A fighter or object standing on stairs keeps the plane at 0 (the test refuses a plane where the footing under the shadow is not one height, so on stairs it gives 0), and all planar shadows share one stencil bit per pass, so a shadow at 0 and one at 1 m that overlap on screen draw once. Medium has one pass (bit 1); High has two (bits 1 and 2, the soft edge), each pass the same rule. Fixing either would need one stencil value per plane height (a bit per height) or a depth-aware shadow; not built, the overlap needs two shadows at different heights to touch on screen.

### P18-28 sound design pass (2026-11-09)

- Scope: audit and decide only; no game code changed (the fixes are built in BP-P18-29). The task (friend, 2026-11-02): audit every sound (hits, blocks, footsteps, objects, menus, crowd, music), find what is missing, repeats too much or sounds thin, decide the changes. Base: `breakpoint.html` at 520d70c (branch `bp-p18-28-snd`, file unchanged). BP-P18-29 keeps three rules: at most 12 impact voices at once (the oldest stops, P13-01 row 12, built by P13-02), the volume settings still cover every sound (there is no mute setting: a volume at 0 is the mute), and the P0-04 check passes.
- Method (no speakers on this PC, so every statement below rests on a number or on the code, none on listening; the owner's and P16-03's phone check stays the last word):
  1. Read `Sound` (13220), `Music` (13543), `Effects` and `Feel` (13101, 13166), every `Sound.*` call site, `HAZARDS[..].snd`, `MATERIALS`, `WEAPONS` and the 8 `audio` rows of `ARENAS`.
  2. Offline render: Node Playwright (scratch folder `C:\Users\GS\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\bp-snd\`: `lib.mjs`, `render.mjs`, `count.mjs`, `music.mjs`, not committed), Chrome headless, audio unmuted, browser closed in `finally`, `TEMP` / `TMP` set; the game file is served with `page.route` and one line added to the served copy that hands `Sound`, `Music`, `Events`, `SimRunner` and the data tables to the page (the file in the repo is unchanged). Every sound is played through the real `Sound` code and the real `Sound.wire()` handlers (only Sound's handlers are installed, with mock event data) into an `OfflineAudioContext` (44.1 kHz, the real bus chain from `Sound.build()`, arena reverb of the Warehouse 1.7 s and wet 0.3, default volumes master 0.8 and effects 0.9), starting 0.4 s into the context (`suspend` / `resume`; a sound started at t = 0 measured about 10 dB too low, an artefact of the first render quantum, which cost a first and a second run). The game's own music scheduler was held off during the renders (it writes into whatever `Sound.ctx` is). One mono mix of the two channels is analysed.
  3. Numbers per sound: peak and RMS in dBFS of the dry signal (bus gains 1, no reverb, no compressor = what the code asks for) and the peak of the heard chain (default volumes, reverb, compressor); the active length (to -40 dB of the loudest 10 ms); the spectral centroid; the share of energy under 600 Hz / from 600 to 2500 Hz / over 2500 Hz (FFT of the active part; "L/M/H"); the nodes created per play (counted by wrapping the context's `create*`); and repetition over 10 consecutive plays with the real `Math.random` but one shared noise buffer: the mean zero-lag correlation of the waveforms ("same" = 1.000 with no spread; "near" = 0.85 or more: the same waveform with a little noise grain; "grain" = only the noise grain changes: the same filter sweep and envelope every time) and the mean distance of the 6-band, 20 ms spectrogram (dB). A level probe (1 kHz sines of gain 0.01 to 1.4 through the chain) shows the chain is linear for peaks: heard peak = dry peak - 2.9 dB (0.8 x 0.9), because the compressor (threshold -14 dB, ratio 5, attack 4 ms) lets the first 8 ms of a transient through and only lowers the body by about 6 dB at full scale.
  4. How often: `SimRunner.run` (seeded, all CPU, items and hazards on) with Sound's real handlers fed from the events and a virtual clock (the tick), `Sound.tone` / `noise` / `grunt` / `swell` replaced by recorders: 4 duels (Warehouse hard seeds 1 and 2, Dojo expert seed 3, Subway normal seed 4; 3.6 min of play), 2 eight-fighter free-for-alls (Warehouse seed 1, Pit seed 2; 0.9 min: the matches ended fast) and one brawl of the player and 6 CPU enemies (Garage seed 3, 0.9 min). It gives events, calls the 35 ms to 90 ms gaps let through or refuse, sources per minute and the peak number of live sources. CPU against CPU fights more than people do, so the rates are an upper bound for a duel; the heartbeat and the menu are not in it.
  5. Music: 4 bars (64 steps) of the menu, fight and tense layers of 4 arena tracks rendered the same way, and a tier 2 hit played into the fight music at three beats (on the kick, on the snare, off beat) with and without the music, to see whether the music hides or squeezes the hit.

#### What the sound engine is today (read)

- Buses: every `tone`, `noise`, `grunt` and `swell` source goes through `sfxBus` (gain = Effects volume), which feeds a dry path and an always-on `ConvolverNode` (the arena's `audio.reverb` 0.4 to 2.4 s stereo IR, wet 0.1 to 0.36); `Music` goes through `musicBus` (gain = Music volume x 0.55) and a low-pass (20 kHz; 1.2 kHz under the heartbeat; 700 Hz paused); both meet in `master` (Master volume), then one `DynamicsCompressor` (threshold -14 dB, ratio 5, attack 4 ms, release 0.18 s) and the destination. Nothing else reaches the destination (the silent one-sample unlock buffer aside), so a volume at 0 mutes every sound: the rule BP-P18-29 must keep. There is no separate bus for the menu, no limiter, no distance falloff and no pan relative to the camera (`panFor` uses the world x of the arena, at most 0.6).
- Voices: `MAX_VOICES` 30 sources at once (a new sound is refused above it; `tone` and `noise` stop at 42), a global gap per sound name (`MIN_GAP`: hit 35 ms, block 40, whoosh 50, step 90, debris 45, grunt 200 per fighter index, objHit 50, menu 30, land 80), no priority (a footstep can take the slot a hit needs), one `StereoPannerNode` per source when off centre, at most 12 layered impact sources (P13-02).
- Calls and rates measured (per minute of play, all CPU): a duel has 55 hits, 74 whooshes (attackActive), 85 footsteps, 11 blocks, 5 landings and 3 knockdowns; an eight-fighter free-for-all 210 hits (3.5 a second), 229 whooshes, 197 footsteps, 75 debris landings, 30 landings; a 7-fighter brawl 522 footsteps. Sources created per minute: 607 in a duel (10 a second), 2,114 in an eight-fighter free-for-all (35 a second), 749 in the brawl; the hit events alone are 54 % and 57 % of them in the duels and the free-for-alls (5.4 to 5.9 sources, 10 to 27 nodes per hit). The peak number of live sources is 16 to 19 in a duel and 45 and 51 in the eight-fighter fights, 24 in the brawl: over the cap of 30, where the engine refuses sounds without any priority. The gaps refuse 14 of 85 footsteps a minute in a duel and 251 of 522 in the brawl, 48 of 242 whooshes and 23 of 210 hits (11 %: a landed hit with no sound at all) in the free-for-alls, 30 of 75 debris landings.

#### Findings (the top problems, each with its number)

1. **The hardest hits clip and the quiet sounds vanish: a 40 dB spread.** Heard peaks at the default volumes: tier 2 hit +0.3, tier 3 +1.9, counter +1.2, KO +2.0, bat +2.2, pipe +2.4, bottle +1.9 dBFS (full scale is 0: seven of the 14 hit rows are over it and the output hard-clips; at master and effects 1.0 they are 2.9 dB hotter); the big glass break is +0.5 dry, the falling load -1.1. At the other end: footsteps -38 (walk) and -32 (run), whooshes -33 to -26, debris -21 to -33, menu blips -24 to -21. There is no limiter, and the compressor's 4 ms attack does not catch the transient.
2. **Every hit is a bass thump.** 93 to 98 % of the energy of every hit row is under 600 Hz (70 to 90 % under 150 Hz; centroid 170 to 340 Hz, the bottle 790), 1 to 2 % between 0.6 and 2.5 kHz, 1 to 6 % above: the layers P13-02 added (slap, snap, crack) lift the share over 2.5 kHz to 1 to 2 % only. Slam, landing, throw, boost, tackle hit and heartbeat are 96 to 100 % under 150 Hz (centroids 59 to 114 Hz), the clinch 92 %. A phone or laptop speaker plays almost nothing under 200 Hz: on those the body of an impact is missing and the heartbeat, the landing and the slam are close to silent. The fight music is the same: 90 to 92 % of its energy is under 150 Hz (centroid 148 to 171 Hz).
3. **Sounds repeat exactly.** Over 10 plays: grunts, menu sounds, countdown, FIGHT, time warning, fanfares, bell, escape, boost, the late / free / stamina cues, heartbeat, the alarm and the zap, train and load warnings are bit-identical (corr 1.000, spectrogram distance 0); hits, blocks, slam, landing, clinch, creak, pick-up, wood and concrete objects, hazard hurt are "near" (0.88 to 0.99: the same waveform, the noise grain only; peak spread 1 to 3 dB, centroid spread under 25 Hz, the bottle 62); whooshes, steps, debris, hiss, fire and the "other" and glass recipes are pure noise through the same filter sweep (the grain differs, the sound does not). Only metal (partials +-5 %) and the glass pings vary the pitch. No sound varies in pitch, level or length from play to play, and the sound a hit makes does not change along a combo. At 3.5 hits a second in a brawl and 1.4 steps a second in a duel this is the machine-gun effect.
4. **Six different events share one slam, one block, one whoosh, one footstep.** `slam` serves knockdown, KO, wall slam, object impact, tackle hit and the throw (which slams at the release, while the body is still in the air, and again on landing). `whoosh` serves every strike (fist, kick, bat), the jump, the sidestep and every throw. `step` serves 8 floors (concrete, planks, tar, tile, mud, club floor), both feet and 8 fighters. `block` serves a high guard, a low guard, a fist and a pipe. The brawl has two fighter voices for 8 bodies (index 0 and everyone else).
5. **The sound is not placed.** A fighter 14 m off in a brawl is as loud as the one at the camera; pan is the arena x, not the screen; no priority (a footstep refuses a hit above 30 sources); the global gaps drop the nearest fighter's step or an 11 % share of hits.
6. **Missing sounds** (the list below has 14): per-surface footsteps and landings, cloth and weapon whooshes, a block that depends on the guard, a throw release that is not a slam, breaks for cardboard, plastic, tile and brick, crowd reactions (the crowd leans and cheers on screen in silence), ambience (the `audio.hum` value of 4 of the 8 levels, 40 to 60 Hz, is data nobody plays), a menu with start, pause, toggle and slider sounds, round start and KO stingers, breathing (row 8 of P13-01 is drawn only), fighter voices.
7. **The menu is quiet and undifferentiated, the cues weak.** All four menu sounds sit within 3 dB (-24 to -21 dBFS) and 24 dB under a hit; every confirm is the same two notes; the menu theme (RMS -49 dBFS) is 15 dB under the fight music (-34): at the default volumes the menu is nearly silent. The countdown beeps are three identical notes at -17; there is no stinger for a round start, a round-ending KO or time up; the `uiSound` event handler has no emitter (dead code).
8. **Music.** The fight bed is kick and bass: 91 % of the energy under 150 Hz, 7.5 % from 150 to 600 Hz and 1 % above (arpeggio, snare and hats together). All 8 levels play the same drum and bass patterns (only bpm 96 to 124, root 49 to 73 Hz and the scale differ); the drums repeat every bar, the bass and arpeggio every 12 bars (bar 1 against bar 3 correlate 0.55 to 0.83). The heartbeat muffle (low-pass 1.2 kHz) removes less than 1 % of the music's energy, so it is hardly audible today. The music does not hide a hit by level (a tier 2 hit measured -17.2 dB RMS alone and -17.2 with the music, music -30), but they share the 40 to 150 Hz band (music 96 %, hit 74 %) and the master compressor sees the sum.

Result: the hit is 12 to 13 dB above the music in RMS and loses at most 0.3 dB inside it: no pumping and no masking by level. The overlap is in the band (both low), so the decision is not to turn the music down but to move the hit up into the mids (E1) and to give the music mids of its own (E8).
#### Engine decisions (E), what BP-P18-29 builds under the sounds above

| # | Decision | How | Bus, voices, cost | Why (number) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Bake the impacts | `Sound.bake()` renders the impact family once with an `OfflineAudioContext` (mono, 32 kHz) the first time the context runs, in 3 idle steps of 12 buffers (`requestIdleCallback`, else `setTimeout`): 27 impact buffers (tier 1 / 2 / 3, 0.20 / 0.28 / 0.40 s, x 3 weight bands 0 to 1 / 2 / 3 to 4 x 3 variants) and 9 material layers (wood, metal, glass x 3, 0.3 s) = 10.6 s of audio, about 1.4 MB (Float32). Each impact is built from the same recipe code as today (so there is one recipe: `Sound.ctx` and the buses are pointed at a throw-away offline graph while it renders, as the harness does) with three parts: the sub thud 55 to 110 Hz (-3 dB), a pitched knock (sine or triangle 220 to 520 Hz falling in 0.08 s, lower for heavier bodies) and a crack (bandpass noise 2.5 to 5 kHz, 8 to 15 ms, gain 0.35 / 0.5 / 0.7 of the thud by tier); tier 3 keeps the 700 to 200 Hz tail. Target spectrum low / mid / high 40 / 40 / 20 % (now 98 / 1 / 1). Played by `Sound.impact(e)`: the next of the 3 variants (never the same twice in a row), `playbackRate` = kick 0.82 x combo ladder (+1 semitone per hit of the combo, to +6, from `e.combo`) x (1 +- 0.05), gain = tier x (1 +- 1 dB) x distance (E5). The old synthesis stays as the fallback while the bake is not ready, where `OfflineAudioContext` does not exist, and if it throws | Effects bus, impact priority; 1 source + 1 gain per impact (about 3 nodes with the shared panner) against 4 to 7 sources (10 to 27 nodes) now; it counts in `layerQ`, so the 12-voice cap holds and now means 12 impacts instead of about 4 | 54 to 57 % of all sources, 10 to 27 nodes per hit, 98 % bass, same waveform every time; estimate after: sources a minute 607 to about 370 in a duel, 2,114 to about 1,250 in an eight-fighter fight (estimate: 1.6 sources per hit instead of 5.7) |
| E2 | Variation on every play | One helper `Sound.vary(value, spread)` (uniform +-spread from `Math.random`, never the sim's `simRng`, so sound never changes a fight or an online checksum) used by every recipe that is not a cue: pitch +-5 to 8 %, level +-1 dB, length +-8 %; the baked impacts round-robin; the P18-04 cue notes, the countdown, the bell and the fanfares stay exact; the menu "move" +-3 % | none (no extra nodes) | 27 of the 88 sounds are bit-identical, 31 more are the same waveform with a little noise grain, and 30 are noise through one fixed filter sweep and envelope (only the grain differs) |
| E3 | Priorities and fair gaps | `allow(name, gap, priority)`: priority 0 (impacts, KO, guard break, cues, stingers, countdown) up to the 30 sources of today; priority 1 (whoosh, grunt, block, land, items, hazards) refused at 24 live; priority 2 (steps, debris, creak, crowd murmur, breathing, crackle) refused at 16. The gap of `step`, `whoosh` and `grunt` is kept per fighter (`name + index`), the hit gap goes from 35 to 20 ms per defender | 0 | 45 to 51 live sources in the eight-fighter fights against the cap 30; 48 % of brawl footsteps and 11 % of free-for-all hits refused by global gaps |
| E4 | A UI bus | `uiBus` (gain = Effects volume) straight into `master`, no reverb; used by `Sound.ui`, the countdown, the time warning and the stingers; `applyVolumes` sets it; `Sound.build` connects it | +1 gain node | menu sounds ring through a 0.4 to 2.4 s room; they need their own level |
| E5 | Place the sound | `Sound.place(x, z)` returns { gain, pan } from `Camera.target` and `Camera.dirRight`: gain 1 at the camera focus falling to 0.5 at 14 m, pan = the offset along the camera's right vector over 7 m x 0.6; one `StereoPannerNode` per event passed to `tone` / `noise` as `dest` (not one per source); used by every world sound, not by the menu, the own-seat cues or the music | 1 hypot per event; -(n-1) panner nodes per event | no distance falloff today; pan from the arena x |
| E6 | Low end that survives a phone speaker | An octave-up partial (triangle, -6 dB, 0.6 x the length) on slam, landing, throw landing, boost wind-up and clinch; the heartbeat gets 124 / 110 Hz triangle partials and a 400 Hz tick | +1 source on each; 0 on the others | 96 to 100 % of their energy under 150 Hz; the heartbeat 99.9 % |
| E7 | Ambience bed | Started by `startMatchMusic`, stopped by `Music.stop`: an oscillator at the level's `audio.hum` Hz (60 / 0 / 40 / 0 / 55 / 50 / 0 / 0 for Warehouse, Dojo, Pit, Rooftop, Subway, Garage, Construction, Club; 0 = none) and its 2nd harmonic at -12 dB, and one looped noise through a low-pass or band by level (Warehouse 400 Hz, Dojo 500, Pit 250 boiler, Rooftop 700 wind, Subway 350, Garage 300, Construction 600, Club 200); level -48 dBFS RMS | On `musicBus` (the Music volume covers it and the heartbeat muffle and the pause duck apply to it); 2 to 3 sources, 5 to 8 nodes, always on | `audio.hum` is defined for 4 levels and never played |
| E8 | Music | Per-level kit: 3 drum patterns and 3 bass lines chosen by the arena index (data, 0 nodes); an octave-up bass partial (square, 50 %, low-pass 900 Hz) and the arpeggio +8 dB, so the fight bed reaches about 60 / 30 / 10 % low / mid / high (now 91 / 8 / 1); the menu theme +12 dB (RMS -49 to -37); tense: the octave bass at 0.12, a rising noise sweep every 4 bars, the step length 4 % shorter; the music bus ducks 3 dB for 120 ms on a tier 3 hit (a `gain` ramp, 0 nodes; the music gets louder in the mids, so it must make room for the hit) | `musicBus`; +2 sources fight, +1 tense | one pattern set for 8 levels; the music is bass only; the menu is nearly silent |

| Light impact | tier 1, kick tier 1 (a kick is the punch of its tier +1 dB, tier 3 capped at -2) | -7.2 to -4.0 | -10 to -9 |
| Defence | plain block / guard break / perfect cue / sway cue | -7.4 / -8.3 / -5.4 / -12.9 | -10 / -6 / -8 / -12 |
| Voices | grunts and the new hurt, effort and KO voices | -22 | -14 |
| Whoosh | tier 1 / 2 / 3, jump | -30.5 / -30.0 / -25.7, -32.9 | -24 / -20 / -16, -24 |
| Footsteps and landings | walk, run, landing, hard landing | -38.4, -32.4, -16.6, -12.6 | -34, -30, -16, -12 |
| Debris and items | debris glass / metal / wood / concrete, pick-up, spray | -21 / -25 / -27 / -33, -20, -10 | -20 all, -16, -14 |
| Small object hits | wood, concrete, metal, glass, other | -12.4, -10.0, -12.8, -7.8, -11.8 | -12 (+-2) |
| Hazards | warnings, starts, hurts | warn -28 to -15, start -23 to -1, hurt -21 to -6 | warn -14, start -8 to -4, hurt -16 |
| Menu | move / confirm / back / refused / start | -23.7 / -20.9 / -22.6 / -21.4 / none | -20 / -16 / -18 / -16 / -12 |
| Cues | countdown / FIGHT / time warning / bell / fanfare / late / free tick / low stamina / heartbeat | -17.2 / -11.7 / -18.3 / -8.7 / -15.5 / -23.6 / -25.6 / -21.1 / -10.7 | -14 / -8 / -14 / -8 / -12 / -16 / -24 / -18 / -14 (with the partials) |
