Buses after the change: `sfxBus` (Effects volume; world sounds; reverb send as now) and `uiBus` (Effects volume; no reverb) and `musicBus` (Music volume x 0.55; the music, the ambience and the murmur) all into `master` (Master volume), then the compressor (unchanged: threshold -14 dB, ratio 5, attack 4 ms, release 0.18 s), then the limiter, then the destination. Nothing else connects to the destination. There is no mute setting and none is added: a volume at 0 mutes its bus (the owner can ask for a Mute button; it would be one `master` gain). Reverb: unchanged (the IR of up to 2.4 s stereo is the largest standing audio cost; the P0-04 check below decides whether the Garage's 2.4 s is cut to 1.6 s).

#### What BP-P18-29 must build and show

- Order, lowest risk first; after each step the harness (the method above; copy the scratch folder) is run again and the numbers of the step are put into this section as "built" lines:
  1. Numbers only: the level plan (gain constants), the limiter (E9), priorities and per-fighter gaps (E3), the dead handler (E10). Gate: no sound over -1 dBFS, every sound in the table within +-2 dB of its target, the 12-voice test still passes.
  2. Variation (E2) and the combo ladder, the UI bus and the new menu sounds (E4, M9), the stingers (M10).
  3. Footsteps, falls and landings by surface (M1, M2), the throw release (M4), the whooshes (M3), the block by guard (M5), voices (M12), breathing (M11), get-up and ring-out (M13), wave horn (M14).
  4. Materials and hazards (M6 and the hazard rows), the partials (E6).
  5. Crowd and ambience (M7, E7), music (E8).
  6. The bake (E1) and the placement (E5) last, with the fallback kept and tested. The bake is the biggest change: if its main-thread cost or memory fails the check below, ship every other step and keep the synthesis for impacts, with E2 and the level plan applied to it.
- Tests to add (names; none may skip, weaken or delete an older one; the P13-02 test `Layered impact sound` moves to the baked sources and keeps its assertions: thud order by weight, one sound per tier, the material layer, the swell, the cap of 12 with 20 hits):
  1. `Sound levels (P18-29): every sound of the table peaks within 2 dB of its target and under -1 dBFS` (offline render, as the harness; Chrome only, one more of the known headless limits).
  2. `Sound variation (P18-29): two plays of a hit, block, step and whoosh differ in at least two parameters, a P18-04 cue never differs` (recorded `tone` / `noise` arguments, runs headless).
  3. `Sound surfaces (P18-29): every level has a footstep recipe and the 6 recipes differ in filter centre or length` (data).
  4. `Sound voices (P18-29): at 28 live sources a step is refused and a hit plays; a baked impact is one voice; the gap is per fighter` (stand-in engine, headless).
  5. `Sound buses (P18-29): every source connects to the sfx, UI or music bus; with master, effects or music at 0 the matching sounds render silent` (offline render, covers every row of the tables; Chrome only).
  6. `Sound bake (P18-29): the buffers exist after unlock, a failed bake plays the synthesis, no bake without OfflineAudioContext` (headless with a stand-in).
  7. `Sound place (P18-29): a sound 14 m from the camera is 6 dB down; pan follows the camera; one panner per event`.
  8. `Cues (P18-04)` gets the new cue sets (countdown notes, milestone notes, stingers) in its "no two outcomes share a note set" check.
  9. The existing determinism test `viewer settings, clocks and Math.random never change the simulation` stays unchanged and must pass (sound reads the sim, writes nothing).
- The P0-04 check, as in P13-02 (Playwright Chrome, 640x360, CPU throttle 4, saved setting `quality: low`, `BREAKPOINT.benchmark(10)`, warehouse, two Expert CPU fighters, five runs of the merge base and five of the branch alternated, pass rule frame p95 <= 18 ms and work p95 <= 8 ms) with three additions: the audio must run (a headless run with no user gesture never creates `Sound.ctx`, and then every Sound handler returns at `ready()`: the P13-02 numbers say nothing about sound unless that run clicked the page, and its notes do not say; click the page first, start Chrome with `--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required` and assert `Sound.ctx.state === 'running'` and `Sound.voices > 0` during the run); the time spent inside the Sound handlers per frame (a wrapper around the `Sound.wire` handlers, p50 / p95; budget p95 <= 0.3 ms at throttle 4); and an audio-load test: record every Sound call of the seeded 8-fighter free-for-all of this section (the Warehouse run) with its time, replay it into an `OfflineAudioContext` for 30 s and report render time / 30 s before and after (it must not rise; expected about 40 % less) plus the peak live sources (at most 30). Also measure the bake: wall time on the throttled page (budget 1.5 s, no frame over 50 ms while it runs), memory (1.4 MB expected).
- Size: expect about +18,000 bytes in `breakpoint.html` (of the 4,000,000 budget) and about +45,000 in `breakpoint-tests.js`; the docs: this section gets the "built" lines, `README` is unchanged (no setting, script or setup changes).
- Not decided here, for the owner and for P16-03 (ears and a real phone): whether the targets feel right on a real phone speaker and on headphones, the heartbeat's audibility, the bake time on a real phone and on Safari (older Safari has only `webkitOfflineAudioContext`: the bake needs the same prefix fallback as `AudioContext` and the synthesis fallback where neither exists), the compressor on Firefox and Safari (the numbers are Chrome's), and the Garage's 2.4 s reverb cost on a low-end phone.
- Decisions (the owner can change each): no new setting and no Mute button (the three volumes cover every sound; the menu sounds follow Effects, the ambience and crowd murmur follow Music); the code-made baked buffers keep "no sound files"; the sway stays silent; hits stay the loudest sound, but under full scale; the cue notes of P18-04 stay exact.
- Lessons for whoever re-runs the harness: a sound started at t = 0 of an offline context measures about 10 dB low (start at 0.4 s with `suspend`); the game's own `Music.update` writes into whatever `Sound.ctx` is (set `Music.active = false` while rendering); `Sound.voices` drops back to 0 when the render ends (read it right after the call); only `Sound`'s handlers must be installed (swap `Events.handlers`) or the other listeners fire with mock data.

### P17-10 built: distinct styles

- Built to the P17-09 decision ("P17-09 distinct styles decided", above): every style has strike moves nobody else plays, and two styles play the same move only where the share list says so. **Built, per-pair balance pending BP-P14-04** (the P17-10 task stops at a coarse screen; the per-pair work at all four difficulties is BP-P14-03 and BP-P14-04, whose runner is saved in `Breakpoint/docs/p17-10-runner/` of the handoffs repo). Base: `main` at b65f60f (P18-01 in) when the work began; `main` at d1b51e0 (P12-03, P18-31, P18-55, P18-57, P18-66 in) was merged in before the review fixes. The Opus review of the first full build found 12 points; where each went is in "Review findings" at the end. Owner can change any pick; the deviations from the written decision are in the table after it.
- What changed in `breakpoint.html` (+35,917 LF bytes against main caa448d, 1,514,034 in all, `breakpoint-tests.js` +40,516; the budget is 4,000,000, so the 30 KB gate of DECIDE 11 is met many times over and no optimization list or split was needed):
  - Engine: `variant()` rows, `SKINS` + `moveFor()` (one cached clone per style and row, same `id`), `ANIM_SPECS` (animations as data, `STRIKE_BUILDERS[name]` built at load; a name used on rows of different heights or limbs names a base per row id or height), `animKey`, the spec keys `pitch`, `brol`, `yaw`, `rdrop`, `STRIKE_ROLL`, the `plant` row flag with `PLANT_SPEED_MOVE` (6 m/s), the `duck` row flag in `Combat.evaluate`, the `strings` position parser (`tableFromPositions`, `STRING_POSITIONS`), the `aiw` weights in `pickMove` and `thinkChain`, `legless` with `Fighter.rowStyle` (a legless style with its arms full, an item or a crate, plays the shared leg rows for its Kick steps, air moves and counters, never its arm versions of them), `THROW_SKINS` with a carry key, `CLINCH_NAMES`, and the stance retune. `STYLE_STRINGS`, `rowsFrom` and the `moves` field of the style rows are gone.

The old single-owner tests ("the new moves have frame data ... of their own style only", "each style with attacks of its own uses them in AI matches") are replaced by them; the other older tests that named the old default rows now read each fighter's own table (Gamepad / Touch / Keyboard string rows and Auto-assist read KAI's table, the Training dummy is a fighter with a Low crouch Kick, Items Kick strings read the Kickboxing table, Throws reads KAI's cell names, Ground submissions counts 6 holds, Creator cosmetics uses one style, the P18-03 links test reads all 16 tables (up to 8 skipped pairs as before; its harness holds the foe at the spacing while a strong first step is followed), the CPU-levels test runs 2000 ticks instead of 1400).

**Hit check and the animations** (no browser: the 59 animation specs were fitted numerically, not drawn by eye)

- Method: every spec started from a hand-written offset list on its base builder; a coordinate-descent fitter (scratch, not kept) moved the spec numbers in steps of 0.4, 0.2, 0.1 and 0.05 rad, with a small cost on every change, until all uses of the animation passed the P17-02 hit check limits (short 0.1, side 0.45, band 0.05, past 0.15 m, 0.015 m of margin), the "Calm poses" joint maxima (3 per cent margin) and the floor rule (no foot below -0.02 m on any tick of a move), on every preset of the style plus KAI's body. Whatever the fitter moved is in the `ANIM_SPECS` line of the animation. The poses therefore are numerically right and **have not been looked at**: some specs carry larger offsets than a hand-made pose would (`boot` hip abduction -1.0, `footSweep` base leg 0.4/0.1/-0.55). Owner device check: look at the 59 animations in the creator preview before the next playtest.
- Context rows: a builder name on a row of another height uses the same look at that height (`HEIGHT_ANIM`: `straight` on a Mid counter is the body punch, `low` on a Mid counter is the front kick), so the identity stays `counter_strike@straight`.
- Round kicks keep the pivot of the round kick when they are derived (`ROUND_KICKS`, `STRAIGHT_KICKS` read the base builder); `techFor` hands a derived animation the style's technique of its base builder.
- Hit check test: the row count dropped from 594 to 500 pairs (Boxing has no Low rows and the grapplers no High ones, so their tables repeat rows); its floor is 480. The eleven-row test "each new move's pose differs from the standard move it resembles" (0.3 rad) and the 0.5 rad gap between the four old hold poses (Wrestling, Sambo, BJJ, Hapkido) are back in `Styles: stance and signature moves ...` and `Styles: Sambo and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu have throws of their own, every hold style has the hold pose ...` (Judo and MMA have their own hold poses since P17-10 and are no longer asserted equal to Wrestling and BJJ). **Note for BP-P18-58 (contact sheets):** five of the new animations sit within 0.3 rad of their base builder and are the first to look at: `switchKick` 0.15, `kravStomp` 0.20, `crescent` 0.25, `shove` 0.30, `hammer` 0.30 (they are skins, so the eleven-row test does not cover them). Technique nudges needed by the stance retune and the new tables: Karate hikite elbow 0.75 > 0.65, Muay Thai off-hand 0.7 > 0.64, Sambo punch lean 0.15 > 0.05, Wrestling punch drop 0 > 0.15 and lean 0.1 > 0.25, Kali punch drop 0 > 0.1, Kickboxing and MMA `teep` leg +0.15, Kickboxing guard width 0.01 > 0 (the clothes test "hem cuts the thigh" failed at 0.01; the guard distance is 0.397 / 0.150 with it, from 0.399 / 0.150).
- Sway pose test (P3-11): a style with no strike of a height (Boxing: no Low strike; the grapplers: no High one) has nothing to check there; the longest strike of a height is a different row for some styles. The clearance of the new rows is fitted into the animations, not excused: the specs of the Boxing Body Hook (`bodyHook`), the Wrestling and BJJ Snap Down (`snapDown`), the BJJ Guard Kick (`guardKick`), the Hapkido Palm (`palm`), the Muay Thai Heavy Shin Kick (`STYLE_TECH.muaythai.roundThai`), the Krav Maga Parry Strike (`STYLE_TECH.kravmaga.parry`), the Kali Thrust (`thrustK`) and the Krav Maga Jab (`STYLE_TECH.kravmaga.straight`) were fitted with `fitsway.js` (saved with the runner), next to the fits of the first build (Karate, Judo, Brawler, Capoeira, Boxing body jab, MMA rows). The 34 floors of the earlier build are gone. Five floors (`shortSlips`) are left, all for the Jab row where the fitter stops: the Kali Thrust (Angle 1 and the Long Thrust are High strikes of Kali too, but the Thrust is the first of the longest the test picks) and the Krav Maga Jab (the only High strike of its table) are 5-frame, 1.4 m jabs, and a jab that goes active on the last i-frame tick passes the head or the torso up to 0.04 m short of the 0.32 / 0.35 bar whatever the spec does (floor = measured clearance minus 0.01). Four of the five are side slips; `kravmaga jab 0` is a straight-back sway, 0.005 m short of the torso bar. **Root cause, a note for BP-P18-58 and BP-P18-59:** the shared 5-frame Jab row against the P17-03 sway pose (the re-review measured that the jab of every style falls short on a side slip; the other styles' longest High strike is a slower row that passes). The real fix is the jab's startup or the sway pose, not another animation fit. The stance test (lowest foot within -0.03 m) and the Technique tests (only the keys `STYLE_TECH` allows; no foot lower than the plain pose by more than 0.05 m on any row of any style) constrain the fits too, which the fitter does not check: they are run after it.

### P18-29 sound design built (2026-11-10)

- Scope: BP-P18-29 builds the P18-28 pass (E1 to E10, M1 to M14, the level plan, the tests of "What BP-P18-29 must build and show") in `breakpoint.html` and `breakpoint-tests.js`. Branch `bp-p18-29-snd` from main b923c72; no setting, script, dependency or file was added, `README` is unchanged. The three rules hold: at most 12 impact voices (`HIT_LAYER_VOICES`, the oldest stops; a baked impact is one voice, so 12 now means 12 impacts), the three volumes still cover every sound (the render test sets master, effects or music to 0 and every row of the table goes silent; there is still no Mute button), and the performance check ran with the audio running (below).
- Method: the P18-28 harness (offline render of every row, one `OfflineAudioContext` per sound, the sound started 0.4 s in), the live `AudioContext` through a script tap after the limiter, the seeded event recorder, and Playwright Chrome (unmuted, `--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required`, TEMP in the browser-profiles folder, closed in `finally`). No speakers were used: every statement rests on a number or the code; the owner's ears and a real phone (P16-03) stay the last word.

#### E decisions: what was built

- **E1 bake.** `Sound.bakeRender` renders 60 buffers once with an `OfflineAudioContext` (mono, 32 kHz; 44.1 kHz where only the prefixed `webkitOfflineAudioContext` exists, see review finding 8) in 5 idle steps of 12 (`requestIdleCallback`, else `setTimeout`): 27 impacts (tier 1 / 2 / 3 of 0.20 / 0.28 / 0.40 s, x 3 weight bands, x 3 variants), 9 material layers (wood, metal, glass x 3, 0.3 s) and, after the Opus review, 24 footsteps (6 surfaces x walk and run x 2 feet, 0.12 s; "Review fixes" below). The recipe is `impactParts` / `materialParts` / `footParts`, one set of parts that the live synthesis (`Sound.material`, `Sound.footfall`) and the bake both play through the same two node builders (`toneNode`, `noiseNode`). An impact is a sub thud, a pitched knock (triangle), a mid body (bandpass noise 1.4 kHz down to 800 Hz) and a crack (bandpass noise 3 to 4.8 kHz), tier 3 with the old 700 to 200 Hz tail; tuned offline to 39 / 37 / 24 % under 600 Hz / 600 Hz to 2.5 kHz / over 2.5 kHz (it was 98 / 1 / 1). Each buffer is normalised to full scale; the level plan sets the loudness at playback (`IMPACT_DB` + the weight band + `IMPACT_TRIM_DB`, the part the master compressor takes off). `Sound.impact(e)` plays one source and one gain per hit: the next of the 3 variants (never the same twice running), pitch = kick 0.82 x the combo ladder (+1 semitone a hit to +6) x 1 +- 5 %, level +-1 dB, through `layer()` (the cap of 12). The old synthesis (`hit` + `layers`, with the level plan and E2) plays while the bank is not ready, where `OfflineAudioContext` (or the prefixed one) is missing, and if a step throws (`bakeFail`, a Diag line). Fix found by the full headless run: `bake()` keeps the context it started with and a throw inside a render step now reaches `bakeFail` (it was an unhandled rejection that stopped the headless run when a test had put `Sound.ctx` back to null).
- **E2 variation.** `Sound.vary(value, spread)` (Math.random only, never the simulation's random numbers) in every recipe that is not a cue: pitch +-5 to 8 %, length +-8 %, level +-1 dB. Exact on purpose: the P18-04 notes (perfect, break-through, ting, late, free), the countdown, the FIGHT chord, the milestones, bell, fanfares and stingers. The menu "move" moves +-3 %.
- **E3 priorities and gaps.** `allow(name, gap, priority)`: priority 0 up to 30 live sources (impacts, KO, guard break, cues, stingers), 1 refused at 24 (whoosh, voices, blocks, land, items, hazards), 2 refused at 16 (steps, debris, creak, crowd, breath, crackle, alarm); the gaps of step, whoosh, voice and hit are per fighter (`'step' + index`), the hit gap 20 ms per defender (35 ms global before).
- **E4 UI bus.** `uiBus` (gain = Effects volume) into `master`, no reverb: `Sound.ui`, the countdown and FIGHT, the time warning, the stingers, bell, fanfares and the wave horn.
- **E5 placement.** `Sound.place(x, z)` = { gain, pan } from `Camera.target` and `Camera.dirRight` (gain 1 to 0.5 at 14 m, pan = the offset along the right vector over 7 m x 0.6); `Sound.at(x, z)` sets it for the event the handler plays; `tone`, `noise`, `swellNoise`, `voiced` and `playBuffer` scale by it and share ONE panner per event (`out()`); the menu, the own-seat cues and the music have no place. Found by the level test (see "The 3 to 6 dB gap" below): a placed sound now always gets its panner (`panner(pan, true)`); before, a sound at pan exactly 0 skipped it and was 3 dB louder than the same sound a hair off centre.
- **E6 partials.** An octave-up triangle on the landing and the body fall, the clinch grip (240 Hz), the boost wind-up (a second rising triangle); the heartbeat plays a periodic wave (sine + octave + fifth) in the same two tone calls (a test pins 2 per beat) plus a 400 Hz tick. Deviation: the slam is the body fall by weight band, so the partial sits on `fall` and `land`.
- **E7 ambience.** `Sound.syncAmbience(track)` (each frame from `Music.update`, and from `Music.stop`): the level's `audio.hum` and its 2nd harmonic, a looped noise through a low-pass by level (`AMBIENCE_HZ`), a second noise bed where a crowd stands; fade in 0.5 s, on `musicBus` (the Music volume, the heartbeat muffle and the pause duck cover it). 3 to 4 sources, not counted in `Sound.voices` (not transient).
- **E8 music.** `musicFor` carries `floor` and `hum`; three drum kits and three bass lines by level (`DRUM_KITS`, `BASS_LINES`: the 8 levels get 8 different pairs); the kick and the saw bass scale with the level's root (`lowK`, 0.7 to 1.4: a low root gets less, so every level has about the same share under 150 Hz); an octave-up square bass, a pad on the third in the mids, the arpeggio +8 dB, the menu theme +12 dB with the arpeggio on two voices an octave apart; the fight bed has its own level (`FIGHT_GAIN` 1.15) and the tense layer is `TENSE_LIFT` 1.26 (+2 dB) over it as a whole, with its octave bass at 0.12, off-beat hats, a rising noise sweep every 4 bars (a looping noise source) and a 4 % shorter step; `Sound.pump()` ducks the music bus 3 dB for 120 ms on a tier 3 hit or a KO (a gain ramp). Measured below.
- **E9 limiter and level plan.** A second `DynamicsCompressor` after the first (threshold -3 dB, knee 0, ratio 20, attack 1 ms, release 0.1 s); every gain constant moved to the mix plan (`HEARD_TRIM_DB` for master 0.8 x effects 0.9).
- **E10.** The `uiSound` handler is gone. Also removed: the `tab` menu kind (no screen has tabs).

#### M items: what was built

- **M1** six footstep recipes by `env.floor` (`STEP_SURFACES`, `FLOOR_SURFACE`; concrete for Warehouse, Pit and Garage, wood Dojo, gravel Rooftop, tile Subway, dirt Construction, club Night Club), left foot 1.0 and right 0.93 pitch (`stepIndex & 1`), +-10 % pitch, run 1.6 x gain and 0.8 x length (the brief said 1.3 x gain; 1.6 puts the run at -30 dBFS; dirt and club have their own run factors, 2.8 and 2, because a low-passed noise gets no louder from a shorter burst). Once the bank is ready a step is one baked buffer, one source and one gain (finding 2 below); the recipes above are what the bake and the synthesis fallback both play.
- **M2** `Sound.fall(f)`: body sine by weight band (0.3 / 0.38 / 0.46 s), the octave partial, the floor's footfall at 3 x gain; `land` the same smaller (its level follows the impact to the power 1.5, so a soft landing falls off faster than a hard one) with a cloth rustle. A KO plays `fall` at +1 dB; a wall slam is the tier 3 baked impact plus a rattle; an object impact (`envImpact`) plays the object's material.
- **M3** whooshes by move: cloth (tiers 1 and 2 and any other), kick, weapon whistle (Q 3, the centre from the item's `len`), jump (flap + the floor's push-off).
- **M4** the throw release is a cry only (`grunt(att, 'effort')`; the whoosh is `throwStart`, the landing is the fall); grip = a cloth tick + thud + partial; submission = lock + creak; boost = rising sine and triangle + a noise swell.
- **M5** block by guard (a low guard is a 95 Hz thud, tier scales gain 0.7 / 1 / 1.3, a weapon adds its material); the guard break adds a tier 3 baked impact at -10 dB.
- **M6** materials: cardboard, plastic, tile, brick and sheet metal have recipes (`materialParts`); a break is ONE burst plus three random-delay debris ticks (`Sound.tick`), the object's `hx x hz` scales the level; debris glass = two noise ticks at 5 to 9 kHz, concrete = a 250 Hz tock.
- **M7** the crowd (Pit, Night Club): the knock-out cheer is the 1.2 s swell + a 1.6 kHz band (`Sound.swell`, still what P13-02 tests), `crowdLean` (an "ooh") on a knockdown, an object break and a hazard, at most one a 1.5 s; the murmur is the second noise bed of the ambience.
- **M8** = E7. **M9** menu: start (three rising notes + a swish), toggle on / off, pause / resume sweeps, slider tick (pitch follows the value), seat join / leave; the call sites in `changeSetting`, `act`, `onGameState` and the lobby were changed.
- **M10** countdown 330 / 392 / 440 Hz, the FIGHT chord (660 + 990 + 1320 Hz) with a sub drop and a noise crash, round start (round 2 and later: n pips; the deciding round: a low double stab), time warning 990 Hz and 1320 Hz at 1 s, time up (a falling buzzer on `roundEnd` for the clock), a round-ending KO (down-sweep + "ooh"; the bell only where the knock-out ends the match: `matchEndsOnKo`), combo milestones 3 / 5 / 8 for a person. The new note sets are in `CUE_NOTES` and the Cues test.
- **M11** breath: from `Sound.frame` every 1 / `PANT_HZ` s for a person under 35 % stamina or exhausted in the calm states.
- **M12** `Sound.grunt(fighter, kind)` with kinds hurt, hurtBig, effort, ko, exhale: pitch by weight class 170 Hz to 90 Hz, x1.35 for `look.gender` F, formant 600 to 1000 Hz by `look.build`, +-8 %. `exhale` plays on a blow of tier 3 that is blocked.
- **M13** get-up (cloth + effort) on `quickRise`; the falling whistle on `fall` and `ringOut`.
- **M14** the wave horn (two sawtooth notes through a 900 Hz low-pass) on `waveStart` and `waveBeat`.
- Also: the car alarm repeats (one oscillator, 4 a second for `ALARM_SECS`); the burning barrel and a burning object crackle while they burn (`Sound.frame`, priority 2); the train gets a two-tone horn with a pitch glide; the steam and the hydrant differ; the open drop is a long whistle and a far thud.

- All 72 classed sounds are within 2 dB of their target and under -1 dBFS in this harness, taken as the median of 5 plays per sound (a noise sound varies by up to 2 dB from one play to the next by design (E2), so one play can sit 2 to 3 dB off: two single-play renders of the same build gave 69 and 63 of 72 within, the outsiders changing from one render to the next; the median is the middle the targets name). The self-test plays all 120 rows of its table with a seeded random and a seeded bank and every row is within 2 dB of its target and under -1 dBFS.
- With the baked bank off (the synthesis fallback, which plays while the bake runs, without `OfflineAudioContext`, or after a failed step; median of 5 plays, after the last fallback fix) 70 of the 72 are within 2 dB; the two outside are the bat hit (-2.8 against -5: its wood layer is played by the synthesis too) and the kick tier 1 (-13.6 against -9: no baked body to lean on). Before the fix the fallback ignored the level of a call to `heavy()`, so the crash and train hurts played 12 dB hot (-4.3 and -3.6 against -16); it is never over -3 dBFS.
#### The 3 to 6 dB gap between the self-test render and the harness: the cause

- The first runs of `Sound levels` read the noise sounds and the hits 3 to 6 dB hotter than the harness. Bisecting with one change at a time (the seeded random, the bank, the reverb, the volumes, the camera, the wait for the bake, one context for the whole table or one per sound: none of them moved it) showed the signal into the master gain was 3 dB hotter in the test, so the cause was before the compressors: the test puts every sound exactly at the camera focus, where the pan is 0, and `panner(0)` returned the bus without a `StereoPannerNode`. A mono source that reaches the bus unpanned is full level on both channels; through a panner at any other pan it is 0.707 per channel at the centre (the equal-power law), so every sound the game places a hair off the focus (all of them, in real play) is 3 dB down on the same sound at pan 0.
- Which level is real: the live `AudioContext` (a script processor after the limiter, real time, music off) gives hit tier 1 -10.9 / -11.0 / -10.0, tier 2 -6.2 / -5.5 / -7.2, tier 3 -3.8 / -3.4 / -2.5, voice hurt -13.4 / -14.1 / -13.3, whoosh tier 2 -20.9 / -16.9 / -17.5, walk step -34.4, bell -7.0, menu confirm -16.2: the harness and the plan are right, the test's exact-centre placement was the outlier. Fix in the engine, not in the test: a placed sound always gets its panner, so dead centre is no longer a 3 dB louder special case (one more panner node per centred event, which the P0-04 numbers below include). The 13 sounds that were then still 2 to 4.7 dB hot in the test got their constants moved: item hits -2 to -3.5 dB, voice effort 1.3 to 1.15, guard break -8 to -10 dB, whoosh tier 1 0.28 to 0.22, weapon whistle 3.5 to 2.35, jump 0.62 to 0.79, dirt and club steps (0.28 to 0.16, 0.05 to 0.034 with their own run factors), landing curve, glass and wood debris, steam warning, combo milestone, breath (+1.9 dB).
- Three more test fixes found on the way: the music bus ducking (`pump`) read the saved Music volume, not the render's 0, so with Music at 0 a heavy hit raised the bed again (the render now sets the three saved volumes for the length of each play); the bake is seeded for the render (the same bank every run: with a random bank one weapon hit moved 2.5 dB between runs and flipped the test); and the three audio tests (levels, buses, bake) are now deferred: `test(name, fn, limitMs)` runs a test that passes a limit after every other test, one at a time, with its own timer. The first full headless run showed why: `run_all` is synchronous, so an async test's timers cannot fire until every later test has finished (about 9 minutes in the headless run), the bake test timed out at its 10 s limit, and every test after it ran against the half-swapped Sound state it had left across its awaits; in a full Chrome run the page's own bake finished under the bake test and put real buffers into the bank it was checking (the bake test now works on an isolated copy of `Sound`, so the page's bake cannot reach it). The levels and buses tests take 19 and 26 s in the full Chrome run (limit 240 s, `SOUND_RENDER_LIMIT_MS`).

#### Review fixes (the Opus review of 2026-11-10, 9 findings, all fixed)

- **1. Layered impact test.** `Layered impact sound (P13-02)` now runs in both paths, the baked bank and the synthesis with no bank, and keeps every assertion it had (thud order by weight, one sound per tier, the material layer, the swell, the cap of 12 with 20 hits).
- **2. Footsteps in the bank.** The footfall of a surface is one recipe (`footParts`) for the synthesis and the bake. The bank holds 24 more buffers: 6 surfaces x walk and run x two feet (the left and the right foot are the 1 and 0.93 pitch), 0.12 s each, so the bank is 60 buffers in 5 idle steps of 12 (27 impacts, 9 materials, 24 footsteps). A step is now one source and one gain (`STEP_DB` -34 and -30 dBFS plus `STEP_TRIM_DB` by surface, +2.2 dB on gravel because it is thin). Before the bank is ready, or when a render step fails, the synthesis plays the same recipe. A footfall under a landing, a fall or a jump goes through `allow('foot', 0, 2)` (finding 7).
- **3. Tense sweep.** The rising noise sweep of the tense layer loops its noise source (`sBuf.loop`), so it lasts its whole bar. It ran out of buffer 1 s in and clicked every 4 bars. Test `Music sweep (P18-29)`.
- **4. Last-round stab.** The low double stab keys on "the next round decides the match" (`Sound.decides`): a drawn round, or both sides one win short in a best of 3 or 5; never in a brawl or a lineup. Before, it keyed on `match.decider` only, which is not set at 1-1 in a best of 3. Test `Round start (P18-29)`.
- **5. Music.** Retuned from measurements, see "Music, measured".
- **6. Deferred audio tests.** `Sound levels` and `Sound buses` take a cancel token and render their own seeded bank (`bakeRender` into their own offline context); they do not wait for the page's bake. The bake test works on an isolated copy of `Sound` and does not wait for the page's bake either. Every row of the table has its own seed. The bake is seeded only inside its synchronous build (`around` in `bakeRender`), never across an await.
- **7. Footfall priority.** See 2: `footfall()` is priority 2 and goes first when the engine is full. Test `Sound footfalls (P18-29)`.
- **8. Old Safari.** Older Safari has only `webkitOfflineAudioContext`, whose `startRendering()` returns no promise and fires `oncomplete` instead. `bakeRender` sets `oncomplete` before it starts and uses the promise when there is one, else the event. The prefixed context most likely accepts only 44.1 to 96 kHz, so where only `webkitOfflineAudioContext` exists the bank is baked at 44,100 Hz (`BAKE_RATE_PREFIXED`, about 2.38 MB of Float32 instead of 1.73 MB); with the standard context it stays at 32 kHz. The bake test runs the render once with a stand-in prefixed context that has the callback form only and throws on a rate under 44,100, and checks the buffers are at 44,100 Hz. No Safari run was possible here; P16-03 lists the real check.
- **9. Fires.** The burning-thing list is cleared at `roundStart` and at `matchEnd`, so a quick Retry has no old crackle. Test `Sound footfalls (P18-29)`.
- **Second review (the Opus re-review of 2026-11-10; verdict pass, 6 findings, all fixed).**
  - The crackle of a burning object lasts as long as its material burns (`MATERIALS[mat].burn` ticks x `FIXED_DT`: cardboard 3 s, wood 8 s; it was a fixed 8 s). The clock that times it advances only in a live fight (`Game.state` FIGHT) and at the speed of the simulation (`Game.clockScale`): a pause no longer shortens a crackle and the slow-motion finisher slows it. Test `Sound fires (P18-29)`.
  - `matchEndsOnKo` no longer repeats the match rule: it calls `Game.match.endsMatch()`, which also reads a double knock-out (a draw round that both sides reach the wins needed with is not the end of the match). The `ko` event fires after the fighter is marked down, so the rule sees it. Test `Sound knock-out (P18-29)`. The first `ko` of two in the same tick still sees only one fighter down; the second one then plays the right sound.
  - Comments and this appendix corrected: 60 buffers in 5 idle steps, `bank.step`, the limit of the audio tests (240 s), which audio tests wait for the page's bake (none), and the 44.1 kHz bake for the prefixed context (finding 8).

#### For P18-60 (the MIDI intro and soundtrack)

- A MIDI player needs its own gain node on `Sound.musicBus` and must keep calling `syncAmbience`. `Sound.pump()` cancels the scheduled values on `musicBus.gain` (it ducks 3 dB on a heavy hit and then sets the gain back to the Music volume x 0.55), so a player that ramps its own volume on `musicBus` would be overwritten; it must make its own gain node and connect that to `musicBus`. If it replaces `Music.update` or `Music.stop`, it must still call `Sound.syncAmbience(track)` (the level hum and the crowd murmur live there, each frame from `Music.update` and once from `Music.stop`).

### P18-55 move list spec for P18-56 (2026-11-10)

Source of the owner's answers: the P18-55 task (2026-11-10). Research: Appendix B, "P18-55 - How fighting games show move lists and combos". Original design: the patterns are genre conventions, no name, icon, art or text of the reference games is used. The spec changes no move, frame number or balance: the list only shows the existing tables (ATTACKS rows, the styles' string positions, skins, throws, holds, clinch, items). Tables read: main at `206be0d` and branch `bp-p17-10-styles` (`moveFor`, `SKINS`, `THROW_SKINS`, `stringsFor(style, kicksDefault)`, `signature`), which has not landed; the spec names tables, not numbers, so it holds when P17-10 lands.

**1. Data model (one builder, three places)**
- `moveListData(profile, held)` is a pure function with no HTML: it returns `{ style, defense, held, groups: [ { id, title, hint, entries } ], strings, trials }`. Both screens and the tests read it. The Move list is never stored: it is built when the screen opens (and when the device changes), so it cannot drift from the tables. The simulation reads nothing new and writes nothing (no `Math.random`, no setting): replays and online stay as they are.
- An entry: `{ id, name, group, input, level, dmg, tags, key, frames }`.
  - `name`: the style's own name (`moveFor(style, row).name` after P17-10; the row's name before it).
  - `input`: an array of tokens `{ a: action, hold?: true, tag?: 'AIR' | 'RUN' | 'COUNTER' | 'CLINCH' | 'DOWN' }`, one array per way to play the move (the two shortest, as now). `a` is one of punch, kick, crouch, defend, grapple, use, or a direction word (toward, away, side).
  - `level`: `H`, `M`, `L` (the row's `h`), `G` for a grab or throw (no level, beats a block), from the same row the simulation plays.
  - `dmg`: the row's damage (a throw's `dmg`).
  - `tags`: at most two, from a fixed list of short ASCII words built from the row: Launches (`kind` launch), Knocks down, Staggers, Breaks guard (`gb`), Wide arc (`width` 0.8 or more), Beats guard (grab), Drains stamina (clinch knee), Counter only, Air only.
  - `key`: true for a move in the style's `signature`.
  - `frames` (filled only when the caller asks, Training only): `{ start, active, recover, onHit, onBlock, stam }`, read from the same row with `frameAdvantage`; a throw has `{ start, escapeUntil, recover, stam }`; a knockdown or launch says so instead of an advantage (as the Training readout does now).
- Where each group comes from:

| Group | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Strings | `stringsFor(style, !!held)` leaf rows (a row no longer row starts with), standing then crouch | a string entry has the steps (name, level, dmg each) and the total; with an item: `weaponTable(style, item)`; with a crate: kick rows only |
| Moves | the steps' rows (`found`), the shared rows with a `ctx` (air, run, counter) and the grab | signature moves first, then Punch moves, then Kick moves, each by tier; moves only in a string are listed in the string and here once |
| Clinch and throws | `CLINCH_MOVES` (2 strikes), `throwFor(grip, dir, style)` for front, rear, low (9), `TACKLE_MOVE` for a heavy fighter only | the style's own throws (STYLE_THROWS, THROW_SKINS) carry a Key mark; left and right are shown once |
| Ground | `style.submit` (names), the down-attack note of `GROUND_NOTES` | only for a style with holds; no frame table exists for holds, so they show name, input and note |
| Items | `weaponTable` and `WEAPON_MOVES` for the held item | only while an item is held (as now: "holding" / "carrying") |
| Defense | `defenseFor(profile)` and `DEFENSE_HELP`, the bin lid rule | one line, not a group of entries |

**2. Input notation as device chips (the controls of the device in use)**
- `inputHtml(tokens, kind, keymap)` draws one chip per token; the legend row above the list shows the chips of the five buttons once. Chips are CSS boxes, no image files, no external font (about 1 KB of CSS for all three devices). A chip is `<i class="g ...">` with a short text; its `aria-label` is the full action name; the row reads as a sentence for a screen reader ("Jab, high, input Punch then Punch").
  - Keyboard: a key cap with the key bound now (`keyLabel`, the P2 layout for the second seat); a rebound key shows at once.
  - Gamepad: a round chip with a drawn face shape (square, triangle, cross, circle: the geometric shapes the labels already name) for Punch and Kick, a small rounded chip with the name for the shoulders and triggers (`R1`, `L2`, `R2`), as in `GAMEPAD_LABELS`; a button with two faces shows the first (as now), the legend names both.
  - Touch: a chip that copies the on-screen button of the same name (same colour classes as `.tb`: PUNCH, KICK, DEFEND, GRAB, DUCK, JUMP, USE, LOCK) at about 70 % size, so the picture matches the glass.
  - Directions are words with an arrow (TOWARD, AWAY, SIDE) on every device: which key is "toward" depends on the Movement directions setting and the camera, so a drawn key would sometimes be wrong. A throw is `[tag CLINCH] [hold SIDE] [GRAB]`.
- Separators: a gap between presses that follow each other (the string window), `+` for held together (Crouch plus a press), `>` between the steps of a string line. A context tag (AIR, RUN, COUNTER, CLINCH, DOWN) is a small word chip before the chips.
- The device: `UI.moveKind()` as now (the device of the person who paused; the controls card's choice in the menus; the Training player's seat). While the screen is open the chips redraw once whenever `Input.lastDevice` changes (a keypress after a stick move, a touch), keeping the scroll position and the focus; no polling in a fight, and none when the screen is closed. P17-06 and P2-01 (no clutter): no new on-screen fight button, no new binding, no new setting; every control is an existing menu control or an existing key.

**3. Strings and combos**
- A string is one card: the input line (chips with `>` between steps), under it the step names with their level glyphs, at the end the total damage ("3 hits, 25 dmg") and, on the heading only, one line of the rule (press again soon after a hit or block; hold Crouch for the low strings). Prefix rows are not listed (`P`, `PP` are stops inside `PPP`); a style with fewer rows shows fewer cards. Standing strings first, crouch strings second; the first string the fighter really has with these hands is the "Start here" card (kept).
- Combos (Training only): `trials`, generated from the same tables, at most six per style, in three tiers (Basic, Next, Hard): (1) the longest standing Punch string, (2) the longest standing Kick string, (3) the longest crouch string, (4) a string whose last step launches or knocks down, (5) a signature move landed, (6) a clinch and a throw. Each has a one-line goal and a pass test on data the Training read-out already has: `lastMove.string` / `comboHits` for strings, `lastMove.result` for the launch, the throw event for the throw. A table change changes the trial list; no hand-written trial data exists. The done mark is saved in Progress as an object of booleans keyed `style:index`, cleaned like `tips` (missing, wrong type or extra key reads as not done) and shown as a tick on the card.

**4. Categories, order, filter**
- Order, fixed: Start here, Strings, Moves, Clinch and throws, Ground, Items, Trials (Training only). Inside Moves: signature first, then Punch, then Kick. The heading of each group has one hint line (a sentence at most, the prose that is today in the Attack strings, Defend and Clinch paragraphs; the full prose stays on the Controls screen, which already shows `DEFENSE_HELP` and `COMBO_HELP`).
- A Show row (an existing option-row control, left / right changes it, arrows on touch): All, Strings, Moves, Throws, Ground, Items, Trials; the entries that do not apply to this fighter are skipped. No sort control and no search (a style has about 20 moves, up to 8 strings and 9 throws).

**5. The three places**

| Place | Opens from | Shows | Extra |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pause menu | the existing Move list item (kept) | the fighter of the person who paused, its held item, its device; fields: name, input, level, damage, tags | no frame data (the pause menu of a Training fight is the next row) |
| Training | the Training pause menu (the existing item) and the Training panel | the same list plus frames line `12 / 3 / 20 f, hit +2, block -4, 5 stam` under a row; Trials group | Show me (demo) and Trials; the Training panel keeps FRAME DATA, STYLE and the read-outs and gains one Trial goal line while a trial runs |
| Fighter select and creator | select: a Move list button in the sticky row, for the focused card; creator: a Move list row under Movement | the profile that would play (a roster fighter; the creator's draft with its style and defense), strings, moves, throws; no frames, no items, no demo | read-only; Back returns with the focus kept (the screen stack does this today) |

- Training pause menu is the only place with frames and Show me: the test is `Game.match.training`.
- Show me: a row button (Training only). It closes the screen, resets the positions as the existing Reset does (scenario 2, close range, the dummy standing), and plays the move with a small scripted controller (a sibling of `DummyController`) that presses the tokens at the right ticks (for a string: the next press when the chain window opens, about 60 % recovered); the input chips of the move show at the bottom with the pressed chip lit; the Training panel shows the frame data of what is played. It plays twice, once at the render slow scale (the knock-out slow motion path, `clockScale`, render clock only, no sim change) and once at full speed, then returns to the list. Any press ends it. If the scripted controller feeds the same action bits as a human seat (BP-P18-56 reads the controller interface first and keeps the sim untouched), the demo is a real move with real numbers.
- Trials: a Trials card starts Training with the Basic positions and the goal line in the panel ("Trial 2: Kick, Round Kick, Heavy Kick. Hits 1 of 3"); success uses the existing banner and saves the mark once.

**6. Fields**

| Where | Fields |
|---|---|
| Every place | name, input chips, level glyph, damage, up to two tags, a key-move star (shape and the words "Key move" for a screen reader) |
| Training only | frames line (start, active, recover, on hit, on block, stamina); the escape tick for a throw; the Trials group; Show me |
| Never | the stamina cost outside Training; the other styles' moves; balance numbers (weights, scaling) |

**7. Navigation and layout**
- Keyboard: Up / Down move between the `[data-nav]` stops (headings, Show row, Back; in Training also the rows that have a Show me button), Left / Right change the Show row, Enter acts, Escape or Backspace goes back, PageUp / PageDown jump to the previous or next heading. Gamepad: stick or D-pad up / down, A (Cross) acts, B (Circle) back, L1 / R1 jump a heading (the Tekken 8 pattern), Start closes. Touch: tap a row to open its details (the frames line in Training, the tag words everywhere); a row is at least 44 px high; the page scrolls by drag; the Back row stays sticky at the bottom (kept). The focus scrolls the page to the stop (today the only stop is Back, so a gamepad cannot scroll the long page: headings become stops).
- Phone portrait (390 x 844): cards, not tables, one column: line 1 level glyph, name, damage; line 2 input chips (wrap); line 3 tags (and the frames line in Training). No horizontal scroll at 375 px (the P17-04 rule stays, and its self-test (5): no overflow at 375, 640 x 360 and 1280 x 720; add 390 x 844 and 844 x 390 to the browser self-test). Phone landscape (844 x 390): two card columns from 640 px wide; the heading and Show row sticky at the top (one line), Back sticky at the bottom, so about 8 cards show.
- Accessibility: text keeps the game's table size and the UI scale setting (0.8 to 1.5); chip height at least 24 px at scale 1 (28 on touch); hit level is shape plus letter plus colour: High = triangle up with H, Mid = square with M, Low = triangle down with L, Grab = circle with G; the colours are the colour-blind-safe set (High vermillion `#d55e00`, Mid amber `#e69f00`, Low blue `#56b4e9`, Grab purple `#cc79a7`), each at least 3:1 against the panel (checked in P18-56 with the High-contrast HUD setting on and off, which adds a white outline); the legend shows the four marks once; the list is readable in greyscale because the letter and the shape carry the meaning; Reduced motion turns the demo's slow pass off (it plays once at full speed).

**8. Change list for P18-56**

| Changes | Kept | Removed |
|---|---|---|
| `screen_moves` (about 7.4 KB, one function building HTML strings) becomes `moveListData` (pure) plus a renderer; entries get level glyphs, chips, tags; strings become leaf cards; groups and the Show row; heading stops and L1 / R1 / PageUp / PageDown jumps; the phone layout from tables to cards; frames only in Training; Show me and Trials (new, Training only); a Move list entry on fighter select and in the creator; one Progress field for trial marks | who the list is for (`moveFighter`, `moveKind`, who paused, P17-04); the rule that no other style is shown; `weaponTable` and the crate rules; `controlLabel`, `GAMEPAD_LABELS`, `TOUCH_LABELS`, the key bindings, the P2 layout; `Start here`; the defense line; the signature star idea (now a shape); the clinch, tackle, throw and hold rows; every table of moves and every number; `frameAdvantage` and the Training FRAME DATA read-out; the Training panel; the Controls card and its prose | the three `table.ctl` move tables (Move / Input / Data, strings, throws); the Data column text and its `Data:` hint paragraph; the text `<kbd>` legend line (becomes the chips legend); the frames and stamina text in every non-Training list; the text `*` mark; the 18-row string table (the prefix rows) |

- Cost estimate (LF bytes, measured: `breakpoint.html` is 1,350,683 on main at `206be0d`, 1,355,634 on `bp-p17-10-styles`; budget 4,000,000): data builder about 2.5 KB, chips and CSS about 2.5 KB, renderer and groups about 3.5 KB, navigation and Show row about 1 KB, trials and Progress about 3 KB, Show me about 2.5 KB, select and creator entries about 0.7 KB: about 16 KB added, about 6 KB removed (the old builder, tables and long paragraphs): net about +10 KB (range +8 to +14 KB, 0.7 to 1 %), so about 1.37 MB, 34 % of the budget. `breakpoint-tests.js`: about +20 KB (CRLF, no BOM). Documentation: this section gets the "built" lines; README only if a setting or key changes (none planned).
- Performance: the list is built on open and on a device change as one `innerHTML` string of about 20 to 30 KB (about 45 to 60 cards), an estimate of a few ms that P18-56 measures once; the chips are CSS, so no image decoding and no per-frame cost; the trial check reads events the Training read-out already receives (a few comparisons per hit); Show me is a normal Training fight. The gameplay frame time is unchanged outside Training; confirm with one P0-04 benchmark (640 x 360, throttle 4, low quality) once in Training with a trial running, and that the menu itself leaves the benchmark path untouched.
- Self-tests (P18-56): the five 'Move list (P17-04)' tests are re-pointed at `moveListData` and keep every assertion (names, inputs, other styles absent, holding / carrying, the device and the paused seat; none is loosened); new: one chip per token and only the device in use named; the chips switch with `lastDevice`; the level glyph table (three shapes, four colours, each with its letter); frames only when Training; leaf strings equal the table's leaves; trials come from the tables, each is reachable (a headless run of its string passes it), and the Progress field cleans; Show me ends in the list with the dummy and the positions restored; heading stops exist and focus scrolls; no horizontal scroll at 375, 390 x 844, 844 x 390, 640 x 360 and 1280 x 720 (browser; the headless stub skips it as today). Never skip or weaken a test to pass it; fingerprint hashes stay as recorded (nothing here touches the sim).
- Owner device checks (for BP-P16-03, not blocking): the chips on a real phone and gamepad; the demo on a phone; the colours in greyscale.

**9. Open questions (decisions that need no change of the spec if the owner picks differently)**
1. Gamepad glyphs use the shape names the game already prints (Square, Triangle, Cross, Circle). A second set for another pad family needs the pad's id: not planned.
2. Stamina cost is listed with the frames, so Training only; the owner's field list names damage, level, note, and frames in Training.
3. Trials: six per style, marks saved, no rewards. A reward or an unlock for finishing them is not decided.
4. The dummy's move list (Soulcalibur VI shows the opponent's list in Training) is not in the owner's three places: one extra Show choice "Dummy" would cost about 0.4 KB; left out unless asked.
5. A looping move preview on the fighter cards (a mini demo) is not planned: it needs a running match or world on a menu screen.

### P18-57 per-move animation briefs, ranking and work order (2026-11-10)

Task: BP-P18-57 (docs only). Input: Appendix B, "P18-57 - Real techniques of the 16 fighting styles", which has the sources, each style's stance, idle, steps, evasions and every technique's phases and faults. Output: this brief for BP-P18-58 (the first 8 styles of the ranking) and BP-P18-59 (the other 8). Owner answers of 2026-11-10: all 16 styles, the worst-looking first; looks only (frame data, reach, damage and the hit check stay as they are, so balance is untouched); the stance, idle movement, steps and evasions change as well as every attack, throw and hold. No code was changed here.

**What was compared.** The move tables, strings, skins, throws, holds and clinch sets of branch `bp-p17-10-styles` (P17-10, not yet on main when this was written; base `537a16b`), `ANIM_SPECS`, `STRIKE_BUILDERS`, `STYLE_TECH`, `STRIKE_SPIN`, `STRIKE_ROLL`, `MOVE_STYLE` guard and rhythm fields, `THROW_POSES` with `DERIVED_THROWS`, `GRIP_POSES`, `CLINCH_STRIKE_POSES`, `HOLD_POSES`, and frames captured from that build (Node Playwright, Chrome, unmuted, one preset fighter per style against KAI in the Gym, the camera at the side, `Game.state` held on PAUSED so only the pose is drawn; per style the idle stance, each key move at 55 percent of its startup and at the first active tick, the style's throws at 55 and 100 percent, the clinch knee and elbow, the hold). The frames are scratch files in `%TEMP%\claude\bp-tech\` (not in the repo): `<style>-idle.png`, `<style>-<row>-wind.png`, `<style>-<row>-hit.png`, `<style>-throw-<pose>-mid.png` and `-end.png`, `<style>-clinch-knee.png`, `<style>-clinch-elbow.png` and `<style>-hold.png` (drawn for all 16 styles). Throws and holds were drawn without the thrown foe and without the floor plant, so their height is only roughly right. The runner is `cap.mjs` next to the frames (it loads the html through a route, no server).

**How an attack is drawn today (what a pose can change).** A strike is two or three key poses on the style's guard: guard, then for a kick the chamber (the knee lerped up to `kickChamber`, or a style's own wind-up spec `pre` for acrobatic moves), then the contact pose at the first active tick, then back. The contact pose is a base builder in `STRIKE_BUILDERS` (about 40) plus offsets from `ANIM_SPECS` (spec keys: `arm`, `off` the guard hand, `sw` the arm of the kicking side, `leg` [hip, abduction, knee] of the kicking leg, `base` the support leg, `front` and `rear` the legs of a punch, `lean`, `twist`, `roll`, `head`, `fwd` the step, `drop` both knees, `wind`, `pivot`, and the whole-body `pitch`, `brol`, `yaw`, `rdrop`) plus the style's `STYLE_TECH` offsets for punches and kicks plus `STRIKE_SPIN` or `STRIKE_ROLL` for turns that go on to a full circle on the way back. The idle, walk, crouch, block and sway poses are the style's guard with `styleRhythm` (bounce, sway, head) on top; the Sway pose (`SWAY_POSE`) and the Crouch and Block poses are the same for every style. Hands have no shapes (a palm strike and a fist look alike) and there is no stick. New levers a looks-only task may add (all drawn, none read by the simulation): a style key in the sway, crouch and walk poses (for a negativa, esquiva, slip, bob or role look), per-style idle loops in `styleRhythm` (a ginga with a step), new builders in `STRIKE_BUILDERS`, new entries in `STRIKE_SPIN` and `STRIKE_ROLL`, new `THROW_POSES`, `HOLD_POSES` and `CLINCH_STRIKE_POSES`.

**Limits every change must keep (the work is looks only).**
1. Frame data, reach, width, damage, stamina, `h` (hit level), `limb`, `plant`, `duck` and every number of `ATTACKS`, `THROW_SETS`, `STYLE_THROWS`, the string tables and the style rows' `aiw`, `defense`, `submit`, `signature` stay as they are. A skin keeps changing only name, `anim`, `limb`, `reach`, `width`, `cat` (P17-10 test 4); a new `anim` name is a look only. The fight, hazard, items and weapons fingerprints and the P0-06 balance numbers must not move (the tests below do not read the drawn pose; run the Chrome gate to see the hashes).
2. P17-02 hit check (`Hit check (P17-02)`, 594 pairs and the P17-10 pairs): at tick `startup + 1` the limb tip (hands key points 9 and 12, feet 15 and 18, the right elbow 33 for the Elbow) is at most 0.1 m short of the front of the hit volume (`reach` x Reach stat + 0.34), at most 0.45 m off the line to the foe, at most 0.15 m past the foe's centre, and in the height band of the row (High hand 1.25 to 1.75 m, High kick 1.0 to 1.75 m, Mid 0.85 to 1.5 m, Low 0 to 0.65 m, times the body scale, 0.05 m of slack); also at a lateral offset of 0.3 m for spin and roll moves. The stride is fitted by the game (`strikeStride`), so the first fix for a short tip is `fwd`, lean or the limb offsets, never a looser limit.
3. `Calm poses (P17-02)`: at the contact tick no joint beyond: arms 2.02 (left) and 2.0 (right), elbows 2.48 and 2.63, hips 1.68 and 1.78, knees 1.8, torso lean 1.05, torso turn 1.5, torso roll 0.9, head 0.68 rad. The whole-body `bodyPitch`, `bodyRoll` and `bodyYaw` are not in that list (Au Batido and Bananeira use them, P17-10 note 2); a move that needs a bigger bend than a limit allows is solved with those or with `rdrop` and `fwd`, not by a larger limit.
4. The floor rule (P17-10 note 5): the lowest foot or hand of every tick of every move is never more than 0.03 m below the floor; an inverted move that has `plant: true` (Bananeira, Au Batido) lowers the hands within 0.05 m of the floor at the contact and Au Batido stays within 0.35 m above it; a new inverted or ground pose without `plant` must be measured the same way tick by tick (use `Fighter.lowestPart()`), and a pose that needs the floor plant (a sit, a roll, a negativa with a hand down) draws on the floor through the existing `plantFloor` only when the move or state is `planted`; adding `plant` to a row is a row change and is not part of this work (open question 1).
5. The Sway pose clearance (`Sway pose (P3-11)`): the drawn slip keeps 0.1 m of air from the plane of a High and Mid strike and the sway i-frames (12 ticks) and the 15 recovery ticks stay; a style's own slip, bob, negativa or esquiva look is drawn inside that body volume (the head and chest key points no nearer to the foe's strike line than the shared Sway pose puts them). The sway state itself stays the same state.
6. Styles stay apart (`Technique`, `Styles (P17-10)` tests: no two styles play one identity outside the share list, a skin's animation base has the height of its row, the stance retune keeps a minimum pose distance of 0.399 between two guards, and the clinch strike poses of two sets differ by at least 0.2 rad), and the share list of P17-10 does not change.
7. Per fighter, `makeMotion` jitters the style fields by `MOTION_JITTER`, so values must leave room for it; the stance retune of P17-10 (minimum pose distance 0.399) is the floor for guard changes; reduced motion (`Settings.v.reducedMotion`) scales the idle loops, so a new idle loop must multiply by `amount`.
8. Size: `breakpoint.html` is about 1,355,000 bytes of the 4,000,000 budget; the animation data of this program is estimated at 12 to 16 KB for all 16 styles. Plain ASCII.
9. Tests to run per style batch (scoped, `node tools/run-tests.js --only "Hit check|Calm poses|Strike step|Styles (P17-10)|Technique|Sway pose|Motion|Clinch strikes|Throw|Submission"`, then the Chrome gate once): the hit check, the calm-pose limits, the P17-10 style tests, the sway clearance, the technique-separation tests; add one new test per batch: every move of the batch's styles at its contact tick shows the signature the brief names (for example the Armada body turned at least 1.2 rad from the line, Bananeira pitch at least 2.9), measured on the `pose` array, and the floor rule over all ticks.

**Per-move briefs.** Each style has its idle and evasion brief first, then one line per move: `row@anim` (Breakpoint name) = the real technique (Appendix B) | today (what the build draws) | verdict (G good, F fair, W wrong, X missing) | keys to set. Keys use the spec language above (sign: `s` = +1 left limb, -1 right). Values are starting points that P18-58 and P18-59 fit with the hit-check probe (`strikeStride`, the tip distance at tick `startup + 1`); they are not measured.

**Ranking: what looks least like the real technique, worst first.** Each line of the briefs below carries a verdict (G good, F fair, W wrong, X missing); the score is 3 per W, 2 per X and 1 per F, so a style with several wrong moves ranks above one with many fair ones; ties go to the style with more W. The idle, the evasion, every strike, throw, hold and clinch line counts once; shared rows count once per style.

| Rank | Style | W | X | F | G | Score | Batch | Why it ranks here |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Capoeira | 4 | 2 | 6 | 3 | 22 | P18-58 | no ginga, negativa, esquiva or role; Armada and Queixada are plain kicks without the turn or the crescent; Queixada and Martelo share one pose (the owner's own example) |
| 2 | Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu | 4 | 0 | 4 | 1 | 16 | P18-58 | a ground style drawn standing: frames, seated guard kicks and sweeps are standing punches and kicks |
| 3 | Wrestling | 3 | 0 | 5 | 2 | 14 | P18-58 | the stance is right but the ankle trips, the snap down and the shot are drawn as low kicks and jabs |

The verdicts come from the frames and from reading the pose code; where the frame and the code disagree the frame is the truth (for example the Taekwondo round kick reads as fair in `ANIM_SPECS` and looks flat in the frame). The counts are of the lines below and move if a line is edited.

**Briefs by style, in ranking order.**

**1. Capoeira (CAPOEIRA: mara, tiago). Verdict: the worst; ginga, negativa, esquiva and role are missing and the spinning kicks do not spin.**
- Idle and stance | today: the shared orthodox guard with `sway` 0.075 at 0.55 Hz, `guardLean` 0.22, `guardCrouch` 0.23 (the frame is a long boxer-like stance leaning forward; the real ginga exists only in `VICTORY_POSES.ginga`) | X | keys: a ginga loop in `styleRhythm` for this style (`motion.ginga`): period 1.0 s (the ginga step is about one per second, tempo scaled), the rear leg swings back along a triangle and the legs swap their lead every half period (`hipLx` 0.5 + 0.35 sin, `hipRx` 0.5 - 0.35 sin, `knL` and `knR` 0.8, `hipLz`, `hipRz` 0.28 as the victory pose has them), `rootSide` +-0.1, `torsoRoll` -rock x 0.12, `torsoTwist` +rock x 0.3; the arms alternate with the legs: the arm on the forward side up at the face (`shLx` 1.6, `elL` 2.0), the other low at the chest (`shRx` 0.6, `elR` 1.2), `torsoLean` 0.25, `headX` kept up so the eyes stay on the foe; multiply by `amount` (reduced motion). Walking uses the same loop at the walk speed.
- Evasions | today: the shared Sway pose (a step back and a lean, or a side bend) for the 'sway' defence | X | keys: a style key in `Fighter.computePose` for `S.SWAY`: the back slip is a negativa (the front leg out long on its heel, `hipLx` 0.9 and `knL` 0.05; the rear knee deep, `knR` 1.7 and `hipRx` 1.1; `torsoLean` 0.9 to 1.0, `headX` 0.2; one hand down beside the front leg (`shRx` 0.4 with `torsoLean` so the hand is near the floor) and the other forearm at the face (`shLx` 1.8, `elL` 2.3)); the side slip is an esquiva (`rootSide` out 0.25, `torsoRoll` 0.5, one hand up at the face, the head off the centre line and inside the existing clearance); the sidestep state draws a role (`rootDrop` -0.3, `torsoRoll` swinging through 0.9, the hands near the floor, the feet crossing low).
