**Work order and what each batch builds.**

Common to both batches (done first in P18-58, reused by P18-59):
1. A style key for the evasion poses: `EVADE_POSE[styleId] = { back: {joint: offset...}, side: {...}, step: {...}, crouch: {...} }`, read in `Fighter.computePose` for `S.SWAY` (and `S.SIDESTEP`, `S.CROUCH`) on top of the shared pose and scaled by `swayOut()`; no state, timing or i-frame changes; a style without an entry draws what it draws now. Capoeira (negativa, esquiva, role), Boxing (slip and bob), Wing Chun (turning stance), Hapkido (circling), Krav Maga (360 defence), Wrestling and BJJ (sprawl, hip escape) use it. Test: the Sway clearance (0.1 m of air) for every style, the head key point never nearer to the foe's strike line than the shared pose puts it.
2. A per-style idle loop in `styleRhythm` (the `ginga`, the hand fight, the Muay Thai rock, the Kali triangle), each multiplied by `amount` so reduced motion calms it. Test: `Calm poses` and the P17-10 stance separation (0.399) and a new one: every loop returns to its first value over one period.
3. New shared bases in `STRIKE_BUILDERS` (each 250 to 350 bytes of source): `legAttack` (Wrestling, Sambo, BJJ, MMA), `snapDown` (Wrestling, BJJ), `gripPull` and `pushout` (Judo, Boxing), `sweepFoot` (Judo, Karate, Sambo, Hapkido), `frame` and `seatPush` (BJJ), `sideKick` (Karate, Taekwondo), `axeKick` (Taekwondo), `armadaKick`, `queixada`, `martelo` (Capoeira), `backfistSpin` (Kickboxing).

P18-58 (the first eight, in this order; cost about 8 to 10 KB):
1. Capoeira: ginga loop, negativa, esquiva and role through `EVADE_POSE`, `armadaKick` with `STRIKE_SPIN.armada` 2.9 and its `pre`, `queixada`, `martelo` (a look of its own), `rasteira` with the hand down, the `tapa` arc, `cabecada`, the guard hand on the bencao, the tesoura takedown. Signature checks: Armada at 60 percent of the startup has `|bodyYaw|` at least 2.0 and at the contact at least 1.0 side-on; Queixada hip abduction at least 0.8; Rasteira hands within 0.05 m of the floor at the contact; the ginga loop moves both hips by at least 0.3 rad over a period.
2. Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu: grip-fighting stance, `snapDown`, `frame`, `seatPush`, scissor and butterfly sweeps from a seat, the guard-pull feet, the armbar legs. Signature checks: Guard Kick and the sweeps lower the root by at least 0.3 m at the contact (the floor rule holds: no part more than 0.03 m below it), the frame rows keep the lead leg lifted, the head at least 0.2 m lower than the guard stance.
3. Wrestling: hand-fight loop, `legAttack` (Ankle Trip, Leg Trip, Single-Leg Trip), `snapDown`, `shoulder` as a shot, `underhook` poses, sprawl, the carry's knee. Signature checks: the leg attacks lower the root by at least 0.25 m and lean at least 0.8; Snap Down has both hands forward and the torso leaning down at the contact; the Sprawl has both thighs behind the body.
4. Taekwondo: the bladed hop stance, `axeKick` (the heel above the head at the wind-up), the lower and straighter dollyeo lean, the back kick's head-first wind-up, the tornado turn, the pull-in hand. Signature checks: the Axe Kick wind-up has the foot at least 1.5 m above the floor (key point 18 y at tick 55 percent of the startup) and the contact has the torso within 0.5 rad of upright; the Round Kick keeps the head above the hips (head key point higher than the pelvis).
5. Judo: grip stance, `gripPull` for the pulls, `pushout`, `lift`, `sweepFoot` for the three sweeps, the two-hand clinch looks, the hip-turn step for Ura-nage. Signature checks: both hands in front of the chest at the idle; the three sweeps keep both arms forward (`shLx` and `shRx` above 1.2) at the contact; no punch pose for a pull (the elbow bends toward the body).
6. Sambo: jacket-grip stance, the lowered boot kicks, `legAttack` for the Leg Pick, `sweepFoot`. Signature checks: the boot kick foot below hip height; the leg pick as Wrestling.
7. Wing Chun: the narrow turned-in stance, the centre-line hands, the trap with the lower hand, the upright thrust kick, the turning-stance evasion. Signature checks: at the idle the ankles are no more than 0.32 m apart (key points 15 and 18) and the knees are not wider than the ankles; the chain punch keeps the torso turn under 0.25 rad.
8. Karate: the hikite idle, the side-on `sideKick`, the more upright mawashi, the zanshin hold. Signature checks: Side Thrust Kick `|bodyYaw|` at least 1.2 at the contact; Mawashi lean within 0.15 rad of upright.

P18-59 (the other eight; cost about 4 to 6 KB): Hapkido (open-hand guard, the circling evasion, the palm wrist angle, the low spinning heel with the head first, the wrist-lock throw with the twist), Kali / Eskrima (the bladed triangle idle, the live-hand checks on every strike, the Angle 2 and Redonda arcs, the angling-off evasion), Kickboxing (the narrower hop stance, the true spinning backfist with `STRIKE_SPIN.backfist` 2.4, the less over-tipped round kicks, the switch-kick feet swap), Krav Maga (the open-hand ready stance, the 360 defence in the evasion pose, the hammer fist's raised wind-up, the groin kick chamber), Mixed Martial Arts (the squarer stance, the level-change idle, the oblique kick's turn), Street Brawler (the wide rolling stance, the flinch evasion, the grabbing head butt, the stomp's knee lift), Boxing (the slip and the bob through `EVADE_POSE`, the clinch shove-off without the hip toss), Muay Thai (the rocking idle, the leg check and shrug, the capped round-kick tip). Signature checks: as in the lines above; the Boxing slip keeps the hands up (`shLx` and `shRx` at least 0.9) and the head moves at least 0.15 m off the line; the Muay Thai round kick keeps the head key point above the pelvis.

For every style, in the same order: (1) the guard values and idle loop; (2) the evasion entry; (3) the W rows, then the F rows, in the order above; (4) the throws, the hold and the clinch strikes; (5) after each row, the hit-check probe (`strikeStride`, the tip distance at tick `startup + 1`, at the lateral offset of 0.3 m for the spins), the calm-pose maxima and the floor rule; fix with `fwd`, lean and the limb offsets, never with a limit; (6) the scoped tests of limit 9, then the Chrome gate; (7) capture the frames again with `cap.mjs` and compare with Appendix B's phases; (8) the owner checks (a phone, a pad) go to BP-P16-03.

Estimated size: 12 to 16 KB of `breakpoint.html` for all 16 styles (budget 4,000,000; the file is about 1,355,000 on `bp-p17-10-styles`), and one new test block per batch (the signature checks) in `breakpoint-tests.js`.

**Open questions for the owner (none blocks P18-58 or P18-59; each has a default).**
1. Ground and seated poses (BJJ guard, Capoeira rasteira and negativa with a hand down): the floor plant only runs for the `plant` rows (Bananeira, Au Batido), the holds and the downed states. Default: build these poses above the floor with `rootDrop` and the hit-check probe, and keep `plant` as it is. If the owner agrees that `plant: true` may be added to a few rows (a drawn-only flag; it only raises the plant speed), the BJJ and Capoeira low moves can touch the floor properly.
2. The leg attacks of Wrestling, Sambo, BJJ and MMA (Ankle Trip, Leg Pick, Single-Leg Trip) are leg rows (`limb` LL), so the hit check measures the foot. A real leg attack is a hand at the heel. Default: show the penetration step (the lead foot and the deep knee) and put the hands low in the same pose; changing the limb of a skin needs a new `reach`, which would be a number change.
3. Hands have no shapes: a palm heel (Hapkido, Krav Maga, Kali), a hammer fist and a fist look alike. Default: leave; the arm path and the guard hand carry the technique. A hand-shape flag in the mesh would cost a little source and one more draw state.
4. Clinch strikes in Judo, Wrestling, Sambo, BJJ and Hapkido are not legal techniques of those sports; the damage and tags stay, only the look changes (a foot block, a shiver, a hand fight). Default: as written; the move list names ("Clinch Knee") are P18-56's list and are not renamed here.
5. Heel Hook (Sambo): the FIAS sport rules read here allow arm locks and leg locks without naming the heel hook; the game's name stays (names are not changed here); the look is the leg lock.
6. P17-10 was not on main when this was written; if its tables change before P18-58 starts, the row names in these lines are re-read from the merged file (the rows and anims are the keys).
7. The frames: 293 images in `%TEMP%\claude\bp-tech` (strikes at the wind-up and the contact for 5 to 9 moves per style, the idle, the style's own throws at 55 and 100 percent, the clinch knee and elbow, the hold). The thrown foe, the floor plant and the camera cut of a real throw are not in them, so throw heights are rough; the rows not drawn (for example Counter Uppercut, Air Strike, Running Lunge, the later string steps) were judged from `ANIM_SPECS` and `STRIKE_BUILDERS`. The frames are scratch files outside the repo; `cap.mjs` next to them redraws them in about 4 minutes.

### P18-66 weapons and armed goons, decided (2026-11-10)

Task: BP-P18-66 (decision only; no game code changed). Builds: BP-P18-67 (the items and the guns) and BP-P18-68 (armed goons). Base: `main` at cd73dd1, facts read in `breakpoint.html` at that commit (line numbers below are that file's). Decided by the agent under the owner's standing go ("balanced", agents decide smaller calls and log them); the owner can change every number and every row. The free choices are listed at the end.

- Owner (2026-11-10, 14:40 to 14:51, verbatim): "Add more appropriate weapons (blades,Guns,blunt) and add if not already goons that come equipped".
- **This overrides the earlier rejection of firearms.** P1-03 rejected "Carried-item management: firearms, item combining, weapon / style swap" (reason: mobile complexity, aim, fire, combine or cycle input; "one held item with `use` is the design") and P1-04 rejected "Kendo, swords, nunchaku, knives, firearms" (reason: not Modern Urban fit, lethal weapon training). The owner's request wins for firearms and knives. Both old reasons are met by this design instead of ignored: no aim input (the existing lock-on picks the target), no combining or cycling (one held item, the one Use press), no new button on any device, and the content stays street-fight level (rules below). Swords, nunchaku and the other P1-04 rejected weapons stay rejected (the owner asked for blades, blunt and guns, not those).
- What exists (read): the 14 items of P7-01 in `WEAPONS` (5629) with classes light, heavy, two, throwable, carry and `WEAPON_STEPS` (5683: 3, 2, 2, 1, 0 Punch steps); `makeWeaponMove` (5755: step damage x1 / x1.2 from step 3 for light, x0.7 then x1 for heavy and two-handed, a strong last step); one Use press (`Fighter.tryUse`, 6190: take, tap = throw at the lock-on target, hold 30 ticks = put down, Crouch + Use = drop); `throwItem` (10682) and `moveItem` / `itemStrike` (10767, 10750: fixed arc, no random number); `Combat.itemBlock` (7416: a front Block stops a thrown item at 1.5x stamina, a perfect Block costs none), `Combat.itemHit` (7431: thrown damage x strength x Momentum boost x defender's taken); `ITEM_MAX` 12 and `addItem` (10609: the oldest resting loose item goes first); the Items rule (`cfg.items`: Settings in Arcade, Survival and Training; a Free Fight row; Tournament sets `items: false`, 13166); `AIController.considerPickup` / `isTossItem` / `considerThrow` and the toss window `AI_TOSS_REST_TICKS` (8861 to 8910, P18-34); goons (`GOON_VARIANTS` BRUISER, SCRAPPER, RUNNER and the leader `g:L`, `GOON_SCALE`, `crewScale`, `waveProfiles` dealing variants in turn, `enterEnemy`, P18-21) and the Arcade brawl stages 1, 3, 5 and 6 (`Story.cfg`, 8718).

#### Decisions

1. **Seven new items, all inside the existing classes and the one Use press.** Blades: Knife, Box cutter, Broken bottle (class light, Punch = a 3-step string; the Box cutter has 4 steps like the Kali stick). Blunt: Tyre iron (heavy, 2 steps, the last strong), Golf club (two-handed, 2 steps, no clinch while held). Guns: Pistol and Revolver, class **throwable** (best thrown, a held strike is weak: the "pistol whip" is the 1-step Punch string). No new class, no new input, no new setting.
2. **Guns.** Use fires at the lock-on target (no aiming input; auto lock-on stays, as the owner asked on 2026-11-10); with no lock the shot goes straight ahead along the facing. A gun has limited ammo (Pistol 5 rounds, Revolver 3) and cannot be reloaded or refilled: there is no ammo pick-up. A loaded gun is never thrown by a tap (a tap fires); hold Use puts it down and Crouch + Use drops it, as for every item. **An empty gun is thrown**: the next Use tap throws it like any throwable (Pistol 4 damage, Revolver 5), after which it is an ordinary loose item. The press starts an aim move (the fighter stops and raises the gun for 18 ticks, Revolver 28; this is the tell); a hit, a throw or a knock-down during it cancels the shot and the round is not spent; after the shot the fighter recovers 12 ticks (Revolver 20). The **bullet uses the deterministic thrown-item path**: it is a transient item (`bullet`, not placeable, not pickable, not drawn as a weapon, not counted in the 12 loose items) launched by `throwItem`'s code with flat flight (no gravity), speed 24 m/s = 0.4 m per tick, aimed at the target's chest (1.05 m) at the position the target has on the tick the bullet leaves, no lead, no spread, no random number; it ends at its first hit, block, wall or object, or after 12 m (30 ticks). It uses `itemStrike` and `itemHit` (damage = the gun's bullet damage x strength x Momentum boost x taken, a hit-stun of 16 ticks, no knock-down) and `itemBlock`. A Sway fighter in its 12 i-frames lets it pass and it may hit a fighter behind; a sidestep or a Sway clears it; a jump and a crouch do not (the feet peak at about 1.05 m, a crouched body still reaches 1.25 m).
3. **Items rule, Tournament and modes.** A gun is an item: with Items off nothing lies about, no goon is armed and no gun exists. The Tournament sets Items off, so there are no guns, no new items and no armed goons in it (the Tournament rule of P7-01 is unchanged: "off in Tournament"). In every other mode guns follow the Items rule. Guns are **never placed on level floors**: they exist only as the loadout of Arcade goons (BP-P18-68) and as what a goon drops, so Versus, Free Fight 1v1, Training and Survival never meet one. The seven items other than the guns are placed (table below) and follow the Items rule like the 14 of P7-01. Arcade duels (stages 2, 4, 7) have no loadouts: main fighters start unarmed (the floor items of the level work as today).
4. **Defending.** A gun's answer is the existing three: a front Block stops the bullet and pays 1.5 x (bullet damage x 0.9) stamina (Pistol 5.4, Revolver 9.5 at guard 1.0; a perfect Block pays none, and a held bin lid pays none), a Sway during its i-frames dodges it, and a sidestep clears the line. Arithmetic for the sidestep: the sidestep moves 7 m/s fading over 18 ticks, so 0.60 m after 6 ticks; a bullet hits within the body radius 0.34 + `ITEM_RADIUS` 0.18 = 0.52 m of its line, so a sidestep that started 6 or more ticks before the bullet arrives is clear (at 5 m the bullet needs 12.5 ticks, so a press during the first 6 ticks after the shot, or during the aim, clears; at 3 m only a press during the aim does). Striking the shooter during the aim cancels the shot. A CPU that is shot at answers the aim like a strike of height M and reach 12 m by the same reaction numbers (Easy 20 ticks is slower than the 18-tick aim, Normal 14, Hard 10 and Expert 8 are inside it), so no new random number exists.
5. **Content rules (existing ones kept).** Modern Urban: a plain pistol and revolver, no brand, no automatic weapon, no shotgun. Non-graphic as P1-03 set: no blood, no wounds, no kills by weapon; a bullet hit shows the same hit flash and flinch as a thrown brick, a knock-out falls as always; text calls it a hit, never a kill. The muzzle flash is a 2-tick light that Reduced motion removes (the tracer stays); the shot sound follows the P18-29 rules (varied by a counter, not by the clock, at most 12 impact voices, covered by the volume settings; sound is outside the simulation and may use its own noise as the other sounds do).
6. **Controls (touch, gamepad, keyboard).** The one Use press, nothing else: touch uses the existing USE button, which shows while an item is held or in reach and reads SHOOT 5 (the rounds left) with a loaded gun and THROW with an empty one; the gamepad Use button and the keyboard Use key do the same; the Use press is buffered like today. Rounds are also shown as pips by the holder's tag. The first time a person holds a loaded gun a once-only tip shows, saved in Progress (`tips.gun`, default false, missing in an old save reads false): "Use fires at your lock-on target. Block, Sway or sidestep to dodge. Hold Use to put it down." No new on-screen button and nothing new to reach at 390 x 844 or 844 x 390.
7. **The CPU and the new items.** A CPU picks up and uses every item through the existing `considerPickup` (a floor item within 2.5 m that is nearer than its target): the five melee items are plain melee items, fetched and used like a bat or a pipe, with no rule change (the Tyre iron's Pry and the Knife's lunge are in the move rows, so the CPU uses them as it uses any step). A gun stays a toss item for fetching (a team takes at most one per `AI_TOSS_REST_TICKS` window, so a dropped loaded gun is not snapped up at once), and a CPU holding a gun does not throw it: **it fires when the target is 3 to 10 m away, it holds a loaded gun, it holds no attack token (the condition `considerPickup` already uses), it has stood 90 ticks since it entered, and its team has no shot aiming or in flight and the last team shot was at least `AI_SHOT_GAP` ago (Easy 150, Normal 110, Hard 80, Expert 60 ticks)**. Closer than 3 m it plays the pistol whip like a melee item; an empty gun it holds is thrown at once at 3 to 8 m, else put down; it never fetches an empty gun. None of this draws a random number.

#### The item table (the 7 new items; P7-01 columns and rules)

Damage values are base damage before the fighter's strength; speed = startup ticks (steps after the first start 1 tick sooner for light items, 2 later for heavy and two-handed); reach = metres beyond the fist (the fist's own reach 0.8 m is added, `WEAPON_ARM`); durability = hits landed or blocked (or throw impacts) before the item breaks into debris of its material. Guns: Dur. counts pistol-whip hits only; Ammo is rounds; the Dmg, Reach and Startup columns are the whip, and the bullet and the aim are in the use column.

| Id | Item | Class | Dur. / ammo | Dmg | Reach m | Startup | Thrown dmg | Distinct use | Its answer | Cap (worst case) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| knife | Knife | light | 10 | 8 | 0.30 | 4 | 7 | Lunge: the 3rd step reaches 0.25 m farther (0.55) | Sway or sidestep: the string is short and fast, a Block pays 1.5x stamina three times | string 44.4 |
| cutter | Box cutter | light | 6 | 5 | 0.15 | 4 | 4 | A 4-step string (5, 5, 6, 6): the longest string, the least damage per step | Block: each hit is 5 base, the 1.5x stamina cost is the smallest of any weapon | string 36.3 |
| broken | Broken bottle | light | 3 | 7 | 0.35 | 5 | 4 | Jagged: each landed step adds 10 ticks of stun (a bottle's SHATTER_STUN), so one landed hit opens the whole string; leaves a glass patch when it wears out | Sidestep or Sway the first step (a Block wears it down: 3 hits and it breaks) | string 38.8 |
| tyre | Tyre iron | heavy | 10 | 12 | 0.65 | 9 | 10 | Pry: **any** landed step makes the foe drop the item in hand (other weapons disarm only on a strong step, a knock-down or a throw); metal, so it arcs an electric panel | Sway or sidestep (the last step is strong and breaks a plain Block); the answer to an armed goon | string 39.3 |
| golf | Golf club | two-handed | 6 | 11 | 1.15 | 11 | 6 | Drive: the last step pushes 2.0 (the bat's is 0.9): wall, hazard and ring-out tool, no knock-down | Sidestep or Sway (a Block is shoved back 2.0) | string 36.1 |
| pistol | Pistol | throwable | 6 / 5 rounds | 3 | 0.15 | 6 | 4 | Bullet 4 base, aim 18 ticks, recovery 12: fast chip that interrupts (hit-stun 16) | Block, Sway or sidestep | magazine 33.5 + throw 6.7 = 40.2 |
| revolver | Revolver | throwable | 6 / 3 rounds | 4 | 0.15 | 6 | 5 | Bullet 7 base, aim 28 ticks, recovery 20: a slow, heavy shot for a foe that is stuck or far | Sway or sidestep (long tell); Block pays 9.5 stamina | magazine 35.1 + throw 8.3 = 43.4 |

Placement (the item's mesh and sound follow the P7-07 and P18-28 rules; the item count of a level stays at 10 or fewer, `ITEM_MAX` 12 leaves room for drops): Warehouse: box cutter on the workbench (0.9) replaces the floor brick; Gym: golf club on the locker bracket beside the broom (1.3), +1 (7); Pit: the second bar bottle becomes a broken bottle; Rooftop: a tyre iron replaces one floor brick; Subway: knife on the kiosk counter (0.9), +1 (9); Garage: a tyre iron replaces the wrench on car A (0.63); Construction: box cutter on carton stack B replaces the brick there (0.9); Club: the bottle on table B becomes a broken bottle. No gun is placed.

**The cap (a full magazine cannot end a full-health round).** Worst case = strength 10 (damage 0.75 + 10 x 0.05 = 1.25), Momentum boost on (`BOOST_DAMAGE_MULT` 1.15), defender's defense 1 (taken 1.2 - 0.04 = 1.16), a plain hit (no counter, no stun state). The thrown path has no combo scale and no stamina penalty, and a bullet is a plain hit (no `impact` factor). The smallest full-health bar is 90 HP (health 1: 85 + 5), and the Health rule can halve it to 45 (hpScale 0.5), so the cap is **45 HP: no new item may take 45 from a full bar in one magazine or one string**.
- Pistol: 4 x 1.25 x 1.15 x 1.16 = 6.67, shown as 6.7; 5 rounds = 33.5; plus the empty gun thrown (also 4 base) 6.7 = 40.2, under 45. Typical case (strength 5, defense 5): 4.0 a bullet, 20 for the magazine.
- Revolver: 7 x 1.25 x 1.15 x 1.16 = 11.67, shown as 11.7; 3 rounds = 35.1; plus the throw 5 x 1.6675 = 8.3 = 43.4, under 45. Typical: 7 a bullet, 21 for the magazine.
- Melee strings: multiplier 1.25 x 1.08 (right-hand weapon) x 1.15 x 1.16 = 1.8009, strong steps also x the defender's impact 1.12 = 2.017, `COMBO_SCALE` 1, 1, 0.9, 0.8 for the 1st to 4th hit. Knife: 8, 8, 9.6 x 0.9 give 14.4 + 14.4 + 15.6 = 44.4. Box cutter: 5, 5, 6 x 0.9, 6 x 0.8 give 9.0 + 9.0 + 9.7 + 8.6 = 36.3. Broken bottle: 7, 7, 8.4 x 0.9 give 12.6 + 12.6 + 13.6 = 38.8. Tyre iron: 8.4 (12 x 0.7) x 1.8009 = 15.1, then the strong step 12 x 2.017 = 24.2, total 39.3. Golf club: 7.7 x 1.8009 = 13.9, then 11 x 2.017 = 22.2, total 36.1. The old bat (52.5) and chair (59) are above the cap and are not changed: the cap binds the new items.
- Several rounds can never be combined past the cap by one gun (no reload, no ammo pick-up); at most 2 loaded guns exist in a fight (loadout rule below); a bullet that the defender blocks, sways or sidesteps deals nothing. Against a goon's gun the numbers are far lower because the bullet takes the shooter's damage factor: a goon's strength 5 (1.0) x `GOON_SCALE` damage x the level's damage: Pistol per magazine about 7.5 (Easy), 8.2 (Normal), 9.1 (Hard), 6.4 (Expert); a leader (x1.3) 9.8 (Easy), 10.6, 11.8, 8.3; Revolver (leader) 11.1 (Normal), 12.4 (Hard), 8.7 (Expert), at defense 5. A gun's danger is the 16-tick hit-stun that lets melee goons in, not its damage.

#### Armed goons: the loadout (what BP-P18-68 builds)

Rules: loadouts exist only in the four Arcade brawl stages (1, 3, 5, 6) and only with Items on. Goons enter unarmed today; this adds an item in the hand at `enterEnemy`. **The first stage with a gun is stage 5** (the champion's crew leader carries a Pistol on Normal, Hard and Expert); on Easy the first gun is stage 6. Easy has fewer armed goons than every other level at every stage.

Armed goons per wave (the number of goons of a wave that enter armed). Columns W1 to W3 are the first three waves, W4 the 4th wave (levels with 5 waves only: Subway, Construction, Club; the Warehouse and the Garage have no W4), L the last wave (leader and crew). Totals in brackets are for 4-wave / 5-wave levels.

| Stage (crew, level) | Easy | Normal | Hard | Expert |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (rival A's crew, home level, 3 waves of 3, 4, 5 goons = 12, no leader) | W1-W3: 0-0-1 (1) | 0-1-1 (2) | 1-1-2 (4) | 1-2-2 (5) |
| 3 (the boss's crew, leader goon; waves 3, 4, 5, (6), 6) | W1-W3, W4, L: 0-1-1, 1, 1 (3 / 4) | 1-1-1, 2, 2 (5 / 7) | 1-1-2, 2, 3 (7 / 9) | 1-2-2, 3, 3 (8 / 11) |
| 5 (the champion's crew, leader goon; same waves) | 1-1-1, 1, 1 (4 / 5) | 1-1-2, 2, 2 (6 / 8) | 1-2-2, 3, 3 (8 / 11) | 2-2-3, 3, 3 (10 / 13) |
| 6 (the Club, 5 waves, one more goon in each wave with the ally: 4, 5, 6, 6, 6 = 27; after "Walk away": rival A leads and is never armed, and the cell's count is then taken from the other goons of the wave) | 1-1-1, 1, 1 (5) | 1-2-2, 2, 2 (9) | 2-2-3, 3, 3 (13) | 2-3-3, 3, 3 (14) |

On screen at once at most 1 (Easy), 2 (Normal), 3 (Hard) or 3 (Expert) armed enemies: a goon that would enter while the cap is full enters unarmed (decided from the live state, so it is the same every run of the same seed). At most 2 loaded guns are carried by enemies at once on every level (a third goon gets the next item down in its column).

What each goon type carries (variants are dealt in turn by `waveCursor % 3`, so every wave mixes the types):

| Goon | Stage 1 | Stage 3 | Stage 5 | Stage 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BRUISER | Escrima stick | Tyre iron | Baseball bat (waves 1 and 3), Golf club (waves 2, 4) | Golf club |
| SCRAPPER | Broken bottle | Knife | Knife | Knife |
| RUNNER | Box cutter | Box cutter | Bike chain | Bike chain; Hard and Expert: the Pistol in the last wave |
| Leader (`g:L`) | none (no leader) | Baseball bat | Pistol (Easy: Baseball bat) | Revolver (Easy: Pistol) |

Guns per fight: stage 5 one Pistol (the leader, last wave); stage 6 the leader's Revolver (Easy: Pistol) and, on Hard and Expert, a Runner's Pistol in the last wave: two loaded guns at most. Every other item is one the game already has.

Which goons are armed, deterministic: when a wave is called its slots are put in an arming order from a stream of their own (the way `spawnItems` places items, so the match's random sequence never moves): `makeRng((cfg.seed ^ 0x3c6ef372 ^ Math.imul(wave + 1, 0x9e3779b1)) >>> 0)`, a Fisher-Yates shuffle of the wave's non-leader slots, always the same number of draws whatever the difficulty. The order is: the leader first (when the table gives the leader an item), on stage 6 Hard and Expert in the last wave the first Runner (the gun), then the shuffled rest; the first N goons of that order are armed (N = the table cell). The same seed gives the same armed goons on every run, and since only N changes with the difficulty, the armed goons of Easy are always among those of Normal, of Normal among Hard, of Hard among Expert (the items of a leader differ by level, see the table). `Story.seedOf` already gives a retry a new seed, so a retry has other armed goons.

When a goon is disarmed or knocked out: the existing rules apply and are not changed (a landed strong step, any knock-down, any throw and a knock-out all make `Fighter.dropHeld` drop the item at the goon's feet through `dropItem` and `addItem`). Pry from the Tyre iron adds one more disarm. The item keeps its durability and a gun keeps its rounds, so the person can pick up a loaded gun and fire it (a person's pick-up is the one Use press as today). The 12 loose items cap holds: `addItem` removes first an **empty gun** that lies about (new rule: it is the least useful loose item), then as today the oldest resting item that is not on a host. A bullet is never counted. A goon that is knocked out holding nothing drops nothing. Armed goons who carry a melee item and are disarmed fetch another by the old `considerPickup` rules; no goon fetches an empty gun.

Cost of an armed crew (the starting table, to be fitted): the table is the **starting value**. BP-P18-68 re-runs the P18-21 fit with `BREAKPOINT.simulate` (Arcade `Story.cfg` stages, a Hard AI person as P18-21 did, `evenDamage: false`, n = 24 per stage and level, Normal re-confirmed at n = 50): the clear rates must stay inside the P18-21 bands (Normal 40 to 70 percent at stages 3, 5 and 6; Hard 40 to 60; Expert 20 to 40) and the Arcade length inside P18-20's band; if they do not, the armed counts in the table move down (not `GOON_SCALE`), and the changed cells are written back here. Easy is not fitted to the old numbers: the owner finds Easy too easy (the 2026-11-10 list; the Easy balance is BP-P18-52), so a lower Easy clear rate is wanted, and Easy gets no armed goon until stage 1's last wave.

#### Free choices (the owner can change any of these; the default is what is written above)

- Gun numbers: ammo 5 and 3; bullet damage 4 and 7; empty-throw damage 4 and 5; aim 18 and 28 ticks; recovery 12 and 20; bullet speed 24 m/s and range 12 m. Raising any must keep the cap (45 HP: the arithmetic above is the check).

- Not decided, default no: a gun on level floors or in Free Fight or Versus (it would let a Versus player start with a gun; default: guns come only from armed goons); armed goons in the Free Fight crowd or in Survival; a Training scenario "a sparring partner fires at you from 5 m" (cheap, about 400 bytes, nothing else needed; recommended if the owner finds the guns hard to learn); a separate Guns setting (Items off already removes them; a row would cost menu space on a phone); Tournament guns (kept off even if a later Tournament rule turns Items on, by the Tournament's `items: false`).
- Rejected: an aiming input or a crosshair (P1-03's reason stands for it); reloading, ammo pick-ups and a gun that never runs dry; automatic weapons and a shotgun spread (a spread needs random numbers: online determinism); an instant (hit-scan) bullet or a bullet with no aim tell (unanswerable); head shots and critical hits (the bullet is a plain hit); a lead on the aim (it would remove the sidestep); guns for main fighters in duels (duels stay a martial-arts bout); blood, bleeding, kills and any lethal text (P1-03); swords, nunchaku and axes (still rejected by P1-04); a 15th class (the guns are throwables); a loaded gun thrown by a tap; goons that fetch an empty gun.

### P18-60 built: the intro and the title song (2026-11-10)

- Scope: BP-P18-60 (owner 2026-11-10: an intro before the main menu, 6 s, the track from its first beat into the menu, `Hikari Samurai.mid` as the main track). Branch `bp-p18-60-intro` from main f281949. Files: `breakpoint.html`, `breakpoint-tests.js`, this appendix, and one new script `tools/midi-to-song.js`. No dependency, no setting, no new on-screen button; the sim is untouched (nothing in the intro reads or writes the seeded RNG; the picture uses `makeRng` with fixed seeds, the audio `Math.random` only for noise offsets, as the music does).
- **Test hook for the Chrome gate and the tests (HANDOFF "How to test" needs one line).** The intro is an overlay (`#intro`, z-index 35) over a menu that is already live: `Game.state` is `MENU` and `BREAKPOINT.diagnostics().state === 'MENU'` from boot, so the tests' menu wait and `BREAKPOINT.selfTest()` from the main menu work with no change. The overlay only reacts to trusted events (`isTrusted`): the synthetic key and pointer events of the self-tests pass it by, and the gamepad menu actions are held back while it is up (`UI.update`). For a page that should have no overlay at all (screenshots of the menu, a Playwright run that presses real keys or taps) load it with `?nointro` (or `#nointro`; a debug `?brawl` also skips the intro), or call `BREAKPOINT.skipIntro()` on a loaded page (card or reveal ends at once, silence). **The Chrome gate URL uses `?nointro`** (`.../breakpoint.html?nointro&nocache=<Date.now()>`); as a safety net `UI.runSelfTest` also calls `Intro.skip()` first, so a card left up cannot hold back the gamepad and menu tests (without it they passed only through the side effect of `Game.beginMatch` calling `Intro.skip()`).
- **Flow.** Load: the card (BREAKPOINT logo, "PRESS ANY KEY OR TAP TO START" over the dark arena picture) waits for ever. A real key (not a modifier, F-key, Escape, Ctrl/Alt/Meta shortcut or held repeat; Escape is no gesture for the browser's audio, so it passes through to the menu), a tap (on release: that is the touch a browser accepts as the audio gesture) or a new gamepad button press starts it: `Sound.unlock()` runs in the same gesture, and when the audio runs (at most `INTRO_ARM_MS` 800 ms of waiting, e.g. a gamepad press that the browser does not count as a gesture; then the reveal plays without sound and the song is never started) the reveal and `Song.start()` begin together. The reveal is 6 s (18 beats of 180 bpm) on the audio clock (`Song.position()` minus the output latency); at 6 s the overlay fades out (0.3 s) and the song plays on in the menu to its end at 28 s, then silence. A key or tap during the reveal (after a 350 ms guard, held keys never) stops the song (80 ms fade) and opens the menu in silence; a touch skip keeps the faded overlay in the way until it is gone so the end of that tap does not press a menu button. A frozen audio clock (a call, a hidden tab) freezes the picture with the song; a watchdog ends the intro after 8 s of frames so it cannot hang. A fight (`Music.start` at intensity above 0) stops the song (0.25 s fade) and any intro still up. Entering the menu again never restarts the song: only the intro starts it (`Song.starts` is 1 per page load). **Known limit:** when the reveal played silent (a gamepad press the browser did not take as a gesture, or no audio), a later key or tap on the menu does NOT start the song late: it is not played that load (a test pins it). While the card or reveal is up, `#screens` is `inert` and the focus is in the card (`role=dialog`, `tabindex=-1`); at the end the menu is live again and takes the focus.
- **The menu is silent (owner: "no code-made menu theme"); that also silences character select, arena select, settings and results.** The code-made theme used to play on every menu screen (it started at the main menu and went on through them); the owner's words ("the menu is silent", "no code-made menu theme") were taken to cover all of them. Only the title song, once, is heard there. The intensity 0 branch of `Music.schedule` (pad and arpeggio) is deleted, `Music.update` returns after `syncAmbience(null)` at intensity 0, and the test table's "music menu theme" row (P18-29, target -22 dBFS) is replaced by "music title song". Every menu screen (character select, settings, results) is silent unless the song is still playing; the fight music and its tense layer are unchanged. `Music.update` pumps the song first, so `syncAmbience` is still called every frame as the P18-29 note asked.
- **Embedding.** The song is a table, not the .mid bytes. Every note of the file starts on a sixteenth (120 ticks of 480) and lasts whole sixteenths, every velocity is 76, the pitch bends are all 0, the rhythm guitar plays one shape (root, fifth, octave: 136 chords of 3 notes and 8 single notes). `tools/midi-to-song.js` (the one source is `music/hikari-samurai.mid`) reads the file with its own small parser and refuses anything off those rules; `node tools/midi-to-song.js` prints the block, `--check` exits 1 unless `breakpoint.html` holds exactly that block (and prints the facts: 180 bpm, 336 steps = 28 s, drums 279, rhythm 416, lead 103, high 36, bass 72 notes), `--write` replaces the block between the `// song-data:begin` and `// song-data:end` markers keeping CRLF and the BOM. Format: drums = one base 64 digit per step (a bit per drum: kick 35, snare 38, open hat 46, high tom 50, crash 57), voices = 3 digits per onset (steps since the last onset, 2 x length in steps + 1 for a power chord, pitch - 24). **Byte cost: the data block 1,966 bytes (LF), the decoder and synth (`Song`) about 9,200, the intro (`introFrame`, `Intro`, constants) about 14,900, CSS 1,000, test-api and hooks 700: `breakpoint.html` 1,408,766 to 1,437,518 bytes with LF, +28,752** (after the review fixes) (budget 4,000,000). The test file grows by the new tests.
- **Synth (all on `Song.nodes.out`, one gain node that connects to `Sound.musicBus`, so the Music volume, the heartbeat muffle and the pause duck act on it; its tail fade is a gain ramp, a stop a gain target).** Distortion guitars (rhythm power chords, lead, high lead): a sawtooth per note through a per-note envelope into one shared bus, a `WaveShaper` (tanh(3x) soft clip, 513 points), a cabinet (high-pass 90 Hz, low-pass 3.8 kHz) and a post gain; lead notes of 0.3 s or more get vibrato (one shared 5.5 Hz LFO, 18 cents, into each note's detune); chugged chords (2 steps or less) are gated at 75 %. Electric bass: a sawtooth and a square an octave up (10 %) through an 800 Hz low-pass. Drums from the shared noise buffer (looped, so a 1.1 s crash cannot run out, the P18-29 lesson) and sines: kick (150 to 45 Hz over 0.12 s), snare (band-pass noise 1.9 kHz + a 190 Hz triangle), open hat (high-pass 7 kHz, 0.22 s), high tom (220 to 130 Hz), crash (high-pass 4.5 kHz, 1.1 s). Scheduling: a look-ahead pump (`SONG_AHEAD_SECS` 0.5 s) from `Music.update` each frame on the audio clock, never `setTimeout` timing; a step that a stalled frame left more than 0.1 s behind is dropped, not played in a burst. Mix constants in `SONG_MIX`; peaks were set by arithmetic (the shaped guitars about 0.17, bass 0.3, kick 0.55), **not heard**: the self-test row "music title song" renders the first four seconds offline in Chrome (it must peak under -1 dBFS, not be silent, and be silent with Music at 0) and the owner's ears (P16-03) are the last word on balance against the fight bed.
- **The reveal (all code, no copied logo).** A dark arena (back wall, floor with a perspective grid, a row of heads along the horizon, three spotlights), the title as two words (BREAK, POINT) in the Impact-italic style of `h1.logo` that smash in on the first two rhythm chords (steps 16 and 24, 1.33 s and 2.0 s: 2.2 times size shrinking over 0.1 s), cracks that grow after each landing and one across the title at step 32, dust off the floor from the biggest landings, a short shake on every impact (scaled by the Camera shake setting over its default, as the fights' shake; 0 = none) and a white flash on the four biggest only (steps 16, 24, 32, 70), the snare roll of bars 5 and 6 (steps 64 to 71) building to the menu at step 72. The table `INTRO_IMPACTS` is keyed to steps where the song has a drum hit or a chord (a test checks it). `introFrame(g, w, h, p, look)` is a pure function of the time: it draws the same picture for the same time on any screen, so a stall or a skip cannot desync it. Layout: the longer word takes 84 % of the width (size capped by 27 % of the height), checked at 390 x 844 and 844 x 390. The picture is drawn at most 1.2 million pixels big. **Reduced motion**: no shake, no flash, no dust, no slam, the heads do not bob and the lights do not sway; the words and the cracks fade in. The Flashes setting scales the flash (Reduced = the same 0.3 cap as the fights, Off = none). The song's vibrato oscillator is stopped with the song when it is cut short. The card's prompt blinks only without Reduced motion (the global `.reduced` rule).
- Self-tests (names start `Intro`): the table decodes to the file (counts per voice, pitches, first steps, 180 bpm, 28 s, the grid, time order, the last note ends with the song); the song is handed over a little ahead, nothing late or left out, every source stops by the end of the tail, one gain node to the music bus, Music volume 0 sets the bus to 0; a stalled frame drops late steps, a stop silences it for good, a new start begins at step 0; the menu schedules nothing at intensity 0, the fight music does, a fight stops the song, entering the menu again does not restart it; the card waits for ever and only a trusted key or tap starts it (not synthetic events, modifiers, F-keys, Ctrl shortcuts, held keys); the reveal ends at 6 s and the song plays on to its end then nothing is scheduled; a skip stops the song (not inside the 350 ms guard, not on a held key); no audio support and a suspended context (silent reveal after the wait, or the song when the audio starts first); a frozen clock freezes the picture and the watchdog ends it; a gamepad (held button, new press, skip, the menu below does not move); the flags; the picture (finite numbers, the title inside both phone shapes, a landing hits, Reduced motion and Flashes Off show no slam, shake, flash or dust, the fade); the timeline against the song; the overlay in a layout engine (Chrome only); the touch path (start on release, skip on press, untrusted taps, every listener removed); `UI.runSelfTest` takes the card down; the card going up as boot puts it up (`Intro.init`: focused dialog, `#screens` inert, a second call and the flags put up nothing; Chrome only); the real `Intro.draw` reading Reduced motion, Flashes (Reduced under the fights' cap) and the Camera shake scale; Escape ignored; no late song after a silent reveal; the vibrato stopped with a stopped song.

### P18-69 mobile-first menu layout, decided (2026-11-10)

- Scope: BP-P18-69 (owner 2026-11-10: "Audit menus for best layout that is mobile first and can work properly both in landscape and vertically (for example in landscape i think i cant use the character creator at all)"). Audit and decision only: no game code changed. Base: main 04bf47a, branch `bp-p18-69-menus`. The evidence (the screenshot matrix and 23 findings L01 to L23) is in Appendix D, "P18-69 mobile-first menu audit". BP-P18-70 builds the fixes below. Line numbers are `breakpoint.html` at 04bf47a.
- **Why the creator cannot be used in landscape (root cause).** The creator panel (`.panel.cr`, CSS 90) takes its height from one media query that is meant for a phone held upright but also matches a phone held sideways: `@media (orientation:portrait),(max-width:760px)` (CSS 143 to 147) sets `.panel.cr{width:100%;height:60%}` and `.screen.creator{align-items:flex-end}`. Every landscape phone that is 760 px wide or less (667x375, 640x360 and the like) matches the `max-width` part, so the panel is 60 % of the height (217 px at 375). The landscape rule below it (CSS 148 to 156) resets only the width, never the height. The panel's fixed parts are the title (19 px), the tab row (57 px), the button row (58 px) and padding, 147 px together, so the list of options gets 60 px (667x375) or 51 px (640x360): one row. On wider landscape phones (844x390) the panel is full height, but the same parts still take 157 px and the list gets 220 px (170 px at 844x340, where a browser bar takes 50 px); the button row is also forced to one line that scrolls sideways (`.tabs, .cr-foot{flex-wrap:nowrap;overflow-x:auto}`, CSS 152), so Fight preview is off the right edge and Save is cut, with no sign that it scrolls. Upright phones have the same fault in another form: the panel is 60 % again, the six tabs wrap to two rows (93 px, `.tab{flex:1 1 4.5em}`, CSS 96) and the six buttons to three rows (151 px, CSS 103 to 104), 296 px of parts; the list gets 177 px at 390x844, 54 px at 360x640 and 13 px at 320x568. With a keyboard open (the viewport gets shorter) the list gets 13 to 20 px and the name field sits under the button row. Nothing in the layout reads the real height of what it must hold: heights are percentages and the parts are fixed.
- **Layout rules (one set for every screen; BP-P18-70 builds them, the layout test holds them).**
  1. Shapes, not devices. Three queries only: `portrait` = `(orientation:portrait)`, `short` = `(orientation:landscape) and (max-height:520px)`, `narrow` = `(max-width:520px)`. Never `max-width` to mean "upright phone" (CSS 143 is the bug). A rule for a width above 520 px is plain CSS with `min()` and `clamp()`, not a query. Phones in landscape get the same layout from 640x360 to 932x430.
  2. Safe areas stay as they are: `.screen` keeps its transparent border of `--sat --sar --sab --sal` (CSS 30), `#hud` and `#touch` keep their insets, `viewport-fit=cover` stays. Nothing new is placed with `position:fixed` outside `#app`.
  3. One vertical scroller per screen: the `.panel` (the creator: `.cr-body`). The page and `.screen` never scroll sideways, and no panel, row, tab bar or button row scrolls sideways; the only sideways scroller is the tournament bracket box (it is a picture, and says so in its sub line). A table that is wider than 360 px becomes stacked rows under `narrow` (rule 8). The sticky Back / Confirm row stays (P18-17 F5); in `short` it is at most 52 px high.
  4. Touch target: every button, row, card, tab, swatch, arrow and chip is at least 44 x 44 CSS px, in every shape (no `min-height:2.3em` in `short`, CSS 361). Room in landscape comes from smaller padding and gaps, never from smaller targets. Text is at least 12 px; 11 px is allowed only for a badge that repeats a longer label. Two controls never overlap, and a control never sits under a sticky row or the HUD.
  5. What a screen may hide: only content that scrolls vertically in its own panel, never a control behind a sideways scroll, never the only control for a function behind a long press or a tool tip. Hints may be hidden (`.cr-keys` already is) but not a control or its state.
  6. Portrait: one column; the panel is at most 100 % of the width and at most 88 % of the height; the 3D picture, when a screen has one (creator, fighter select), keeps at least the top 28 % or 190 px. Landscape (`short`): panel and picture side by side, the panel on the side with more room (as now), the picture strip at least 30 % of the width; the panel is the full height of the screen minus the safe area. Lists of cards (fighters, levels) use 3 columns in `short` (`minmax(8em,1fr)`), 2 under `narrow`, auto above.
  7. Long lists and two-column screens: a two-column screen (the Controls and result tables, Players and teams, the lobby rows) has a narrow form where every row is one stacked block (label above, controls below), built with `grid-template-areas` as `.onrow` does (CSS 272 to 276, P12-06). Results: the action buttons are one sticky row at the bottom of the panel in `short` (as every setup screen), not at the end of the stats.
  8. Font scaling: the base is 16 px times `--ui` (Settings, 0.8 to 1.5). The effective scale is capped by the width so that a screen never scrolls sideways: `min(setting, (width - 24) / 300)`: 1.22 at 390, 1.12 at 360, 0.98 at 320, the full 1.5 from 474 px. Text uses `em` from the panel; no fixed `px` font under 12 px; headings use `clamp()`.
  9. Focus, gamepad and keyboard: the order of `[data-nav]`, `data-default`, the P18-17 looks (one focus look, one remembered-pick look), `scroll-padding-bottom:5em` and the Coach strip are unchanged. One change: a screen opens at the top of its panel (the first focus uses `preventScroll:true`), so the title is not scrolled away by a Back or Start button at the bottom (L12). The one exception is a screen whose default is a remembered pick (`.sel`: the fighter cards, the level list): it scrolls to the pick, as now. Later focus moves scroll as now.
  10. Keyboard (soft): while a text field of a panel has focus the panel is in "typing" mode: its tab row and button row are hidden, the field is scrolled to the middle, and the panel takes the whole free height. Leaving the field restores them. No screen depends on the viewport being as high as at load.
- **Creator layout.** Portrait: the picture on top, the panel under it, `height:clamp(18em,72%,calc(100% - 11em))`; title one line; six tabs in one row of equal buttons when the panel is at least 340 px wide, else a 3 x 2 grid (two rows of 44 px); the six buttons in one row from 520 px and a 3 x 2 grid under `narrow` (two rows of 44 px, not three); by the sums of the fixed parts the list gets about 380 px at 390x844 (now 177), 200 px at 360x640 (now 54) and 150 px at 320x568 (now 13). The same six buttons and tabs, in the same order, with the same texts: no button is added or removed. Landscape (`short`): picture strip on the left (at least 30 % of the width, the fighter fully in view as now), panel on the right, `width:min(44em,72vw)`, the full height, padding .2em, tabs one row (44 px plus 5), button row one row of six that wraps to two rows instead of scrolling when the panel is under 480 px (`flex:1 1 auto; min-width:0; font-size:.7em; letter-spacing:.03em`); the list gets about 245 px at 844x390 (now 220), 195 px at 844x340 (now 170) and 190 to 235 px at 667x375 (now 60; the lower figure if the buttons need two rows). These are sums, not measurements: the layout test measures them. Both: the fitness pad is `min(9em,30vh)` high, the photo crop square is `min(16em,72vw,42vh)` and in `short` the crop dialog is two columns (square left, rows and buttons right). The preview camera and `CreatorUI.measureFocus` stay as they are: the panel's left edge still tells the camera where the free strip is.
- **Fix list for BP-P18-70, in this order** (sizes are LF bytes added to `breakpoint.html`; the tests are in `breakpoint-tests.js` and do not count against the game file; total about 4,900 bytes, 0.4 % of the file, budget 4,000,000):

  | Step | Fixes | What | Bytes |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 0 | all | Write the layout test first (below) and watch it fail on L01 to L16. | 0 (tests about 7,500) |
  | 1 | L01, L02, L06 | Creator in `short`: change the query at CSS 143 to `(orientation:portrait)`, drop `align-items:flex-end` and `height:60%` for landscape, compact the chrome, the button row wraps (no `overflow-x`), panel `width:min(44em,72vw)`. | 600 |

### P12-08 built: deterministic simulation math (2026-11-10)

- Scope: BP-P12-08 (Appendix D row J01). Branch `bp-p12-08-math` from main 9d73ccb. Files: `breakpoint.html`, `breakpoint-tests.js`, this appendix. Only the arithmetic of the simulation changed; no move, damage, timing or AI rule did.
- **DMath.** One small object (`DMath`, in the core section after `wrapAngle`, about 6.0 KB with its comments): `hypot(x, z)` = `Math.sqrt(x * x + z * z)`, `sin`, `cos`, `atan2` and `exp`, built from + - * / sqrt and floor / round / abs only, which every engine rounds the same (the library functions may differ in the last bit; that one bit is what put Chromium, Firefox and WebKit out of step in P12-03). `sin` and `cos` reduce the angle to quarter turns with the three-piece pi / 2 of fdlibm (exact for up to 2^20 quarter turns, so angles up to about 1.6 million rad; beyond 1e6 the angle is first taken modulo 2 pi) and use the fdlibm kernel polynomials; `atan2` is the fdlibm atan with its four ranges and the signed-zero and infinity rules of `Math.atan2`; `exp` is the fdlibm one (k ln 2 plus a polynomial, k doublings by multiplication, so no `pow`). Accuracy against `Math.*` (the test `DMath (P12-08, J01)` holds these limits on 80 001 angles from -55 to 55 rad, 20 000 directions at radii 1e-3 to 1e3 and 30 001 exponents from -30 to 6: 3.4e-16 absolute for sin and cos (1.5 ulp, so that an engine whose own sin is only good to 1 ulp passes too; the hash is the cross-engine proof), 2.3e-16 relative to max(1, the angle) for atan2 (the engine's own atan2 is 1 ulp, 4.4e-16, away near pi in Chromium and WebKit), 4.5e-16 relative for exp, 5e-16 relative for hypot, i.e. sqrt of a sum within about 1.5 ulp; the signs of the special values -0, +-Infinity and NaN match). Measured worst cases against V8 on denser samples (4 million angles in -4 pi to 4 pi, in -1000 to 1000 and 2 million in 0 to 1e5, 2 million exponents in -3 to 0 and in -50 to 50, 3 million directions): sin and cos 1.1e-16 absolute (2.2e-16 for cos near 1e5 rad), atan2 bit-equal to V8 on all 3 million directions (V8 uses the same fdlibm code), exp bit-equal in -3 to 0 and within 1 ulp in -50 to 50; relative errors next to a zero of sin or cos reach 10 ulp, where the absolute error is 5e-31 (the dropped tail of the pi / 2 split).
- **Replaced: 123 sites.** 86 `hypot`, 12 `sin`, 11 `cos`, 8 `atan2` and 2 `exp` calls in method bodies, plus the four load-time cone constants (`PICKUP_CONE_COS`, `SPRAY_CONE_COS`, `LOCK_VIEW_COS`, `LOCK_STICK_COS`, now `DMath.cos(degrees * Math.PI / 180)`). Where: `Fighter` (the `fwdX` / `fwdZ` getters, `faceOpponent`, `updateFree`, `integrate` (the knock-back damping `exp(-k * dt)`), `animate` (the `liftY` decay, which `Fighter` reads when a hold breaks), `guardWalking`, `stepRoom`), all of `Combat`, all of `AIController`, `DummyController` and `CrowdDirector` (the ring slots), `MatchSim` (line-up and wave placement, `readStick`, `softFace`, items, hazards, `separate`, `stepEdge`, `stepBodies`), and `Arena.linkConductors` / `gap`. Left on `Math.*` because they only pose, draw, aim a camera or play a sound and no checksum field reads them: the pose methods of `Fighter` (`computePose`, `levelTorso`, `walkLegs`, `clinchPose` and the other pose builders), `MatchSim.itemDebris`, `hazardParticles`, `drawFlames`, `loadHidesFighter`, `drawHazards`, the `Arena.draw*` methods and `lampAngle`, `hash01`, `Camera`, `Showcase`, `Cutscene`, `FX`, `R`, `M4`, `Sound`, `Music`, `UI`, `PlayerInput` (the stick and the camera yaw become a finished intent before they are sent, and every peer plays the decoded byte value, J06). `Tournament` uses `Math.log2` of 4, 8 or 16, which is exact in every engine and is not in a tick.
- **Rule and test.** `DMath (P12-08, J01)`: DMath against `Math.*` on the dense samples above with the limits above, the special values, and one fnv1a hash of a fixed 20 000-number sample (the constant `DMATH_SAMPLE_HASH`): the same constant in Chrome, Firefox and Safari is the cross-engine proof the owner can run on a phone. `Determinism: no transcendental Math call in the simulation (P12-08, J01)`: the simulation code of `breakpoint.html` sits between `// <<SIM BEGIN: name>>` and `// <<SIM END>>` comments (12 sections: the core maths and random (`TAU`, `clamp`, `wrapAngle`, `DMath` itself, `makeRng`); the `ITEMS` and `WEAPONS` tables; `newHeld` and the `HAZARDS` table; `aimFromIntent` and `escapeStartFor`; the weapon move builders `weaponSwing`, `makeWeaponMove`, `weaponTable`; all of `Fighter`; `Combat`; the CPU and the training dummy; the match section with `coopEnemyCount`, `MatchLineup`, the controllers, `koEndsFight`, `CrowdDirector`, `MatchSim`, `SimRunner`; the online lockstep with the input codes, `matchChecksum`, `NetSeatController`, `LockstepSession`; `Arena`), and the test scans everything between the markers as text (the page script comes from `document.scripts`; `tools/run-tests.js` now gives its stub document the same list), constructors, static methods, setters and nested objects included, for sin, cos, tan, atan, atan2, asin, acos, the hyperbolic ones, exp, log, pow, hypot, cbrt, `Math[` and any `**` (its exponent could have a fraction; none is in a section). Cut out of the scan are only the methods named in the test's `VISUAL` list (the `Fighter` pose methods, `MatchSim.itemDebris`, `hazardParticles`, `loadHidesFighter`, `lampAngle` and the 20 `draw...` methods of `Arena`, `Fighter` and `MatchSim`, each named one by one: a new simulation method called `draw...` is scanned); a name in the list that is not in a section any more fails, the section markers must pair up, 32 named objects and helpers must lie inside them, and the scan must read at least 12 sections, 250 000 characters and 100 DMath calls. New simulation code goes between such markers; code outside them is not scanned. Proof that it bites (scratch copies, each failed naming its section): `Math.atan2` in the `MatchSim` constructor, `Math.atan2` in a new top-level helper before `koEndsFight`, `a ** 0.5` in such a helper, and `Math.hypot` in a new static method of `MatchSim`. The four cone constants are checked by value.
- **Cross-engine proof (Playwright 1.64.1: Chromium 156.0.8078.4, Firefox 157.0, WebKit 27.2; `file:` page with `?nointro`, every browser closed in `finally`).** Seven seeded matches, the state checksum (`matchChecksum`: positions, velocities, health, stamina, states, timers, items, hazards, breakables, the simRng state) taken after every tick: 1v1 (Warehouse, Hard, items and hazards, seed 23, 2400 ticks), Free Fight with ring-out and hazards (Rooftop, seed 3, 2400), Brawl with waves (Subway, 3 enemies, seed 5, 3600), a four-team lineup (seed 9, 2400), a thrown body (the P18-13 Gym ring throw at two spots, 300), a tournament fight (Dojo ring, seed 41, 2400) and a scripted person's seat against the CPU (Subway, seed 17, 2400). Before the change (main 9d73ccb) six of the seven differed between Chromium and Firefox and between Chromium and WebKit (first different tick: 1v1 11, ring-out 5 and 10, waves 1, lineup 1, tournament 22, person 1 and 2; only the thrown body was equal). After: all seven are equal in all three engines at every tick (15 900 ticks per engine), so equal at every 60th tick too. Chromium before against Chromium after differ from tick 1 (the last bits moved), which is why the fingerprints are the coordinator's to check.
- **Mixed online run.** Playwright drives the game's own Online screens (the codes pasted as text through the boxes, Add another player twice, every guest presses Ready, the host presses Start on a 4-seat Brawl in the Warehouse; the three guests and the host press direction, punch and kick keys all the time): host Chromium 156, guests Firefox 157, Chromium 156, Firefox 157 (the host screen lists the kinds: "Browser: Firefox.", "Browser: Chrome or Edge.", "Browser: Firefox." and Start is on, no warning). It ran 305 s of wall clock (start at 37 s, ended at 342 s; the browsers ran at about three quarters of real time, so about 9 500 ticks, i.e. 160 s of game time, in three matches: the first, and two the host started with Rematch when everybody had finished) with no "Out of sync", no "Connection lost", no page error and no session ended; at the end all four pages were at tick 4524 to 4529 of the third match and the checksums of frames 4380, 4440 and 4500 were equal on all four pages (the session compares every 60th frame, so every comparison of the 5 minutes passed). Playwright's WebKit has no RTCPeerConnection on Windows ("This browser has no WebRTC" on its Online screen), so WebKit cannot join a real link here: Safari against the PC stays with P16-03 (the WebKit engine itself is covered by the equal per-tick checksums above). Scripts: the scratch folder bp-p1208 (mixed.js, xeng.js), not kept in the repo.
- **Protocol version 4.** `ONLINE_NET_VERSION` is 4 (was 3): an itch build from before this change and this one now refuse each other's codes with the version message instead of connecting and falling out of step from tick 1 (the old build's maths gives other bits). Its comment now says "raised when the messages or the simulation's bits change": the next change of the simulation's arithmetic raises it again.
- **Extreme magnitudes.** `DMath.hypot` squares its arguments, so it overflows above about 1e154 and loses precision below about 1e-154 where `Math.hypot` scales; the simulation measures metres and speeds in a few hundred, so this never happens in a match.
- **The stopgap is gone.** `ONLINE_MESSAGES.sameBrowser` and `joining`, `OnlinePlay.mixedKinds` and the refusal in `OnlinePlay.start`, `OnlineUI.mixedKinds` / `joining` and their lines in `startProblem`, `ONLINE_HELLO_WAIT_MS` and its redraw timer, and the sentence "Use the same kind of browser on every device" in `ONLINE_LIMITS` are removed; the host's Start no longer waits for a guest's hello. The guest's kind is still sent (`bp-hello:`) and shown on its line ("Browser: Firefox."): it is information, not a rule. The tests that asserted the refusal now assert the opposite (a mixed set starts; a guest of another kind or one that has not said its kind does not hold Start; the limits note and the message table hold no same-browser text).

The rows are not `display:none`, so the keys and the pad still reach their buttons (`UI.moveFocus` cannot focus a `display:none` item). The class is set by the page (`syncKeyboard` in `installGlobalHandlers`), not by CSS `:has` and not by the focus alone: it is on while a creator text field (`.crin`) has the focus and `softKeyboard(visual viewport height, innerHeight, the height the page had with no field in focus)` says the visible height is more than 80 px lower. A turn of the phone with the field in focus starts the "height with no keyboard" again (`keyboardFullHeight`: the width changed), so typing mode does not come on in landscape with no keyboard. It needs no `:has`, so every browser of the target gets it. The plan used `focusin` and `focusout`; this adds the keyboard test. Honest limit: with the viewport meta as it is, the layout viewport does not shrink on current phones, so the panel keeps its height and the keyboard covers its lower part; the collapsed rows give the list room mainly in landscape, where the field stays above the keyboard. ### P18-64 collisions audited, decided (2026-11-10)

Owner, 2026-11-10: "Evaluate issues regarding collisions,hitboxes,hurtboxes and their accuracy (floating through etc)". The findings, the method and the probe matrix are in Appendix D ("P18-64 collisions, hitboxes and hurtboxes audit"); this entry is the decision on hit volumes and the order of BP-P18-65.

- **Decision: hit volumes between fighters stay stat-driven.** A strike hits by the move's `reach` times the Reach stat plus the foe's radius, its `width`, and the height class (`Combat.evaluate`); the pose is fitted to that volume (P17-02: the drawn stride, `strikeStride`), never the other way round. They do not follow the drawn limb. Reasons, with the measurements of Appendix D (342 moves of the 16 styles, foe at 9 distances and 3 side offsets, 9,234 trials, 5,462 hits):
  - The volume is already close to the limb where it matters: at the hit tick the drawn tip is within 0.2 m of the foe's body in 91.6 % of hits and within 0.3 m in 95.5 %, and only 97 hits (1.8 %) end 0.2 m or more short of the body (the rest of the outliers are tips that went on through it, below); a foe at the front of the volume is struck by a tip inside it (the P17-02 hit check, unchanged).
  - What is visibly wrong is not the reach but the pose at short range: the limb goes on to its full length whatever the distance (826 hits, 15 %, end 0.34 m or more past the foe's centre, up to 1.13 m at point blank). That is a drawing fault with a drawing fix (scale the extension to the foe's distance; K06), it needs no new hit rule.
  - Following the poses would change balance: the reach numbers are the P14-01 and P17-10 tuned values (a pose-driven volume moves with the stride, the build, the style technique and the hold of each tick; 342 moves would have 342 new hit shapes), every fingerprint and the P14-04 per-pair balance would have to be redone, and the P17-02 hit check would become a tautology. A pose is also not simulation state: it reads `Settings.v.reducedMotion` in its idle, boost and tired branches, `plantFloor` and the stance of the day; a hit rule that reads it breaks the P12-05 rule that no viewer setting reaches the simulation, and would be one more place where two engines' `Math.sin` can drift apart online.
  - The cost would be small in time (a pose and skeleton is 21.5 microseconds, 113 microseconds a whole 2-fighter tick, 319 with 8; the poses are computed every tick already) but large in tuning and tests; the gain is a few percent of hits.
- **One exception, scenery only: the hit sphere on props may follow the limb.** `Combat.hitObjects` puts a 0.4 m sphere at 0.8 of the reach at a fixed height (1.4 / 1.0 / 0.35). Props are not fighters, so no balance or fingerprint reads it (K05: 41 % of hits on a low crate have the limb 0.2 m or more away; every High hand strike hits it with the fist 0.48 m over it). BP-P18-65 sets the sphere height from the move's drawn tip height (the `strikes` cache per style and build that `strikeStride` already keeps, measured with the stride off, so it reads no viewer setting) and keeps the 0.8 reach. Hazard posts use the same sphere (`hazardStrike`): they follow it.
- **Hurt volumes stay the 0.34 m cylinder, 1.85 m high** (`Fighter.radius`, `itemStrike` top 1.85 / 1.25 crouched, `LOW_REACH_UP`, `MID_REACH_UP`): the same for every body by design (6172), the drawn body is 0.49 to 1.0 m wide. Not changed: K07 is fixed by keeping bodies off props and walls (the lying and standing extents below), not by a per-build radius, which would change reach, push and balance (a DECIDE for the owner if it is ever wanted).
- **Order of BP-P18-65** (sizes are LF bytes added to `breakpoint.html`, about 3,300 in all, 0.2 % of the file, budget 4,000,000; its tests go in `breakpoint-tests.js` and do not count; the file is 1,514,034 bytes now):

  | Step | Fixes | What | Bytes |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 0 | all | Write the tests of "Proposed tests" in Appendix D first and watch each fail. | 0 (tests about 9,000) |
  | 1 | K02 | A knocked-out body in a brawl stays solid for `KO_BODY_TICKS` (150: it is pushed out of, like any pinned body), then is skipped by `separate` and drawn fading; a wave replaces it as before. | 350; `p7-bodies.js` part C re-run: the walk through a knocked-out body in a brawl first passes at tick 172 (78 before) |
  | 2 | K01 | `Combat.evaluate`: after the reach test, a blow whose line crosses a collider (the `sightBlocked` / `crossesFootprint` rule) taller than the blow's height (0.35 Low, 1.0 Mid, 1.4 High; a grab 0.9) misses; glass blocks; a deck or a stair step does not; props the attacker stands on do not. | 450; `p12-through.js` re-run: blows that landed through a prop 223 to 44 of 303 (the rest are over props not taller than the blow) |
  | 3 | K03 | The lying direction: on the tick a body enters DOWN, KO or GETUP choose the drawn `lieYaw` among the four directions (the facing first) so that the head and the feet, 0.8 m from the centre, are inside the walls and clear of props (`Arena.insideSolid`); the body is drawn along `lieYaw`. Sim position and radius do not change. | 650; capped at 0.35 m of slide (`LIE_SLIDE_MAX`); `p9-down.js` re-run: against a wall 0.1 m or more beyond 1,134 of 1,696 to 51 (0.3 m or more 630 to 36: the Dojo ring and the Garage and Club walls, where the body needs more than the cap), against a prop 7,148 of 12,576 to 1,582 (0.3 m or more 756 to 54); AI sweep drawn pieces in props 871 to 333 samples |
  | 4 | K04 | Footing: in `resolveFighter` a standable top gives footing when the centre is within 0.15 m of its footprint (`SUPPORT_REACH`), not the whole 0.34 m cylinder; the walls and props keep the cylinder. The nav foot heights follow. | 220 |
  | 5 | K08, K09 | A non-standable top is passed only when `f.y >= c.top - 0.05`; `pushOut` leaves through the nearest side at most 0.6 m away, else it slides the body 0.3 m a tick towards it. | 300 |
  | 6 | K10 | `STAIR_UP` 0.5 to 0.3 (a tread of 0.25 plus 0.05; the Garage ramp, 0.2 m treads, would need 0.25: give `makeObject` an `up` of rise plus 0.05 for a step); the stair, ring-step and nav tests must stay green. | 60; `p8-raised.js` re-run: the largest lift of a step approach 0.5 to 0.25 m |
  | 7 | K05 | The scenery sphere height from the drawn tip height (above). | 250; `p10-prop.js` re-run: low crate hits with the limb 0.2 m or more from it 345 of 838 to 163 of 571, tall crate 14 to 13; misses with the limb inside the box 10 to 249 of 1,594 |
  | 8 | K06 | `Fighter.attackPose`: the extension is scaled by `(distance to the target - 0.3) / (the tip's forward distance at full extension)` below 1, so the tip stops about 0.1 m past the foe's centre; the stride is unchanged. Draw only. | 350 |
  | 9 | K07, K11 | Standing and walking: nothing in the sim; the lowest-part correction `plantShift` also runs for ATTACK kicks so no part goes more than 0.1 m under the floor; K07 is left to steps 1 to 5 and the owner's DECIDE above. | 150 |
  | 10 | K12 to K15 | K12: draw `grate` and `boards` decks solid (a plate and a skirt: the collider already is a block); K13: the item push-out stays inside the arena and no resting item hangs more than 30 % over an edge (`ITEM_FOOTING` test over its length); K14, K15: the Club wave spot moved 0.2 m, the nav map's ledge exemption narrowed. | 500 |

- Effect on balance: none of the steps changes a reach, width, damage, startup or frame of any move; K01 removes blows that landed through scenery (a CPU or a player standing behind a column loses that attack, the P14-04 per-pair screen is run once after step 2), K02 removes nothing from the fight except a passage, K04 and K08 change where a fighter falls by 0.2 m. The seeded fingerprints of the fights on Warehouse and Dojo are the ones to watch; re-record only what the steps 1 to 5 move and say so here.
- Not decided here, kept as they are: the drawn stride (P17-02: STRIKE_STRIDE_MAX 0.9 m, STRIKE_ROOM 0.6 m), the throw and tackle ranges, the 0.68 m body spacing, the ring-out rule (`stepRingOut`: it fires on all four levels that have it), the item and body speeds, and K07 (a per-build radius needs the owner).
- Owner device checks to add to BP-P16-03 are listed in Appendix D under "Notes for the fix".

### P18-65 built (2026-11-11)

BP-P18-65 fixes the collision, hitbox and hurtbox findings of BP-P18-64 (Appendix D, K01 to K15) in the order of the plan in "P18-64 collisions audited, decided". Branch `bp-p18-65-collide` from 346a8a6. Hit volumes between fighters stay stat-driven: no move's reach, width, damage, startup or frames changed, and no per-build radius was added. 16 tests, "Collisions (P18-65, K01)" to "(P18-65, K15)" (K01 to K10, then K11, K12, K13, K15, and a second K04 and K09 test from the review round; K14 is open, see below); each was written first and fails on the unfixed game (checked at the end with the new test file against the step 0 game, a579ae5).

- What each step does, as built (code sites by name; the line numbers moved):
  - Step 1, K02: a knocked-out body in a brawl (`!alive`) is solid for `KO_BODY_TICKS` (150) like a pinned body (`MatchSim.separate` pushes the living one out, the body does not move), then `separate` skips it; it is drawn fading from tick 150 and gone at 210 (`Fighter.koFade()`, `KO_FADE_TICKS` 60; `part()` draws on the alpha layer through `BODY_FADE`; `Fighter.bodyFades` is set for every fighter of a brawl, the enemies a wave brings included).
  - Step 2, K01: `Arena.blowBlocked(x1, z1, x2, z2, y)` in `Combat.evaluate`, after the reach test, for a strike and a grab: an active collider taller than `max(att.y, def.y) + blowHeight(mv)` (H 1.4, M 1.0, L 0.35, a grab 0.9) whose base is below it and whose footprint the line crosses stops the blow; glass stops it; a deck (so a stair step and a scaffold tier), a hazard's post, a ring rope (a rail with `bounce`) and a scaffold pole do not. The rope and the pole are beyond the plan: "Raised ground (P18-44)" strikes across the Dojo ring's edge and on scaffold tiers. The CPU counts a blocked line as out of range (`AIController.inRange`, `lineBlocked`), so it walks round a post instead of swinging at it (without that it started 25 attacks in 15 s against a post).
  - Step 3, K03: draw only. `Fighter.steerLie` (at the end of `animate`) measures the drawn box of a lying body from the simulation's own key points `pts` (plus `LIE_THICK` 0.15; a lying body is 2.0 to 2.3 m long, 0.7 to 1.2 m wide and lies up to 0.33 m off its centre), turns the drawn direction (`lieYaw`, `bodyYaw()`) to the first of the four directions (the facing, a quarter turn each way, the back) in which the box needs no room, else the one that needs least (`LIE_TURN` 0.3 rad a tick), and slides the drawn body clear of the wall or prop by the room it still needs (`lieDx`, `lieDz`, `LIE_MOVE` 0.1 m a tick, at most `LIE_SLIDE_MAX` 0.35 m in all: a body that needs more is drawn 0.35 m moved and a limb may touch, it does not jump across a prop; the frame blends from the last tick). The simulation body, its place and its 0.34 m radius are unchanged. It runs for fighters of a match only (`mates` set): the menu, the creator and the cutscenes draw their fighters where they are put.
  - Step 4, K04: `Arena.resolveFighter`: a standable top (deck, crate, bench, step) gives footing over the whole 0.34 m cylinder only to a body that rises, moves toward the footprint (jumping or stepping up onto it, landing on it) or is in line with a flight of stairs (`held`; the first version kept it on every step in every direction: round 2 below); a body that stands still or walks along or off the edge keeps it to `SUPPORT_REACH` (0.15 m) past the footprint and then falls (the first version also kept the cylinder for a body that stood still, and it hovered 0.25 to 0.3 m past a crate's edge: found by the review). The treads of a stair are as narrow as the body, so a step keeps the cylinder (a tight cylinder failed the raised-ground stair tests), but only along its flight (`Arena.alongFlight`, from the `lane` {dx, dz, prev, next} that `builtOf` gives every step): within `SUPPORT_REACH` of the flight's width and beyond an end that has a neighbouring tread of the same flight, for a body that is not walking away from the step, and also beside a deck or crate whose top is within 0.3 m of the step's (`STAIR_BESIDE_REACH` 0.4 m, `STAIR_BESIDE_HEIGHT` 0.3 m, `Arena.stepHolds`, `beside` in the collider: the CPU crosses from a flight to the deck by the corner and fell off it without this); past the sides and the open ends of a flight in the open, and walking down off a step, it is the 0.15 m rule. Two more things followed from the existing "Levels: ... a CPU goes up to a target on each deck and ledge" test, which failed with the strict rule (no arrival on the Construction 3.0 m tier and on the Subway 1.5 m deck in 700 ticks): `supportAt` (the CPU's probes) applies the same rule to a step, and the nav map counts a step only under a cell's centre (it was 0.1 m beyond), because the CPU walked along the 0.1 m margin at the side of the scaffold stair and fell off it when a blow stepped it sideways (it arrives in about 205 ticks, 233 before; the Subway deck in about 424, 418 before). A plain 0.15 m for everything made the CPU miss narrow ledges and failed the nav tests of the levels ("a CPU goes up to a target on each deck and ledge"). Walls and props keep the cylinder. `supportAt` and the nav map are unchanged except for the steps of a flight (above, round 2), and the CPU's edge probe (`dropAhead`) is unchanged.

Review round 2: a chair, a stool or a sofa that cannot be stood on as a whole is stood on at its drawn seat (`seat` in the collider, `Arena.seatTop`: the highest drawn part that is no higher than the collider, by `lookTop` as for the items that lie on a sofa; Rooftop and Club chairs 0.50 to 0.30 m, Club stools 0.70 to 0.42 m, Club VIP sofas 3.40 to 3.11 m; the back and the arms of a sofa stand higher), and a falling body that was above the top a tick ago lands on it even if the fall of that tick (up to 0.07 m) crossed the 0.05 m of `PASS_UNDER` (with the seat the K08 trials popped a body off a Rooftop chair by 0.48 to 0.54 m before this). `pushOut`: when the clear side is more than `PUSH_OUT_MAX` (0.6 m) away and the nearest side inside the arena is within it, the body leaves through the near one (the three audit flights moved the body 2.3 to 5.0 m); deeper in a block (the nearest clear side more than 0.6 m away) it is moved at most `PUSH_DEEP` (1.2 m) a tick toward it, in the first pass of the tick (a spawn in the Warehouse container or the Rooftop housing was moved 1.9 and 2.3 m in one tick), except where the way out is more than `PUSH_ESCAPE` (3 m) away (the end of a collapsed Garage deck walled in by rubble: the existing "no object traps a fighter" test needs the body out within 4 ticks), where it is out at once.
