### P18-77 z-fighting and rendering artifacts on the 8 levels, decided (2026-11-12)

- Owner, 2026-11-12 18:46: "There are various parts in the levels where z fighting and similar glitching artifacts occur." Branch `bp-p18-77-zfight`, base `c0e10f0`. The findings, the method and the before and after numbers are in Appendix D "P18-77".
- Rule (self-test "Z-fighting (P18-77)"): two faces of different colour, layer or light that face the same way, lie within `Z_FIGHT_GAP` = 0.002 m of each other and share more than 0.0002 m2 (0.004 m2 for a parked weapon) must not both show to a fight camera. Same-coloured neighbours (the posts of a frame) cannot be told apart on screen and do not count. 0.002 m is eight steps of the depth buffer at the farthest surface a fight camera shows (see the clip planes below). Every fix puts the faces `FLUSH_GAP` = 0.01 m apart (a leg ends under its deck plate, a collar ends under its column's cap, a wall top stands 0.01 m under the one it crosses), the stair tread 0.004 m past its block on every side (`STEP_LIP`), a pilaster or a mirror strip 0.005 to 0.02 m behind or in front of the poster it shares a wall with.
- How it was fixed, and what was not used: the geometry moved or was trimmed, at the cause (a prop, a look part, a draw call). No polygon offset on solids (it moves a whole surface in depth, so it would only trade one tie for another where three surfaces meet; the planar shadow pass keeps its own, `polygonOffset(-2, -2)` on a plane 0.012 m up, which is 55 depth steps at 43 m), no logarithmic depth (writing `gl_FragDepth` turns off early depth rejection on the weak GPUs the game is tuned for), no per-frame depth sort of the transparent layer (measured, Appendix D: reversing every alpha batch changes at most 8 pixels by more than 60 of 765 in any fight view, and the push order never changes between frames, so nothing pops).
- Clip planes: near 0.3 to 0.5 m and far 120 to 80 m (`CAMERA_NEAR`, `CAMERA_FAR`). The fight cameras show surfaces from 0.75 m to 43 m away; the eye stays `CAMERA_WALL_MARGIN` = 0.6 m inside the walls and reaches that margin only when it looks along or away from the wall, so the four corners of the near plane stay inside the room (at least 0.148 m clear; self-test "Arena bounds (P17-08)" checks the corners at every wall and corner of every level, on a wide, a phone-landscape and a portrait screen) and 0.5 m cuts nothing a camera shows; the 24-bit depth step at 43 m goes from 0.37 to 0.22 mm (self-test "Depth precision (P18-77)": at least eight steps in 0.002 m, far at least 60 m). The ceiling-prop fade now ends at the near plane: the opacity is 1 at `CAMERA_PROP_FADE` and 0 at `CAMERA_NEAR` (it was 0.8 at the fade edge, a jump from solid to 0.8 as the eye crossed 1 m; self-test "Ceiling props (P18-77)": no step over 0.05 per 0.01 m).
- Detail budget: `Arena.updateLod` gives a plain object its look back only `LOD_KEEP` = 2 ranks inside the budget and takes it away only 2 ranks outside it, so two objects that trade ranks at the edge of the budget (Low keeps 14 in full, Medium 28) no longer swap looks every 20th draw (self-test "Detail budget (P18-77)"). A budget left unused (every near object plain after the camera turned to another part of the level, or a budget of 2 or less) goes in the same recount to the nearest plain objects inside the slack; a full budget is not touched (self-test "Detail budget fill (P18-77)": budgets 0, 1, 2, 5 and 14). It draws nothing new and costs a comparison per object.
- Review round 1 (3 Lows, fixed): the Low pass of "Z-fighting" turned every object plain, fixed decks and walls too, which a game never does (`updateLod` skips them); with only destructibles plain it found the yellow deck lip sharing its front face with the two garage kerbs (0.024 m2 each): the lip stands `FLUSH_GAP` back from the deck's edge, and the board gaps of a timber deck stop 0.02 m short of each end to stay inside it. A budget of 2 that started all plain kept only 1 object in full, and Low kept 12 of 14 after the camera turned: fixed by the fill above.
- Collisions: no collider, bound or simulation value changed. Every edit is in `buildProps` (props are not colliders), `dressWalls`, `LOOKS`, `drawColumn`, `drawDeck`, `drawHazards` (drawing only), `Camera.apply` and `Arena.updateLod` (`far` is read by the draw functions only). The collision tests (Levels, Collision groups, BP-P18-64/65) stay green; the list of collision surfaces moved is empty.
- Fingerprints: none moved (no test with a recorded hash changed its result).
- Cost: the P0-04 benchmark (`BREAKPOINT.benchmark(10)`, Chrome on the RTX 2060 Super, 640x360, CPU throttle 4, Low, 3 rounds each, run twice in turn; the arena it picks is now the Rooftop) gives frame p50 / p95 / max 17.6 / 18.2 / 52.7 and 53.5 ms and work p50 / p95 / max 5.7 / 9.0 / 53.8 and 5.7 / 9.5 / 59.2 ms before, 17.6 / 18.2 / 52.9 and 53.1 ms and 5.7 / 8.6 / 54.2 and 5.7 / 9.2 / 58.2 ms after, 10 draws and 360 to 369 instances both (the 0.2 ms over the 18 ms rule is the machine under load, equal before and after). The edits add no draw, no instance and no state; the detail recount adds one comparison per object every 20th draw. Size: `breakpoint.html` is 1,554,239 bytes with LF endings and the BOM (1,550,266 before; budget 4,000,000). The headless run of all 810 tests: 790 pass, the 17 known headless limits and the 3 online-link tests that time out only in a full run (P12-01, P12-06, P12-07) fail as on main; the 4 new tests also pass in Chrome (`BREAKPOINT.selfTest('P18-77')`) and fail on `c0e10f0`.
- Left alone, each with its reason: the weapon models (two parked items can share a 0.002 m2 face; below the 0.004 m2 floor of the test and a few pixels on screen), the fighter bodies (a 1.3 mm pair on the torso, 0.004 m2: not a level), the binary fade of the hanging load (it switches between solid and 0.25 when a fighter stands behind it; smoothing it needs a state in the hazard record, which is the simulation), the 0.012 m shadow plane and the floor decals at 0.009 to 0.02 m (at least 40 depth steps at 43 m; no acne or floating shadow was seen), the noise on rough surfaces (a 0.125 m cell is 2.5 px at the farthest wall; the floor pattern is filtered by `fwidth`).
- Owner device check for BP-P16-03 (addition to the list in Appendix D "Notes for the fix"): on a phone, hold it upright in the Warehouse, the Garage and the Construction Site and look at the column tops, the deck edges and the back wall for shimmer. The measurements are from a 24-bit depth buffer; a phone with a 16-bit one (0.056 m steps at 43 m, near 0.5 and far 80) would show ties the tests cannot.

### Free Fight: watch-only fights (2026-11-12, BP-P18-75)

Owner request 2026-11-11 18:19: in Free Fight, slot 1 can be set to CPU like any other slot, so a fight can be all CPUs (2 to 8 fighters, any teams, any CPU level) to plan and watch. Branch `bp-p18-75-cpu-slot1` from c0e10f0. Agent decisions are marked "agent decision"; none changes how a CPU plays.

- Slot 1: `MatchLineup.fix` no longer sets `slots[0].human`. The control cell of slot 1 on Players and teams cycles CPU / Player like the others (touch, gamepad and keyboard use the same cell); the old toast "Slot 1 is always a player" is gone. Saved with the Free Fight setup as before (`human` of slot 1). An old save loads unchanged: `Game.loadSetup` reads slot 1 as a person unless the save says `human: false` (every old save wrote `true`; a missing field also counts as a person). An empty lineup still starts as a person against a CPU.
- A lineup with no person is valid (`MatchLineup.check` lost "A match needs a player"). Quick types: with no person a 2-slot lineup is typed Duel (Versus needs exactly two people), "Players vs CPU" deals the slots in turn onto Team A and Team B (agent decision: dealing everyone to the CPU team would leave one team and an invalid lineup), the other deals are unchanged. The even-teams handicap is the CPU-only rule it already had (a team smaller than the biggest may get under 1, never a person's team). Co-op (the crowd) still makes every slot a person. Online friends need a person in slot 1 (the host plays on this PC): `fix` drops an Online flag otherwise and makes that slot a CPU again (not a person at this PC), and the control cell offers Online only on slots after a person in slot 1 (agent decision; the online start code is untouched).
- One helper: `MatchSim.hasPerson()` (a lineup: some slot is a person, read from `personFighters`; any other fight: some controller is `human`). The lead of a lineup (fighters[0]) is already the first person when there is one, so a person in slot 2 or later is the lead, reads its own seat (`Inputs.forFighter`) and gets the camera, HUD marker, controls card and tips as slot 1 did. Readers that took `controllers[0].human` as "the player" now ask the helper (`Coach.eligible`); the HUD, camera and results ask it for a lineup (`setup`) only.
- In a fight with no person: no fighter reads an input seat (every controller is an `AIController`); lock-on, assist and the stamina edge are applied to people only (unchanged code, tested); `Game.inputPlan()` returns 'versus' (`Game.watchOnly()`: the running config has `humans` 0), so both keyboard layouts and both pad seats can pause, restart or quit; the third and fourth gamepad have no seat, so while `Game.watchOnly()` `Inputs.mergeMenuPads` also merges `Inputs.anyPadMenu()` (now with `start`) into the menu buttons and sets `Inputs.menuStartPressed`, and Start on any connected pad pauses and resumes (`Game.pollMatchInput`, `UI.update`) while any pad moves and confirms on the pause screen and the results; the pause screen and the results work as for any lineup; with touch the stick and fight buttons stay hidden and the PAUSE button shows. The camera frames every living fighter (`Camera.followGroup(..., everyone)`, as it does a person on another team). The HUD shows every fighter without a "P1" or "1P" marker (the lead's heading reads CPU, the tags read CPU), no held-item, combo, stamina warning, hint or off-screen attacker arrow for the lead, and no first-fight controls card.
- Records (agent decision, as the task proposed): a fight with no person never counts. `Coach.eligible` is false, `Game.onMatchEnd` sets `playerWon` false (so `gradeResults` saves no grade; no challenge, unlock or record is reached by a Free Fight lineup anyway) and marks the results `watching`; the Progress save is byte for byte the same after such a fight. A person in another slot counts by today's rules for people (grade for a win, none for people only, tips). The results show "X wins" (the winning team) or "Draw", a row per fighter, and one line "Nobody played: this fight does not count."; the end banner says "<WINNER> WINS" (no "VICTORY") and the victory jingle plays only when a team won; a draw shows the "DRAW" banner of the draw path and no jingle.
- Determinism: the simulation reads nothing new; lineups with a person in slot 1 build the same `plan` and the same match as before, so no fingerprint changed and none was re-recorded (hashes are recorded in Chrome only).
- Self-tests: "Watch-only Free Fight (P18-75)" x4 (rules and saves; an all-CPU 1 vs 1 and an 8-fighter team brawl to a result with no input, results, the draw and win banners, Progress, same seed, a person in slot 2, HUD, camera and input plan; the end jingle for a watched win, a watched draw and a fight with a person; the Free Fight flow in the menu state, with Start on a third and a fourth pad pausing and resuming), and the three existing tests that said slot 1 is always a player now say it can be a CPU.
- Owner device checks for BP-P16-03: set slot 1 to CPU on a phone (touch), a gamepad and the keyboard, start, watch to the end, pause and quit with each device, and look at the lineup screen and the results.

## Appendix D - Audit findings

(Filled by P0-02 and P16-01. Columns: ID, severity, area, location, reproduction, fix task, status.)

### P18-74 the full self-test run: four online-link tests, the sound bake and a sound level failed (2026-11-12)

- Symptom (base `c0e10f0`, full `BREAKPOINT.selfTest()` in headless Chromium): "Online link P12-01", "Online loopback P12-01", "Online failures P12-07" and "Online link P12-06" fail with "no result after 10000 ms"; alone (`selfTest('Online')`) they pass. Later, once the first cause was gone, "Sound bake P18-29" and the "bat hit" row of "Sound levels P18-29" failed in some full runs.
- Not the cause (measured): leftover connections. Over the whole run 34 RTCPeerConnections were made, 34 closed, 0 open at the end; one AudioContext (the game's own).
- Cause 1, the runner: `run_all` runs every test in one synchronous pass (478 s in a full run: a 50 ms interval saw no tick between 0.3 s and 478 s), and an async test started inside it had its 10 s limit and its own `waitFor` / `until` clocks running while the event loop was shut. The four tests started about 267 s into the pass; when the loop opened their result said `ms` 211 800. A test that needs a timer loses the race against its own expired limit, which is due first; the earlier full runs that passed are not explained by anything measured here (the order of such tasks is not guaranteed). The audio tests were already deferred by `limitMs`; now every `async` test is deferred the same way (a limit of 10 s, 30 s `REAL_LINK_LIMIT_MS` for the four tests over real WebRTC), and the four promise-returning tests were made `async`. "Skipped tests" is deferred too, so it reads the settled results of the async tests (it used to see them still running).
- Cause 2, the game: `UI.say` and `UI.banner` scheduled one timer per call and never cancelled the older one. The tests' matches called them 76 187 times in the pass; at the end 76 035 were waiting, and running them (an aria-live write each) kept the page busy for 136 s right after the pass, which also starved the first deferred test (the sound bake). Now each keeps one timer (`UI.sayTimer`, `UI.bannerTimer`) and cancels the one before it: an older banner timer did nothing anyway (its id was not the latest), and announcements said within the same 30 ms are read out together by the one timer (`UI.sayPending`, each text once, the newest `SAY_PENDING_MAX` = 4), so two knock-outs on one tick are both announced. After the change 357 of 76 185 timers ran.
- Sound bake: each bake step waits for `requestIdleCallback`; a page that is drawing is never idle, so every step ran after its 500 ms timeout (about 700 ms each) and five steps came within a hair of the 4 s wait of the test (it failed 2 of 3 runs alone on the base). The test now puts a prompt stand-in in place for the idle call.
- "bat hit": `renderSounds` shared the page's own `Sound.lastVariant` (which variant of a baked sound plays next); the matches of the earlier tests had filled it (`{"h10":0,"h11":1,"h12":2,"h21":0,"h31":2,"mwood":0}`), so the bat hit peaked at -2.94 dBFS in a full run and -4.42 alone (target -5, within 2). The render now starts with an empty record, and "Sound levels P18-29" no longer depends on which variants play: it renders every row that picks baked variants once per combination of them (3 variants per pick, 9 for a hit with an item's material layer, the variants forced, not drawn) and every level must be within 2 dB of the target. Players hear any variant, and the check found two rows outside: the loudest variant combinations of the bat hit and the bottle hit. Fix (`ITEM_HIT_TRIM_DB` in `Sound.impact`): the bat hit is 1.2 dB lower and the bottle hit 1.5 dB lower (the pipe hit was inside and is unchanged). Peaks of the 9 combinations in dBFS (target -5, allowed -7 to -3), before / after: bat hit -4.03 -3.23 -3.73 -4.09 -4.55 -3.46 -4.42 -3.17 -2.94 / -4.98 -4.01 -4.62 -5.07 -5.49 -4.28 -5.17 -3.95 -3.74; bottle hit -3.04 -4.49 -4.17 -4.18 -3.99 -2.33 -4.43 -5.07 -3.50 / -4.12 -5.57 -5.47 -5.35 -5.27 -3.44 -5.62 -6.51 -4.78; pipe hit (unchanged) -4.30 -6.04 -4.83 -5.95 -5.93 -5.50 -5.04 -6.45 -5.46. Measured in headless Chromium, offline render, combination order (first pick, second pick) = 0..8 with the first pick the fast digit.
- Real-link tests, measured alone with a free event loop: CSP 1.8 s, loopback 3.3 s, two peers 5.3 s, four peers 10.4 s. The old inner limits were 8 s and 9 s; the new ones, 20 s (two peers, measured 5.3 s) and 25 s (four peers, measured 10.4 s, above the old 9 s), stand on these measured durations and nothing else. Why the base `selfTest('Online')` still passed in Chrome is not explained by them: in a frozen loop the overdue timer fires first, so the old limits did not hold because the clock stood still.
- Guards added to the list: "Test runner (P18-74)" (an async test starts after the pass; a plain test that returns a promise fails with "return a promise only from an async test" instead of starting inside the pass), "Announcer (P18-74)" (1000 banners and announcements leave at most 2 timers; fails on the base with 3000; announcements said within one tick are all in the live region, each once, with one timer), "Online links (P18-74)" (no RTCPeerConnection made by the tests is open when they are done; `run_all` counts them by wrapping the constructor, once even when runs overlap, and puts the real one back in a `finally` after the deferred tests).
- Result: two full runs in a row in headless Chromium, 809 of 809 each (618 s and 660 s; the base run was 772 s with 4 failures); headless stub run 792 of 809 with the 17 known limits and 0 other failures.

### P18-64 collisions, hitboxes and hurtboxes audit (2026-11-10)

- Owner, 2026-11-10: "Evaluate issues regarding collisions,hitboxes,hurtboxes and their accuracy (floating through etc)". Audit only: no game file changed (base `9d73ccb`, branch `bp-p18-64-collide`); the fixes are BP-P18-65, the decision on hit volumes is in Appendix C ("P18-64 collisions audited, decided"). Result: 15 findings (3 High, 7 Medium, 5 Low), all open for BP-P18-65. The simulation itself is sound (no body inside a prop in 424,372 fighter-ticks, no body-body overlap beyond 4.8 cm, no tunnelling in 9,408 thrown-body flights and 2,079 item throws); what the owner sees comes from three places: blows and bodies that ignore scenery, bodies that are drawn larger than the 0.34 m cylinder they collide with, and the footing rules at edges and steps.
- Status after BP-P18-65 (2026-11-11): K01 to K12 and K15 fixed, K13 fixed for the item pushed out past the wall (Appendix C "P18-65 built" has the as-built steps and where a limit differs from the plan); the rest of K13 and K14 are open for BP-P16-01 (their rows say what is left). Appendix C "P18-65 built" has the as-built steps, the numbers and the existing tests that changed. Review round 2 corrected K04 (a step no longer keeps the cylinder in every direction), K05 (the foot's reach, the probe artifact), K08 (chairs, stools and sofas stood on at the drawn seat) and K09 (the push-out is 1.2 m a tick over all the passes); the cases that remain are the last row of the probe table of Appendix C "P18-65 built".
- Method: every probe is a headless script run inside the game closure with the P0-06 harness (`extract.js` + a copy of `harness.js` that evaluates a probe file; Node, no browser, no dev server), on the real `MatchSim`, `Arena`, `Fighter` and `Combat`, never on a model of them. The drawn body is read exactly: `Fighter.walkSkeleton(draw = true)` with `R.push` swapped for a recorder gives the world box of every piece the renderer would draw (about 30 per body), so "drawn" below means the boxes of the real pose. Scripts and result files are in the scratch folder `C:/Users/GS/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/bp-p1864/` (not in the repo): `lib.js` (helpers), `p3-sweep.js` (AI fights), `p4-strike.js`, `p10-prop.js`, `p12-through.js` (blows), `p5-nav.js`, `p8-raised.js`, `p8b-stairs.js`, `p8c-edge-trace.js`, `p9-down.js`, `p7-bodies.js`, `p6-items.js`, `p13-jump.js`, `p14-sink.js`, `p11-cost.js`; run with `bash run.sh <probe> <out.json> '<params json>'`. Everything is deterministic (seeds below); a fixer re-runs the same file after the fix.
- Not reproduced, with the method (so the next reader does not look again): see "Owner symptoms" below.

#### Owner symptoms: reproduced or not

| Symptom | Result | How (levels, fighters, seeds, steps) |
|---|---|---|
| Fighters pass through each other (live bodies) | Not reproduced | 64 AI-vs-AI sims (4 duels and 4 crowd brawls with 5 enemies on each of the 8 levels, seeds 100 to 407, up to 1,800 ticks each, hard CPUs, items and hazards on): 424,372 fighter-ticks; `separate` kept every grounded pair at 0.68 m except 33 ticks of a crowd corner squeeze (deepest 4.8 cm). |

#### Notes for the fix

- The probes found nothing wrong with the number-level rules (`separate`, `resolveFighter`'s wall clamp, `pushOut`'s order, `moveItem`'s collision test, `stepBodies`, `stepRingOut`, the nav map's connectivity); every finding above is a missing case or a mismatch between what is drawn and what collides. At the 6.4 m/s throws and 11 m/s item speed a tick is 0.11 and 0.18 m, smaller than the thinnest collider zone (0.2 m), so no swept test is needed.
- Cost of the drawn-pose reads the fixes may use (`p11-cost.js`, headless, one core): `attackPose` plus `walkSkeleton` 21.5 microseconds per call, the skeleton alone 6.6; a whole tick is 113 microseconds with 2 fighters and 319 with 8. The pose is computed every tick for every fighter already (`Fighter.animate`).
- Proposed tests for BP-P18-65, one per finding, each written to fail on the current game (the scratch probes are the first drafts): K01 two fighters across every prop of every level, the blow must not land when the prop is taller than the blow's height and between them, and must land with no prop between; K02 a knocked-out brawl body is solid or gone before the next living fighter can reach its centre (min distance 0.5 m); K03 a knocked-down and a knocked-out body against every wall side and prop side lies inside the wall plane and overlaps no prop by more than 0.05 m, in all 8 levels; K04 a body walked off a crate and the Subway mezzanine starts to fall when its centre is 0.15 m past the edge and no drawn foot is more than 0.4 m past it at the deck height; K05 a High strike does not damage a 0.95 m crate it passes over, a Low strike does; K06 the P17-02 hit check extended to foes at 0.68 m, 1.0 m and the volume front (the tip is not more than 0.34 m past the foe's centre, and not more than 0.2 m short of its body); K07 the widest and narrowest bodies standing against every prop: drawn overlap at most 0.1 m; K08 a jump at each non-standable prop below 1.3 m: the cylinder is at most 0.05 m into it, no tick moves the body more than 0.15 m; K09 no flight moves a body more than 0.6 m in one tick; K10 per-tick rise at most 0.26 m on every approach to every flight from 8 headings; K11 the lowest drawn part within 0.1 m of the floor in every move; K12 a body under a `grate` or `boards` deck is either possible or the look is solid (decide); K13 no item ends outside the arena; K14 map free cells push the body at most 0.1 m.
- Owner device checks to add to BP-P16-03: on a phone, knock a fighter down against a wall and against a crate in a brawl and look at the body; walk off a crate and off the Subway mezzanine and watch the feet; knock out an enemy in a brawl and try to walk over the body; jump at a bench, a car and a fence rail; throw a brick at a crate from 3 m.

### P18-40 critical issue sweep (2026-11-05)

- Result: 1 Critical and 1 High found and fixed (the first review of this sweep found them; the first pass of the sweep had listed both as "seen, not critical"). Critical = a mode or choice that cannot be used, a soft lock (no way forward or back), lost progress, a crash. The sweep covered the main menu, the mode list and the eight modes (Arcade, Survival, Training, Free Fight, Versus, Brawl, Co-op Brawl, Tournament with Continue tournament), their fighter, rules, Players and teams, arena, join and bracket screens, fights (win, loss, clock, Quit from pause), results, Rematch, Change fighters, Continue and Main menu, and Controls, Move list, Settings, Unlocks, About and the creator (with its Fight preview) on keyboard 1, keyboard 2, gamepad and touch / mouse.

| ID | Sev | Area | Location | Reproduction | Cause and fix | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E01 | Critical | Lost progress | `UI.confirmFighter` (Arcade), `UI.confirmTournamentPick` | Play, Enter (Arcade is the default button), Confirm with a saved Arcade run at stage 5: the run is replaced at once. The same with the last fighter confirm of a new Tournament over a saved bracket. No warning, no undo. | `startArcade` and `playTournament` write the new save as soon as they start. Fix: with a save present the confirm opens a new screen `replace` ("Replace your saved run: NAME, stage 5 of 7?" / "Replace your saved tournament: 8 fighters, next: Semi-final?") made of the game's ordinary panel and menu buttons: Keep (the default, it is Back, so Esc, B and a tap on Back all keep) returns to the fighter screen with the save and the pick as they were, Replace starts the new run. The screen has the double tap guard of Pause and Results. | [x] fixed, self-tests added |
| E02 | High | Gamepad | `UI.update` (join screen branch), `Inputs.lobbyPad`, `UI.onLobby` | Gamepad only on the Tournament or Co-op join screen: the Entrants row and the CPU level button cannot be reached or changed (the pad reads only the lobby there). | Fix: `Inputs.lobbyPad` also reports up / down (focus moves) from any gamepad, joined or not, left / right from a gamepad that has not joined (`adjust`; a joined one's `cycle` is the same press) and A on a joined one (`press`). `UI.onLobby`: up / down move the focus; left / right from a gamepad (events marked `pad`) change the Entrants row in focus (and the CPU level in a Tournament), else choose a joined pad's fighter as before; a key reaches the page twice (the lobby and `UI.onKey`, which already steps the row), so key events never change the row here (a review found Entrants stepping twice and staying put after a keyboard joined; a self-test now checks one step per press for both keyboards); A changes the row in focus once the focus was moved to it. Co-op keeps left / right for the joined pad's fighter, join, leave and Start are as before, and Tournament seat cards still do not cycle (P18-41). The hint text says so. | [x] fixed, self-test added |

- Method: 21 self-tests in the new section "Mode flows (P18-40)" of `breakpoint-tests.js`. They press only what the screen on show offers (the `data-act` of its enabled buttons: what a tap, Enter and a pad's A all press), through `UI.act`, `UI.onClick`, `UI.onKey` (Esc, arrows, Enter) and the lobby events of fake gamepads. The page is stood in for: the real `Game.go` with `GS_TRANSITIONS`, then `UI.onGameState` on stand-in elements; the screen's focusable elements are listed as `UI.navItems` lists them and `document.activeElement` follows the focus, so arrow keys and a pad's stick move it and Enter or A clicks it. A reach check fails when the keys or the pad (a pad's stick down, once per element) never land on an enabled element of a screen. Fights are played to their end by the match itself (a real knock-out or the clock, then the game loop's VICTORY to RESULTS step, Punch skipping the pose); every screen drawn is checked for a way out and for no enabled button without `data-nav`. At the end of a test on a page the game state goes to the menu the real way, so the music and the touch buttons follow the menu, and the frame loop numbers (`Game.last`, `acc`, `frameAvg`, the `Diag` frame stats) and `Game.tournamentResume` are put back.
- Tests: one flow per mode (Arcade, Arcade with all scenes to the clear and the ending, Survival, Training, Free Fight with and without a lineup, Versus, Brawl, Co-op Brawl with a keyboard and a pad, Tournament on touch to the title, Tournament left and continued, Tournament for two devices, two people in one bout); the two replace questions (Keep, Back, Esc, the pad's B, a tap straight after the question, Replace, for an Arcade run and for a bracket of one and of two); the join screens by the arrow keys and a pad (joined or not); lineups that cannot start; three and four people on pads; Back and Esc from every screen of every mode; the side screens and the creator; and seeded random walks (presses, taps and keys on option rows, Esc, joins, pauses, fights; custom fighter, saved run and bracket, story, ring-out, items and hazards settings on some seeds). After every press a walk checks: the game state and the screen agree, no state change was refused, `Diag.errors` is unchanged, a joined person is read from a device in play, the join screen has co-op input and the lobby on, and the saved progress (records, unlocks) equals the memory copy and never falls. Now and then and at the end, Back / Quit / Main menu alone must lead to the main menu.
- On the old game (HEAD) the Arcade and Tournament replace tests and the join screen test fail ("Confirm did not ask", "the confirm did not ask", "right on a gamepad that has not joined did not change Entrants"), and so does the Co-op test through its reach check ("the gamepad never reaches back"); all four pass now. Four deliberate breaks of the game made earlier (Back from the arena, the Tournament confirm, Back from the bracket, Quit in the pause menu) were each caught by 3 to 11 tests.
- Evidence: 592 walks of 100 steps passed before the fixes (seeds 1-150, 1000-1011, 2000-2199, 3000-3039, 4000-4039, 5000-5149); after them 60 more (seeds 6000-6059) with the new checks and 30 (seeds 7000-7029) with the final form of the join-screen code. The suite keeps 5 walks (seeds 1-5) because a walk costs 2 to 3 s.
- Two false alarms of the harness were found and fixed in the tests, not in the game: a walk that pressed Skip on a scene with a question never answered it (Skip still asks the answer, and the answer buttons are on screen), and a wave scene that pauses a fight (Arcade stage 3) must be played through before the match goes on.
- Seen, not critical (not fixed):
  - Co-op Brawl cannot be started with touch or mouse alone: a device has to join with Punch or A first, and "Choose arena" stays off until one has. By design (the mode list says "keyboards and gamepads", the join screen says "Touch controls are not used in co-op"); Brawl with one player covers a solo crowd fight on touch. Versus and a lineup with two or more people likewise need a second keyboard layout or a gamepad.
  - A saved Tournament bracket with two or more people waits on the join screen until as many devices have joined; with fewer devices Back is the only way on, and the bracket stays on the mode list until a new Tournament is drawn over it (which now asks first).
  - Back from a fighter screen to the mode list leaves the last `Game.run` set (Quit to main menu clears it); every mode starts its own run, so nothing reads the old one.
  - A Versus lineup that cannot start (the second slot set to CPU on Players and teams) is not stopped on the Versus rules screen: "Choose arena" is on, the arena screen's "Start fight" says why (toast) and stays, and Back leads to the lineup to fix it.
- Checks: headless run with `BP_FILTER="Mode flows"`: 21 / 21; full headless run through `heavy.mjs`: 501 / 518, exactly the 17 known failures (16 "needs the main menu", 1 "blank faces"), listeners 25 / 25 before and after; `breakpoint.html` is 1,173,238 bytes (LF, BOM counted) of 1,200,000. Still open: the same tests in Chrome (the stand-in page elements are used there too; on a page each test ends by taking the game state to the menu the real way), and the owner's device checks, which now include the replace question and a gamepad on the Tournament join screen.

### P18-38 ground submissions (2026-11-05)

- Owner, 2026-11-03: "On a ground armbar i float above the ground." Measured with the new self-test (lowest drawn part of each fighter above the floor, from the drawn matrices): armbar holder (Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, MMA) up to +53 cm in the air, the kneeling pin (Wrestling, Judo) down to -14 cm and the Hapkido wrist lock down to -12 cm into the floor, the Sambo leg lock +1 cm, the held fighter +2 to +5 cm face up; a knocked-down or knocked-out fighter (unheld) lies 2 to 5 cm above the floor face up and 7 to 16 cm into it face down.
- Cause: `rootHeight()` puts the root where the legs of a STANDING body reach the floor, and only the `lie` blend (the knockdown pose) overrides it. The four `HOLD_POSES` (pin, leg, arm, wrist) kneel, sit or lie but set no `lie`, so the body hung at the standing height of its leg angles: the armbar lay back with its legs up and the root stayed 50 cm high. `LIE_HEIGHT` (0.17) is one value for every build, and a face-down body is deeper than a face-up one, so no single value fits.
- Fix 1 (`Fighter.animate`, `plantFloor`, `lowestPart`, `skeleton`, `part`, `probeLow`): on every tick a fighter in a hold (the holder in SUBMIT) or lying down (DOWN held or not, KO, and the GETUP out of them) is walked once without drawing (`part`, `pieces` and the held item record the lowest height of every box, ball and cylinder instead of queuing it, `PROBE_LOW`), and `plantShift` lifts or lowers the drawing so the lowest drawn part is on the floor whatever the pose, body and build. The lowest part moves to the floor from where the last tick drew it, and back to the pose's own lowest `PLANT_RELEASE_TICKS` (20) ticks after the pose ends, at most `PLANT_SPEED` (1.5 m/s, 2.5 cm a tick), so it neither sinks nor jumps while the pose blends (review finding: an ease of the shift at a fixed rate let the half-blended pose sink 16 to 18 cm into the floor and jump 13 cm in one tick at the start and the end of a hold; the first version of this fix). Everybody else is not measured, so nothing else pays for the extra pass. `frameScale` returns a reused array (the measuring pass calls it too). Drawing only: the simulation, hit boxes, timing and key points used by hits are unchanged (the key points feed only effects and scene placement).
- Fix 2 (`HOLD_POSES`): the armbar lies flat on the back (`bodyPitch` -1.5, `lie` 1, head up) with legs and arms keeping their old directions in the room (hips 1.5 and 1.3 became 0.9 and 0.7, shoulders 1.2 became 0.6, because the body lies 0.6 further back); the leg lock sits back on the floor with the legs raised (`bodyPitch` -1.1, `lie` 1); the pin kneels (knees 2.5, so the shins lie along the floor instead of a deep crouch). The wrist lock stays a low crouch, now with its feet on the floor.
- Check: `Ground submissions (P18-38)` in `breakpoint-tests.js`. Test 1 plays every style that can hold (6 styles, 4 hold poses) on the 8 test bodies, the foe face up and face down alternately, and the 3 one-handed items (bat, chain, bottle) in the holder's hand: both fighters stand 30 ticks, the foe is knocked down, Grapple 2 ticks later, 100 ticks of hold, then the holder lets go and both get up; the lowest drawn part of both is read on EVERY tick until both have stood 30 ticks. It fails if the part is deeper than 0.2 cm under the floor while lying (or under the standing stance it came from), more than 3 cm under the stance while standing, more than 3 cm above the floor 25 ticks into a lying pose, or moves more than 3 cm in one tick (the get-up is checked too). Worst after the fix: 0.0 cm in every hold and lying pose; at the start and the end of a hold the part is only at the standing stance's own toe sink (-3.4 to -8.0 cm, as when standing), and the biggest one-tick move is 2.5 cm. Test 2 checks that nobody is measured while standing and that the measuring is gone once both stand again. Test 3 lays a knocked-down and a knocked-out fighter, face up and face down, on the 8 bodies, 40 ticks after the fall (a knock-out needs 26), and needs -0.2 cm to +3 cm; on the old code it fails with +1.8 to +4.8 cm face up and -7.5 to -15.9 cm face down, after the fix every one is 0.0 cm.
- Left alone: a standing guard stance draws the toes up to 8 cm below the floor line (the standing toes were not part of this task); `LIE_HEIGHT` and `liePose` are unchanged, the shift corrects the drawn height on top of them. The flight of a throw is not corrected. The get-up now stays on the floor too (it sank 28 cm into it on the old code); for the 20 ticks the pose blends back to the stance the lowest part is held at the depth of the fighter's guard stance (`stanceLow`), not at 0, so a fighter who is up again is not lifted by his toe sink (review finding). The test also fails if a standing row is more than 3 cm above the stance, and once 25 ticks into a lying pose it needs -0.2 cm.

### P18-36 crowd camera and body stacking (2026-11-05)

- Found during P18-34: the `Brawl camera` hidden-player test (warehouse, 141 ticks in a row, limit 54) failed on seeds 3 and 8 on the code before P18-34 and on 5 and 7 after it, and the `1v6 brawl` test (two bodies closer than 0.3 m) failed on seed 2 before and on 5 and 9 after. Both tests were pinned to seed 6 to pass. They now loop over seeds 1 to 12 (`CROWD_SEEDS`); on the code before this task they fail on seeds 5 and 9 (1v6, 0.24 m and 0.22 m) and on seeds 7 and 8 (camera, warehouse, 141 and 139 ticks).
- Camera cause: the warehouse metal rack at x -10.9, z -4.0 (1.2 m x 2.6 m, 2.4 m tall) stands against the west wall. A player in the corner just behind its end (x -11.1, z -5.7) is in line with it as seen from the usual eye position (the eye is held 0.6 m off the side wall, 0.5 rad of pitch). Every pose in `CAMERA_OCCLUSION_TRIES` stayed hidden: the azimuth swing is limited to +-0.55 rad round the base (a clear view needs 1.0 to 1.4 rad from the side), and the pitch was capped at 1.15 rad (66 degrees), which still looks along the rack. The camera then waited for the enemies to move, up to 141 ticks.
- Camera fix (`CAMERA_STEEP_SWING`, `CAMERA_ELEV_STEEP_MAX`, `swungElev`, `CAMERA_OCCLUSION_TRIES`): the list ends with two nearly straight-down views, `[0, 0.9, 0]` and `[0, 0.9, 1]` (normal aim, then aimed at the players). A pitch swing of 0.9 or more may reach 1.4 rad (80 degrees); every other swing and the normal camera keep the cap `CAMERA_ELEV_MAX` of 1.15 rad (66 degrees), so every earlier pose is exactly as before (a first version of this fix raised the one cap to 1.4, which also let the 0.7 swings reach 1.16 to 1.25 rad; the review caught that). The two are tried last, so every case that was clear before behaves as before; the swing releases 0.6 s after the normal view is clear, as always. A pure pitch swing keeps the camera azimuth, so the stick directions the player has learned do not turn. The limit in the test (grace 0.3 s plus 0.6 s) is unchanged. The 1v1, Versus and Training camera does not use the swing.
- Body cause: `MatchSim.separate` skipped every pair with a THROWN body, however low it was. A body that is thrown (or juggled) lands in `afterCollision`, after the separation of that tick, so one that came down on a standing or walking fighter stayed inside it for the whole landing tick (0.22 to 0.24 m apart; the next tick pushed them apart, so it lasted exactly one tick in every case found). In the test seed 5 was a thrown enemy landing on the standing player, seed 9 the thrown player landing on a walking enemy.
- Body fix (`MatchSim.separate`): a THROWN body counts as flying only while it is above its footing or rising; once it is at its footing and not rising (the same test that lands it in `afterCollision`) it is pushed apart like any body on that tick. The push, the height test (1.25 m) and the clinch, hold and grapple exceptions are unchanged; a body still in flight passes over the others as before.
- Balance: no combat number changed. The simulation changes only on the landing tick of a throw that lands inside another body.

### P18-44 raised ground (2026-11-05)

- Audit: every raised surface of the 8 levels (19 decks, rings and scaffold tiers and 23 stair slopes) was played with both fighters on it, one on it and one on the floor beside it, and on two steps of each stair slope, for every strike class (Punch, Crouch + Punch, Kick, Crouch + Kick, jump kick, running lunge), every one of the 14 items swung, the grab and its throw, the tackle, the stomp, the ground hold, the pick-up (person and CPU seat), the thrown item and the set-down item, and for a CPU seat (how it sees the foe, its strikes and its grab). On the old code 8 of the 11 tests failed, on the new code none.

| ID | Sev | Surface | Action | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R01 | High | every deck, scaffold tier, ring, stage and stair step above 0.3 m, every level | Grab, throw, clinch (player and CPU) | `Combat.evaluate` refused a grab when `att.y > 0.3` or `def.y > 0.5`, measured from the floor: a fighter standing on a footing above 0.3 could never grab (65 of the 99 runs wrong) | measured from the fighter's own footing, plus the grab ledge (`breakpoint.html` `Combat.evaluate`) |

### P12-05 determinism audit (2026-11-07)

- Base: `main` at 8aa8c39 (P18-43 fight rules, P17-19 touch crouch and the P18-40 sweep are in; P18-05 difficulty is built, 1194ead). No game code and no test was changed, nothing was run (this pass is read-only: `rg` and reading only). AC-001 (equal checksums with Reduced motion on and off) is not verified: P12-05 stays open until T2 runs, and D08 stays open, so every statement about two machines giving different numbers is a reading of the code and of the engines' rules, not a measurement; the cross-engine rows (J01, J02) need the golden-hash test below on a real iPhone and a PC. Line numbers are `breakpoint.html` at this commit (1,178,607 bytes with LF and BOM, of 4,000,000).
- Scope: the task's wording (all gameplay randomness through the seeded RNG, no frame-rate-dependent logic, no `Math.random` in the simulation, no viewer setting that changes the sim) plus what a peer would compute differently: clocks, locale, screen size and pixel ratio, quality, camera, DOM, pause, iteration order, sort stability, floating-point functions, input sampling. The sim is everything one `MatchSim.step` (11105) runs: `stepFight` 11151, `readIntents`, `Fighter.update` and `integrate`, `Combat`, `Arena.update`, items, hazards, fire, ring-out, waves, `AIController`.
- Result: 5 High, 6 Medium, 4 Low, 5 Informational (20 findings). Nothing found makes two runs of the same build on the same engine with the same seed and the same per-tick intents give different state: `Math.random` is used 0 times in the sim, `Date.now` and `performance.now` 0 times inside a tick, `Settings.v` inside a tick only in `animate`'s pose and trail code (6336, 6372, 6537, 6569, 6755), which no sim field reads, `dt` other than `DT` 0 times, and the AI reads nothing that is only drawn. What blocks online play is what is missing around the sim (a state hash, a way to save and load state, a tick driver that is not the wall clock, a wire form of the input) and one unmeasured risk across engines (J01).

**Recommended automated tests (new task, after J03; the helper is `MatchSim.stateHash()` and a per-tick log of it)**

1. T1 `Determinism: per-tick state hash` - the same seed and the same scripted human intents (a 1800-tick script that walks, jabs, kicks, blocks, grabs, throws) twice, plus an AI against AI run in Free Fight, Brawl with waves and a ring-out level; equal hash at every tick, the first differing tick and field printed on failure.
2. T2 `Determinism: viewer settings` (AC-001) - one run per row of the matrix (Reduced motion on/off, Shake 0/1, Flashes off/reduced/on, Effects low/high, Quality low/high with `Quality.apply()`, Shadows, Trails, Movement mode, Auto-assist off with an input that never reads it): hash equal to the baseline at every tick. Closes row D08.
3. T3 `Determinism: frame rate` - drive `Game.frame(now)` with a fake clock at 30, 60, 144 fps and a jittered 20 to 90 fps, steps below `MAX_STEPS_PER_FRAME`, the same per-tick intents (fed through a controller that returns the recorded intent for `m.tick`): the hash at tick N equal in all.
4. T4 `Determinism: input replay` - record the intents of a keyboard-driven run (scripted `keydown` events) and replay them through the wire form of J06: equal hash.
5. T5 `Determinism: no outside input` - run once with `Math.random` replaced by a different generator, with `Date.now` and `performance.now` shifted by an hour and jittered, and with `navigator.language`, `devicePixelRatio` and the window size changed: hash equal (catches any future leak of a clock, a locale or a screen size).
6. T6 `Determinism: golden hashes` - five fixed matches (1v1, Free Fight with ring-out and hazards, Brawl with waves, a lineup, a thrown-body case) with the hash every 60 ticks recorded as constants; the owner runs the self-test on the iPhone and on the PC (add to P16-03): equal constants prove J01 is harmless on those engines, a mismatch names the first tick.
7. T7 `Determinism: source scan` - the test fetches `breakpoint.html`, finds every `Math.random`, `Date.now`, `performance.now`, `Settings.v` and `.sort(` and checks the line is in an allow-list of function names (draw, sound, input, start, menu); a new use in sim code fails with its line. Together with T5 this keeps the audit true after P17-10, P18-05 and the online tasks.

#### P12-05 result (2026-11-09, base e1b263a)

The read-only audit above was redone with `rg` on this base (no new `Math.random`, `Date.now`, `performance.now`, `Settings.v`, `Camera.` or `Quality.` use in any code a tick runs; no `for in`, `Set` or `Map` loop in a tick) and then proven by a run. One code fix, one test, one comment. AC-001 is met: the test plays a scripted person against a Hard CPU in a Free Fight (warehouse, items, hazards; every breakable and the deck broken at tick 120) and a four-fighter brawl on the Pit (everything breakable broken at tick 200), takes one checksum per tick (every fighter's position, speed, knock-back, yaw, hp, stamina, state, move, momentum, burn, blind, item; every level object's hp and state; every loose item's place, speed, mode and wear; every hazard's state and timer; the tick, the phase, the round, the wins, the clock, the hit stop and the two id counters) and requires the same list from every other run: again; Reduced motion on; Reduced motion with its effect rows; every viewer setting flipped together; and each of the 14 settings flipped alone (Movement mode only shows that the sim never reads it: the scripted seat writes `fwd` and `side` itself, so the stick conversion in `PlayerInput.toFighterFrame` never runs); `Math.random`, `Date.now` and `performance.now` are replaced in exactly two runs, "every viewer setting flipped" and "clocks and Math.random replaced". It also requires the low quality preset to throw fewer debris pieces than the high one (so the cap was exercised) and the checksum to move (so the scenario plays). Checked by breaking the game on purpose in a scratch copy: a hit stop that Reduced motion shortens fails at tick 146, Auto-assist leaking into the intent fails at tick 19, a deck piece draw skipped on a low quality cap fails at tick 135 (duel) and tick 200 (brawl), and removing the counter reset fails at tick 0.

### P18-46 performance profile and plan (2026-11-07)

- Scope: read-only profile of `breakpoint.html` at `8aa8c39` (Chrome 157, i5-9600K, Windows 11). No repo file was changed. This is the plan for BP-P18-47.
- Method (P0-04, run from `file://`): Playwright Chrome, CDP `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`, setting `quality` saved in `breakpoint.v1.settings`, `BREAKPOINT.benchmark(10, opts)` (1 s warm-up, 10 s measured, 3 runs per cell). Low-spec = viewport 640x360, throttle 4, quality `low` (render scale 0.6, 384x216). Desktop = 1280x720, throttle 1, quality `auto` (resolved to high, scale 1).
- Scenes: the P0-04 benchmark 1v1 (Expert vs Expert) and the same scene as a crowd brawl, `benchmark(10, { enemies: 6 })`. The crowd maximum is 7 fighters (`BRAWL_MAX_ENEMIES` = 6 plus the player), not 8. The benchmark picks `rooftop` today (most destructibles; fire and drop hazards; all objects smashed every 2 s, debris and particles at the quality cap), not `warehouse` as written in P0-04. A hazard scene is therefore covered by the benchmark itself; `subway`, `construction` and `pit` crowd brawls were measured on low-spec as a cross-check (below). Menu = main menu showcase, 6 s.
- Tools: (1) `performance.now()` wrappers around about 35 systems in a scratch copy of the game (`window.__bp` exposed; the copy is outside the repo); (2) CDP `Profiler` sampling at 200 us; (3) CDP `HeapProfiler` sampling (allocation by function); (4) Chrome trace with the V8 GC categories. Wrapper overhead inflates per-system times by roughly 15 to 25 %: use them for ranking and proportions, not as absolute values. Scratch files (temporary, may be gone): `C:\Users\GS\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\p1846\`. To repeat without them: (1) copy the game and insert `window.__bp = { Game, R, FX, Debris, Arena, Camera, Quality, Diag, Events, UI, Showcase, Settings, SimRunner, Tournament, Fighter, MatchSim, AIController, Combat, Music, Sound, Inputs }` before `window.BREAKPOINT = {`; wrap each listed method with a `performance.now()` sum and count (the `MatchSim.prototype` steps, `Fighter.prototype.animate`/`update`/`draw`/`computePose`/`walkSkeleton`, `AIController.prototype.think`, `Arena`/`Debris`/`FX` `update` and `draw`, `R.render`, `UI.update`/`frame`, `Inputs.update`, `Game.frame`, the WebGL calls and `navigator.getGamepads`); a frame over 12 ms logs every system that took over 0.8 ms of it. (2) CDP: `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate {rate: 4}`; `Profiler.setSamplingInterval {interval: 200}`, `Profiler.start`/`stop` around one benchmark; `HeapProfiler.startSampling {samplingInterval: 32768, includeObjectsCollectedByMajorGC: true, includeObjectsCollectedByMinorGC: true}` / `stopSampling` around the same 10 s; `Tracing.start` with categories `devtools.timeline`, `disabled-by-default-devtools.timeline`, `v8`, `disabled-by-default-v8.gc`, `blink.user_timing`. (3) Long frames and start-up: a `requestAnimationFrame` interval counter running beside `BREAKPOINT.benchmark(10, opts)` (the first second skipped, as the benchmark does), and an init script that records `performance.now()` at the first frame where `BREAKPOINT.diagnostics().state` is the menu.
- Not measured: GPU time (frame interval is pinned to 16.7 ms by vsync, so GPU headroom is unknown; draw calls are only 6 to 13, so the draw-call count is not a problem) and a real phone (P16-03).

#### Baseline (3 runs each; ranges are min to max over the 3 runs)

| Run | Frame p50 / p95 / max (ms) | Work p50 / p95 / max (ms) | Draws | Instances | Debris / particles | Heap (MB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low-spec, 1v1 | 16.7 / 16.8 / 33.3 to 33.4 | 3.1 to 3.6 / 5.1 to 5.5 / 26.1 to 40.8 | 10 | 351 to 366 | 60 / 140 | 9.5 |
| Low-spec, crowd 7 fighters | 16.7 / 16.8 / 33.4 to 50.1 | 3.8 to 4.5 / 5.8 to 6.8 / 30.5 to 34.9 | 9 to 10 | 517 to 519 | 60 / 140 | 9.5 |
| Desktop, 1v1 | 16.7 / 16.8 / 17.1 to 17.4 | 1.1 to 1.2 / 2.2 to 2.5 / 6.0 to 13.4 | 13 | 731 to 769 | 170 / 520 | 9.5 |
| Desktop, crowd 7 fighters | 16.7 / 16.8 / 16.9 to 17.2 | 1.2 to 1.5 / 1.9 to 2.5 / 6.1 to 20.8 | 12 to 13 | 1038 to 1091 | 170 / 520 | 9.5 |

- P0-04 pass rule (frame p95 <= 18 ms, work p95 <= 8 ms): met in every run; the one reading above 8 ms was a profiled run (8.3 to 8.5 ms with the Profiler attached). The game is not slow on average; what is left is headroom on a real phone (about 4x slower than this CPU, plus a GPU not measured here), single-frame spikes, and menu idle cost.
- Long frames (frame intervals over 20 ms in the 10 s after warm-up, runs 1 / 2 / 3 per row, no profiler or trace attached, 2026-11-07 11:00): low-spec 1v1 4 / 0 / 1 (max 35.8 ms); low-spec crowd 3 / 3 / 3 (max 36.1 ms); desktop 1v1 1 / 0 / 0 (max 21.0 ms); desktop crowd 1 / 0 / 0 (max 24.0 ms). In today's counter runs every low-spec long frame was one missed vsync (33 to 36 ms); the baseline runs above once reached 50.1 ms (two missed vsyncs); work spikes of 26 to 41 ms cause them. On desktop only the first run after a page load has one. The traced low-spec crowd run had 21 after its first 0.5 s (tracing adds cost).
- Start-up (navigation start to the first menu frame, served from the local preview, so no network time; a phone download of the 1.18 MB file comes on top): throttle 4 at 640x360 621 to 684 ms (script parsed and run by 271 to 290 ms; the boot routine `Diag.startupMs` 266 to 298 ms: renderer, pools, input, showcase); desktop 230 to 231 ms (boot 106 to 116 ms). Not a hotspot today; P18-47 keeps it in the benchmark result and checks it on a phone in P16-03.
- Allocation and GC (crowd, low-spec, 11 s trace; desktop GC not measured): the trace's V8 events show 2 scavenges (`MinorGC`, 7.4 ms total, max 3.9 ms) and 2 mark-compacts (`MajorGC`, 16 ms total, max 9.1 ms, with 52 incremental marking slices). Their used heap before and after (42.5 to 10.3, 37.5 to 10.8, 35.7 to 9.9, 21.7 to 10.2 MB) shows about 96 MB reclaimed in 11 s, about 8.7 MB/s or about 145 KB per frame; the young generation grows to about 30 MB before a scavenge, which is why there are only 2. The heap sampler's figure (about 182 KB per frame, about 11 MB/s, settings as in Tools) is of the same size and also counts what is still alive at the end. GC is 0.2 % of the time, but the two major GCs line up with the 25 to 35 ms frames that no system accounts for (spike log below). The 9.5 MB in the table is the benchmark's `performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize`, which Chrome rounds; the trace's used heap after each GC is 9.9 to 10.8 MB and does not grow, so there is no leak.
- Main-thread split (trace, low-spec crowd, 10 s): animation-frame callbacks 3.7 s of 10 s at 4x; style recalculation 0.42 s, layout 0.11 s, paint 0.08 s (the HUD DOM is about 5 % of the thread).
- Sim cost without rendering (`BREAKPOINT.simulate`, desktop): 22 to 35 us per tick (warehouse 35, rooftop 29, dojo 22, subway 25). A Tournament of 8 = 7 CPU matches = 648 ms, 28,148 ticks (about 90 ms per match as one uninterrupted task, about 360 ms at throttle 4). A 16-bracket is 15 matches. Of one headless match (160 ms instrumented): `Fighter.animate` 34 %, `readIntents` (AI) 15 %, `updateFighters` 9 %, `physics` 6 %.

Per-system cost per frame (ms, throttle 4, low, instrumented; share of frame total):

| System | 1v1 | Crowd | Menu |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frame total | 4.18 | 4.93 | 1.96 |
| Sim step (all ticks) | 1.21 (29 %) | 1.52 (31 %) | 0.27 animate only |
| of it: `Fighter.animate` (pose + matrix pass) | 0.39 | 0.46 | 0.27 |
| of it: AI `readIntents` / `ai.think` | 0.22 / 0.20 | 0.41 / 0.39 | - |

| of it: HUD DOM (`UI.frame` > `hudUpdate`) | 0.66 (16 %) | 0.80 (16 %) | 0.05 |

Desktop (throttle 1) crowd for scale: frame total 1.64 ms, render 0.86, sim step 0.59, HUD 0.22, GL submit 0.16. Menu desktop 0.56 ms per frame. Crowd cross-check on low-spec in other arenas: `subway` 4.73, `construction` 3.99, `pit` 4.82 ms per frame (same split; hazard drawing 0.05 to 0.08 ms; 6 to 7 draws).

Spike log (low-spec, frames over 12 ms, which system took more than 0.8 ms of them): the AI think of one tick took 9 to 13 ms at ticks 5, 58, 354 (right after the benchmark's object smash); `resolveCombat` 9.8 ms once; `Fighter.draw` 14.5 ms once (an expression face repainted into the atlas); HUD `UI.frame` 11.5 ms once; `Inputs.update` 6 ms once; about half of the over-20 ms frames have no system above 2 ms (garbage-collector pauses and the browser).

#### Hotspots, ranked (by frame share, then by spike or allocation harm)

1. Fighter pose and skeleton matrix walk (3 passes per fighter per frame: `computePose`, `walkSkeleton` once per tick in `animate` with draw off, once per frame in `draw`). Evidence: `Fighter.animate` 0.46 plus `draw.fighter` 0.47 = 0.93 ms in the crowd (19 % of the frame, 1v1 0.62); second run, 7.6 draw walks and 7.9 sim walks per frame, `walkSkeleton` + `computePose` 1.8 ms instrumented; Profiler self time `walkSkeleton:6740`, `computePose:6361`, `rotX/rotY/rotZ` (about 3 % together); allocations `walkSkeleton` 19 KB and `computePose` 9.5 KB per frame (15 % of all garbage); in the headless sim it is 34 % of the run.
   - Change: (a) in the sim pass (`Fighter.animate` > `skeleton(..., false)`), skip the walk when pose, position, yaw, scale and plant shift are bit-identical to the last walk (idle, stunned, down and held fighters; the key points `pts` are kept); (b) in the draw pass only, replace the generic 4x4 matrix stack by cheaper steps (cached sine and cosine, no `Float32Array`/array allocation per call); (c) remove per-call allocations in `computePose`/`walkSkeleton` (scratch arrays).
   - Expected gain: (a) is unproven: `computePose` reads `animT` (`:6366`), which `animate` advances every tick (`:6321`), so even idle, stunned and down fighters rarely get identical inputs; measure first how often the inputs repeat, and drop (a) if they rarely do. Until then the gain rests on (b) and (c): about 0.15 to 0.3 ms per frame at throttle 4 (3 to 6 % of the crowd frame), a few percent off the headless sim, about 25 KB/frame less garbage.
   - Risk: medium for (a) and (c) (they touch what hit detection reads), low for (b) (render only).
   - Sim and fingerprints: unchanged only if (a) skips exactly when the inputs are bit-identical and (c) keeps the operation order; (b) must not touch the sim pass, because any reordering of floating-point steps in the sim pass can shift `pts` in the last bits and change a fingerprint. Verify with the full self-test and with the `simulate` canary below.

2. HUD DOM update, every frame (`UI.frame` > `hudUpdate`, `tagMarker`, `edgeMarks`, `setTransform`, `setHtml`, `bar`, floating hit pops). Evidence: 0.80 ms per frame in the crowd (16 %), 0.66 in 1v1; the top JavaScript self-time function in the Profiler (`hudUpdate:14638`, 240 ms of 12.3 s, plus `setTransform:13360` 136 ms, `setHtml:13359` 43 ms, `bar:14641` 31 ms); 5.8 KB/frame garbage (name-tag strings, `toFixed`, label concatenation built before the cache compares them); style recalculation 4 % of the thread; 11.5 ms spike once.
   - Change: compare numbers before building strings (quantize hp and stamina fractions to the 1/1000 step first and compare the integers; build a name tag's label and status only when the fighter's state or hp changed); update the 7 tags and the pops only when their rounded position or text changed; skip `touchContextUpdate` when no touch input has been used; update text-only fields (round label, mode info, timer, items) on state change or at 10 Hz, not 60 Hz.
   - Expected gain: 0.3 to 0.4 ms (6 to 8 %); 5 KB/frame less garbage; fewer style recalculations.
   - Risk: low (display only, values read from the sim, never written).
   - Sim and fingerprints: unchanged (the HUD reads the match, it never writes it; the HUD tests keep the output text identical).

3. Navigation map rebuild after every collider change, and AI think. Evidence: `navMap:3564` is the top allocator (32 KB/frame, 18 % of all garbage); 16 rebuilds in one 10 s crowd run, 2.1 to 14.8 ms each at throttle 4 (123 ms total; 2,520 cells x all colliders), twice per smash (after `Arena.reset`, then after the breakage); the AI-think spikes of 9 to 13 ms at the first ticks after a smash; `pathBlocked:3552` 4 KB/frame and `obstacleSupport:4155` 3 KB/frame. In real play one rebuild happens each time a prop breaks or a deck collapses, so every breakage is a one-frame hitch on a phone.
   - Change: rebuild only the cells within a collider's box plus its reach (`r`, 0.1 and the step slack) when a collider changed, instead of the whole grid; keep the buffers across `Arena.reset` (no new typed arrays when the cell count is equal); hoist `for...of` iteration and the temporary arrays in `pathBlocked` and `obstacleSupport`.
   - Expected gain: removes the 5 to 15 ms hitch per breakage at throttle 4 (1.5 to 4 ms on desktop); about 35 KB/frame less garbage in a breaking scene (about 19 % of all garbage); the average frame gain is small (0.1 ms) but the p95/max gain is the largest of the plan.
   - Risk: medium (the map decides where the CPU walks).
   - Sim and fingerprints: unchanged by construction only if the incremental result equals the full rebuild cell for cell: add a self-test that applies random collider changes and compares `foot` and `ok` with a full rebuild, then run the fingerprints.

4. GL submit and instance upload (`R.render`). Evidence: 0.47 to 0.51 ms per frame in every scene (10 % of the crowd frame, 24 % of the menu frame, constant regardless of what is drawn); per frame 9 to 13 `bufferData(DYNAMIC_DRAW)` calls with a fresh `subarray` view each (`subarray` 6.3 KB/frame garbage), about 33 uniform calls, about 13 VAO binds, state toggles for stencil, polygon offset and blend; the instrumented calls cost: `bufferData` 0.2, `uniform*` 0.17, `clear` 0.08, `bindVertexArray` 0.07 ms.
   - Change: upload with `bufferSubData` into buffers sized once (grown only when a batch grows), or the `bufferData(target, data, usage, srcOffset, length)` overload with no view allocation; cache the environment uniforms (light, fog, sky, point lights) and set them only when the arena or environment changed; one `uVP` upload per frame; skip empty layers earlier; no `clear` of stencil when the shadow mode is off.
   - Expected gain: 0.15 to 0.25 ms (3 to 5 %), 6 KB/frame less garbage; larger share in menus.
   - Risk: low (output must be pixel-identical: compare screenshots of three scenes before and after).
   - Sim and fingerprints: unchanged (render only).

5. Per-frame garbage and repeated work in the scene draw (`Arena.draw`, `drawRubble`, `drawFireDoor`, hazards `hput`, `drawItems`/`useCues`, `Debris.draw`, `FX.draw`). Evidence: together 0.74 ms per frame in the crowd (15 %: arena 0.26, items 0.17, debris 0.13, fx 0.11, hazards 0.07; `drawItems` costs 0.16 to 0.20 ms even with no item on the floor); allocation samples: `draw:3801` 9.0 KB, `draw:4172` 7.6 KB, `drawRubble:4052` 6.7 KB, `draw:4243` 5.1 KB, `drawHazards` 2.4 KB, `drawItems` 2.1 KB per frame (about 15 % of all garbage). Causes seen in the code: `C('#hex')` colour parsing and `for (const s of [-1, 1])` array literals inside draw loops, `cued` array rebuilt each frame, a `hput(..., '#hex', ...)` string parse per hazard part.
   - Change: hoist all colour literals to module constants parsed once, reuse scratch arrays, return early from `drawItems` when `this.items` is empty and no cue is active; optional second step: keep the instance data of intact static props (no bob, no lean, no fade, not in LOD change) and re-push only the changed ones.
   - Expected gain: step 1 (garbage and hoisting) 0.1 to 0.2 ms and 25 KB/frame less garbage (14 % of all); step 2 (static cache) a further 0.15 to 0.2 ms (arena 0.26 to about 0.1).
   - Risk: low for step 1; medium for step 2 (stale cache when an object breaks, the camera ceiling fade, the LOD swap every 20 draws).
   - Sim and fingerprints: unchanged (render only).

6. Gamepad polling every frame (`Inputs.update` > `navigator.getGamepads()`). Evidence: `Inputs.update` 0.18 to 0.21 ms per frame (4 % of a match frame, 9 % of a menu frame); `getGamepads` 0.13 to 0.15 ms of it (instrumented) and 0.3 % in the Profiler; a 6 ms spike once.
   - Change: poll only when a pad has been announced by `gamepadconnected` (or one was seen once); keep keyboard and touch untouched.
   - Expected gain: 0.1 to 0.15 ms (2 to 3 %).
   - Risk: low, but check that Chrome still lists a pad that was connected before the page got focus (the pad appears on the first press; the event fires then), so test with a real pad in P16-03.
   - Sim and fingerprints: unchanged (input is read the same way once a pad exists).

7. Face atlas repaint on an expression change. Evidence: one 14.5 ms (throttle 4) frame in `Fighter.draw` (`FaceTex.slot` > `paint` on a 2D canvas, then `texSubImage2D` of 16 KB cells with a CPU premultiply loop in `texels`).
   - Change: paint a fighter's expressions when the match is built (or spread one per frame over the countdown) so the fight never paints; precompute the premultiplied cell once.
   - Expected gain: removes a 5 to 15 ms single-frame hitch on the first hurt, tired or win face of each fighter.
   - Risk: low.
   - Sim and fingerprints: unchanged (render only).

8. Menu idle cost. Evidence: the main menu draws the showcase every frame at 60 Hz: 1.96 ms at throttle 4 (0.56 ms on desktop) with nothing happening (arena 0.33, GL submit 0.48, 2 fighter walks 0.5, input 0.18). On a phone this is constant battery and heat for a screen that mostly shows panels.
   - Change: draw the showcase at 30 Hz (every second frame, game time still advanced) while a menu panel is open and no preview is being turned or dragged, and at 60 Hz in the character creator preview, the pause screen and the results; stop drawing when a full-screen opaque panel covers the canvas.
   - Expected gain: about 50 % of the menu cost (about 1 ms per frame at throttle 4, averaged); no effect during a fight.
   - Risk: medium for feel (menu animation at 30 Hz): a DECIDE for the owner, or keep 60 Hz and only stop drawing behind opaque panels.
   - Sim and fingerprints: unchanged (the showcase is outside the match and the fixed tick).

9. Tournament and bracket simulation blocks the main thread in 90 ms (desktop) to about 360 ms (throttle 4) chunks per CPU match (`Tournament.simulate` > `SimRunner.run`, 22 to 35 us per tick, 4,000 to 5,700 ticks per match, one `setTimeout(0)` between matches only).
   - Change: let `SimRunner.run` run in time slices (for example 6 ms, then yield through `MessageChannel` or `setTimeout(0)`) with the same state kept between slices, so the bracket progress bar and touch stay responsive. The run uses page-wide state: it swaps `Events.handlers` (`:11413`, restored at `:11451`), draws from the shared `simRng` (`:393`, `:9753`) and builds its level in the shared `Arena` and `Debris`/`FX` (the caller resets `Showcase.arenaId` after it, `:12274`). So each slice saves and restores `simRng`, `Events.handlers` and the Arena/Debris/FX state around itself, or the menu scene stops updating and drawing until the run ends (simpler; the bracket screen then shows only the progress bar).
   - Expected gain: no change in total time; longest task falls from about 360 ms to about 8 ms at throttle 4.
   - Risk: medium (the run loop becomes resumable; the result must be identical).
   - Sim and fingerprints: unchanged only if nothing outside the run touches `simRng`, the handlers or the level between slices (above); check by running the same seeds sliced and unsliced in the live page with the bracket screen open, not headless, and comparing the whole result objects.

10. Whole-program garbage. Evidence: 182 KB/frame, 2 scavenges and 2 mark-compacts per 10 s (max 9.1 ms at throttle 4), unattributed 25 to 35 ms frames. Items 1(c), 2, 3, 4 and 5 remove the top allocators (together about 60 % of the sampled bytes).
   - Target: below 70 KB/frame, no mark-compact in a 10 s benchmark; count with the same `HeapProfiler` sampling and trace.
   - Risk and sim effect: as the items above.

Rejected or left alone: draw calls (6 to 13 per frame; instancing already merges every part of a layer and mesh, nothing to gain); `FX.update`/`Debris.update` (0.03 and 0.09 ms); the Web Audio and `Music.update` (0.006 ms); camera (0.13 ms); moving the sim to a Web Worker (the game is one closure in one file and shares state with the renderer: large change, no measured need); lowering the fixed 60 Hz tick (changes the fighting game and every fingerprint, never).

#### Plan for BP-P18-47 (order of work, one measured change at a time, same method as above)

- Order: 2 HUD, 4 GL submit, 5 step 1 garbage, 6 gamepad, 7 face prepaint (all render or display side, sim untouched); then 1(b) draw-pass skeleton; then, each behind its own proof, 3 nav map (incremental rebuild with the equality self-test), 1(a)/(c) sim-pass skip; last 9 slicing, and 8 only after the owner decides. Item 5 step 2 only if the sum falls short.
- Expected result at low-spec crowd (to be confirmed by measuring, not promised): work p50 4.0 to about 3.0 ms, p95 6 to 8 ms to about 4.5 to 6 ms, work max 30 to 40 ms to below 20 ms, garbage 182 to below 70 KB/frame, no mark-compact per 10 s; menu 1.96 to about 1 ms. Sum of the item gains at throttle 4 is about 1.0 to 1.5 ms of the 4.93 ms frame (20 to 30 %), with 1(a) counted as zero until it is measured.
- Proof per item (the sim must not move): full browser self-test (497 of 497 at last count, plus the new tests), the fingerprint tests unchanged, and the canary below before and after; every render item also a screenshot comparison of the menu, a 1v1 and a crowd brawl at 640x360 and 1280x720. Small items (0.1 to 0.25 ms) are judged on the instrumented per-system time (median of 5 runs) and the canary, because with 3 runs the whole-frame work p50 already spreads by up to 0.7 ms; the rule that the new whole-frame range must not overlap the baseline range applies to the final sum. No other metric may get worse.
- Determinism canary (`BREAKPOINT.simulate({ playerId: 'kai', opponentId: 'mara', arenaId, difficulty: 'expert', seed: 7, winsNeeded: 2, timer: 60 })`, desktop Chrome 157, commit `8aa8c39`): warehouse winner 1, 4303 ticks; rooftop winner 1, 4290 ticks; dojo winner 0, 4809 ticks; subway winner 1, 5751 ticks. Re-record on the day P18-47 starts (main moves), then compare after each change; the whole result object (damage per type, health left) must match, not only winner and ticks.
- Add a long-frame counter (frame intervals above 20 ms) and the allocation figure to the benchmark result so later runs compare the same numbers.
- Size: the changes add a few hundred bytes to a few kilobytes of code; far below the 4,000,000 byte budget.
- Owner decision: item 8 (menu drawn at 30 Hz); device check on a real phone and a gamepad goes to the P16-03 list (frame numbers, `getGamepads` change, GPU time with a timer query).

### P18-17 menu selection audit (2026-11-07)

- Base: `main` at 2041038, `breakpoint.html` read only (no edit, no run, no browser; this pass is `rg` and reading). Line numbers are that file at that commit. Severity: High = a screen on a main path where more than one item looks current, or the current one cannot be told from a remembered pick; Medium = a wrong or missing current item on a device combination, or an item that looks usable and is not; Low = cosmetic; Info = a note. Findings marked "not verified" come from the code and the browsers' documented rules, not from a measurement; each names the check that settles it.
- Scope: every screen in `UI.screen_*` (main, modes, char, coop, freefight, freemore, lineup, setup, arena, controls, moves, settings, story, scene, unlocks, credits, pause, results, replace, bracket) and the creator (`CreatorUI.render`, tabs, rows, swatches, Library), on mouse, keyboard (`UI.onKey` 13590), gamepad (`UI.update` 14546, `Inputs.lobbyPad`) and touch (`UI.onClick` 13626, registered at 13254). Question asked of each: how many items look current at once, which look means what, and does the look follow the device in use.
- Result: 15 findings: 3 High, 6 Medium, 5 Low, 1 Info. Root cause of the High findings: one outline style (`3px solid var(--a1)`, offset 2px, background `#182a55`) is used for four different meanings - keyboard / pad focus (`:focus-visible`), mouse hover (`:hover`), a remembered pick (`.sel`) and a chosen swatch (`.sw.on`) - and the game never moves the focus to where the mouse is. A second item looks current either from a second input (a parked mouse, a sticky touch hover) or on its own (a remembered pick next to the focus; chosen swatches, M08).
- Task status: AC-001 has four parts. Met by this entry: "Appendix D lists each finding". Not met: "exactly one item looks current with mouse, keyboard, gamepad and touch" (M01 to M06 and M08 still happen in the code), "a remembered pick has its own look" (F1) and "a self-test checks the rule on each menu screen" (none exists; F4). P18-17 stays open until F1 to F4 are built and their tests pass in Chrome; the touch and pad checks go to P16-03.
- Supersedes F10 (= M02, M04) and F11 (= M01) of the P17-01 audit; mark both "moved to P18-17".
- The looks today (CSS lines): `button.mi:hover, :focus-visible, .sel` 41 (plus the "▶ " prefix on `:focus-visible` and `.sel` 42); `.opt:focus-visible, :hover` 48; `.card:hover, :focus-visible, .sel` 54; `.tab:focus-visible, :hover` 87 (the chosen tab has its own look, 86); `.beat` 247; `.scenebox` 255; `.sw.on` 101 (`.sw:hover` only whitens the border, 100); `.crin:focus` 114. No `@media (hover:hover)` and no `:not([disabled])` anywhere in the stylesheet. Page-wide: no `pointerover`, `mouseover`, `mouseenter` or `pointermove` handler on the menu (`rg` finds only the creator drag at 15083 and the touch stick at 14959), so hover never becomes focus.

| ID | Sev | Area | Location | Reproduction | Fix (task) | Status |

| M01 | High | Remembered pick looks like the focus | CSS 41, 42, 54; markup `fighterCard` 13881 (used 13896, 13899, 14131), arena list 14151, Library slot card 15817 | Play > Arcade (or Training, Versus, a Free Fight slot, a Tournament entrant): the fighter screen opens with the picked card (`.sel`, ✓) focused. Press Right or Down, or push the stick: the focus moves to the next card, but `.sel` stays on the first (focus only moves; the pick changes on Enter, `pickFighter` 13747). Two cards now show the identical outline and background. On the arena list both items also carry the "▶ " prefix (42), so the two are identical down to the glyph. Pressing Enter on the focused one picks it, so the player cannot tell from the look which Enter will pick and which will start the fight ("picking the card already selected confirms it", 13746). The three High findings (except M02's after-a-click case, which rests on M05) and M03, M07, M09, M12, M13 are plain stylesheet and markup facts.
- Existing tests: `breakpoint-tests.js` has no test on how a menu looks (`rg` for `outline`, `focus-visible`, `.sel`, `getComputedStyle` finds none; the P18-40 flow tests use stand-in elements and `document.activeElement` only, header of "Mode flows (P18-40)"). The one layout test that needs a page, "Tournament (P11-03) ... the bracket of 8 drawn in the page fits" at `breakpoint-tests.js` 11673, shows the way: it returns `'skipped: ...'` in a headless run and measures in a browser.

**Fix design (for the tasks below)**

1. One meaning per look. Current (one at a time, always the DOM focus): the existing outline + background; also "▶" on `button.mi`. Remembered pick (`.sel`): no outline, no ▶; a 2px `var(--a1)` border and a corner ✓ badge (CSS `::after`), with a faint tint; same for arena items, fighter cards and Library slots; swatch: white border and ✓ only. Hover: no outline at all.
2. The pointer drives the focus only when it moves. A `pointermove` handler on `#screens` (only `pointerType === 'mouse'`) focuses `e.target.closest('[data-nav]')` with `focus({preventScroll:true})` and no sound, and only when `clientX`/`clientY` changed since its last call. `pointerover` is not used: Chromium fires boundary events when the content under a still pointer changes (a scroll from `focus()`, a `rerender`), and a parked mouse would take the focus back. Skipped for disabled items, while a creator text field is being typed in, and while `CreatorUI.drag` is set. Then the `:hover` outline rules can be deleted (cursor stays); touch has no hover look, so nothing sticks (M04).
3. The focus look uses `:focus` inside `#screens` instead of `:focus-visible` (every focus there is a menu focus), so the ring no longer depends on the browser's last input guess (M05).
4. `onClick` focuses the nearest `[data-nav]` of the target (`preventScroll:true`) before it acts, so `rerender(true)` finds it on Safari (M06).

### P18-69 mobile-first menu audit (2026-11-10)

- Base: `main` at 04bf47a, branch `bp-p18-69-menus`; `breakpoint.html` read only (no game file changed). Line numbers are that file. The decision and the fix list are in Appendix C, "P18-69 mobile-first menu layout, decided".
- Method: headless Chrome 157 driven from Node with `playwright-core` (found in the npx cache, used as a library, nothing installed), `--use-angle=swiftshader`, launched with `TEMP` and `TMP` in the browser-profiles folder and closed in `finally`. The game was loaded from a scratch copy of `breakpoint.html` with one added line, `window.__bp = testApi();`, before `boot();` (the game does not export its screens; no other byte differs), with `?nointro`, from a `file:` URL, no server. Touch emulation (touch, mobile user agent) at 390x844, 844x390 and 768x1024, mouse at 1280x720, device scale 1. Each screen was reached through the game's own `UI.act`, `Game.chooseMode`, `Game.applyType`, `CreatorUI.switchTab` and a real fight played to its end (the opponent or the player knocked out through `Combat.knockOut`). Per screen a script measured: sideways scroll of the page and of every scroller, the way to every control (scrolled into view, then `elementFromPoint` at its centre must return it), the size of every control, overlaps (boxes cut by their scrolling parent), text clipped by `overflow:hidden`, text under 12 px, the panel box and, in a fight, the HUD boxes against the touch buttons. The touch scrolling of the creator was tried with real touch events (`Input.dispatchTouchEvent`). The screenshots and the numbers (`results-*.json`) are in `C:/Users/GS/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/bp-p1869/` (not in the repo).
- Captured: 54 states at each of the four sizes (52 screens and overlays of the matrix, the intro card, and the creator's Identity tab with a keyboard open, shown as a shorter viewport) = 216 screenshots; plus the creator and 9 other screens at 667x375, 640x360, 844x340, 360x640 and 320x568 (the shapes of an iPhone SE and mini, an Android phone, a phone with a browser bar), the main screens at UI scale 1.5 (390x844 and 844x390) and the creator touch test. Zero page errors in every run.
- Severity: High = a screen on a main path cannot be used, or a control cannot be found, at a size a phone has; Medium = it can be used but a control is under 44 px, hidden behind a scroll, covered, or the screen starts in the wrong place; Low = looks wrong, nothing is blocked; Info = a note.
- Result: 23 findings: 5 High, 11 Medium, 6 Low, 1 Info. No control was unreachable (every one can be brought into view) and the page itself never scrolls sideways at the four sizes; a panel or row does in five places (L02, L05, L16, L20 and the bracket box, which is meant to). The Highs are the creator at every phone shape but the 768 and 1280 ones, and the Controls table. The 3D menu picture is never covered by a control; it is covered by the panel only on the creator and fighter screens, where the fighter stays in view at every size.
